title: incidents
body:
incidents

incidents-bot: :rotating_light: SEV-2 alert: elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate across us-west-2. Trigger: 5xx rate > 2% for 10m. Incident channel opened.

maria.lopez: saw the page 20m ago. oncall responding now. observing sustained error spike and token-level latency increase. user-facing errors ~1.8% at peak.

kevin.chen: paging in — I can take lead for mitigation. which customers are affected? any big tenants?

samir.patel: quick glance at dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/ab12/prefix-cache?orgId=1 shows a simultaneous drop in `prefix_cache_hitrate` around 15:07 UTC. looks like a cache miss storm.

anne.wu: confirming, our KV cache hitrate dropped from 92% -> 12% within ~3 minutes. CPU on serving boxes spiked too.

jules.carter: customers with high QPS on /v1/generate saw amplified cost and latency — support ticket #SUP-4127 opened.

maria.lopez: mitigation plan: 1) rate-limit or throttle non-urgent routes 2) enable fallback-model route for enterprise tenants 3) investigate cache invalidation pipeline. who's on logs?

kevin.chen: running log query on log-shipper:```
# quick ELK query
index=redwood-logs env=prod "prefix_cache_miss" | stats count() by service, cluster, minute
```

samir.patel: sharing quick sample from request logs (sanitized):```text
2026-03-15T15:06:49Z service=runtime shard=shard-12 msg="cache miss" key=prefix:customer123:session42
2026-03-15T15:06:50Z service=runtime shard=shard-07 msg="cache miss" key=prefix:customer456:recent
2026-03-15T15:06:51Z service=runtime shard=shard-12 msg="cache invalidate" key=prefix:customer123:session42 cause=ttl
```

anne.wu: note: TTLs didn't change in config. there was a config push ~15:05 but it was for logging flags only. deploy-bot, any deploys around that time?

deploy-bot: Deployment event: devops/service-telemetry @ 2026-03-15T15:04:30Z by ci-cd. Changes: logging metadata only. No cache config updates detected. :white_check_mark:

kevin.chen: hypothesis A: automated rewarm job failed -> mass cache invalidation + many cold misses. Hypothesis B: mistaken mass `DEL` or prefix invalidation from internal tool. we need to check invalidation logs and KV admin audit.

maria.lopez: person on audit logs? can someone grep KV admin actions between 15:00-15:10 UTC?

jules.carter: running KV audit query now:```
# KV audit
index=redwood-admin namespace=kv_actions action=invalidate OR action=del | where timestamp >= "2026-03-15T15:00:00Z" and timestamp <= "2026-03-15T15:10:00Z"
```

jules.carter: results: 1 automated job `prefix-rewarm` attempted targeted invalidation at 15:05:12 UTC but returned repeated `timeout` errors and then issued a fallback broad invalidate at 15:06:10 UTC.

samir.patel: that matches the hitrate drop. looks like the rewarm tool retry logic flipped to broad sweep on failures — producing the fallthrough.

kevin.chen: mitigation actions executed in order:```text
- 15:08 UTC: disable rewarm job (manual kill)
- 15:09 UTC: enable cache-bypass for non-enterprise tenants -> reduced churn
- 15:12 UTC: scale serving pool + add read replicas for KV
```

maria.lopez: impact assessment: peak error rate 1.8% for 9m, increased tail latency ~300ms p99 for 12m. logged customer escalations: 2 paying customers reported degraded throughput; no data loss.

anne.wu: post-mitigation: hitrate climbed back up to 88% by 15:30 UTC. CPU normalized by 15:40 UTC.

kevin.chen: for the in-thread RCA we should collect: KV audit logs, rewarm job logs, admin tool logs, timeline of deploys, and the prefix invalidation diffs. I'll take rewarm job logs. assigning: @kevin.chen -> rewarm logs; @jules.carter -> KV admin audit; @samir.patel -> serving runtime metrics and hit-rate graph; @anne.wu -> customer impact summary + support tickets.

jules.carter: copying truncated rewarm job log snippet:```text
[15:05:11] rewarm: start scan prefix=customer_* batch=100
[15:05:20] rewarm: write timeout to kv shard-07 err=ETIMEDOUT
[15:05:22] rewarm: retry 1
[15:06:05] rewarm: retry limit reached, escalating to broad-invalidate
[15:06:10] rewarm: issued broad_invalidate(scope=prefix_approx)
```

samir.patel: runtime metrics link: https://grafana.redwood/internal/d/ab12/prefix-cache?from=2026-03-15T15:00:00Z&to=2026-03-15T16:00:00Z — attaching differential export and a small ascii timeline:```text
15:04 - normal
15:05 - rewarm start
15:06 - broad invalidation issued -> hitrate cliff
15:08 - rewarm disabled
15:09 - bypass enabled, partial relief
15:12 - scaled pool
15:30 - hitrate ~88% back
```

maria.lopez: quick decisions for RCA action items: 1) immediate: add safer fallback for rewarm job (no broad invalidates) 2) short-term: circuit-breaker to prevent retries turning into broad ops 3) long-term: redesign rewarm to use guarded, per-shard invalidation + back-pressure. assign owners and due dates.

kevin.chen: logging TODOs added to incident ticket INC-2026-0315-08. I'll create a PR to change rewarm fallback logic to fail-safe by EOD.

anne.wu: customer comms: drafting a summary for the two affected customers, ETA 2h. adding follow-up: credits + postmortem after RCA.

jules.carter: evidence bundle: attached KV audit export, rewarm logs, grafana snapshots, support tickets. storing in /incidents/INC-2026-0315-08/artifacts.

maria.lopez: good work everyone. we'll reconvene tomorrow for RCA write-up. tagging follow-ups: @kevin.chen (rewarm PR), @jules.carter (audit export), @anne.wu (customer comms). closing live mitigation thread. :white_check_mark:

title: eng-releases
body:
eng-releases

Connor O'Brien: perf gate flaked again on the 1.18.1-lts RC. Gate says p95 latency regression > threshold on A100. Anyone else looking at the perf-canary artifact?

perf-canary-bot: ❌ LTS Perf Gate: FAILED
Branch: runtime-1.18-lts
Candidate: rc-2025-03-05-1
Workload: chat-mix-v2 (seq_len mixed)
GPU: A100-80GB
Metric: p95 end-to-end latency
Result: +3.4% regression (threshold: +2.0%)
Artifact: https://perf-canary.redwood.dev/runs/1741192871

Connor O'Brien: It passed on H100 and L40S, and throughput deltas are basically noise. This one is just p95 A100. Before we hit the panic button: is this runner contention again?

Sahana Iyer: CI side: runner pool for perf is super hot right now. Queue depth jumped after we merged the release-branch workflow changes. I see 4 other perf jobs sharing the same bare metal host group. Not supposed to, but the scheduler is packing.

Marcus Reed: Looking at the run details now. The p50 is actually slightly better (-0.6%). p95 is where it blows up. That pattern (p50 ok, p95 worse) is usually tail latency from noisy neighbor / CPU steal / IO hiccup vs a real kernel change.

Claire Dubois: +1. Also check if we had a different prompt distribution on this run. The artifact says “chat-mix-v2”, but sometimes the seed changes and the long-tail prompts amplify noise.

Marcus Reed: Seed looks consistent with the last passing run. But the host telemetry panel shows occasional spikes in “host cpu wait” and “disk read latency”. Not huge, but aligned with the p95 spikes.

Jonas Weber: Reminder: we tightened p95 thresholds for LTS in perf-canary PR-427. We’re now at +2.0% for p95 on that workload. That’s fine, but it also means we need an explicit anti-flake policy (rerun count / median) or we’re going to keep burning release days.

Connor O'Brien: For *this* RC: do we rerun and proceed if it clears? Or do we hold and investigate deeper? We’re trying to publish today.

Sean Gallagher: From SRE POV: I’m ok with a rerun *if* we can attribute the failure to infrastructure noise. But I don’t want “rerun until green” as the implicit policy. We need one controlled rerun on a known-clean runner pool.

Allison Grant: Checking the perf runner dashboards: around the failure window there’s a spike in GPU host interrupts and CPU iowait on the A100 pool. Also another long-running job started ~3 min before the p95 went sideways. So it’s plausible contention.

Rafael Mendes: If we ship with a real p95 regression we’ll hear about it fast (Dedicated customers are super sensitive). I’d support rerun once on a drained host group, and if it fails again, we block.

Devon Price: Mechanically we can force a rerun on the “perf-a100-dedicated” label (the smaller pool, less shared). It’ll take ~45 min to start though.

Kira Volkov: Another data point: the failure run has higher variance than usual. Standard deviation on p95 looks ~2x compared to baseline. That’s usually infra noise. I can paste numbers if helpful.

Connor O'Brien: Please do. I want something we can link in the release thread so it’s not vibes.

Kira Volkov: From artifact:
- Baseline p95: 412ms (run-to-run stddev ~3.1ms historically)
- This run p95: 426ms
- Within-run stddev: 9.4ms (normal is ~4-5ms)
So the point estimate is +3.4%, but the run itself is noisy.

Claire Dubois: That within-run stddev is a red flag for measurement stability.

Jonas Weber: Proposal for today:
1) Trigger rerun on dedicated A100 runner pool.
2) If rerun <= +2.0% => accept and proceed.
3) If rerun still > +2.0% => block release and open a perf investigation issue.
Longer term: change gate to “median of 3” or “2 consecutive failures required”.

Connor O'Brien: +1. Sahana/Devon can we do #1 without messing with anything else? No code changes, just rerun.

Sahana Iyer: Yep. I can kick a rerun with the dedicated label and also pause new submissions to that pool while it runs. Give me ~5.

Devon Price: I’ll start a note for an action item: perf-canary should auto-detect noisy hosts and mark as “invalid run” rather than hard fail. But that’s a bigger change.

Sean Gallagher: Also we should capture this in the runbook: “Allowed rerun count: 1 (on isolated pool). Waiver requires SRE + Release Eng approval.”

Connor O'Brien: Agree. No waivers for perf unless we can explain. :thumbsup:

perf-canary-bot: 🔁 Rerun requested by Sahana Iyer
Queue: perf-a100-dedicated
New run: https://perf-canary.redwood.dev/runs/1741194210

Marcus Reed: While that runs: any chance the new scheduler regression tests are stealing CPU on these hosts? I saw some overlap in time windows.

Sahana Iyer: The scheduler tests run on separate CI runners, not on the perf hosts. But the perf hosts share a control plane service with other jobs (artifact upload, etc). Still shouldn’t cause this, but possible.

Allison Grant: Another thought: the failure window aligns with the backup job on the perf NFS volume (weekly snapshot). That would explain IO latency spikes. I’ll ping infra after this thread.

Connor O'Brien: That would be… very on brand.

Jonas Weber: If that’s the culprit, we should schedule snapshots away from release windows OR move perf inputs local.

Rafael Mendes: For the record: if we need to block, we message Support/CS that the patch is delayed due to perf gate investigation. But hopefully rerun clears.

perf-canary-bot: ✅ LTS Perf Gate: PASSED (rerun)
Branch: runtime-1.18-lts
Workload: chat-mix-v2
GPU: A100-80GB
Metric: p95 end-to-end latency
Result: +1.1% regression (threshold: +2.0%)
Artifact: https://perf-canary.redwood.dev/runs/1741194210

Marcus Reed: Nice. p50/p95 both look normal and variance is back to expected range.

Connor O'Brien: Ok, we proceed with publish. I’m going to note in the release thread that the initial fail was infra noise; rerun on dedicated pool passed.

Sean Gallagher: +1 proceed. But we need follow-ups:
- identify NFS snapshot / contention root cause
- define rerun policy in perf gates doc + runbook

Allison Grant: I’ll open an infra ticket re: snapshot timing + noisy neighbor alerts for perf pools.

Sahana Iyer: I’ll open an internal issue to prevent perf runners from being packed + add an admission control during patch week.

Jonas Weber: I’ll draft a small change to the gate logic: require 2 consecutive failures before hard-fail OR automatically run 2 and take best/median (we can bikeshed, but current is too sensitive).

Connor O'Brien: Action items recap:
- Allison: infra ticket re snapshot / IO contention
- Sahana: runner packing / scheduling guardrails
- Jonas: gate anti-flake proposal
I’ll add a note to the retro doc. Thanks all.

title: customer-success
body:
customer-success

sam_cs: Heads-up — customer reports function-calling validation errors after our latest SDK/runtime deploy. Error: "schema validation failed: expected array for 'orderItems' but got string". Repro steps below.

customer-ops: This started ~2026-03-15 18:28 UTC. We call createOrder via the SDK. Getting 400s from function validator.

leo_support: Can you paste the exact payload you sent and the system prompt you use?

customer-ops: Sure — payload we sent (redacted):
```json
{
  "function": "createOrder",
  "arguments": "sku1,sku2,sku3"
}
```
And the system prompt (company-managed):
```
You are a helpful assistant. When asked, show order items as a short comma-separated list.
```

leo_support: Ah — arguments are a string, not an array/object. That makes the validator fail (schema expects orderItems: [{sku:string,qty:int}]).

tara_engineer: Quick diagnosis: the system prompt's few-shot/example phrasing strongly pushes the model to emit a CSV string for items. We also shipped an example in the docs that used snake_case `order_items: "sku1,sku2"` which doesn't match the function schema (camelCase + array). Model is mixing styles => schema drift.

sam_cs: Customer says they didn't change their client code; this started after our runtime/SDK update rolling out a new normalization of examples in the docs.

jamie_platform: I'll pull traces. @deploy-bot can you surface recent deploy notes for the docs/examples change?

deploy-bot: Deployed docs update #PR-4821 at 2026-03-14T02:14Z — example for createOrder unintentionally used `order_items` as CSV in the quickstart.

tara_engineer: Immediate mitigation options: 1) customer edits system prompt to explicitly instruct: "Return a JSON object named "orderItems" as an array of objects matching the function schema." 2) set the SDK to bypass automatic function-calling (call_functions: false) and send structured args manually. 3) our runtime can add a temporary permissive parser that will accept CSV/string and convert to the array shape (normalization).

sam_cs: Customer prefers short-term prompt edit. Can eng-ml add temporary normalization for snake_case/csv inputs while we revert docs?

jamie_platform: We will add an input-normalizer in the runtime to coerce common variants (comma string -> array of skus, snake_case -> camelCase) and add a healthcheck. Will target hotfix tomorrow.

customer-ops: Prompt edit worked for now — we forced an explicit assistant instruction: "Output a JSON object matching the createOrder function's argument schema exactly; do not wrap in prose." That eliminated the 400s during our testing.

leo_support: Filing a scoped postmortem and action items: - eng-ml: implement runtime normalizer (P0) - devex/docs: fix the quickstart examples and add a lint check to reject examples that don't match registered function schemas (P1) - cs: notify affected customers and recommend prompt patch for short-term (P1)

tara_engineer: Also adding a regression test in our eval harness that runs function-calling end-to-end using the live docs examples to catch drift.

sam_cs: Thanks all. Customer is green for now but asked for ETA on hotfix. Jamie/ Tara, can you ping back here once deploy is scheduled?

jamie_platform: Will post ETA — aiming for 24h.

sam_cs: Marking ticket RED until runtime fix deploy.

customer-ops: Appreciate the quick turnaround. :thanks_heart:

title: support
body:
support

Customer_42: Hi, we just have a serious billing issue. One API call apparently charged our card three times. request_id=rQw9-231.
Maria Gomez: omg, sorry to hear — can you paste the request body you sent (redact any PII)?
Customer_42: sent. here's the chat payload (redacted):
```
{
  "model": "redwood-chat-1",
  "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"charge $9.99 for order 987"}],
  "tool_call": {"name":"charge_customer","arguments": {"order_id":"987","amount":9.99}}
}
```
Customer_42: The API returned a 400 with body saying \"schema validation failed: missing transaction_id\" but our bank shows three charges. We only sent once.
Jake Park: Thanks — that implies our runtime retried the tool call despite a schema error. Can you give me the exact error payload and request id?
Customer_42: error body: `{ \"error\": {\"type\": \"tool_error\", \"code\": \"schema_validation\", \"details\": \"missing field transaction_id\"}, \"request_id\": \"rQw9-231\" }`
Olivia Chen: grabbing runtime logs for rQw9-231, snippet below:
```
[2026-03-10T14:22:11Z] REQ rQw9-231 -> dispatch tool charge_customer
[2026-03-10T14:22:11Z] TOOL charge_customer START args={order_id:987,amount:9.99}
[2026-03-10T14:22:11Z] TOOL charge_customer ERROR schema_validation missing transaction_id
[2026-03-10T14:22:11Z] RUNTIME retry policy: classify error -> transient -> retrying (attempt=1)
[2026-03-10T14:22:12Z] TOOL charge_customer START args={order_id:987,amount:9.99}
[2026-03-10T14:22:12Z] TOOL charge_customer SUCCESS charge_id=ch_A1
[2026-03-10T14:22:12Z] webhook -> payments provider processed ch_A1
[2026-03-10T14:22:13Z] TOOL charge_customer START args={order_id:987,amount:9.99}
[2026-03-10T14:22:13Z] TOOL charge_customer SUCCESS charge_id=ch_A2
[2026-03-10T14:22:13Z] runtime returning success to client
```
Olivia Chen: logs show a retry loop and multiple successful executions. runtime returned success after first success but retries continued due to how retry controller was implemented.
Sana Patel: billing: we received webhook events for ch_A1 and ch_A2 and processed both. Customer reports three charges — need to correlate with provider (could be another duplicate on provider side).
Maria Gomez: urgent: customer needs refund. We also need an engineering hotfix.
Jake Park: initial root cause: (A) our retry classifier treated schema_validation as a transient error, (B) charge_customer is non-idempotent but tool args didn't include a transaction_id, (C) runtime will continue retries even after first success in some race conditions.
LLM-ops-bot: Recommendation: require an explicit idempotency token for payment tools and/or reject calls that don't include transaction_id as a pre-dispatch validation. Also add X-Redwood-Idempotency header handling.
Jake Park: agree. short term: block automatic retries for any tool marked non-idempotent in tool metadata. Also add a pre-dispatch schema gate that returns 400 before attempting tool when required fields are missing.
Olivia Chen: PR opened to change retry classification: https://git.redwood/internal/infra/PR-489 (maps schema_validation/invalid_arguments -> permanent)
Olivia Chen: another PR to fix the retry controller so that once a tool execution returns success, remaining retry attempts are aborted: https://git.redwood/internal/runtime/PR-1023
Sana Patel: billing processed two refunds for duplicates (refund_tx=rf_7721 and rf_7722). Left one charge as valid (ch_A1). Emailed receipt to customer. Ticket BILL-1124 created.
Maria Gomez: customer message drafted: \"We're very sorry — our system retried a failed payment attempt and caused duplicate charges. We issued refunds for duplicate charges and are disabling retries for payment tools while we roll out a fix. We'll follow up when patch is live.\" :pray:
Customer_42: thanks for the quick help — please confirm once refunds are complete.
Sana Patel: refunds processed, customer emailed. We also flagged payment provider with case #PP-9902 to verify there wasn't an extra duplicate at their end.
Jake Park: longer-term plan:
- enforce idempotency token required for non-idempotent tools (transaction_id)
- add a dedupe layer at dispatch that uses explicit idempotency token and short TTL
- treat schema_validation and invalid_arguments as permanent errors (no retries)
- add telemetry: alert when retry_count > 0 for non-idempotent tools and when duplicate downstream webhooks spike
- runtime: ensure first success cancels in-flight retries and that we only return a single success event to client
Olivia Chen: temporary mitigation: deploying canary that disables retries for tools where metadata.non_idempotent==true to dedicated and private zones. Monitoring channel: #billing-alerts and #runtime-alerts.
Jake Park: UX change idea: when a tool schema error occurs, instead of blind retry, the assistant should respond with a structured assistant message asking the user to supply missing fields, e.g., \"I couldn't call charge_customer: missing transaction_id — please provide a transaction id or confirm you want to proceed\". Avoids side effects.
Maria Gomez: follow-ups: Olivia keep me posted on canary, Jake link PRs here once merged, Sana finalize refund and closure, I'll update the customer ticket.
LLM-ops-bot: Incident logged -> INC-2026-tool-retry-billing.
Maria Gomez: closing note to customer: \"Refunds issued, duplicate charges reversed. We've deployed a fix to stop retries on payment tools and are rolling additional idempotency checks. Sorry for the disruption.\" :white_check_mark:

title: incidents
body:
incidents

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Triggered alert: Hosted API p99 latency burn (us-east) is above threshold for 10m
Signals: chat.completions p99=18.7s (baseline 4.2s), timeout_rate=3.8%, 5xx_rate=1.1%
Dashboards: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/hosted-api-us-east-overview?from=now-30m
Runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ONCALL/Hosted+Overload+Circuit+Breaker+Runbook

Rafael Mendes: seeing this too. oncall says mostly chat.completions, model=rw-llama-70b in us-east. Anyone already digging in runtime signals?

Aisha Bello: looking at overload dash (new one). shed_rate is basically 0 (not enabled), but runtime queue depth is spiking hard. prefill_q_depth p95 ~ 140 (normally <20). decode tokens/sec saturated ~ 95-98%.

Christine Wong: pulling request samples from gateway logs. a bunch of client timeouts, retries overlapping. seeing long prompts too (preamble ~12-16k tokens). looks like burst + long-context.

Ethan Park: gateway side: concurrency is unbounded for that route right now besides tenant quota. we can put a temporary cap per-route in us-east if needed. question is do we want to flip breaker canary early?

Peter Holtz: +1 consider canary. concern: if we start returning 503/overloaded without Retry-After in all paths we could trigger retry storm. do we have the hotfix everywhere in us-east?

Christine Wong: Retry-After consistency should be good post pr-18472 but I’m not 100% if prod us-east has it on all handlers. I can verify quickly.

Mina Haddad: routing perspective: we can also enable fallback to us-west for a subset if policy allows. but careful: cross-region latency and west is already ~70% utilization.

Sofia Ivanova: runtime: sched backlog is real. batching is already at cap. we’re also seeing kv cache pressure on a subset of GPUs (fragmentation proxy up). if we keep admitting at this rate, p99 will keep walking.

Rafael Mendes: ok, goal is stop cascade. options:
1) temporary gateway cap (concurrency + token bucket)
2) enable breaker canary (us-east only, small tenant slice)
3) routing fallback (only for tenants configured)

Aisha Bello: error budget burn is accelerating. for the last 15m, availability SLI for hosted in us-east is trending <99.0 if this continues.

Amara Diallo: I can apply a per-route concurrency cap via the gateway config toggle (no deploy). We have a “soft reject” mode that returns 429 w/ Retry-After when at cap. But do we want 429 or 503 here?

Nikhil Sharma: from PM side: prefer stable semantics. overload should be 503 with explicit code if it’s platform saturation. 429 is more “client throttled”. but if we only have 429 available quickly, do it + clear messaging.

Peter Holtz: +1 semantics, but priority is stop tail-latency + timeouts. timeouts are worst UX.

Christine Wong: checked a few live responses in us-east via replay. overload handler is not active so no direct proof. but the common 503s we see are upstream timeouts (no Retry-After). :grimacing:

Ethan Park: the breaker framework is behind flag `overload_protection.breaker_enabled`. canary mode exists: `breaker_mode=canary` + `canary_tenant_hash=5%`. It would return 503 with `error.code=overloaded` and set Retry-After.

Rafael Mendes: that sounds like what we want, but we’re mid-incident. are we confident it won’t false-positive and take out healthy traffic?

Aisha Bello: thresholds from tuning sheet for us-east: open when queue_depth>120 for 30s OR token_sat>0.95 for 60s. We’re currently above both for ~8-10m. So it would definitely open.

Sofia Ivanova: from runtime side, opening would help immediately. we need to reduce admission. we can also temporarily reduce max_tokens cap under duress, but that’s a broader behavior change.

Mina Haddad: if breaker opens, routing can attempt fallback only when configured. do we have default fallback configured for self-serve? I think no (opt-in).

Ethan Park: correct, no default fallback. breaker open would primarily shed/queue at gateway.

Connor O'Brien: FYI deploy status: us-east control plane updated yesterday, runtime patch is current. no deploys in progress. if we flip flags, it’s immediate.

Peter Holtz: can we do a two-step? apply a small gateway cap now to reduce blast radius, then flip breaker canary to get correct error semantics + correlation IDs.

Amara Diallo: I can set cap to 80% of current observed throughput and add token bucket on chat.completions only. That will start returning 429 w/ Retry-After=2 for excess.

Nikhil Sharma: if we do 429, please make sure Support gets a heads up. customers will ask.

Rafael Mendes: ok do the cap now. then we enable breaker canary 5% tenants in us-east, monitor for 5-10m, then decide expand.

Ethan Park: ack. I’ll flip breaker canary flag for us-east only after Amara’s cap is in. Christine can you monitor error payloads to ensure Retry-After present + correlation id?

Christine Wong: yep. I’ll tail gateway responses and spot-check.

Amara Diallo: applying cap now…

deploy-bot: Config change applied: gateway/us-east route=chat.completions
- concurrency_cap: 2200 -> 1600
- token_bucket_rps: 0 -> 900 (burst 1200)
- reject_status: 429
- retry_after_seconds: 2
Requested by: Amara Diallo

Aisha Bello: immediate impact: queue depth is starting to flatten (not climbing). timeout_rate down from 3.8% -> 2.6% last 5m but still high.

Rafael Mendes: good. Ethan go ahead with breaker canary.

Ethan Park: flipping `breaker_enabled` to canary (us-east, 5%).

deploy-bot: Feature flag updated: overload_protection.breaker_enabled
- region: us-east
- mode: canary
- canary_tenant_hash: 5%
- error_status: 503
- error_code: overloaded
- include_retry_after: true
Requested by: Ethan Park

Christine Wong: seeing 503 responses now with payload:
`{"error":{"code":"overloaded","message":"Service is temporarily overloaded. Please retry.","request_id":"req_7f2..."}}`
Headers include `Retry-After: 3` and `x-request-id` present. :thumbsup:

Peter Holtz: nice. any sign of clients ignoring Retry-After and hammering?

Aisha Bello: retry traffic is elevated but not spiking further. overall RPS stabilized. breaker_open_rate for canary slice ~0.9 (expected given saturation). also seeing 503s replacing timeouts for that slice.

Sofia Ivanova: runtime now recovering: decode backlog down ~20%. token/sec sat still high but not pegged. should see p99 improve in ~10-15m.

Rafael Mendes: decision point: expand breaker beyond canary? or keep canary + cap until load subsides.

Mina Haddad: keep canary only for now. expanding means more hard 503s and we haven’t notified Support / status page. if p99 improves w/ cap, that’s enough.

Nikhil Sharma: agreed. for now keep impact minimal.

Rafael Mendes: ok. action items:
- Keep gateway cap for 60m, reassess.
- Keep breaker at 5% canary in us-east.
- Aisha to watch SLO burn + p99.
- Christine to confirm Retry-After coverage on remaining overload paths.

Aisha Bello: update: p99 chat.completions us-east is down to 11.2s (from 18.7s). timeout_rate now 1.4% and trending down.

Peter Holtz: :thumbsup: can we also add a note in #support that some tenants may see 503 overloaded w/ Retry-After, expected during incident mitigation.

Rafael Mendes: I’ll ping Support liaison.

Rafael Mendes: @Dev Patel heads up: us-east had burst traffic causing timeouts. We applied temporary caps and enabled 5% breaker canary. Some tenants may see 503 `error.code=overloaded` with Retry-After; guidance is exponential backoff + respect header.

Connor O'Brien: FYI for postmortem: capture current thresholds, cap values, and canary config. I’ll open an incident doc.

Christine Wong: one more thing: some 429s from cap don’t include `error.code` right now (just message). not ideal but ok short-term. I’ll file a bug / link to overload taxonomy task.

Aisha Bello: metrics stable for last 10m. p99 now 8.6s. still above baseline but improving.

Rafael Mendes: holding steady. if it continues improving, we can remove cap gradually and keep canary running for another day to collect data.

incident-bot: :information_source: Incident status updated by Rafael Mendes: MITIGATING
Summary: us-east saturation due to burst + long prompts. Applied gateway admission caps + enabled 5% breaker canary to convert timeouts into explicit overload errors.
Next update in 30m.

title: incidents
body:
incidents

IncidentBot: :rotating_light: Alert triggered: Hosted canary / runtime-1.21 / kernel_autoselect_v2
Signal: p99 latency +42% (baseline 1.9s -> 2.7s) for chat.generate
Scope (initial): us-east-1, canary pool "hosted-canary-rt121", GPU=L40S
Error rate: stable
Start: 12:03 PT (auto)
Runbook: https://confluence.redwood/eng-serving-runtime/runbooks/kernel-selection-v2-override-and-rollback-runbook

Sean Gallagher: oncall here. Seeing the spike on the canary dashboard too. It’s narrow but pretty sharp. Anyone around from runtime kernels/selector?

Omar El-Sayed: here. Looking at selection telemetry panels now (sampling 1%). It looks like selection distribution shifted specifically on L40S: prefill kernel choice is skewing to `prefill_fa2_packed_qkv` (which we normally avoid on this SKU for long context).

Aisha Bello: confirming from SLO view: only p99 is affected; p95 is up ~8%. No corresponding increase in 5xx. Tail looks like long-context requests.

Allison Grant: +1. Alert threshold tripped on p99 only. No error-budget burn yet but we should mitigate before the canary window continues.

Connor O'Brien: release train perspective: canary is supposed to run for another 3 hours. If we need to flip gate we can, but let’s keep it scoped if possible.

Yuki Sato: I’m in. That kernel shouldn’t be getting picked on L40S unless we’re in the short-prefill bucket. Do we know what seq bucket the selector thinks these are?

Omar El-Sayed: looking at the event fields: `seq_bucket=prefill_short` on a bunch of these, but request traces show prompt_tokens ~14k+ on the slow ones. Smells like misclassification / bad token count estimate.

Marcus Reed: I can cross-check with perf-canary scenario logs. In canary, we enabled scheduler hint passthrough last week—could be feeding the selector stale distribution hints?

Hiro Tanaka: L40S is sensitive to that packed QKV path at long context; it can blow up tail if it hits the wrong memory pattern. Agree this is likely wrong bucket or wrong SKU mapping.

Sean Gallagher: proposing immediate mitigation: disable v2 only for L40S in us-east-1 canary pool. That should snap latency back while we debug.

Benji Okafor: I can apply a deny rule in the gate config: `kernel_autoselect_v2=false` when gpu_sku=L40S AND env=hosted-canary AND region=use1. Hot reload should be <2 min.

Ethan Park: control plane gate supports that. Benji, please do it via the standard policy repo so we get an audit trail. Link the incident.

DeployBot: Change requested by Benji Okafor
Repo: control-plane-policy
Change: disable kernel_autoselect_v2 for gpu_sku=L40S region=us-east-1 env=hosted-canary-rt121
Status: pending

Sahana Iyer: while that rolls, I’m pulling selector debug dumps from a couple slow traces. If we see `prefill_short` + 14k prompts, it’s definitely feature extraction/hinting.

Yuki Sato: Omar/Marcus: can you confirm whether the selector is using request-level token counts or scheduler-provided `workload_hint` for bucket? In v2 we added “mixed workload stability” using observed distribution hints (PR-28502).

Marcus Reed: in hosted canary, I believe we enabled `selector.use_scheduler_hints=true` for that pool (for stability testing). If the hint says “mostly short prefill” it could bias bucket decisions.

Omar El-Sayed: yeah, field `hint_source=scheduler` shows up in the telemetry for most of these. That’s probably it.

Sean Gallagher: if that’s the case, mitigation (disable v2) is fine. We’ll need a follow-up: either lower weight of scheduler hints or cap hint influence when request prompt_tokens exceed threshold.

DeployBot: Change applied successfully
Status: live

Aisha Bello: watching p99 now. Already dropping—p99 back to ~2.0s within the last 3 min window. Looks like mitigation worked.

Allison Grant: alert should auto-resolve once the 10-min window clears. Please keep an eye on cardinality/telemetry; but this looks clean.

Sean Gallagher: great. Let’s keep canary running for non-L40S SKUs. Benji/Ethan, thanks. Omar/Yuki/Hiro/Sahana: can you own the RCA?

Yuki Sato: yep. Hypothesis: scheduler hint incorrectly biasing seq bucket selection for long-context requests; selector uses hint too aggressively. Action: add guardrail: if `prompt_tokens >= long_context_threshold`, force `prefill_long` regardless of hint. Also check if token count is coming in late/estimated.

Sahana Iyer: I have one debug dump showing:
- request prompt_tokens reported to selector: 1024 (estimated)
- actual prompt_tokens at execution: 14832
So we might be using pre-tokenization estimate (or truncated) in the selector feature extraction.

Hiro Tanaka: that matches older bug class: token count isn’t final until after tokenizer pass / prefill setup. If selector runs earlier, it sees a default/placeholder. We should rely on max of (scheduler hint + conservative upper bound) or delay selection until real token count is known.

Omar El-Sayed: we can also add a safety rule: if `prompt_bytes` is high (or input length in chars), treat as long context. Not perfect, but better than misclassifying to short.

Connor O'Brien: for release notes / comms: this is canary-only and mitigated by gating. Please document that L40S in us-east-1 canary had v2 disabled pending fix. We’ll want to mention “scheduler hint integration guardrail” as a patch.

Sean Gallagher: incident summary for the thread:
- Impact: brief p99 latency spike in hosted canary pool on L40S only
- Mitigation: disabled kernel_autoselect_v2 for L40S us-east-1 canary via gate (hot reload)
- Status: recovered
Next: RCA + patch, then re-enable and re-run canary.

IncidentBot: :white_check_mark: Alert resolved: p99 latency returned to baseline for chat.generate (hosted canary / us-east-1 / L40S)
Duration: 18 minutes
Owner: Sean Gallagher

Allison Grant: please file a follow-up ticket and link here; also add an explicit rollback trigger note to the canary checklist (“if selector sees estimated tokens, force conservative bucket”).

Omar El-Sayed: will do. I’ll also add a temporary dashboard annotation so future viewers know why L40S selection distribution changes abruptly at ~12:12 PT.

Benji Okafor: gate change is scoped + reversible. I’ll leave it in place until runtime confirms fix.

Ethan Park: +1. Make sure we capture the exact policy condition; we’ve had SKU normalization issues ("L40S" vs "NVIDIA-L40S" vs instance family) in the past.

Sean Gallagher: closing out. Thanks all.

title: support
body:
support

Miguel Santos: Hey folks — got a Dedicated customer asking what the burst denial reason codes mean. They’re seeing intermittent `429` + a `burst_denial_reason` in the response headers (and in the Console panel). What’s the best way for Support to explain these in plain terms + what actions to take? Also, do we have something linkable (runbook / docs) we can send?

SupportBot: :ticket: Linked customer case: SUP-28503 ("429s when burst cap reached")

Sean Gallagher: +1 we should give Support a crisp mapping + “what you should do next”. We also need to be careful to not imply burst is guaranteed capacity.

Peter Holtz: The short version: burst is opportunistic + guarded. Denials happen for a few distinct reasons, and the customer action differs.

Kira Thompson: I can write the customer-facing blurb, but I need the canonical list + recommended retry guidance. @Benji Okafor can you paste the current codes we’ve standardized on?

Benji Okafor: Yep. Current denial reasons (what customer sees) are:
- `BURST_CAP_REACHED`: tenant hit configured burst cap (their max extra concurrency/GPU-seconds above baseline). This is “you used up your allowed burst headroom right now”.
- `POOL_SATURATED`: burst pool for that region/hw class is at/near capacity (can’t safely admit more burst without impacting others).
- `FLEET_SAFETY_CIRCUIT_OPEN`: global/fleet safety cap tripped (protecting non-burst SLOs). Temporary, usually resolves when load drops.
- `COOLDOWN_ACTIVE`: tenant is in cooldown window (anti-thrashing + fairness). Deny until cooldown expires.
- `PRIORITY_DEFERRED`: admitted other higher-priority burst traffic first (tiering + fairness). Typically transient.
- `BURST_DISABLED_BY_POLICY`: burst disabled for tenant/route/model (feature flag, allowlist, or policy gate).
- `CONFIG_INVALID`: tenant config is missing/invalid (rare; generally a control-plane misconfig).
- `TELEMETRY_UNCERTAIN`: we can’t confidently determine safe capacity due to telemetry lag/partial outage, so we fail closed.

Benji Okafor: Not all tenants will see all of these; most common in the wild are `BURST_CAP_REACHED` and `POOL_SATURATED`.

Miguel Santos: Super helpful. How do we want Support to phrase `POOL_SATURATED` without making it sound like our platform is “out of GPUs” broadly?

Peter Holtz: Suggestion:
- “Burst uses a shared Redwood-managed burst pool in your region/hardware class. During peak demand, the pool can be fully utilized. When that happens, we deny additional burst requests to protect performance for all tenants (including your baseline).”

Sean Gallagher: + explicitly: baseline dedicated capacity is still protected; burst is “best effort within guardrails”.

Kira Thompson: For retries: are we recommending immediate retry on all denials? Or only some?

Rafael Mendes: For Support guidance:
- `BURST_CAP_REACHED`: retrying won’t help until usage falls below cap / window resets. Recommend: reduce concurrency, schedule batch job differently, or request higher cap via CSM.
- `POOL_SATURATED`, `PRIORITY_DEFERRED`: retry *can* work. Use exponential backoff + jitter; don’t hot-loop.
- `FLEET_SAFETY_CIRCUIT_OPEN`: retry after backoff; if persistent > X mins, open Support escalation (SRE oncall) because it indicates neighbor impact risk.
- `COOLDOWN_ACTIVE`: retry after a short delay; cooldown is usually on the order of minutes (Support can check the dashboard panel).
- `TELEMETRY_UNCERTAIN`: retry after backoff; if it persists, treat as incident (telemetry pipeline / admission controller health).

Rafael Mendes: We have a runbook draft that covers “how to interpret denial reasons” + “what to check in dashboards”: https://confluence.redwood.internal/eng-sre/runbooks/burst-pool-overload-mitigation-runbook (still WIP, but good enough for internal Support).

Miguel Santos: Nice. Do we have something customer-visible yet?

Kira Thompson: Not a public doc yet; I can add a short section to the Dedicated burst guide once PR-928 is merged. For now, Support can paraphrase + we can share a snippet if needed.

Sean Gallagher: For now please avoid linking internal confluence to customers. Instead: provide a short explanation + offer to review their burst config + suggest backoff behavior.

Benji Okafor: Also: if customer asks “why did I get 429 instead of queueing?” — our semantics are immediate deny (no queue) once guardrails say no. Queueing is intentionally out of scope for v1 to avoid tail-latency blowups.

Miguel Santos: Got it. Any quick checklist Support can follow when customer says “denials higher than expected”?

Peter Holtz: Internal checklist:
1) Confirm their baseline vs burst cap (`burst_max_ratio`, per-tenant cap) in control plane.
2) Check burst pool saturation dashboard for their region/hw.
3) Check `FLEET_SAFETY_CIRCUIT_OPEN` events + any SLO regression gate alerts.
4) If `TELEMETRY_UNCERTAIN` spikes, check admission controller + telemetry lag panels.

Rafael Mendes: + if they’re hitting `BURST_CAP_REACHED` constantly, it’s often a client-side concurrency spike / retries amplifying load. Recommend: cap parallelism + use idempotency keys to avoid double work.

Kira Thompson: Draft customer-facing phrasing (Support can copy/paste):
“Burst capacity provides temporary throughput above your reserved baseline when shared burst pool capacity is available. If a request is denied with a burst denial reason code, it means one of the guardrails is preventing additional burst to protect performance and fairness. Your reserved baseline capacity remains unchanged. For saturation-related denials, retry with exponential backoff + jitter; for cap-related denials, reduce concurrency or work with us to adjust limits.”

Miguel Santos: Perfect. I’ll respond to the customer with the mapping for the two codes they saw (`POOL_SATURATED`, `BURST_CAP_REACHED`) and include the retry guidance. I’ll also link the internal runbook in the case notes for future.

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: Please ping if you see `FLEET_SAFETY_CIRCUIT_OPEN` in a customer case — we want to know ASAP.

Benji Okafor: I’ll add a short “Support glossary” section to the denial reason codes ticket so it stays canonical. :writing_hand:

title: eng-runtime
body:
eng-runtime

Marcus Reed: Dropping early bench results for compaction branch (allocator+relocate behind flag). Ran mixed-length burst scenario + long-lived sessions. TL;DR: p99 looks better once fragmentation starts, but budget too high can show up as decode jitter. Sheet: https://drive.google.com/…/kv-frag-results-jan

Rina Kobayashi: :eyes: which scenario version? is this with the new churn generator or the older mixed-length script?

Marcus Reed: New churn generator from benchmark-lab PR-881 (1.5k concurrent, cancel rate ~12%, prompt lens bimodal 128/2k, decode 256). 30 min steady + 5 min burst every 10.

Samir Qureshi: Nice. Can you paste the headline deltas? Particularly fragmentation ratio and bytes moved.

Marcus Reed: Sure (H100, llama3-70b-ish profile, decode-heavy):
- Baseline (no compaction): frag_ratio climbs 0.18 -> 0.47 over 25 min, then oscillates 0.40-0.52
- With compaction (trigger 0.28, budget 96MB/step): frag_ratio stabilizes 0.12-0.22
- p99 decode token latency during burst: 185ms -> 128ms
- p95: 62ms -> 55ms
- Throughput: -1.8% avg tokens/s
- Bytes moved: ~22GB over 30 min (peaks during burst)

Omar El-Sayed: That p99 drop is the first “real” number I’ve seen that matches the hypothesis. :thumbsup:

Sofia Ivanova: What’s “budget 96MB/step” mapped to in scheduler terms here? per-iteration? per decode boundary? (I’m trying to reason about worst-case stalls.)

Marcus Reed: Current wiring is “per scheduler loop iteration, after decode batch finishes” (so it can run multiple times/sec depending on load). In these runs, compaction ran ~4-8 times/sec under churn.

Sofia Ivanova: ok that’s the concern. 96MB x 8/sec is a lot of copy if it lines up badly. Do you have trace exemplars showing per-iteration compaction time?

Marcus Reed: Coarse timing from logs (not full tracing spans yet): p50 compaction step 0.4ms, p95 1.7ms, p99 3.6ms. But there are spikes when it has to relocate a “bad” chain; saw a couple 7-9ms steps.

Julian Moore: Were those 7-9ms spikes on the same iterations where decode batch got smaller? (i.e., compaction stealing time from scheduling?)

Marcus Reed: Hard to say without the spans. My intuition is yes. You can see minor sawtooth in per-token latency when budget >128MB.

Samir Qureshi: I can add a hard time cap as well as bytes cap. Right now it’s bytes-first. If we do min(bytes_cap, time_cap) we can bound worst-case.

Allison Grant: +1 time cap. From SRE side we’ll want an explicit “compaction_time_ms” distribution anyway, but “budget_ms_per_step” is a cleaner knob for guardrails.

Omar El-Sayed: Agree. Also: budgets should differ for Hosted vs Dedicated. Hosted cares about jitter; Dedicated customers tend to accept stable throughput tradeoffs if it prevents OOM/evictions.

Nikhil Sharma: For Hosted: if this introduces occasional 8-10ms stalls, that will show up in p99 immediately for chat workloads (and we’ll get paged). I’d rather ship conservative defaults + ability to ramp.

Lauren Bishop: Dedicated: our biggest pain is burst-driven tail + forced shedding when fragmentation causes allocator “thrash.” If we can keep arena healthy, I’m ok paying a few % throughput. Dedicated buyers will prefer “predictable” over “max peak.”

Sean Gallagher: If we do tiered defaults, we need to be super explicit what metrics trigger rollback in canary. Suggest we keep initial Hosted budget low enough that even worst-case compaction can’t exceed, say, 2ms/loop.

Sofia Ivanova: That implies budget should be expressed in time not bytes (because bytes->time depends on GPU + copy path + contention). Bytes cap can be secondary safety.

Samir Qureshi: Implementation idea:
- budget_ms_per_step (default 1.0ms Hosted, 3.0ms Dedicated)
- budget_bytes_per_step (cap, default 32MB Hosted, 96MB Dedicated)
- trigger_frag_ratio (0.30 Hosted, 0.25 Dedicated)
- cool_down_ms between steps to avoid “hammering”

Marcus Reed: I can rerun a sweep to see where the knee is. My current sweeps were 32/64/96/128MB per step.

Rina Kobayashi: Please include A100 too. Some Hosted pools still A100 and their H2D/D2D copy behavior differs.

Marcus Reed: yup. Will queue A100 (80GB) tonight.

Omar El-Sayed: Another nuance: Dedicated has more long-lived sessions (agents). Compaction might be higher ROI there because fragmentation accumulates over hours. Hosted churn is high but sessions shorter.

Nikhil Sharma: Hosted also has more “noisy neighbor” patterns. If compaction eats budget during bursts, I’d rather we integrate with backpressure (i.e., pause compaction when queue depth is high).

Sofia Ivanova: We can gate compaction on scheduler health signals (queue depth, decode backlog, “time_since_last_tick”). I can add “skip compaction if scheduler_lag > X” or “if backlog > threshold.”

Sean Gallagher: For guardrails: if p99 token latency increases >5% over baseline for 10m AND compaction_time_p99 > threshold, auto-disable flag for cohort.

Allison Grant: Metric naming reminder: we’ll need at least:
- kv_compaction_steps_total
- kv_compaction_bytes_moved_total
- kv_compaction_time_ms (hist)
- kv_fragmentation_ratio (gauge)
- kv_evictions_total (once added)
…and they must be labeled by model + tier.

Samir Qureshi: Re budgets, I’m leaning:
Hosted default: 0.75ms step + 32MB cap, trigger 0.30
Dedicated default: 2.5ms step + 96MB cap, trigger 0.25
Both with “max_steps_per_sec” = 5?

Marcus Reed: In the H100 run, 32MB cap wasn’t enough to keep frag under control once it crossed ~0.40. It slowed growth but didn’t reverse fast. Might be ok if trigger is earlier.

Omar El-Sayed: That’s key: early trigger + small steps might be safer than late trigger + big steps.

Sofia Ivanova: Exactly. Let’s avoid “panic compaction.” We’d rather do continuous small maintenance.

Lauren Bishop: Dedicated bursts though: if they have a spike after idle, we may already be fragmented. Are we okay letting it heal slowly?

Samir Qureshi: Dedicated could allow a short “catch-up” mode when below load (prefill quiet). Like: if backlog low, temporarily raise time budget up to 5ms.

Nikhil Sharma: Please do NOT do catch-up mode in Hosted without a hard on/off flag. That’s the kind of thing that surprises us.

Sean Gallagher: +1. Keep Hosted behavior monotonic/simple for first release. No dynamic modes unless we can explain and monitor.

Julian Moore: If we keep it simple: tie compaction to a fixed phase boundary (end of decode batch) AND cap by time. That gives us deterministic-ish behavior.

Marcus Reed: Action items I can take:
1) Sweep trigger (0.22/0.26/0.30/0.34) with small time cap (0.5/1.0/2.0ms) on H100
2) Repeat on A100
3) Add a chart “p99 vs frag_ratio” to the sheet so we can pick trigger at the inflection point

Omar El-Sayed: :thumbsup: please also include “throughput delta” and “compaction bytes moved/sec” so we can sanity check copy load.

Allison Grant: And label runs with “Hosted-like” vs “Dedicated-like” workload profiles (session length distribution differs).

Marcus Reed: will do. I’ll add two workload presets in the harness and mark in the sheet.

Sofia Ivanova: Once you have the sweep, we can pick initial defaults and bake into runtime-1.22 config. Let’s keep Hosted conservative and plan to ramp via canary if results hold.

Samir Qureshi: I’ll open a follow-up PR for time-based budget + “max_steps_per_sec”. Should be small diff.

Sean Gallagher: Please ping me when it’s up; I want to review the metrics + failure modes (what happens if compaction never runs / always runs).

Marcus Reed: :ok_hand: Will post updated numbers tomorrow after the A100 run finishes.

title: incidents
body:
incidents

incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate (gateway) and tail latencies observed in us-east-1 starting ~2026-03-15T03:12Z. 5xx spike at ingress gateway + downstream KV cache timeouts. Auto-detect: 5xx rate = 3.8% (5m), tail p95 latency = 980ms. Triggered pager to oncall. Metrics: https://dash.redwood/internal/gw-us-east?range=15m

mike: I'm on pager. grabbing context. Any active deploys or config changes in us-east in last hour?

anya: I see a big uptick in cache evictions on the edgepool: kv-cache eviction_count spiked from ~200/min -> 12k/min starting 03:12Z. Also seeing a correlated increase in backend connection timeouts to ml-workers.

sam: we did roll a config tweak to the prefix-invalidation job earlier that reduced batch size, but there was also a change to edgepool kv max-size (2GB -> 512MB) to test memory headroom. suspect combined effect.

infra-sre: logs show repeated prefix invalidation events from the job:
```
[03:12:07Z] prefix_invalidate: job=prefix-cleanup id=pr-441 keys_invalidated=14290 duration=320ms
[03:12:07Z] kvcache: evict triggered by mem-pressure used=97% limit=512MB
```
This caused thrashing and increased tail latency for requests that rely on prefix KV hits.

mike: ok. immediate ask: can we reduce traffic to us-east by shifting some percent to eu-west for a quick mitigation? what's the risk on cross-region auth/session affinity?

sam: session affinity is sticky by default for short requests, but long streaming chats may break if we cross-region. We should route non-streaming and short-gen traffic first.

incident-bot: routing-change suggested: shift 25% non-streaming traffic away from us-east -> eu-west to reduce pressure. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kv-evict#mitigation

alice: CS update: we have 9 customer reports of failed requests; top impacted: AcmeCorp (prod), PaperTrail (staging). Errors are 502/504 during longer prompt chains. Customers are seeing intermittent responses.

support-lead: drafting status note. recommend immediate customer-facing message once we confirm mitigation progress.

mike: I'm going to perform a staged route change for non-streaming routes now. command: `augman route adjust --from us-east --to eu-west --percent 25 --filter non-streaming`

infra-sre: heads up: changing weights will trigger some connection churn. we'll monitor connection pools. also preparing a hotfix to increase kv-cache limit to 1.5GB on edgepool as a less-disruptive alternative, but that requires rolling restart of ~20 nodes (10-15 min).

sam: quick mitigation: enable model fallback for heavy long-context requests to quantized variant (gptq-16k) which uses less worker memory; `redwoodctl model route --from model:prod-large --to model:gptq-16k --percent 50 --filter long-context`

mike: route change executed. now: non-streaming -> eu-west +25%. Observing immediate drop in 5xx from 3.8% -> 2.1%. p95 latency down ~180ms.

anya: KV eviction rate still high but less downstream pressure. I can start the rolling increase to kv-cache limit on a staggered set to avoid simultaneous restarts. proposing 3 nodes at a time.

infra-sre: we also found the invalidation job had a bad regex that matched too broadly (PR #441). PR created to tighten matches: https://git.internal/redwood/prefix-cleanup/pull/441. If we can pause the job temporarily, that will immediately reduce evictions.

sam: pausing job now. `kubectl patch cronjob prefix-cleanup -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}'`

incident-bot: Cronjob prefix-cleanup suspended by sam at 03:26Z.

alice: CS: sent interim note to impacted customers: short blurb + we are mitigating by shifting traffic and pausing cleanup job. link to status page: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/1770012345

mike: ramped route shift to 40% (non-streaming) -> eu-west. 5xx now 0.9% overall. Tail latency p95 ~420ms. Noting a single OOM on node edgepool-12 during restart; investigating crash logs.

anya: OOM stack: `rss > limit` while handling a large prefix list during eviction. Looks like some large keys are being touched repeatedly. We're quarantining that node and bringing up replacement.

sam: PR #441 merged. will roll out fix to invalidation job after we validate the patch in staging.

eng-pm: proposed next steps: 1) keep routing shift in place for 30m monitoring 2) complete kv-cache limit bump with staggered restarts 3) roll out invalidation-fix and re-enable job on controlled schedule 4) postmortem to follow.

support-lead: recommend customer comms update after 30m if metrics hold. prepping language now.

infra-sre: started staggered kv limit bump (3 nodes at a time). so far 6/20 done, no further OOMs. eviction rate trending down.

mike: monitoring window: 15m stable. I'll keep oncall until we hand back. If metrics regress, we'll revert route to 75% us-east.

incident-bot: incident status: MITIGATED -> traffic diverted + job paused + kv limit bump in progress. Severity downgraded from P1 -> P2 at 03:45Z.

alice: CS: updated customers with mitigation summary and ETA for full resolution (config fix + re-enable job).

sam: final note: root cause appears to be combined effect of (a) aggressive kv-cache size reduction, and (b) a broad invalidation regex in the cleanup job. change to one alone might have been fine; together they caused eviction thrash. PRs: #441, #442 (kv limit rollback).

mike: handing off to infra-sre for monitoring and postmortem. I'll file the incident ticket and notify leadership. thanks all for quick response.

eng-pm: filing postmortem and action items: add guardrails for cronjob regex changes, add canary check for kv-limit config flips, and a playbook step to pause invalidation job automatically if eviction > 1k/min.

support-lead: closing customer comms loop after final note.

mike: incident thread closed; follow-up ticket: INT-2026-477 created for postmortem and action items. If anyone finds residual errors, re-open thread. Thanks. :thumbsup:

title: devex
body:
devex

Monica Patel: Trying to lock “safe by default” timeout/retry settings for templates (Python + TS) before we merge PR-103. Specifically: request timeouts, retries/backoff, and what we do for streaming disconnects. Can we align here so SDK + templates match? (ref ENG-4186 + ENG-4187)

Ibrahim Khan: +1. We need something we can defend to SRE + support. Also reminder: today we *can’t* truly resume a generation mid-stream (no server-side resume token), so streaming reconnect behavior has to be conservative.

Dana Lo: For TS template: current implementation uses `fetch` (undici) + SSE parser. We’ve seen corporate proxies kill idle/chunked connections. If we auto-retry mid-stream we risk duplicate tokens / duplicated tool calls. So I’m leaning: retry only if we got **zero** content.

Christine Wong: Agree. From ops POV: mid-stream retry is worse than failing fast unless we have idempotency + resume semantics. Partial output + an error is at least diagnosable.

Monica Patel: Ok. Let’s break it down:
1) Non-streaming call defaults (chat/completions)
2) Streaming defaults
3) Retryable error classes (429/5xx/etc)
4) “circuit breaker” / max attempts

Allison Grant: + please make sure whatever we pick is observable (log + span attributes). If we’re retrying, I want `retry.count`, `retry.reason`, and final `http.status_code`. Also don’t add high-cardinality stuff.

Brian Murphy: API behavior notes:
- 429 responses will sometimes include `Retry-After` (seconds). If present, we should respect it.
- 408/409/425 are rare but we can treat as transient.
- 401/403/404 are never retry.
- Streaming responses are SSE over HTTP; when proxy drops you may see `ECONNRESET` / `UND_ERR_SOCKET` / `unexpected EOF`.

Ibrahim Khan: Proposed baseline (consistent w/ what we’ve done elsewhere):
- `connect_timeout`: 5s
- `request_timeout` (total): 60s for non-streaming
- retries: max 2 retries (3 attempts total)
- backoff: exponential w/ jitter starting 250ms, cap 4s
- retry only on: network errors (connect reset, DNS, timeouts), 429, 502/503/504
- respect `Retry-After` for 429 with upper bound (don’t sleep > 10s by default)

Dana Lo: 60s total might be too short for first token on some models if user sets huge context. But template should also cap max_tokens anyway.

Christine Wong: I’d prefer we’re strict on timeouts by default + document overrides. “Safe” = don’t hang processes, don’t DDOS ourselves on retries.

Monica Patel: For templates we also have ingestion/indexing steps (RAG) that might take longer than 60s, but those are local operations. For LLM calls, 60s seems ok.

Alex Martinez: The thing we should optimize for is: new user runs quickstart, gets a response, doesn’t get stuck. If someone needs longer, they can tune env vars.

Allison Grant: +1 to env overrides. Just ensure we emit the configured values into a startup log (once) so support can sanity check.

Monica Patel: Streaming proposal (v1):
- `connect_timeout`: 5s
- `time_to_first_token` soft timeout: 15s (if no tokens by then, abort + treat as retryable once)
- `stream_idle_timeout`: 30s (if no bytes/events for 30s, abort)
- retries: **at most 1 retry** and only if we received 0 tokens / 0 SSE `data:` events
- if we received partial output: surface partial + raise a `StreamingDisconnectedError` with guidance

Dana Lo: This matches what I can implement without hacky buffering. For Node we can count “events received” easily.

Ibrahim Khan: Python side: httpx streaming gives us chunks; we can track whether we’ve yielded any token. Same logic.

Brian Murphy: Question: How do we detect “0 tokens” if model streams tool calls (JSON) vs text? Sometimes first event might be a role delta w/ empty content.

Dana Lo: Good point. For TS we can consider “any SSE message received” as “started”. Not perfect but avoids infinite retry loops.

Christine Wong: I’d rather we don’t retry if we’re unsure. “Any SSE message received” => no retry.

Monica Patel: Ok: streaming retry gate = “received_any_sse_event”. If true, no retry.

Allison Grant: Please add a log field like `stream.started=true/false` and `stream.events_received` (bounded int) so we can debug without leaking content.

Sahana Iyer: From CI smoke tests (ENG-4186), we can simulate:
- disconnect before first event
- disconnect after N events
- 429 w/ Retry-After
But tests get flaky if timeouts are long. If defaults are 15s/30s we should set smaller timeouts in CI via env.

Monica Patel: Yep we’ll parameterize via env + in tests set tiny values.

Ibrahim Khan: On retries/backoff: we should have a global cap on total sleep time. Otherwise a few calls can stack up.

Christine Wong: Also note: retries + streaming = extra cost. Make sure we’re not multiplying tokens. If we retry only pre-first-event, cost should be near zero.

Brian Murphy: SDK limitation callout: TS SDK currently doesn’t expose a clean hook for “time to first token” timeout. Dana’s template might need to wrap AbortController. Python SDK has request timeouts but not “time to first token” separate from total.

Dana Lo: Yeah, we’re doing AbortController + a timer that cancels the fetch if no events yet. If we get an event, we clear that timer and rely on idle timeout.

Monica Patel: Great. Let’s confirm non-streaming timeout values:
- total request timeout: 60s (default)
- connect timeout: 5s
- read timeout: (N/A separate in TS fetch), but Python httpx has read timeout; we can set read=30s maybe?

Ibrahim Khan: For httpx it’s usually `Timeout(connect=5, read=30, write=30, pool=5)`. Total semantics can be confusing. We can approximate with per-phase + a global “deadline” in our wrapper.

Christine Wong: Keep it simple: connect=5s, read=30s, and an overall deadline of 60s enforced at the wrapper level (monotonic time). Document how to override.

Allison Grant: Make sure the wrapper records whether it was a phase timeout vs total deadline timeout.

Monica Patel: Retry counts:
- non-streaming: max_retries=2
- streaming: max_retries=1 (only pre-first-event)
Backoff:
- base=250ms, multiplier=2, jitter=full jitter, max_delay=4s
429:
- respect Retry-After up to 10s; if Retry-After missing, use backoff.

Dana Lo: What about 500? Do we retry 500s?

Ibrahim Khan: I’d say retry 500 only if it’s a network error or a known transient gateway class. Pure 500 might be application bug. But from user POV, transient 500s happen.

Christine Wong: SRE preference: retry 502/503/504, *not* generic 500. Otherwise we can hide real bugs and spam logs.

Brian Murphy: Agree. 500s are rare and usually correlated with bad request edge cases. Better to fail and show request id.

Monica Patel: Ok retryable status codes: 408, 425, 429, 502, 503, 504. (No 500.)
Non-retryable: 400/401/403/404/422.

Allison Grant: Also don’t retry on 413 (payload too large). We should surface a clean error message.

Monica Patel: +1. We’ll classify 413/422 as user action.

Dana Lo: How do we handle tool calling in streaming? If stream disconnects after tool call request emitted by model, we might have already executed the tool. Retrying the model call could trigger the same tool call again.

Christine Wong: Another reason to not retry mid-stream.

Monica Patel: Exactly. For agent loop: we’ll treat streaming disconnect as a terminal error for that turn. We log `agent.turn_failed=true` and show “retry the user request” (manual).

Sahana Iyer: Do we want a “circuit breaker” when repeated 429s happen? Otherwise template demos might hammer.

Ibrahim Khan: For v1, simplest: cap attempts, and for 429 specifically we should add guidance in error message: “reduce concurrency” + link to docs.

Alex Martinez: We’ve seen internal beta users hitting 429 because they copy/paste and run load tests. If the template defaults do 3 parallel requests, that’s on us.

Monica Patel: Separate thread but noted. For this one: we’ll ensure retries don’t create extra concurrency.

Allison Grant: Observability requirements (minimum):
- Span: `llm.request`
- Attributes: `redwood.request_id` (if present), `http.status_code`, `retry.count`, `retry.max`, `retry.reason`, `streaming=true/false`, `stream.started`, `timeout.type` (connect/read/idle/deadline)
- Logs: single-line structured log on final failure with `error.type` and remediation hint

Brian Murphy: Also surface `x-redwood-request-id` in exception string. Support needs that.

Dana Lo: We should also ensure that if user sets custom headers (template telemetry tag) we don’t accidentally retry with headers that corporate proxies reject. (We had that “unknown header blocked” issue.)

Monica Patel: Yep, but for retries we’ll just re-use the same request. Telemetry headers will be opt-in anyway.

Ibrahim Khan: Summarizing defaults we’re agreeing to:
Non-streaming:
- connect_timeout=5s
- deadline=60s
- retries=2
- backoff 250ms -> 4s cap, full jitter
- retryable: network errors, 408/425/429/502/503/504
- respect Retry-After <= 10s
Streaming:
- connect_timeout=5s
- time_to_first_event_timeout=15s
- idle_timeout=30s
- retries=1 only if no SSE event received
- never retry after stream started

Christine Wong: Works for me. Add docs on how to tune for “long context / slow model”: increase time_to_first_event + deadline, but caution about hanging requests.

Allison Grant: + make sure metrics aren’t exploding in cardinality; `retry.reason` should be from a small enum.

Sahana Iyer: I’ll update smoke tests to set `TIME_TO_FIRST_EVENT_TIMEOUT_MS=2000` etc. and validate retry only happens pre-first-event.

Monica Patel: Great. I’ll update PR-103 description + template env schema (ENG-4187) and ping SDK teams about gaps. Also will add a note that TS uses AbortController and Python uses wrapper deadline logic.

Alex Martinez: Ship it. Please include in README troubleshooting: “Streaming disconnect behind proxy” + recommended env knobs.

Monica Patel: Will do. :thumbsup: (closing this thread unless someone objects)

Christine Wong: :thumbsup:

Allison Grant: :thumbsup:

Dana Lo: :thumbsup:

Ibrahim Khan: :thumbsup:

title: eng-sre
body:
eng-sre

Connor O'Brien: heads up, need SRE eyes on proposed backfill plan + risk before we push the button.

Context: we have ~3.1% of Hosted API usage_events missing `cache_hit` + ~0.6% missing `region` over the last ~45 days (mostly from the ingestion retry window + one bad deploy). Product/Finance want the backfill so usage exports + experiment attribution stop being noisy.

Proposal (current):
- Run a replay job over `request_logs` -> regenerate usage events with the v2 mapper (same codepath as live)
- Write into `usage_events_v2_backfill` (partitioned by `event_day`)
- Dedupe using `usage_event_dedupe_key` (request_id + attempt_id + response_fingerprint)
- After backfill completes, flip the `usage_events_current` view to union (live v2 + backfill for historical partitions)

Ask: do we need to run shadow billing compare first? and what are the biggest "oops we changed billing numbers" risks here.

Aisha Bello: +1 on doing this carefully. immediate question: does anything in the backfill change `billed_tokens` or only fills dims (`region`, `cache_hit`)?

Connor O'Brien: the intent is dims-only. BUT the v2 mapper also includes the retry/fallback double-count fix (PR-27463) and the tool-call token attribution unit tests (PR-27471). so if we replay with v2 mapper, there *could* be token deltas in edge cases.

Mei Lin: that means it’s not “dims-only”, it’s “recompute canonical usage events”. which is fine, but it’s definitely billing-impacting if we ever use those recomputed events for ledger.

Logan Wright: yup. the backfill job is essentially the same pipeline as live. it will recompute:
- prompt_tokens / completion_tokens / billed_tokens
- cache_hit attribution
- region normalization
- retry path mapping

If we constrain the backfill to ONLY populate null fields, we’d need a custom patch job (and we’d still have to deal w/ how we decide which record is authoritative).

Nadia Rahman: strongly prefer not doing a patch-in-place. we’ve been burned with partial updates + mismatched semantics. if we’re going to fix, fix with canonical replay and then treat the result as `event_version=2`.

Emily Stone: Finance/RevRec POV: absolutely no retroactive invoice changes without explicit sign-off. Replaying historical usage into anything that the billing ledger reads is a big red flag.

If this backfill is ONLY for (a) customer usage exports and (b) experiment analysis tables, we can do it with guardrails. If it touches ledger inputs for already-issued invoices, we need (1) materiality analysis and (2) documented approval.

Aisha Bello: SRE POV: we should assume “billing-impacting until proven otherwise”. shadow compare seems required if v2 mapper changes token counts.

Also: what’s the blast radius + rollback? If `usage_events_current` flips, dashboards + exports will change immediately.

Connor O'Brien: rollback plan: keep view flip behind a feature flag in the warehouse (`use_usage_events_v2_backfill`). If we see anomalies, flip it off and we’re back to current.

Caleb Johnson: operational risk: replay will hammer Snowflake + the event enrichment workers. we should isolate the backfill compute (separate warehouse) and cap concurrency. Also watch duplicate rate.

Here’s the draft job config:
```yaml
job: usage-events-backfill-v2
range_days: 45
partitions: event_day
max_parallel_partitions: 6
max_retries: 3
write_table: usage_events_v2_backfill
emit_metrics: true
metrics:
  - duplicates_rate
  - null_region_rate
  - null_cache_hit_rate
  - billed_tokens_delta_vs_v1
```

Mei Lin: can we do this in 2 stages?
1) shadow billing compare first (no view flip), to quantify deltas
2) if deltas are within expectation + Finance signs off, then apply backfill + view flip for exports/analytics

And explicitly exclude closed periods / issued invoices from any ledger recompute.

Logan Wright: +1. Also, shadow compare should break down by:
- account_id
- model
- region
- endpoint (openai-compat vs native)
- streaming vs non-streaming

We’ve seen drift concentrate in openai-compat streaming.

Aisha Bello: what thresholds are we thinking? we need something SRE can page on during the run.

Connor O'Brien: proposal:
- page if `duplicates_rate > 0.05%` for any partition
- page if `billed_tokens_delta_vs_v1` > 0.25% overall OR > 1% for any top-20 account
- page if any partition freshness lag > 6h (job stuck)

(Mei/Logan sanity check?)

Mei Lin: 0.25% overall seems fine as an initial guardrail. for top accounts, 1% might still be a lot $$$. maybe add an absolute $ threshold too (e.g., >$2k delta in a day) once we map token deltas to rates.

Emily Stone: agree with absolute threshold. percent-only hides “big customer small %”.

Nadia Rahman: we can compute an estimated $ impact using current price sheet per account plan. won’t be perfect (discounts/credits), but good enough for alerting.

Caleb Johnson: for duplicates, watch both:
- duplicate dedupe_key within backfill output
- collisions between backfill + live events when the view unions

If we union by partition, we should ensure backfill partitions don’t overlap with live partitions post-cutover (or we do `QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER()` by version).

Connor O'Brien: good call. current plan is:
- for days in backfill range, `usage_events_current` will pick v2_backfill preferred
- live ingestion continues writing v2_live
- view logic:
```sql
SELECT * FROM (
  SELECT *, 2 AS event_version FROM usage_events_v2_backfill
  UNION ALL
  SELECT *, 2 AS event_version FROM usage_events_v2_live
  UNION ALL
  SELECT *, 1 AS event_version FROM usage_events_v1
)
QUALIFY ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
  PARTITION BY usage_event_dedupe_key
  ORDER BY event_version DESC, ingested_at DESC
)=1;
```

Aisha Bello: ok, that makes rollback easier too.

PagerDuty: (auto) Aisha Bello added "metering" tag to this thread.

Logan Wright: re: shadow compare — we already have `shadow_billing_compare` service (PR-27518) that computes old vs new meter output per request. We can run it against a sampled set (or full) for the last 7 days first.

If we see big deltas, we can isolate to retry/fallback scenarios.

Mei Lin: can someone paste the query we use for delta breakdown? want to make sure we’re consistent with Finance.

Caleb Johnson: this is the v1 snippet (can adapt):
```sql
WITH deltas AS (
  SELECT
    event_day,
    account_id,
    model,
    endpoint,
    SUM(billed_tokens_v1) AS bt_v1,
    SUM(billed_tokens_v2) AS bt_v2
  FROM billing_shadow_compare_daily
  WHERE event_day >= DATEADD('day', -7, CURRENT_DATE())
  GROUP BY 1,2,3,4
)
SELECT
  event_day,
  account_id,
  model,
  endpoint,
  bt_v1,
  bt_v2,
  (bt_v2 - bt_v1) AS delta_tokens,
  (bt_v2 - bt_v1) / NULLIF(bt_v1, 0) AS delta_pct
FROM deltas
ORDER BY ABS(delta_tokens) DESC
LIMIT 200;
```

Emily Stone: please ensure shadow compare outputs are retained + immutable for audit trail (at least through close). We’ll need evidence if we’re asked “why did usage exports change” even if invoices don’t.

Connor O'Brien: noted. we’ll write compare results to `billing_shadow_compare_daily` with run_id + code_sha.

Aisha Bello: suggestion for change control:
- run shadow compare for 72h on full traffic (or at least last 7d) BEFORE backfill
- then run backfill in prod but keep `use_usage_events_v2_backfill` flag OFF
- review deltas + SRE/Finance sign-off
- flip flag during low-traffic window

Also add a post-flip monitor for 24h.

Nadia Rahman: +1. also recommend we explicitly exclude the “usage freeze window” days for month-end close from any view flip until Finance says ok.

Mei Lin: which days are freeze? last thread said we freeze usage after T+3 days for close, right?

Emily Stone: correct. For Feb close, we’ll freeze through 2026-03-04 23:59 UTC (tentative). Anything affecting Feb numbers after freeze needs revrec approval + documented exception.

Connor O'Brien: ok, plan update:
1) Run shadow compare (full) for last 7 days tonight
2) Evaluate deltas w/ Mei + Emily tomorrow; if any top acct > $2k/day delta, we pause
3) Run backfill for last 45 days into `usage_events_v2_backfill`
4) Keep flag OFF through freeze window
5) After freeze + sign-offs, flip flag for exports/analytics only (ledger stays on current billing snapshots)

Aisha Bello: :thumbsup: from SRE. but I want a clear statement: ledger will NOT read `usage_events_current` directly for already-issued invoices.

Connor O'Brien: confirmed. ledger uses `billing_ledger_finalized` snapshots per invoice period. We are not regenerating those. This is about usage exports + experiment analysis tables.

Logan Wright: (reaction :white_check_mark:) also we should annotate usage exports: “usage definitions updated (event_version=2) as of <date>” so customers don’t think they’re being stealth-rebilled.

Emily Stone: +1, and Support/Sales should have the FAQ ready (billed vs raw tokens, caching, retries). Otherwise we’ll get tickets.

Mei Lin: last ask: can we ensure the backfill job has a kill switch mid-run? if duplicates spike, we should stop without corrupting partitions.

Caleb Johnson: we can write per-partition with atomic swap:
- write to `..._staging`
- validate counts/dupes
- then `ALTER TABLE SWAP` for that partition

Connor O'Brien: done. I’ll update the runbook + add the kill switch flag (`BACKFILL_ENABLED=false`).

Aisha Bello: cool. please link the runbook + dashboards in the deploy message before kickoff.

Connor O'Brien: will do. kickoff tomorrow 10am PT after we review shadow compare output.

Emily Stone: loop me on the shadow compare summary. if anything is material, we’ll take it to Laura (CFO) before proceeding.

Connor O'Brien: ack.

title: incidents
body:
incidents

Incident Bot: 🚨 *INCIDENT OPENED* (SEV-2)
Service: audit-ingest / audit-log pipeline
Symptom: ingestion backlog growing; end-to-end delivery latency > 10m
Started: ~12:37 PT
Incident Commander: @Sean Gallagher

Sean Gallagher: Looking now. Seeing `audit_ingest_queue_depth` climbing fast in us-west. Exporter also showing lag. Anyone recently deploy to audit-ingest or observability-pack?

Aisha Bello: I’m on the dashboard. p95 audit delivery latency jumped from ~25s to 11m in the last 20 mins. Drop rate still low-ish but the “dropped events” metric is sparse (we might be blind here). Link: https://grafana.redwood/dev/audit-pipeline (internal)

Kevin Osei: Exporter side is healthy, but it’s polling slower because ingest is behind. Splunk target queue is steady; Sentinel target queue steady too. This looks upstream.

Rafael Mendes: On-call note: we saw a similar pattern last week during load test when continuous batching spiked admin actions (lots of policy edits). If it’s the ingest workers, quick mitigation is scaling consumers.

Logan Wright: Telemetry stream is showing a gap window (events arriving but delayed). Coverage dashboard checks are timing out because it queries “last 5m” and there’s nothing “fresh”. Might trigger false “missing events” alerts.

Sean Gallagher: OK, first objective: stop backlog growth.
Hypothesis: ingest consumer lag + small buffer + bursty producers.
Action: scaling `audit-ingest-consumer` from 6 -> 18 in us-west.

Incident Bot: @Sean Gallagher updated incident status: *Mitigating*.

Allison Grant: Any indication it’s a single tenant spamming? Cardinality explosion in `event_type` labels?

Aisha Bello: Quick look: top event_types are normal: `rbac.role.updated`, `apikey.created`, `policy.routing.updated`. Volume is higher than baseline but not insane. However we’re seeing a lot of retries from a couple services (`control-plane` and `console-backend`) due to 429 from ingest.

Nadia Rahman: FYI we rolled out request_id/trace_id propagation yesterday (PR-22047). Doesn’t change volume but adds a couple fields; shouldn’t affect ingest throughput unless the payload size tips batch limits.

Kevin Osei: Payload size could impact if we’re hitting max batch bytes and flushing more often. In exporter I see avg event size went from ~1.1KB to ~1.8KB (rough estimate).

Sean Gallagher: Consumer scale is in progress. Also bumping Kafka topic partitions from 12 -> 24 for `audit-events-v1` in us-west to reduce hot partitions. @Rafael Mendes can you do that change?

Rafael Mendes: Yep. Running partition increase now. ETA 5-10m.

Allison Grant: +1 on payload size. Also check compression settings? If we turned off gzip somewhere, this could be bad.

Aisha Bello: Ingest CPU is pegged at 95-100%. GC time elevated. Looks like it’s just struggling to keep up.

Sean Gallagher: Once backlog is stable, we can consider temporarily loosening best-effort behavior vs blocking admin actions. But I’d prefer not to touch producer behavior in an incident.

Incident Bot: :information_source: Deploy Bot
`audit-ingest-consumer` scaled to 18 replicas (us-west). Rollout complete.

Aisha Bello: Seeing consumer lag start to drop. Queue depth flattening. p95 latency down from 11m -> 7m and trending.

Rafael Mendes: Partition increase complete. Producers/consumers rebalancing; expect a short wobble.

Kevin Osei: Exporter lag decreasing now. SIEM targets still receiving, just delayed.

Logan Wright: Coverage dashboard is still yelling but that’s because it looks at “last 5 minutes”. Once we catch up it should recover. I’m muting “missing events” alert temporarily to avoid paging everyone.

Sean Gallagher: Approved. Please document mute + reason in the incident notes.

Allison Grant: Any evidence of data loss?

Aisha Bello: Not seeing drops in the ingest side counters, but the metric is not great. We have `events_received_total` and `events_written_total` but no strong “dropped” metric. At-least-once + retry suggests duplicates possible but loss unlikely.

Kevin Osei: Exporter has retries that can duplicate; customers de-dupe by `event_id`. But that’s export-side. For ingest, we need a better “accepted vs rejected” signal.

Sean Gallagher: Current state?

Aisha Bello: Lag is draining. Queue depth down ~60%. p95 delivery latency now ~2m.

Rafael Mendes: Rebalance looks stable. No further errors. We should keep elevated replicas until we hit steady state.

Incident Bot: @Sean Gallagher updated incident status: *Monitoring*.

Sean Gallagher: Monitoring for 15 mins, then close if stable.
Follow-ups we need to capture:
