1) Buffering/backpressure: we need a real buffer so a short burst doesn’t cause 429 + retry storms. (maps to ENG-4829)
2) Better alerting: alert on consumer lag + end-to-end delivery latency, not just exporter queue. (ENG-4835)
3) Dashboard/runbook updates: add “how to validate no loss / duplicates” + mute guidance for coverage dashboard. (runbook owner @Rafael Mendes)
4) Payload size regression check from trace_id addition; confirm batch sizing/compression. (@Nadia Rahman + @Allison Grant)

Marcus Lin: Thanks for jumping. Please ensure the post-incident notes explicitly mention customer impact: delayed audit events (up to ~11m) in us-west, no confirmed loss, possible duplicates not observed. Also add a note for enterprise accounts if anyone asks.

Logan Wright: +1. I’ll also add an action item: coverage dashboard should look at “last seen within X” based on ingest watermark, not wall clock. Otherwise we’ll page ourselves during any backlog.

Sean Gallagher: Good call. Add that as follow-up for telemetry team.

Aisha Bello: Metrics now: p95 delivery latency 38s, queue depth back to baseline. I think we can scale consumers back down gradually (18 -> 10) to keep headroom while we investigate.

Sean Gallagher: Do it in steps and watch lag.

Incident Bot: :information_source: Deploy Bot
`audit-ingest-consumer` scaled to 10 replicas (us-west). Rollout complete.

Rafael Mendes: Stability looks good. I’ll start a short incident write-up and link the runbook section for “audit pipeline backlog”.

Sean Gallagher: Closing.

Incident Bot: ✅ *INCIDENT CLOSED*
Duration: ~1h 10m
Summary: audit ingestion backlog in us-west caused audit log delivery latency spike (peak ~11m). Mitigated by scaling consumers + increasing topic partitions. Follow-ups filed for buffering/backpressure + alerting improvements + runbook updates.

title: support
body:
support

Ben Carter: Heads up: escalation from Northwind AI. They say usage dashboard token totals are ~20% higher than their estimates. They do streaming + client timeout + retry. Tracking in SUP-1842.

Vanessa Ortiz: I’m on it w/ customer. They assume timed-out attempts shouldn’t count.

Priya Natarajan: Likely retries counted as separate attempts + prompt tokens counted once admitted even if stream cancelled. Let’s make sure we explain it cleanly.

Aisha Rahman: Do we have a standard blurb for “attempt” vs “logical request”? If not, we should add to KB.

Ben Carter: I’ll draft something and link it here once Confluence page is up.

title: eng-infra
body:
eng-infra

Victor Alvarez: heads up, we’re proposing DNS TTL reductions for regional failover (Hosted + some Dedicated endpoints). Want a quick risk assessment here before we merge the tf changes.

Victor Alvarez: current state (most public records): TTL=60s (a few are 300s still). Proposal: drop to 20s for the failover-weighted records, keep everything else at 60s.

Irene Choi: 20s is… aggressive but maybe fine. Can you clarify which records exactly? `api.redwoodinference.com` is behind the geo/latency policy right?

Victor Alvarez: yep. Specifically:
- `api.redwoodinference.com` (latency/weighted policy)
- `stream.api.redwoodinference.com`
- `dedicated.<region>.redwoodinference.com` NOT in scope (those are customer-specific and already pinned)
- a couple internal healthcheck CNAMEs used by probes

Miles Thornton: +1 to being careful. Remember TTL is only one lever; resolvers don’t always respect low TTL.

Emily Zhao: confirming: some enterprise customers terminate behind corporate resolvers that clamp to min TTL (I’ve seen 30s/60s). Also Java apps tend to cache DNS “forever” unless configured (security property). So lower TTL helps, but it’s not deterministic.

Rafael Mendes: from SRE side: we’re trying to get faster convergence during a region impairment, but we don’t want surprise traffic shifts during normal ops. If TTL change causes more query load or weird caching behavior, that’s a bad trade.

Victor Alvarez: risks I’m tracking:
1) Resolver TTL floors (min TTL) => won’t see benefit for some clients
2) Negative caching (NXDOMAIN) if we misconfigure or a provider returns transient NXDOMAIN
3) Increased QPS to authoritative (Route53) and potential throttling (unlikely but worth quantifying)
4) Partial propagation mismatches during change window => weird split-brain (some clients re-resolve, others don’t)

Allison Grant: observability angle: if we do this, we should annotate dashboards and watch:
- DNS query rate at Route53
- `5xx` + tail latency by region
- ingress RPS shifts (esp. eu-west)
If there’s a subtle traffic drift we need to detect it fast.

Peter Holtz: also watch retries. Lower TTL can cause more reconnect churn on clients that resolve per request, but main risk is *failback* when a region recovers. If the record flips back quickly, some clients will thrash. We should pair with hold-down timers in routing policy.

Miles Thornton: right, DNS TTL != policy flap protection. The controller has hold-down, but DNS-based steering has to respect that too (don’t “bounce” answers).

Irene Choi: provider caveats:
- Some recursive resolvers serve stale records longer under load/outage (serve-stale RFC). During an internet event, low TTL might not matter.
- Cloudflare / public resolvers sometimes prefetch and extend caching behavior.
- On AWS, Route53 health checks can lag; but we’re not relying solely on R53 health checks for failover anyway.

Victor Alvarez: yep, this TTL change is meant to reduce the *best-case* convergence time when routing weights are adjusted, not to be the only trigger.

Emily Zhao: question: are we changing TTL for apex/ALIAS? If it’s ALIAS to a load balancer, TTL semantics are a bit weird. Route53 sets TTL but ALIAS answers can behave differently than plain A/AAAA from a client POV.

Victor Alvarez: `api.*` is ALIAS to regional NLBs via latency-based routing. TTL should still apply, but yes: some resolvers treat ALIAS just like A records. We’ll test with `dig` against common resolvers.

Rafael Mendes: can we do staged rollout? like: lower TTL only for a canary hostname first, run a planned weight flip in staging, then do prod.

Victor Alvarez: rollout plan draft:
Phase 0 (today): add canary record `api-canary.redwoodinference.com` with TTL=20s, same routing policy as `api.*`.
Phase 1 (staging): run a controlled weight shift us-east -> eu-west and measure convergence. Record:
- time-to-traffic-shift at edge (ingress)
- DNS query rates
- client error/latency
Phase 2 (prod, low blast): change TTL to 30s first on `stream.api.*` only (lower traffic), observe 24h
Phase 3 (prod): change TTL to 20s on `api.*` during a weekday window w/ oncall present
Rollback: revert TTL to 60s + stop further changes if:
- Route53 qps spikes >2x baseline for >15m
- unexplained region traffic shift >10% sustained

Sean Gallagher: I like staged. But I’d prefer 30s as final unless we can prove 20s doesn’t create noise. The bigger win might be getting rid of the 300s outliers.

Irene Choi: +1. Removing 300s is low-risk / high value.

Victor Alvarez: fair. Alternative proposal:
- Standardize to 60s everywhere
- Drop only failover steering records to 30s (not 20s)
- Keep canary at 20s for measurement

Miles Thornton: works for me. Also check: some mobile clients use OS caching with min TTL (iOS) + captive networks. Don’t assume perfect.

Allison Grant: if we do canary, please ensure dashboards include: `dns_ttl_seconds` label or annotation so we can correlate.

Victor Alvarez: we can add an annotation in the failover dashboard + a runbook note. I can also emit a one-time “infra change” event to the timeline feed.

Peter Holtz: any interaction with anycast? we have anycast notes in the networking doc but our public endpoint is still DNS->regional NLB. Anycast is only for internal edge proxies in a couple POPs, right?

Victor Alvarez: correct. No anycast change here.

Emily Zhao: another caveat: if we lower TTL but keep connection reuse high (HTTP/2), many clients won’t re-resolve until reconnect. So the effective traffic shift time is bounded by connection lifetimes too.

Miles Thornton: which is why the gateway redirect + retry-after stuff matters. DNS is just one piece.

Rafael Mendes: action items:
- Victor: update tf PR to set TTL=30s for prod records, add canary at 20s
- Allison: prep dashboard annotation + quick query for Route53 QPS
- Miles/Victor: add note to game day plan re: DNS TTL expectations (not deterministic)

Terraform Bot: PR opened: redwood-terraform/pr-1442-dns-ttl-and-failover-routing-updates (diff includes TTL changes for `api.redwoodinference.com` + new `api-canary.redwoodinference.com`).

Irene Choi: can you also add a guardrail in the PR description: “no other routing policy changes included” to keep scope tight.

Victor Alvarez: yep, will do. Also adding a checklist:
- [ ] verify no 300s TTL remain on failover records
- [ ] verify healthcheck CNAMEs unchanged
- [ ] confirm Route53 limits + current qps baseline

Sean Gallagher: and include explicit “stop” conditions + who has rollback authority (infra oncall + SRE lead). We don’t want to debate mid-change.

Victor Alvarez: ack. Rollback authority: infra oncall (primary) with SRE lead consulted, Irene as final escalation.

Allison Grant: :thumbsup: once PR is in, I’ll add the dashboard annotations & a temporary alert on Route53 qps anomalies.

Miles Thornton: one more thing: make sure we don’t reduce TTL on any records that are used for data residency pinning (some enterprise tenants depend on region-locked hostnames).

Victor Alvarez: confirmed out of scope. Only the global Hosted API hostnames.

Irene Choi: ok. +1 to proceed with the 30s plan + canary at 20s. Let’s schedule staging measurement before prod change.

Victor Alvarez: sounds good. I’ll update PR + drop a calendar hold for staging test with Emily + Allison.

Rafael Mendes: thanks all. linking this thread in the reliability initiative doc so it doesn’t get lost.

maya: Heads up — deploy-bot just kicked the eu-west canary at 01:00 UTC but our change window was entered as 01:00 LOCAL (CEST). looks like the scheduler used the local TZ value from the chart values copy.

deploy-bot: INFO: canary-job 2026-03-20T01:00Z started -> canary-id=canary-2551234567, chart=redwood-api:4.3.0, replicas=2, traffic-shift=10pct
ryan: Ugh timezone drift + wrong values. two separate problems. Suggest we cancel the canary and pin to 4.2.1 then reschedule into the proper change window (03:00 UTC).
sre-oncall: If we cancel mid-shift we might leave partial traffic split. what's the current traffic percent?

ryan: Commands: ```deploy-bot cancel canary-2551234567 --reason \"tz-mismatch + wrong values\"``` then ```helm upgrade --install redwood-api redwood/redwood-api --namespace prod --version 4.2.1 --values values/prod-pinned.yaml --set forceRollout=true```
maya: Doing the cancel now. @deploy-bot cancel please.

(30s later)
deploy-bot: NOTICE: canary-id=canary-2551234567 cancelled by maya. reason=\"tz-mismatch + wrong values\". rollback-suggestion=manual-pin

ryan: Agree. Also adding a deploy-bot pre-check to validate TZ fields: ```if values.release.window_tz != \"UTC\": warn()``` — we should default to UTC for scheduled releases.
maya: Action items: 1) adrian PR to pin chart + release notes; 2) infra to add values preflight check (ryan); 3) reschedule canary to 03:00 UTC after PR merges (maya).

title: people-ops
body:
people-ops

Jordan Yang: Quick question@people-ops I'm moving to Tokyo permanently in ~6 weeks. Want to stay an employee on Redwood payroll if possible. Whatsteps do I need for payroll cutover, benefits, and the WFH stipend vs coworking reimbursement? Any tax/nexus concerns?
Mei Chen: Congrats Jordan! Short answer: we can support JP payroll but thereare a few items. Need visa copy, JP address, local bank details. Also legal will check PE risk based on role activities. Do you plan to remain on US payroll or move to local?
Jordan Yang: I have a spouse visa that allows work. Prefer local payroll if that simplifies taxes and benefits, but want to understand impacts to US 401k/medical.
Arjun Patel: Flagging legal/tax: spouse visa with work means effectively local employment. One headcount usually low PE risk, but depends if you sign contracts or lead sales. I'll coordinate with external counsel for definitive guidance and run RSU withholding implications.
Rachel Ortiz: Payroll vendor (GlobalPayroll) supports JP. Typical vendor onboarding 30-45 days. Required: signed local payroll addendum, copy of passport and visa, Japanese bank (Zengin) details, and residential address. If you switch to JP payroll we typically offboard US medical and 401(k). Benefits team will propose enrollment in statutory health/pension.
Rachel Ortiz: Stipend mechanics: the regular WFH stipend is prorated monthly. Coworking reimbursement is receipt-based up to 15,000 JPY/month with manager pre-approval. Relocation allowance is a separate one-time claim; submit relocation form.
Mei Chen: Practical checklist we use internally:
- Jordan: provide visa/passport + JP address + bank details
- Decide payroll model (US payroll temporarily or cutover to JP payroll)
- People Ops: open vendor onboarding ticket (Rachel)
- Payroll: create PR ticket and upload link (payroll-bot)
- Legal/Tax: PE and withholding memo (Arjun)
- Benefits: enroll/opt-out of statutory plans and discuss 401k rollover
Jordan Yang: If I move to JP payroll mid-month, when will my first JP pay happen? Any payroll cutoff rules?
Rachel Ortiz: If we hit vendor cutoff for the month you will be paid on US payroll for that month and cutover next month. Vendor ETA ~35 days after ticket + docs. We'll confirm exact dates once GlobalPayroll schedules your onboarding.
Jordan Yang: Does Redwood maintain a separate relocation policy for international moves? Any extra support for visa or family?
Mei Chen: We have a relocation guide for international moves. It covers one-time relocation allowance, temporary housing reimbursement, and a visa support checklist. We don't directly handle visa sponsorship for spouse visas but we can connect you with recommended immigration partners.
Arjun Patel: Action item: I'll draft a short memo on PE risk + RSU taxation and post here within 48 hours.

payroll-bot: Created PR-8342 for Jordan Yang (Japan onboarding). Upload required docs here: https://payroll.internal/upload/PR-8342. Estimated vendor timeline: 30-45 days.
Jordan Yang: Uploaded passport and visa to the link. Filled the relocate form. Thank you all.

title: eng
body:
eng

Amina Yusuf: heads up, hitting a validation failure in Private when configuring audit-log-exporter destination via installer. Customer trying to set Splunk HEC.

Amina Yusuf: error from `rw-private configure`:
```
validate.export: destination.url must be https URL (got "http://splunk-hec.local:8088/services/collector")
validate.export: tls.verify must be true when destination.url is https
```

Amina Yusuf: their Splunk is internal + only http behind VPN. do we actually want to hard-reject http in Private?

Kevin Osei: the strict https check came from exporter PR-851. In Hosted/Dedicated we assumed any outbound SIEM target should be https.

Kevin Osei: for Private, there are legit on-prem SIEMs behind a trusted network that still run http (…unfortunate but real).

Vivek Kulkarni: +1, we can’t brick Private installs over that. But we should make it “secure by default” and loudly warn.

Sean Gallagher: what’s the current default endpoint behavior in Private? is it trying to hit the in-cluster exporter service or a customer SIEM directly?

Amina Yusuf: both cases exist.
- default: control-plane emits -> in-cluster `audit-log-exporter` at `http://audit-log-exporter.audit-logging.svc:8080/ingest`
- optional: exporter forwards -> customer SIEM (Splunk HEC, Sentinel)

Amina Yusuf: right now the installer validation is applied to *the forward destination*, not the in-cluster ingest.

Michael Nguyen: so the failing field is the forward target URL. got it.

Diego Santos: for parity: Hosted/Dedicated exporter only supports https to external endpoints, right? Private should behave the same unless explicitly configured.

Kevin Osei: yep. We did that to avoid “oops we sent audit logs over plaintext to the internet”.

Hanae Suzuki: I’m okay allowing http only if we also require an explicit `allow_insecure_http: true` (or similar) and we emit an audit event when that’s toggled.

Vivek Kulkarni: +1. Security stance: allow but make it intentional + audited.

Felix Schneider: also Console should show a big warning banner when insecure transport is enabled. (We can do later, but validation should align.)

Amina Yusuf: what about TLS settings? the error says `tls.verify must be true when destination.url is https`.

Kevin Osei: that’s because we saw folks setting `verify=false` to “make it work” with self-signed certs.

Kevin Osei: preferred approach is to support `tls.ca_bundle` / `tls.ca_file` for private CAs, not turning off verify.

Kira Thompson: Private customers often have an internal CA chain. The installer can accept a PEM and mount it for exporter.

Michael Nguyen: can we change validation to:
- https required unless `transport.insecure_http_allowed=true`
- `tls.verify` defaults true
- if https + verify=false => require `transport.allow_insecure_tls=true` and force an audit event
- if https + custom CA => allow

Sean Gallagher: +1 but be careful with naming. “insecure_tls” will get attention during security reviews.

Diego Santos: also define what’s “default endpoints” vs “customer endpoints”. In-cluster service is http but inside the cluster network. External should be https unless explicitly overridden.

Amina Yusuf: yep. Another gotcha: customer left destination empty expecting default, but installer wrote `destination.url=""` and exporter rejects empty.

Kevin Osei: that should be treated as “unset” and fallback to default (i.e., exporter disabled / no forward target). Empty string shouldn’t be a real value.

Connor O'Brien: (release angle) can we patch installer to omit the key if user doesn’t set it? low risk.

Amina Yusuf: also question: what changes do we need to audit when someone edits exporter config in Private?

Hanae Suzuki: minimum sensitive actions:
- enable/disable audit export
- change destination type (splunk/sentinel/generic webhook)
- change destination URL/host
- change auth method (token/header)
- rotate credentials (but never log secret)
- change TLS verify / CA bundle / client cert (mTLS)
- change batching/retry settings if they affect delivery guarantees materially

Kevin Osei: +1. We already have event type in taxonomy draft: `audit.export.config.updated` (and `audit.export.config.created` / `...deleted` in Hosted).

Kevin Osei: For Private installer actions, we also talked about `private.install.config.applied` but it’s too coarse. Better to emit the same `audit.export.config.updated` with `deployment_mode=private`.

Diego Santos: parity requirement: “equivalent action => equivalent event_type”. So exporter config should be `audit.export.config.updated` everywhere.

Sean Gallagher: what about TLS cert changes? Those are often part of config apply. Still need explicit audit.

Michael Nguyen: we can have installer emit one event per setting group, but keep it bounded. Maybe a single event with a diff summary:
`changed_fields=["destination.url","tls.verify","tls.ca_fingerprint"]`.

Hanae Suzuki: careful with cardinality. `changed_fields` should be allow-listed strings only (no raw values). And no cert PEM in logs.

Kevin Osei: exporter already computes a normalized diff (keys only) for console path. We can reuse the same helper.

Amina Yusuf: for TLS, what should be allowed?
- https + verify=true + system roots => ok
- https + verify=true + custom CA => ok
- https + verify=false => only if `allow_insecure_tls=true`
- http => only if `allow_insecure_http=true`

Kevin Osei: yep. And if insecure flags set, include `security_override=true` in audit event + a `reason` field but constrained (enum) like `"customer_on_prem_http"` not free-form.

Felix Schneider: if we need a reason, Console can present a dropdown. Installer can take `--reason` from a fixed set.

Sean Gallagher: plus, from ops perspective, we should add metrics for “insecure transport enabled” so SRE can flag high-risk installs during support.

Redwood Deploy Bot: deploy-bot: `redwood-private-installer` build #611.7 is live in staging (eu-west-1).

Amina Yusuf: ok, action items:
1) adjust installer to treat empty destination as unset
2) add explicit `allow_insecure_http` + `allow_insecure_tls` gates
3) support custom CA bundle path in Private
4) ensure installer emits `audit.export.config.updated` when any export config changes (incl TLS toggles)

Kevin Osei: I’ll open a patch PR on exporter validation logic + doc snippet for “Private on-prem Splunk over http (not recommended)”.

Hanae Suzuki: please loop me in on the wording. We should be super clear: enabling insecure transport is customer responsibility.

Vivek Kulkarni: and make sure this is in the Private parity checklist. Also mention default endpoint behavior so customers don’t confuse in-cluster http with external http.

Amina Yusuf: will do. I’ll link this thread in the Private installer ticket for audit events + config validation.

Connor O'Brien: ping me when PR is ready, we’ll decide if it’s a patch release or bundled with the next Private drop.

Sean Gallagher: also: once we change validation, let’s update runbook / troubleshooting doc with the exact error strings so support can search.

Amina Yusuf: :thumbsup: noted

title: eng-platform
body:
eng-platform

Logan Wright: seeing weirdness in dogfood checklist state. steps are flipping from complete -> incomplete in Console. anyone else seeing this?

Chloe Martin: yep. Dylan pinged me w/ screenshots. it looks like "Create API key" shows complete, then refresh and it's incomplete, then complete again.

Dylan Brooks: +1. internal tenant `dogfood-devex-17` had "First successful request" completed yesterday, now showing not started. not just UI; API `GET /checklist/progress` returns regressed state.

Nadia Rahman: do we have raw events for that tenant? if this is ordering / dedupe, we should check ingest_time vs occurred_at.

Caleb Johnson: pulling from telemetry topic now. i see out-of-order arrival in a couple places (gateway retries + async publish). sample:
```
tenant_id=tn_8c1...
event=onboarding.step_completed step=first_success
occurred_at=2025-02-08T19:02:11.421Z ingest_at=2025-02-08T19:02:11.900Z

tenant_id=tn_8c1...
event=onboarding.step_started step=first_success
occurred_at=2025-02-08T18:59:58.003Z ingest_at=2025-02-08T19:02:12.120Z  <-- arrived after
```
if progress service uses ingest order, it'll overwrite.

Ethan Park: that matches what i suspected. control plane emits key-created event synchronously, gateway emits first_success + some clients send a "started" hint. if the hint arrives late, it can reset.

Amara Diallo: gateway side: for streaming we emit `step_started` when we see `Accept: text/event-stream` and then `step_completed` once we flush first token. those can come on different workers; also publish is best-effort async.

Logan Wright: ok so root issue: progress service treating step state as mutable and allowing non-monotonic transitions (completed -> started) when a late/duplicated earlier event arrives.

Jada Williams: looked at progress service code (PR-28431). reducer is basically "set state to whatever the latest event says" with `updated_at = ingest_at`. there isn't a guard like max(state).

Chloe Martin: also idempotency: retries from gateway are producing duplicates. i'm seeing same `step_completed` published twice with different kafka offsets.

Caleb Johnson: yep. and some events have null request_id, so dedupe isn't possible.

Brian Murphy: reminder: ADR said server-side emission w/ limited client hints. do we *need* `step_started` from client hints at all for MVP? seems like it causes more harm than value.

Nadia Rahman: agree. but even without started, we still need monotonic transitions: NOT_STARTED -> STARTED -> COMPLETED, never go backwards. and we need a stable idempotency key per "emission" so duplicates don't churn.

Ethan Park: what fields do we have today in schema v1? is there `event_id`?

Caleb Johnson: schema has `event_id` optional but not populated consistently. gateway sets `event_id` sometimes, control plane doesn't. we do have `trace_id`/`span_id` for some events, but not for api key creation.

Amara Diallo: we can add `dedupe_key` at emission time in gateway as `sha256(tenant_id + step + request_id + event_name)` where request_id is our internal `x-redwood-request-id`. for streaming, use the initial request id.

Logan Wright: ok. but we need fix in progress service regardless: should compute step state w/ monotonic rule and ignore older precedence.

Jada Williams: proposal:
- treat each step as a state machine w/ ordering NOT_STARTED(0) < STARTED(1) < COMPLETED(2)
- persist per (tenant_id, step_id) a single row w/ `state_rank` and `state_updated_at_occurred`
- when ingesting an event: map to rank; only apply if rank > current_rank OR (rank == current_rank AND occurred_at > current_occurred_at)
- do NOT use ingest_at for ordering
- store `last_event_ids` (bounded) or `dedupe_key` for 24h to prevent churn

Chloe Martin: +1. also for started events, we should make them low priority; completed should always win.

Nadia Rahman: agreed. also: some events don't have occurred_at? if missing, we should set occurred_at=ingest_at at source (gateway) to avoid null comparisons.

Caleb Johnson: we do have occurred_at in the envelope, but client hint events had occurred_at set on client (can be skewed). i would rather drop client hints from progress computation.

Brian Murphy: +1000. client clock skew is nasty. for MVP, let's only compute from server events: api_key_created, first_2xx, first_stream_token, first_429, etc.

Dylan Brooks: from Console POV, if we lose started state it's fine. we mostly care about "done" and "not done". started is nice-to-have.

Leila Farouk: fwiw e2e tests are flaky because state flips. if we do monotonic completion, tests stabilize.

Logan Wright: ok action plan:
1) progress service: enforce monotonic transitions + occurred_at ordering, ignore regressive events
2) gateway: add consistent dedupe_key/event_id, and ensure request_id always set
3) telemetry: add data quality check for missing event_id + occurred_at nulls

Amara Diallo: i can patch gateway instrumentation (ENG-5812/5812? sorry) with required `x-redwood-request-id` + event_id and send PR today.

Nadia Rahman: for telemetry checks, i’ll add a canary query: % events with null event_id by source. if >1% alert in #eng-platform.

Jada Williams: i’ll implement reducer change. do we need to migrate existing rows? currently we store `status` string and `updated_at`.

Chloe Martin: we can do forward-only migration: add `state_rank` int + `state_updated_at_occurred` timestamp, backfill rank from status and set occurred=updated_at for existing. then apply new logic.

Caleb Johnson: also watch out for "reset" admin override. support tool may emit a reset event. that *should* allow regress, but only when `source=admin_override` and with explicit reason.

Logan Wright: good call. let’s define a separate event `onboarding.step_reset` that bypasses monotonic rule *only* if actor is support/admin and permissioned.

Dylan Brooks: Console team can treat reset as a separate state in UI anyway (shows as incomplete + note). but backend needs to handle it.

Ethan Park: question: what about replays/backfills? batch job will emit synthetic events for existing tenants. those will have occurred_at in the past and could be ingested after new events.

Jada Williams: monotonic + occurred_at compare solves: if tenant already completed, replay should not downgrade. if tenant not completed, replay can still advance (if rank higher). but if replay is older completed and tenant later was reset, we'd need the reset event to win based on occurred_at.

Nadia Rahman: yep. reset should set rank=0 but with occurred_at new, and it should be treated as "override" transition.

Caleb Johnson: adding example ordering rules to be explicit:
- normal events: only allow rank to increase
- admin_override/reset: allow rank to decrease and set a `reset_at`
- after reset_at, ignore any normal events with occurred_at < reset_at

Chloe Martin: ^ that last bullet is key. otherwise old events keep re-completing steps after reset.

Logan Wright: love it. please bake that into reducer.

DeployBot: PR opened: redwood/pr-28510-fix-checklist-state-race-condition by @jada.williams

Jada Williams: PR-28510 includes:
- step_state table migration
- monotonic reducer + reset watermark logic (`ignore_if_occurred_at < last_reset_at`)
- unit tests for out-of-order + duplicate events
reviewers requested: @logan.wright @chloe.martin @caleb.johnson

Leila Farouk: can we add an integration test w/ synthetic out-of-order events? i can wire it into our QA plan.

Jada Williams: yep, i’ll add a fixture in `progress_service/tests/fixtures/out_of_order.jsonl` and a test that replays in wrong order.

title: eng-ml
body:
eng-ml

sara: did a quick smoke on the eval harness for q4-model-4. pass@1 ~8% lower than baseline and BERTScore avg down 0.03. CI smoke failed with a metric assertion.

kevin: which runner? local vs ci container? tokenizer/shard config changed? @yusuf do you recall recent sampling changes?

sara: ran `eval-runner --config ci/smoke.yaml --model q4-variant` inside the CI image. logs:

``
INFO  eval.runner: loading 1..1000
WARN  eval.metrics: pass@k denom mismatch: expected 100, got 87
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/src/eval/runner.py", line 412, in <module>
    main()
AssertionError: k > n
```

yusuf: yep, PR #412 added `unique_candidates` which can reduce per-example n. pass@k impl assumed n >= k. We should handle n < k. two approaches:
- per-example clamp k' = min(k, n) and use estimator
- sample with replacement to reach k
I'll put up a patch with the clamp plus a tests.

elaine: for BERTScore delta I reproduced locally; culprit was tokenization: the new model's preproc lowercases and strips punctuation. Harness used default tokenizer, not model-specific one. we need to pin tokenizer in the eval config per model.

sara: action items: (1) make pass@k robust for n<k, (2) pin tokenizer in harness config, (3) make calibration bin math tolerant of zero-count bins so CI doesn't blow up on edge cases.

kevin: calibration code currently does `acc = bin.correct / bin.count` — add guard for `bin.count == 0` to skip or treat as empty to avoid NaN. also add unit tests for empty bins and for n<k.

yusuf: will open a small PR with three commits: passatk clamp + tests, tokenizer pin, calibration-bin-safety + tests. will bump metric-impl version string and add CHANGELOG.

sara: one more: add `--metric-version` output in runner header/telemetry so dashboards show which metric implementation produced numbers (we had numbers change overnight and dashboards had no impl id). example: `Metric-Impl: v0.9.3+pr412` printed at start.

eval-bot: CI queued: eval-smoke/2051 started by sara (job id ci-eval-2051)

elaine: I'll review and run smoke against quantized build. if confirmed, add a regression alert on smoke that fires when pass@1 drops >5% vs baseline.

kevin: also add short doc snippet about pass@k edge cases (n<k, deduped outputs, ties) in the eval metrics docs.

sara: sounds good — tag PR `eval:ci-smoke` and assign to yusuf. after green, roll to canary. :thumbsup:

kevin: moving follow-up to new thread for rollout steps.

title: eng-platform
body:
eng-platform

Allison Grant: hey folks — need a quick dashboard pass for the FP8/INT8 sprint.

Looking for TTFT + TPOT + tokens/s broken down by:
- model (top hosted list)
- GPU SKU (H100 / A100 / L4)
- kernel mode (baseline / fp8 / int8)
- region (at least us-east / eu-west)

This is for both benchmark runs and perf canary rollout monitoring. Can someone help spec + wire a Grafana dashboard? Ideally linkable in the runbook + canary page.

Julian Moore: +1. we just added scheduler prefill/decode split metrics (queue depth + backpressure counters) and it’d be nice if the dashboard has those too, at least as “debug” panels.

Marcus Reed: do we already have `kernel_mode` as a label on the runtime histograms? i know PR for tagging is in flight but not sure it hit prod.

Rina Kobayashi: right now in staging we have `quant_mode=fp8|int8|fp16` on some counters but not consistently on histograms. can do a first pass with what’s available, but the “real” breakdown will need the metrics-tagging PR (i think 19934) to land.

Allison Grant: yep, that’s the thing. SRE is asking for “no more screenshots” and wants a single place to triage regressions by model/GPU/mode. Even if the first version is partial, let’s at least have the skeleton + filters.

Rafael Mendes: from canary side: must have p95 TTFT and p95 TPOT with a baseline overlay. Also error rate. If we don’t see “baseline vs canary” on the same panel it’s hard to justify rollbacks.

Vanessa Ortiz: capacity question: are we slicing by cluster too? would prefer region-level first to avoid leaking which clusters are in use (and reduce cardinality).

Allison Grant: agree — region is enough. cluster can be a hidden debug var if we really need it.

Irene Choi: fwiw H100 nodes differ by driver in a couple clusters right now (we’re pinning in the benchmark runner but not everywhere). if you can show `driver_version` somewhere it’ll save time when variance pops up.

Marcus Reed: careful on cardinality. adding `driver_version` label to all the histograms will explode. could show it as a table from build metadata / node exporter? or just as an annotation when the runner is pinned.

Allison Grant: ok let’s scope:
1) main panels (canary): TTFT p50/p95, TPOT p50/p95, tokens/s, error rate
2) debug: prefill/decode time breakdown, queue depth, GPU util/mem, saturation (if we have it)
3) templating vars: model, gpu_sku, kernel_mode, region, cohort (baseline vs canary)

Rina — can you confirm exact metric names we should use?

Rina Kobayashi: current names in prod:
- `rw_inference_ttft_ms` (histogram)
- `rw_inference_tpot_ms` (histogram)
- `rw_inference_tokens_per_sec` (gauge)
- `rw_inference_requests_total{status=...}`
labels: `model`, `region`, `gpu_sku` exist. `kernel_mode` only in staging for now.

we can still do per-model/per-gpu dashboards now and leave kernel_mode as “coming soon” var.

Julian Moore: scheduler metrics (new):
- `rw_sched_prefill_ms` (hist)
- `rw_sched_decode_ms` (hist)
- `rw_sched_queue_depth` (hist)
- `rw_sched_backpressure_events_total` (counter)
labels include `model`, `region`, `gpu_sku` (same set)

Marcus Reed: for overlay baseline/canary, we can use `cohort` label? do we have that consistently?

Rafael Mendes: canary adds `cohort=perf-canary` on the canary fleet only. baseline doesn’t have cohort label (empty). we can either treat “missing cohort” as baseline or we add a relabel rule to set cohort=baseline. i’d prefer the latter.

Allison Grant: +1 relabel baseline. otherwise PromQL gets gross and people copy/paste it wrong.

Grafana Bot: Allison Grant created dashboard draft “FP8/INT8: Runtime Perf Canary (WIP)” in folder “Serving Runtime / Perf”.

Allison Grant: ok, draft is up but it’s ugly. here’s what I have so far:
https://grafana.redwoodinference.net/d/rt-fp8int8-canary/runtime-fp8-int8-canary?orgId=1

Notes / gaps:
- kernel_mode var is stubbed (no data yet)
- TTFT/TPOT panels work but no baseline overlay yet
- tokens/s is noisy when sample is small

Can someone sanity check the queries?

Marcus Reed: looking. for TTFT p95 you have:
`histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(rw_inference_ttft_ms_bucket{model=~"$model",region=~"$region",gpu_sku=~"$gpu"}[5m])))`

You’re missing cohort + also need to preserve cohort in the `sum by` so we can compare baseline vs perf-canary on same graph:

Try:
`histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le, cohort) (rate(rw_inference_ttft_ms_bucket{model=~"$model",region=~"$region",gpu_sku=~"$gpu",cohort=~"$cohort"}[5m])))`

Then set `$cohort` default to `baseline|perf-canary`.

Allison Grant: yep that’s better. i’ll patch.

Rafael Mendes: also set min sample size? we had false positives from tiny volumes. even a panel that shows request count over the window would help.

Allison Grant: good call. adding “reqs/min” and “tokens/min” panels.

Rina Kobayashi: for request rate:
`sum by (cohort) (rate(rw_inference_requests_total{model=~"$model",region=~"$region",gpu_sku=~"$gpu",cohort=~"$cohort"}[5m]))`

Error rate panel:
`sum(rate(rw_inference_requests_total{status=~"5..",...}[5m])) / sum(rate(rw_inference_requests_total{...}[5m]))`

Make sure to exclude `status="canceled"` if that’s present in the series.

Julian Moore: if you have room, add a panel for “prefill fraction”:
`sum(rate(rw_sched_prefill_ms_sum{...}[5m])) / (sum(rate(rw_sched_prefill_ms_sum{...}[5m])) + sum(rate(rw_sched_decode_ms_sum{...}[5m])))`

helps explain cases where kernels win microbench but not end-to-end.

Allison Grant: added. also dropped in queue depth p95.

Irene Choi: on the driver stuff: can we at least annotate dashboard with runner metadata when it’s a benchmark run? (not prod traffic). we have the benchmark artifact metadata json; could scrape into Loki and show a table.

Allison Grant: for now I’ll add a text panel: “benchmark runs must be pinned driver/CUDA; see benchmark-runner PR-851”. Longer term we can add a Loki panel.

Vanessa Ortiz: +1 keep it simple for sprint. i mostly want something that tells us “is eu-west worse on H100 fp8 canary” quickly.

Allison Grant: updated dashboard with cohort overlay + req count.

Link (v2):
https://grafana.redwoodinference.net/d/rt-fp8int8-canary/runtime-fp8-int8-canary?orgId=1&refresh=30s

Panels:
- TTFT p50/p95 (baseline vs perf-canary)
- TPOT p50/p95 (baseline vs perf-canary)
- tokens/s (avg) + req/min
- error rate (5xx)
- debug row: prefill ms, decode ms, prefill fraction, queue depth p95, backpressure events

kernel_mode is still hidden until tagging lands.

Marcus Reed: looks good. one nit: tokens/s panel should also split by cohort, otherwise people assume it’s comparable.

Allison Grant: fixed.

Rafael Mendes: can we add a quick “diff” stat? e.g., canary p95 / baseline p95 for TTFT + TPOT. makes go/no-go faster.

Allison Grant: added two stat panels at top:
- TTFT p95 ratio (perf-canary / baseline)
- TPOT p95 ratio (perf-canary / baseline)

They’re crude but will help.

Julian Moore: :thumbsup: also once kernel_mode label is live, we’ll want cohort *and* kernel_mode — i.e. baseline fp16 vs canary fp8 is the main compare.

Rina Kobayashi: metrics-tagging PR should land tomorrow; once that’s in prod we can expose `$kernel_mode` var and add a “mode compare” row.

Allison Grant: cool. i’ll hold off on extra panels until the label exists.

Action items:
- Allison: update runbook to link this dashboard
- Rina: ping when kernel_mode tag is live; we’ll add the mode filter
- Rafael: confirm cohort relabel rule for baseline (so queries don’t require missing-label hacks)

Rafael Mendes: baseline relabel is in the canary config PR, should roll with next deploy. will confirm in #eng-sre when it’s in.

Allison Grant: thanks all. please drop comments directly on the dashboard if you want changes; i’ll keep iterating as the sprint goes.

title: eng-platform
body:
eng-platform

Ethan Park: Question for SRE + telemetry folks: for Dedicated staged rollouts, how should gate eval behave if metrics are missing / delayed (telemetry lag, ingest outage, etc.)? We need to pick fail-open vs fail-closed before we lock the state machine.

Peter Holtz: +1. we saw “Unknown” gates during last week’s dogfood when prometheus remote_write was backpressured. Promotion logic needs a deterministic rule.

Logan Wright: Missing can mean a few things:
- no traffic (0 reqs) => some metrics legitimately absent
- traffic exists but tag mismatch / cardinality drop => stage labels not present
- ingest delay => data is there but late
- hard outage => no data at all
We should distinguish “no samples” vs “telemetry stale”.

Sean Gallagher: SRE preference: default should be fail-closed for *promotion*. If you can’t prove it’s healthy, don’t advance. But we need an escape hatch (force-promote) with audit + RBAC.

Jordan Lee: Agree on deterministic. If gate evaluation returns UNKNOWN due to missing data, treat as FAIL for the policy engine decision (block auto-promotion). But we should also surface “why unknown” so oncall isn’t guessing.

Allison Grant: +1 on surfacing reason codes. Can we standardize:
- PASS
- FAIL
- UNKNOWN_NO_DATA (no samples in window)
- UNKNOWN_STALE (data older than staleness threshold)
- UNKNOWN_ERROR (query execution error)
Then promotion logic uses a mapping.

Ethan Park: That works. We also have the “manual gates” phase (operator checked) in Phase 1. In that case, missing metrics shouldn’t hard-block manual promote, but should warn.

Rafael Mendes: careful: even for “manual”, the UI should still show the gate status as UNKNOWN and require a reason string if you override. We need paper trail for change mgmt.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: On RBAC: force-promote should be a separate permission (admin-only) vs normal “promote” (operator). And force-promote should *require* `reason` + ticket link if possible.

Jordan Lee: Mechanically in policy engine, I propose:
1) Gate evaluation returns (status, observed_value?, threshold?, window, samples, reason_code)
2) Promotion eligibility:
- if any gate FAIL => block
- if any gate UNKNOWN_* => block (same as FAIL) unless `override=true`
3) Override path is explicit action: `POST /promote?override=true` with audit event capturing reason_code(s) + freeform justification.

Peter Holtz: what about abort/rollback triggers? If metrics go missing *after* promotion to a stage, do we auto-abort? That’s different than blocking promotion.

Sean Gallagher: yeah, we shouldn’t auto-abort just because telemetry blips for 2 mins. But we also can’t keep progressing. I’d say:
- auto-promotion stops if telemetry is unknown
- auto-abort only on explicit fail signals (error rate, saturation, OOM)
- if telemetry is stale beyond X minutes while in an early stage, raise an alert + optionally auto-hold

Logan Wright: +1. We can implement staleness detection using the max timestamp in the timeseries. e.g. `now() - last_sample_ts > 3m` => STALE.
Also, we should treat “0 traffic” specially: for error-rate / latency gates, if req_count < min_samples, status should be UNKNOWN_NO_DATA (not PASS).

Allison Grant: we already have min sample size standards for SLO alerting. Can reuse: e.g. min 100 reqs over window, or min 5 req/min sustained for 10m. But Dedicated can be low volume.

Ethan Park: Dedicated low volume is real esp for some enterprise batch jobs. For those, do we allow promotion w/ low samples?

Rafael Mendes: I’d keep the rule consistent: if you don’t have enough samples, you don’t have enough confidence. But then force-promote exists. Also we can allow stage duration to be longer (wait for samples) rather than relaxing min_samples.

Jordan Lee: +1. We can add “max_wait” / “min_duration” per stage. Promotion requires:
- stage >= min_duration
- all gates PASS
If min_samples not met, gates are UNKNOWN => stage just waits.

Peter Holtz: Make sure waiting doesn’t deadlock the rollout forever. Need a “held” state or “timed out” event.

Priya Natarajan: Popping in — directionally I want fail-closed for promotion. We got dinged in the last incident retro for “blind” changes. But product needs an operational escape hatch.
Concretely:
- default behavior: UNKNOWN blocks promotion
- manual override allowed for admins with reason + audit
- UI should loudly indicate telemetry outage / staleness
- do NOT auto-rollback on UNKNOWN alone; do auto-hold and alert after some threshold

Ethan Park: Thanks @Priya Natarajan. What’s the staleness threshold? 3m? 5m?

Logan Wright: For our pipeline, p95 end-to-end latency is ~45s, p99 around 2m during load. I’d set staleness at 5m to avoid false STALE during normal backpressure.

Sean Gallagher: 5m is fine. But the eval window might be 10–15m; if you’re stale for 5m, you’re already missing half the window. The status should be UNKNOWN_STALE and block.

Allison Grant: +1. Also add a distinct alert: “Gate eval stale” should page telemetry oncall if it’s global, vs ticket if it’s pool-specific tag mismatch.

Jordan Lee: We can detect global vs pool-specific by checking a control query (no stage tag) and comparing. If base metrics exist but stage-tagged ones don’t => likely tagging / cardinality issue.

Peter Holtz: that would’ve caught SUP-28605 earlier (gate evidence empty due to tag mismatch). +100.

Kaitlyn Nguyen: Re audit fields, please include:
- actor
- pool_id
- rollout_plan_id
- from_stage -> to_stage
- override=true/false
- override_reason
- gate_snapshot (list of gate statuses)
Even if we don’t store full payload, we need enough for compliance.

Ethan Park: ok summarizing proposal:
- Gate eval returns PASS/FAIL/UNKNOWN_* with reason codes + samples + window.
- Promotion: fail-closed on UNKNOWN.
- Auto-abort: only on FAIL (objective fail), not on UNKNOWN.
- If UNKNOWN persists > 10m (config), transition to HELD + alert.
- Override requires admin RBAC + reason, emits audit.
I’ll thread this into the design spec + policy engine PR.

Priya Natarajan: Sounds good. Please make sure Product understands “unknown blocks promotion” so we don’t surprise anyone in beta.

Logan Wright: I’ll add to telemetry backlog: expose `gate_eval_data_freshness_seconds` and tag-mismatch detector. Also document “no traffic” vs “missing telemetry”.

Jordan Lee: I’ll update the policy engine contract to include `reason_code` and `staleness_ms`. We should keep the response stable for Console.

Sean Gallagher: :thumbsup: once you have the exact mappings, post in #eng-sre too so oncall playbook matches.

Ethan Park: will do. closing loop after I write it up.

title: sales
body:
sales

marta (sales): Heads-up — Saffron Labs is greenlit for a 2-week POC. They want a dedicated GPU pool for inference and evals. Need guidance on SKU/region sizing, VPC access, and pricing. Target start ~Apr 8. cc @kai @ravi

ravi (solutions): Quick q: what throughput/concurrency do they expect? also model family (LlamaX-70B-ish?) and seq lengths?

marta (sales): Good call. They plan to run LlamaX-70B and one smaller 13B reranker. Typical prompt seq ~1024 tokens, evals with longer convs up to 2048. Expected steady QPS ~6 requests/s, peak ~18 req/s for short jobs. Concurrency target ~48 simultaneous sessions during load tests.

kai (infra): For those numbers we should avoid pure A100 unless cost is priority. H100 80GB is ideal for 70B at 1024/2048. EU-west1 H100 capacity is limited this week — we can do a mixed pool: primary H100s + A100s for lower-priority batch/evals.

marta (sales): They asked for 8 H100-equivalent GPUs available, with ability to burst another 4 GPUs for large evals. Preferred EU but can tolerate EU-central as fallback. Need VPC peering + mTLS for control plane, and dev API keys scoped to the pool. Any compliance blockers?

dena (security): mTLS + per-route API keys is fine. We'll need customer CIDR for peering, KMS integration for any keys stored, and audit log forwarding. If they want BYO certs for mTLS, we can support but need cert rotation plan. Also require that Saffron sign the enterprise DPA before provisioning.

ravi (solutions): Confirming: pool size request = baseline 8 H100-equivalent + burst +4 (total 12). Autoscale policy: keep min=6, target=8, max=12? Also do they want preemptible/spot for burst GPUs or strictly reserved?

marta (sales): Prefer reserved for baseline, spot for burst is ok if it doesn't affect SLAs for the POC. They want an estimate for monthly cost vs metered during the 2-week POC.

kai (infra): Proposed config: mixed-sku pool: 6 x nvidia-h100-80gb (reserved commit), 4 x nvidia-a100-40gb (spot-burst), autoscale min=6, target=8, max=12. Region: attempt eu-west1 first; if capacity shortfall, fallback to eu-central1 with cross-region routing. Provisioning ETA: 72-120h depending on quota approvals.

kai (infra): Network/CIDR notes: we'll need a routable customer CIDR for peering (recommend 10.100.0.0/22). We require outbound HTTPS to control-plane IPs and inbound only from our proxies. I can paste the minimal firewall rules after ticket is created.

dena (security): Checklist to include with provisioning request: KMS key ARN, SOC2/ISO attachments (if requested), list of admin users, IP CIDR for peering, certs or BYO cert intent, retention period for audit logs. Also need contact for security review (email).

kai (infra): Ok I'm going to open an internal provisioning ticket with ops. Please reply with billing contact and CIDR so I can attach.

marta (sales): Billing contact: finance@saffron.ai. CIDR provisional: 10.100.8.0/22. They will confirm exact CIDR after legal sign-off.

kai (infra): creating ticket...

deploy-bot: Provisioning ticket PR-4821 created by kai. Details: saffron-poc-mixed-h100-a100, requested region eu-west1 (fallback eu-central1), pool config attached. ETA provisioning window 72-120 hours. Link: https://internal.redwood/provision/PR-4821

marta (sales): perfect — can you include a quick cost ballpark for 2-week POC (reserved baseline vs metered)? I can pass to Saffron so they can budget.

kai (infra): Ballpark: reserved-equivalent commit for 6 H100s ~ $85k/mo (region variance). For a 2-week metered trial (min 6 active, avg burst to 10 for 30% of time) ~ $50-60k for the two weeks. Adding A100 spot bursts reduces cost by ~20% during heavy runs. I'll add precise calc to PR-4821.

dena (security): Also note: if they want private deployment (Private VPC) instead of peering, that adds setup time + extra compliance review. Mention to customer now to avoid surprises.

marta (sales): noted. I'll add to the kickoff. Kai — once PR-4821 has the cost calc and network firewall snippet, I'll schedule the kickoff call with Saffron and copy security. Thanks all :thumbsup:

kai (infra): Will do. Firewall example to attach: ```allow outbound 443 to control-plane.redwood-internal: 35.207.0.0/16, allow inbound from 10.100.8.0/22 to pool-private-ips TCP 22,443; NAT for egress required```

marta (sales): ack, adding to Saffron packet. Scheduling call for Monday.

ravi (solutions): I'll prepare a short perf test plan (throughput & 99p latency checks) to run once pool is up.

marta (sales): awesome — marking thread blocked-on: PR-4821 (kai) and DPA signed (legal).

body:
support

alex (support): Heads-up — ACME reporting p99 API latency ~3x since ~18:30 UTC yesterday. Customer repro attached. They see long time-to-first-byte and responses queued.

alex (support): Error samples: HTTP 202 slow-accept -> 200 delayed body. They said it correlates with high concurrent runs.

sam (eng-runtime): looking. Can you paste a sample request id / trace?

alex (support): trace id t=acme-9f3b, sample curl below:
```
curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED' -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"lm-xl","input":"hello"}' -v
```
Response times: TCP established ~30ms, initial status 202, body arrived after 1.8s (p99 ~1.8s, baseline 600ms).

elaine (eng-sre): Metrics show request_queue_length for region us-west-2 jumped from 40 -> 410 around 18:15 UTC. Worker pool CPU saturated on several nodes.

sam (eng-runtime): I see a recent config change to admission rules rolled yesterday 17:50: `tenant_concurrency_limit` lowered for tenant-tier 'startup' to 50. ACME is labeled startup. That could cause queue pileup when bursty.

murad (oncall): Confirmed: increase in per-tenant queue waits and inflight throttle rejections. No errors besides delays. No auth/billing errors.

sam (eng-runtime): Quick mitigation: temporarily bump ACME concurrency to 200 and enable fallback to 'lm-large' for cold starts to reduce token latency. Command I can run: 
```
redwoodctl tenants update acme --set concurrency=200 --enable-fallback=lm-large
```
Do we want to do that now?

alex (support): Customer on phone and ok with temporary bump. Please proceed and advise ETA.

sam (eng-runtime): executing now. will post deploy-bot output.

deploy-bot: executed redwoodctl tenants update acme --set concurrency=200 --enable-fallback=lm-large 
Status: success. Change id: ch_20260317_01

elaine (eng-sre): After change, queue_length dropped to ~60 over 3 minutes, p95 improved from 1.2s -> 520ms. CPU normalized on the hot nodes. Looks like admission threshold was the bottleneck.

murad (oncall): Keeping watch for 30m. Recommending follow-up: revert the general tenant limit change and instead set an adaptive fairshare policy so single tenants don't cause global pressure.

sam (eng-runtime): Agreed. Root cause: over-aggressive global startup-tier concurrency cap deployed without workload smoothing. Action items: (1) rollback yesterday's broad cap or narrow to newly onboarded accounts; (2) add a slow-roll canary for admission policy changes; (3) add alert on sudden queue length deltas per tenant.

alex (support): Noted. I'll update ACME that we applied temporary config and they should see improvement; they'll verify for next 2 hours and tell us if any regressions.

elaine (eng-sre): I'll open a follow-up RFC for adaptive fairshare and add a Prometheus alert: tenant_queue_delta > 100 for 5m.

sam (eng-runtime): Also adding a short-term mitigation: auto-fallback policy to lighter model if queue wait > 800ms. Will PR config.

murad (oncall): Marking this thread as actively monitored. If p99 stays stable for 2h, we close and do postmortem notes.

alex (support): ACME confirms latency back to normal in their staging run. Thanks all :thumbsup:

sam (eng-runtime): leaving follow-up tasks in #eng-runtime backlog.

elaine (eng-sre): postmortem tag: ingress-admission-fairness-20260317. I'll capture timelines and the deployment that changed limits.

alex (support): closing loop with customer, will ping if they see anything.

murad (oncall): After 45m observed: p99 stable at baseline. Moving to monitoring-only.

alex (support): resolved for now.

[2026-03-15T10:02:11Z] gateway: proxy writev->upstream 10.4.2.7:443 id=rq_az987 status=200 bytes_sent=1421
[2026-03-15T10:02:11Z] gateway: writev: broken pipe id=rq_az987
[2026-03-15T10:02:11Z] gateway: classify: closing connection early -> labeled 502 id=rq_az987
```
That classification is why it shows as a 5xx and why billing counted it as server error path.

alex (Eng-Oncall): looks like this is our classic early-eof vs client-abort heuristic. Right now our gateway code maps an early `writev: broken pipe` during chunked transfer to a 502 if the server didn't explicitly send a final chunk header. In practice that mislabels customer-driven aborts (client closes after first chunk) as server 5xx.

Can you confirm: for rq_az987 did the upstream model respond with a 200 and at least one chunk before the socket closed? maria: logs show bytes_sent=1421 which implies at least one chunk made it out.

maria (Support): Correct — upstream returned 200 and we wrote data. The `bytes_sent` > 0. Yet classify->502 happened.

alex (Eng-Oncall): Ok. Proposed short-term mitigation: change classification so that if bytes_sent > 0 and upstream returned 2xx, then an `EPIPE`/`ECONNRESET` during response streaming is recorded as `client_disconnect` and not emitted as a 5xx metric or billed as a server error. We can roll that as a config tweak in the gateway logging/metrics. That should stop these from inflating 5xx and creating billing disputes.

raj (Infra): I can roll the config change to us-west-2 cluster in a canary (5% traffic) in ~10m. Note: metrics backfill won't change historical counts; we'll need to add an exception in billing pipeline to retroactively mark the two request ids as not-billed pending investigation.

maria (Support): @tess_acme we will issue a credit for rq_az987 and rq_bx123 while this is being fixed — filing billing-case #98765. Are there other request ids or times you can share? Also, can you try the same repro but set `--no-buffer` and then allow the client to stay connected to determine if the problem reproduces when the client keeps the socket open?

`tess_acme (Customer):` I can run that. Most of our clients do aggressive reconnects so it reproduces frequently. Appreciate the quick turnaround. 🙏

alex (Eng-Oncall): I'll open ENG-5432 for the code fix and link this thread. Fix plan:
- Change gateway heuristic: if upstream status is 2xx and bytes_sent > 0, treat EPIPE/ECONNRESET during response as client_abort (non-5xx).
- Add tracepoint to log `bytes_sent_at_abort` and `client-close-flags` to help debugging.
- Add unit + e2e that simulates client closing mid-chunked-stream.
- Add a metric `client_disconnect_after_first_chunk` to monitor regression.

Here's a quick grep command I used to fetch gateway lines for a request id:
```
kubectl logs gateway-abc -n prod | rg "rq_az987" -n
```
and to search for `EPIPE` across a time window:
```
rg "writev: broken pipe|EPIPE|upstream closed" /var/log/gateway/*.log | tail -n 50
```

raj (Infra): Rolling the canary now. Will post when done. ingress-bot:deploy started.

ingress-bot: deploy gateway-config v2026.03.15-canary -> us-west-2 (5% traffic) started by raj

raj (Infra): Canary completed, observing a drop in new `502-classify` counts for client-abort pattern in the canary subset. No perf regression noted. Rolling to 20% then 100% over 30m.

maria (Support): @tess_acme we added billing-case #98765 and put a provisional credit on those two request ids. Once ENG-5432 lands we'll follow up and keep you posted.

alex (Eng-Oncall): Follow-ups I put in the ticket: add an automated check to avoid counting these as 5xx in dashboards (so historical alerts don't re-fire), and add a small observability dashboard for `client_disconnect_after_first_chunk`. Also adding a regression test to the streaming e2e harness.

`tess_acme (Customer):` Thanks everyone — I'll test the repro against staging and report results in this thread. Appreciate the refund and the fast action. :raised_hands:

maria (Support): Closing the support thread for now; ENG-5432 and billing-case #98765 are open for tracking. Reopen if you see new ids after the rollout. cc @alex @raj

title: eng-ml
body:
eng-ml

jin: quick debrief from this morning's 'early-reject' probe on the new 13B quant build. trying an entropy-informed partial-prefill instead of full prefill skip.

marco: define partial-prefill? short description pls.

jin: logic: for each prompt, compute rolling prefix entropy over first 8 tokens. if entropy < 0.9 -> only warm first 1 kv block (8 tokens) and stream rest without full prefill. else do normal prefill. goal: reduce kv-copy + decode ops while preserving conditioning for short, factual prompts.

elaine: nice. did you change scheduling? micro-batching?

jin: micro-batch=4 (was 8), async-kv-copy=true, speculative-decode=false for the run. command:
```
./bench/run_prefill_probe.sh \
  --model redwood/13b-q4_0 \
  --policy early_reject \
  --entropy-window 8 \
  --entropy-threshold 0.9 \
  --micro-batch 4 \
  --async-kv-copy true
```

perf-bot: job/7839 queued -> running. dashboard: https://console.redwood/internal/runs/7839 :bar_chart:

marco: baseline vs probe numbers? especially p50/p95 and exact match on short QA.

jin: short summary (baseline -> early-reject): p50_token_ms 22.6 -> 19.8, p95_token_ms 85 -> 77, per-request tokens emitted -6.2% median. EM(SQuAD_short) 84.5 -> 83.1 (1.4pt drop), Rouge-L (long-form slices) unchanged within noise.

elaine: that EM hit is smaller than the earlier prefill-drop tests. promising. what's the error mode? wrong span length? hallucinated shorter answers?

jin: inspected 30 failures: ~60% were off-by-1 token at span boundaries, ~25% were missing a number (unit/quantity), rest were paraphrase mismatches. seems like partial-kv warmup sometimes lost tiny ngram cues.

marco: try forcing full warmup when the prompt contains a question mark or starts with "what/when/who/why" — heuristics to catch interrogative short prompts.

jin: good call. also want to test q4f layout (previously q4_0) — layout interacts with attention norm & tiny value shifts. launching q4f now with same policy + a canary rollout (10% traffic) against baseline.

perf-bot: run/7840 started (compare q4f-earlyreject vs baseline). artifacts: s3://redwood/runs/7840/artifacts

elaine: add nm-gram overlap and exact-span-length CDF to the artifact set. helps quantify off-by-one.

jin: will add. also toggling sampling temp 0.7/0.9 to ensure policy doesn't couple with softmax tail changes.

marco: don't forget to flag regression if EM drop >2pts on short QA or if p95 increases >5%. we'll block rollout otherwise.

jin: noted. setting auto-block thresholds in the experiment config.

elaine: once q4f results are in, let's run a small RAG pass to see if retrieval + partial-prefill amplifies or mitigates the issue. retrieval tends to make early tokens denser with facts so could matter.

jin: agree. scheduling RAG+earlyreject after q4f canary completes. ETA ~3h. will post artifacts + a 3-line summary when ready. :rocket:

maya: Heads up — after the v7.0 rollout around 11:22 UTC we saw p95/p99 latency jump ~2.5-3x for a subset of hosts. Error rates stayed flat but throughput dropped on those hosts.
sam: Noticed this too. Correlates with an uptick in long-seq requests (>=1024 tokens) and a spike in KV cache miss rate on the same machines.
jordan: Rollback initiated for the canary group? Did we try switching to the prior tokenizer variant to confirm? :thinking:
maya: Yep, rolled the canary back to v6.9 at 11:38 — latency returned to baseline on those canary machines. Prod is still on v7.0 for ~80% traffic.
li: Quick profiling from one affected host attached. Seeing kernel selector flip to the slower attention kernel for ~30% of long calls, and batcher is forming smaller batches for seq>=1024 (batch size drop from 16->6). Logs:

```
[profile] seq_len=1024, selector=attn_v2_slow, batch_size=6, kv_cache_miss=0.42
[profile] seq_len=64, selector=attn_fast, batch_size=16, kv_cache_miss=0.03
```

This matches the observed per-token cost increase.

ops-bot: deploy-event: v7.0 rollout started 2026-03-17T11:20:00Z

sam: Two hypotheses: 1) Tokenizer change in v7.0 causes longer tokenization for some inputs -> longer seq distribution tail. 2) Model binary changes led to kernel misselection for moderate sequence lengths (512-1024).
maya: Also seeing KV cache eviction rate up ~3x on affected hosts (evict ops during prefix-heavy workloads). Could be memory pressure from different attention kernel memory layout.
jordan: Any noisy neighbor reports? Maybe another tenant spiking memory/IO causing eviction and smaller batches.
li: Checked host metrics — no obvious noisy tenant CPU hog, but one noisy shard had heavy memory fragmentation after the model load. Kernel memory allocator logs:

```
[allocator] host=host-23 mem_fragment=0.38 after mmap(model_v7)
[evict] reason=frag_threshold, freed=512MB
```

sam: Interesting. If allocator fragmentation causes frequent evictions, KV hits drop -> more recompute -> slower kernels -> batcher timeouts and smaller batches.
maya: Action items I propose:
1) Pause v7 rollout. (done for canary, request prod hold) 
2) Re-run tokenizer A/B: run v7 model with v6 tokenizer in a small canary to isolate tokenizer vs binary. 
3) Force kernel override to attn_fast for seq<=1024 on canaries to test selector hypothesis. 
4) Add a KV-cache eviction gauge to tracing and correlate with batch sizes.

li: I'll run a synthetic workload with heavy prefix reuse to exercise kv and measure eviction with and without the override.
sam: Also let's capture per-request tokenization length distribution before and after tokenizer swap. If tokenizer expands tokens for certain Unicode sequences in v7, that'll explain the tail.
maya: Good. If we confirm allocator fragmentation is root cause we should consider changing model mmap flags or pre-touch memory to reduce fragmentation on model load.

li: Synthetic run shows tokenizer A/B: v7 tokenizer increases token counts by ~12% on our noisy corpus (emoji-heavy chat logs). That pushes many requests over 512->1024 boundary.
sam: So both things contributed: tokenizer shift increased seq-tail which exposed allocator+kernel selector fragility.
maya: Summary: tokenizer change moved distribution into region where kernel selection + allocator frag caused higher memory churn and evictions -> batching heuristics produced smaller batches -> overall p99 spike. Plan: revert tokenizer change in next patch, add selector guardrails, and improve allocator behavior on model load. I'll write a short postmortem and rollout checklist.

1795012345

mia: Quick question — hitting a few customer reports where our Python streaming client turns some API errors into a generic SDK exception and loses the request_id. Behavior looks different if the upstream returns a 502 vs a 4xx with JSON body. Anyone seen this? 

alex: Can you paste a minimal repro or the log lines? Is this during connect or mid-stream? :thinking:

mia: Mid-stream. Customer calls chat.stream() -> after ~3s the connection drops. Our client raises SDKError('service error') with no inner code and no request id. Runtime logs show the upstream returned a JSON error + header: `X-Request-Id: r-12345abc`.

sam: We had a similar case last month — the runtime surfaces error payload in the HTTP body but the SDK only parses headers for request ids on non-stream endpoints. Streaming path uses a framed transport and we swallow the body when framing fails.

leah: Repro logs from customer (sanitized):
```
[2026-02-18T14:22:05Z] client: start stream chat.stream() req=client-867
[2026-02-18T14:22:08Z] upstream: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-Id: r-12345abc

{"error": {"message": "kv cache mismatch", "code": "KV_CACHE_MISMATCH", "retryable": false}}
[2026-02-18T14:22:08Z] client: raised SDKError('service error') req=client-867
```

leah: Looks like SDK maps anything non-200 during stream to SDKError without extracting `error.code` or X-Request-Id.

alex: Yeah — we should map specific codes -> exceptions (e.g., KVCacheMismatchError, TransientBackendError) and always attach request_id in the exception metadata. That makes debugging and support 100x easier.

mia: Proposed change: in stream error handler, try to parse framing/body as JSON; if JSON has error.code -> pick exception class; also grab X-Request-Id from headers (fallback to body.request_id) and include it on exception and logs. Also add a debug flag to print full raw response.

sam: Two caveats: 1) streaming transport sometimes yields partial frames, so JSON parse can fail — make it defensive. 2) Retries for streaming are tricky: if error is non-idempotent (e.g., KV_CACHE_MISMATCH), do NOT retry; if transient (502 without code), allow reconnect + resume only if resume token exists.

alex: Agree. Suggested pseudo for Python client error mapping: 
```
try:
    body = await read_error_body_safe(resp)  # returns None or dict
except Exception:
    body = None
code = (body or {}).get('error', {}).get('code') if isinstance(body, dict) else None
request_id = resp.headers.get('X-Request-Id') or (body or {}).get('request_id')
if code == 'KV_CACHE_MISMATCH':
    raise KVCacheMismatchError('kv cache mismatch', request_id=request_id)
elif resp.status >= 500:
    raise TransientBackendError('5xx', request_id=request_id)
else:
    raise SDKError('service error', request_id=request_id)
```

leah: Could `read_error_body_safe` limit to first 8k bytes and catch JSONDecodeError? We don't want to block streaming reads.

alex: Yes — also make sure we don't allocate huge buffers. Limit and return None if not parseable. Add unit tests simulating partial frames.

mia: For support: can we update the default debug log format to include request_id if present? E.g. "[ts] client: error ... req_id=r-12345abc code=KV_CACHE_MISMATCH". That will make triage much simpler.

sam: Agreed. For retries: add a clear predicate function `should_retry_stream(error, idempotent)` that checks error type + headers (Retry-After, Retryable in body). If resume token present and idempotent, allow reconnect and resume; otherwise bubble.

ci-bot: ci/build-status: small-patch tests passed (python, node) — 12/12

alex: I'll draft a small PR to implement mapping + request_id propagation and a feature flag `SDK_STREAM_DEBUG=true` for verbose raw-response dumps. Will add unit tests for: header-only request id, body-only request id, partial JSON body.

leah: Awesome. Can you also add a short blurb in SDK docs under "Error handling" showing the new exception classes and example of catching KVCacheMismatchError vs generic SDKError?

mia: Thanks — once PR is up I'll share with the customer (and include the request_id in support ticket). If anyone has objections to the plan, speak now. Otherwise assign to alex. :+1:

sam: No objections. Thanks!

alex: Assigned and starting now. I'll ping here when draft is ready for review.

- Alex R.: follow-up: collect full KV cache eviction trace and config snapshot -> ticket INF-4356
- Miguel P.: investigate autoscaler cooldown logic and add unit tests -> ticket INF-4357
- Jamie L.: coordinate postmortem and write initial summary -> ticket OPS-9001

Jamie L.: postmortem scope: timeline, root cause (cache eviction + scale race), why alerting didn't page earlier, and remediation plan.
Alex R.: Pager tuning notes: the alert threshold for svc_inference_api.errors should not page at 1% transient spikes. Proposal: only page if errors >= 3% sustained for 10m OR if error burn rate crosses 5% in 5m AND p95 latency > 1.5s. Also add a suppression window for autoscaler-driven flux.

title: devex
body:
devex

Alex K: Pushing a tiny starter that wires Redwood SDK + Next.js + LangChain types. Needs review — telemetry + auth/retry weirdness in CI.
Maria P: Nice. Can you repro the auth retry locally? Which SDK version?
Alex K: Using @redwood/inference-js 0.9.1-beta. On CI we see repeated 401 then backoff hits and opaque request body on retry. Logs show 'auth-middleware: token missing' after a 200 sometimes.
Jin: That sounds like token rotation race. Are you using the browser edge runtime or serverless API route?
Alex K: SSR API route (app/api/generate/route.ts). Token fetched from env via server components. Repro steps: 1) start dev server 2) run playwright tests 3) hit /api/generate concurrently 4) sometimes one request returns empty string and subsequent retry 401.
Tyler (devex): Could be our fetch wrapper not cloning Request properly before streaming. Alex, can you paste the route code? Also include headers you're forwarding.
Alex K: ```ts
export async function POST(req){
  const body = await req.json();
  const resp = await inference.generate({model:'gpt-redwood-1', input: body.prompt});
  return NextResponse.json({out: await resp.text()});
}
```
Maria P: Hmm looks like you're calling resp.text() — with streaming that might consume body and break retries.
Alex K: Good catch. I switched to readableStream piping — but then types broke in LangChain connector.
Jin: SDK parity issue: JS runtimes expect Response-like streaming; our LangChain helper expects a string. We should add a typed stream adapter in the sample app.
devex-bot: Reminder: file a small PR to devex/starter-templates with failing test + fix so CI tracks it :memo:
Alex K: Created PR 2345 with failing test and fix. Also added telemetry events: 'starter.eval.run' typed with {scenario:'playwright-concurrency', tokens: 'int'} — realized we didn't strongly type tokens in telemetry schema.
Tyler (devex): Let's avoid ad-hoc telemetry shapes. Devex, can we add a validator in SDK that enforces telemetry schema at compile time (TS) and runtime for JS? @Maria can you pair on this?
Maria P: Yep. I'll scope a small change to add zod schemas for telemetry events in the SDK and update starter to import them.
Jin: Also adding a LangChain adapter in the sample that exposes .stream() vs .text() and a small unit test.
Alex K: Thanks — tests passing locally. Deploying a canary of the starter to staging to validate CI flakes.

title: devex
body:
devex

Alex M: Heads-up — onboarding sample app is flapping on the rerank endpoint when the batching helper + auth retry logic both run. Getting vector-dim mismatch 400s.
Priya K: repro steps?
Alex M: Quick notes: we batch 6-8 queries in Node sampleapp, a transient auth retry re-queues the request and we sometimes end up with mixed vector lengths in the payload (1536 vs 1535). API responds with `400 embedding.length mismatch`.
Samir P: hmm classic TypedArray.view gotcha. Node's helper uses subarray to avoid copies; Python client builds fresh lists so it's fine. Which SDK version?
Alex M: Node SDK v0.9.2 in sampleapp. Tests were running Python 0.8.x. I can paste snippet:
```
// batch helper
const batches = batchify(vecs, 8)
await Promise.all(batches.map(b => send(b)))
// send requeues original req on retry
```
Alex M: On retry we re-use the same underlying ArrayBuffer view; later mutations shorten one vector and the requeued request carries the short slice.
Priya K: can you capture a minimal repro? if it's subarray we should either copy or ensure the retry path clones body.
Ethan L: opened PR #3421 — quick patch copies vectors before enqueue, and adds an integration that simulates auth 401->retry. CI shows one flaky test failing locally though.
Samir P: long-term fix: SDK retry middleware should deep-copy request bodies (or mark them immutable). Prefer to fix middleware so all helpers benefit.
Alex M: temporary mitigation: set env BATCH_RETRY_STRATEGY=single-send for the sampleapp to avoid requeueing batches. Not ideal for latency.
Priya K: API side: can we improve error text to include batch index? Current `embedding.length mismatch` is terse. Something like: `vector dims differ in payload (expected 1536 got 1535) at batch index 2` would help debugging.
Platform APIs: Noted. We can add batch-index to the error envelope in the next minor release, but need SDKs updated to read the new field gracefully.
Ethan L: after copying buffers in node helper, I hit a different issue — response envelope changed when rerank deduping kicks in (we return items out-of-order). Adding tests for stable ordering in PR.
Priya K: follow-up action items: 1) merge copy-in-enqueue fix (short term), 2) update retry middleware to deep-clone bodies (medium), 3) API error text change (coord w/ Platform APIs), 4) add node+py parity E2E for batching+retry.
CI Bot: PR #3421 pipeline passed :white_check_mark:
Alex M: deployed hotfix on staging — onboarding run passed end-to-end :tada:
Priya K: will open a tracking ticket for SDK lint rule to forbid subarray reuse for request bodies.
Samir P: also add a small note in the DX onboarding guide: "avoid reusing TypedArray.subarray for request bodies; clone if you'll retry".
Alex M: thanks all — leaving issue link in the sampleapp README.

maria.s: Heads-up — I hit a weird edge where the Ruby SDK doesn't retry a request when the token refresh happens mid-stream. JS client silently retries. Anyone else seen this?

aj: Hmm, can you paste the call pattern? stream vs non-stream matters for our current retry hooks.

maria.s: It's non-stream text generation. Basic flow: `client = Redwood::Client.new(api_key: ENV['REDWOOD_KEY'])` then long-running process rotates keys via refresh hook. After refresh the next request raises `AuthError` instead of retrying.

sam.k: That sounds like the retry middleware isn't wired after `auth_refresh` step for ruby. We had a similar fix in JS that wraps auth with `retryable()` so it replays.

maria.s: I attempted a quick patch in my branch to re-insert `RetryMiddleware` after `AuthMiddleware` and added a small unit test. CI failed on flakey net spec though.

ci-bot: build #4521 failed — spec: `spec/clients/retry_spec.rb:42` — timeout 120s. Logs: `expected to receive :sleep but received 0 calls`

oliver_p: @maria.s can you share the PR link? I'll take a look at the middleware stack order. Also we should add an integration test that simulates token rotate mid-request.

maria.s: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ruby-client/pull/128 — the change is tiny but I wasn't sure about the global config effects. Test harness uses `WebMock` so I'm stubbing a 401 then 200. CI flake might be timing where backoff sleeps are skipped in test env.

kyla: For parity notes: JS has `retry.onAuthFailure` behavior because browser tokens rotate a lot. We should document that in CHANGELOG and add a small helper `with_retry_on_auth` for common flows. Also agree on making the middleware order explicit in README.

aj: Quick workaround for now: add this to your app until PR lands — `client.middleware.insert_after(:auth, Redwood::Middleware::Retry)` — that should be safe.

sam.k: I'll queue a follow-up PR after merge that adds the integration test and a tiny helper method. We should also ensure the `client` factory in tests exposes middleware for deterministic ordering.

maria.s: Thanks — will update PR with test change and add a short note in the changelog. small ask: can someone run the failing spec locally? My mac timing is weird.

oliver_p: I'll run it on Linux CI image and report back. :eyes:

ci-bot: triggered rebuild #4522 by oliver_p

ci-bot: build #4522 passed — all specs green :white_check_mark:

maria.s: awesome, thanks everyone! I'll squash and request merge. :pray:

eli_oncall: mitigation plan: 1) enable bypass-read fallback to persistent store for affected prefixes 2) reduce read fanout threshold 3) temporarily scale up prefix-shard replicas 4) if needed, rollback sidecar image. I'm going to run the bypass.

anya_sre: can we force resync for shard 7 rather than full rollback? a resync would repair the on-disk index without impacting other shards.
matt_eng: yes, we have a repair job: `kv-tool resync --shard 7 --mode=incremental` will attempt to rebuild prefix index from SSTs. cost: brief increased IO, should be safe behind bypass. scheduling now.
eli_oncall: kicking resync at 10:02Z. will keep bypass on.
(ops-bot automated): Pager escalated to SRE layer for 30s: @anya_sre paged.

matt_eng: follow-ups: 1) patch sidecar to validate format compatibility on startup and refuse to join cluster (fail fast) 2) add preflight check during rollouts to validate checksum parity 3) improve observability: histogram for checksum-validator latencies and mismatch tags 4) run a sweep job to revalidate all shard checksums proactively. owners: matt_eng + jun_ml.
