title: devex
body:
devex

sam-devx: Heads up — we got a bug report: onboarding sample fails after @redwood/sdk@6.2.0 when deployed to Bun and Cloudflare Workers. Error in runtime: `The requested module \"@redwood/sdk\" does not provide an export named \"default\"`

noah-runtime: That usually means our ESM entry doesn't supply a default export while consumers still do `import SDK from '@redwood/sdk'`. Which exports map shipped in 6.2.0?

sam-devx: We hardened the exports map and added conditional types. Snippet: "exports": { ".": { "import": "./esm/index.mjs", "require": "./cjs/index.cjs", "types": "./esm/index.d.ts" }, "./package.json": "./package.json" }

ivy-eng: Two separate problems: 1) some sample code still uses default imports; 2) a few bundlers / edge loaders (Bun, Workers) don't fall back to CJS so they hit the ESM path, which currently only has named exports. 

ben-qa: Repro steps I used: clone onboarding-samples, `npm i @redwood/sdk@6.2.0`, run `bun dev` -> immediate default export error. Also ran `wrangler dev` with same result. Quick fix locally was changing imports to `import * as SDK from '@redwood/sdk'`, but that breaks call-site code expecting a callable default.

ivy-eng: For TypeScript, some setups fail to pick up the `types` conditional inside exports and show `Could not find a declaration file for module '@redwood/sdk'`. Adding a package-level "types": "esm/index.d.ts" usually fixes that for older TS resolvers.

noah-runtime: Proposal for a fast patch: add a tiny ESM compat shim that re-exports the factory as default: in esm/index.mjs add `export { createClient as default } from './client.js'`. Also add top-level "types": "esm/index.d.ts" to package.json to improve TS resolution.

sam-devx: Also noticed some onboarding samples import `@redwood/sdk/compat` and `@redwood/sdk/internal/logger` deep paths. We intentionally removed wildcard subpath exports. Users relying on internal exports are one cause of breakage — we should either restore a small explicit `./compat` subpath or update samples to avoid internal paths.

ben-qa: I'll add smoke tests to sample-apps CI that spin up Bun, Workers, and Node+esbuild and install the published package tarball to catch these kinds of regressions before release. Also will add `tsc --noEmit` against the installed package to validate types resolution.

ivy-eng: Long-term: add an export-map validator step in the publish pipeline to detect accidental wildcards pointing into internal/ dist-internal folders, and add a compatibility policy in the SDK README about default import vs named exports and a deprecation timeline.

pr-deps-bot: PR Draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1275 - patch adds ESM default shim, top-level types field, and an explicit `./compat` subpath that points to the previous convenience entry.

sam-devx: OK, once PR is green let's cut 6.2.1 and push a short migration note in the changelog and update onboarding samples to prefer `import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk'`. I'll message support with the temporary workaround (pin to 6.1.x or switch to named imports) and coordinate docs updates.

title: eng-runtime
body:
eng-runtime

alex.k: heads-up: observed a 2.8x latency spike on qwen2.5 serving at ~1am during the nightly load test. tracing shows kernel-selector choosing the fallback matmul for long seqlens > 1k.
maya: ack. which path is the selector taking? slow gemm or an emulated path? :eyes:
samuel: looks like the fallback is the 'dense_fallback' path we added for non-contiguous KV layouts. profiler shows heavy memcpy and no cublas calls.
alex.k: exact dump (sanitized):
```
PROFILE: qwen2p5 / batch=12 / seq=1100
kernel_selector: chosen_kernel=matmul_fallback
memcpy_bytes=3.2GB
cublas_calls=0
cpu_ms=120.4
gpu_ms=118.7
```
maya: interesting — this flare started after the autokernel heuristics patch that prefers packed kernels when kv_stride==1. maybe some tokenizers produce non-packed KV?
samuel: i ran a quick trace. multilang tokenization for zh + en mixes produces variable token lengths: some batches end up with per-sample seqs [64, 1024, 1100, 400]. our continuous-batching sampler currently pads to max per-batch which creates very sparse KV layout for some heads.
jia: could be the head/kv-dim reduction in the last model rollout too — we shipped a patch that reduces KV projection to 64 for some fused heads to save memory. if kernel expects head_dim % 32 == 0, it falls back.
alex.k: good point. hypothesis: combined effect of mixed-long sequences + kv_dim not aligned -> kernel selector rejects fast path -> memcpy-heavy fallback. impact visible only for qwen2.5 because of its head packing layout.
maya: propose a quick mitigation: change batching heuristic to group by rounded seq buckets (like 0-128,129-512,513-1024,1025+) for continuous sampler so we avoid mixing 1k sequences with 64s in same micro-batches. also try relaxing kernel alignment check to accept KV stride 16 for aligned GPUs.
samuel: i can prototype sampler buckets tonight and run the nightly job. also will add a kernel-selector metric to logs so we can see chosen_kernel per request.
jia: for repro, here's a minimized repro command:
```bash
make bench-model MODEL=qwen2p5 BATCHER=continuous SEQ_DISTR="mix:zh,en" BATCH=12 ITER=100
```
perf-bot: scheduled bench run 2351234578 -> /artifacts/bench-2351234578 (will post summary when done)
samuel: quick note from the first run: with sampler buckets enabled, tail latency drops from p99=380ms -> 130ms. but throughput for some shapes dipped ~6%.
maya: that's acceptable as a hotfix. long term we should: 1) make kernel-selector aware of kv_stride alignment and offer a tuned kernel for kv_dim==64 2) improve quantization/packing detection in the model loader so we don't lose SIMD advantages 3) add per-route policy to avoid mixing languages aggressively.
ajex.k: (typo) alex.k: assigning follow-ups: samuel -> prototype sampler patch & logs, jia -> validate kv-projection packing on model release, maya -> spec change for kernel-selector tests. please post PR numbers here.
samuel: will open draft PR 2353 with sampler grouping + opt-in flag. will attach before/after traces.
jia: i'll audit the model artifacts and post findings by EOD. if we see head_dim mismatch we may need a small model shim to pad KV projections to 128.
maya: thanks. if anyone hits this live, enable the route-level fallback to previous model variant for now. :thumbsup:
alex.k: closing loop later after perf-bot summary. thanks team!

josh: pool=dedicated-us-west-2-58, req samples: r_8342, r_8343, r_8349. They switched to longer prompts yesterday (median tokens ~450 -> 900). No model swap. Also getting many short char-count requests from another tenant at same time.
talia: Quick hypothesis: continuous-batcher is fragmenting windows due to mixed short and long sequences. If tiny 1-5 token requests interleave, packer may create many small microbatches and prefill thrash.
sara: Can you share recent metrics? avg_batch_size, median_tokens_per_batch, scheduler quantum, and queue_depth over 30m window?
josh: pasted metrics snapshot:
```
avg_batch_size=3.1
median_tokens_per_request=42
median_tokens_per_batch=96
continuous_batcher.queue_depth=1200
pack_fails=0.02
prefill_rate_spike=2.8x
autoscale_actions=scale_down @ 02:58, scale_up @ 03:12
```
sara: Interesting — avg_batch_size very low for this pool (3.1). median_tokens_per_request seems dominated by short requests even though customer has long prompts. That explains token-inefficient packing. Also saw autoscale bouncing during the window — quick scale down then scale up while queue depth high which might cause throughput drop.
talia: Two vectors: (1) packing skew -> increase wasted per-token overhead; (2) autoscale cooldown too aggressive so nodes throttle while backpressure piles up. Both amplify throughput loss.
sara: Repro steps I'd run:
- Replay mixed traffic locally with same distribution (50% 1-8 token, 25% 40-100 tokens, 25% 800-1200 tokens) at target qps.
- Observe continuous_batcher stats: batch_fill_time, pack_efficiency, microbatch_count.
- Try changes: bump `continuous_batcher.max_batch_tokens` to 2048, set `target_batch_tokens`=1024, enable token-aware packer with `fairness_window_ms`=50. Also increase autoscale cooldown to 300s.
josh: Can you paste the config snippet we should try? I can push a canary to the customer's pool.
sara: Snippet:
```
continuous_batcher:
  max_batch_tokens: 2048
  target_batch_tokens: 1024
  token_aware_packer: true
  fairness_window_ms: 50
scheduler:
  quantum_ms: 6
  prefill_score_weight: 0.6
autoscale:
  scale_down_cooldown_s: 300
  scale_up_cooldown_s: 90
```
talia: Also recommend enabling tenant isolation throttle for suspected noisy tenant (BrightCart reported other noisy tenant with lots of 1-token health-checks). If we can't isolate, add a temporary rate-limit on 1-5 token requests at the pool level.
bruce: Customer-success note: BrightCart is losing critical revenue. They want ETA for mitigation and whether we can pin a model variant while we tune. They requested a short-term fix today.
sara: Plan: I'll run a canary with the config changes on a subset of nodes in pool at 03:50 UTC, monitor avg_batch_size, tokens/sec, tail latency. If good, roll to rest of pool. I'll also coordinate with infra to hold aggressive scale-downs during canary.

talia: If the canary doesn't help, next step: instrument per-tenant queueing metrics and consider soft tenant isolation or moving heavy token users to a dedicated pool.

title: eng-sre
body:
eng-sre

Nate: heads up — multiple customers reporting elevated p99 for /v1/generate from eu-west-1 starting ~2026-03-15T10:38Z. Support thread: https://acme.example/complaints/4532. p95 stable but p99 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.7s. Can SRE triage?

Elaine: on it. which backend pool are these hitting (hosted vs dedicated)? any recent deploys?

Nate: most are hosted. last deploy was a low-risk routing tweak ~09:50Z by infra to propagate new anycast config. No service code changes.

Jin: pulling traces now. I see a cluster of high-latency requests with repeated TLS handshake attempts and 502-ish early disconnects from edge -> origin. Sample curl from haproxy logs (client IP redacted):

```
curl -s -w '\ntime_namelookup: %{time_namelookup}\ntime_connect: %{time_connect}\ntime_appconnect: %{time_appconnect}\ntime_pretransfer: %{time_pretransfer}\ntime_starttransfer: %{time_starttransfer}\n' -o /dev/null 'https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate'
# output (representative):
# time_namelookup: 0.012
# time_connect: 0.080
# time_appconnect: 0.950
# time_starttransfer: 1.712
```

Jin: notice time_appconnect ~950ms on p99. tcpdump at edge shows full TLS handshake happening repeatedly rather than resumed sessions: TCP 3-way fine but TLS full handshake on new server behind LB.

Elaine: could that be cache/KV eviction of session tickets due to anycast egress bouncing? If requests get routed to different POPs mid-session, session resumption would fail resulting in full handshakes.

Maria: I checked our route telemetry — around 10:35Z there was a small BGP flap reported by one upstream provider in eu-west region, influencing egress-priority for ~3m. Probably caused some flow pinning to shift across AZs/POPs.

Kevin: DNS looked normal, but I saw short TTL on the CDN map: CNAME chain resolves to regional anycast LB; TTL was 30s. If the upstream adjusted routes, clients re-resolve quickly and could move between POPs.

Nate: support noted that affected customers are mostly in Ireland/northwest EU. Some reported intermittent MJ refreshes during single request flows. They hit us with single-shot requests (no streaming).

Jin: grabbed a traceroute+tlsdebug from an affected customer:

```
traceroute to api.redwood.example (35.201.xx.xx), 30 hops max
 1  10.0.0.1 ...
 5  34.120.xx.xx  (local-pop-1)
 8  34.121.xx.xx  (local-pop-2) <-- path flips
\nOpenSSL s_client -connect 34.121.xx.xx:443 -servername api.redwood.example -msg -tlsextdebug
  -> TLS1.3, ClientHello
  -> ServerHello (new session) ... no ticket resumption
```

Jin: the key is the path flip between hop 5 and hop 8 inside the same region — likely the anycast edge decided to forward to different egress nodes mid-flow.

Elaine: mitigation plan: 1) force local-egress policy for eu-west for customer-tiered hosts (route at control plane); 2) temporarily raise session ticket cache and session-resumption TTL on the edge (if possible) to reduce full-handshakes; 3) bump DNS fallback TTL to 120s to reduce rapid re-resolve churn while upstream stabilizes. Which is feasible quickly?

Kevin: I can push a control-plane flag to prefer same-POP egress for sessions older than 30s. That is low-risk. Deploy-bot, can we toggle `force_local_egress: true` for namespace eu-west-1 (hosted) as a canary to 10%?

deploy-bot: @Kevin requested change `force_local_egress=true` for scope eu-west-1. Scheduling canary rollout to 10% of hosted traffic. No infra restart required.

ops-bot: Canary rollout started at 10:56Z. Targeting small subset of customer traffic. Monitoring p99 on /v1/generate.

Maria: also opened support ticket with upstream provider (AS12345) referencing BGP flap and asked for routing history + ROA checks. Ticket #UP-789.

Elaine: I pushed a config change to edge: increase session ticket cache from 2k -> 8k and session-ticket TTL from 300s -> 1200s. That'll make resumption more likely across short egress shifts. No restart.

Jin: after canary started (10% at 10:56Z) we see immediate improvement for that cohort: p99 dropped from ~1.7s -> ~260ms. Rolling to 100% now?

Kevin: I'm going to expand to 50% then 100% if no regressions in 5m.

deploy-bot: Canary expanded to 50% at 10:59Z.

ops-bot: 50% cohort p99 = 280ms, overall p99 trending down to 420ms at 11:01Z.

Nate: customer outreach: told Acme that we're actively rolling a mitigation and will follow up with RCA. They asked for ETA — told them ~30m for full roll.

Kevin: expanded to 100% at 11:02Z. Monitoring.

deploy-bot: Full rollout completed at 11:03Z. No errors reported during rollout.

Jin: post-roll metrics (11:05Z): regional p99 back to ~210-320ms depending on burst windows. Connection-level metrics show resumption rate increased from 12% -> 86%.

Elaine: next steps: 1) keep edge ticket TTL increased until upstream confirms BGP stability; 2) ask infra to evaluate anycast egress pinning improvements (sticky-eid or 5-tuple hashing) to avoid mid-flow egress flips; 3) coordinate with network vendor for BGP dampening thresholds; 4) write incident summary and schedule a 1hr postmortem.

Maria: I'll take vendor coordination and open a tracking doc.

Nate: I'll follow up with customers and draft the incident note. Please add any logs/snippets you want included to the incident doc: https://internal.redwood/incident/1855550000

Kevin: FYI — no service code change required. This was routing/edge behavior + ticket resumption guardrails.

support-bot: Created incident 1855550000 in incidents channel and alerted oncall.

Elaine: marking this thread resolved from SRE side for now. If anyone sees p99 creep again, re-open. :white_check_mark:

title: architecture
body:
architecture

maya: Quick follow-up from the canary yesterday — we saw in-flight streaming requests get dropped when the edge binary rolled. Not a total outage, but a bunch of clients saw truncated streams. I want to sketch a couple approaches and get opinions.

maya: Problem summary: when we cut traffic to a new edge version, the old proxy has N inflight streaming sessions with KV-prefix state in memory. New proxy starts with different memory layout and can't continue. We need a handoff so the new proxy can resume or the old proxy can proxy-through until sessions finish.

alex: Can you paste the minimal repro logs?

maya: Sure — here's the edge log around the cutover:```
[edge-1] 2025-06-12T15:02:11Z INFO accept stream session id=anchor:abc123 seq=240
[edge-1] 2025-06-12T15:02:18Z INFO draining sessions 240->0 canary=true
[edge-2] 2025-06-12T15:02:19Z WARN unknown resume token id=abc123
[client] 2025-06-12T15:02:20Z ERROR stream truncated by server
```

maya: Proposal A (stateful proxy handoff): when canary starts, new proxy sends an RPC to old proxy `/handoff/anchor/{id}` to request a small checkpoint (KV pointers + last-seq). Old returns checkpoint blob and keeps proxying until acks. New rehydrates and continues stream. Pros: low client-visible impact. Cons: requires direct proxy-proxy RPCs, auth, and lifetime/GC semantics.

maya: Proposal B (stateless resume token): include an opaque `x-rdwn-resume` header on the initial response that encodes enough to reconstruct state from a shared store (control-plane checkpoint s3) e.g.:
```
x-rdwn-resume: v1;anchor=abc123;seq=240;store=s3://rdwn-checks/anchor/abc123
```
New proxy fetches checkpoint from store and resumes. Pros: simpler proxies, no proxied RPCs. Cons: higher resume latency (S3 fetch), needs durable store and GC, possible stale checkpoints if not flushed.

sam: Leaning toward B for simplicity and SRE ownership of GC. But we need a small fast-path for low-latency resumption (cold fetch is rough for short-lived streams).

alex: What about hybrid: keep a short-lived in-memory lease on the old proxy for T seconds and write the same checkpoint to the store. New proxy asks old proxy first (fast in-cluster RPC), falls back to store if old doesn't have lease. That minimizes S3 hits while avoiding permanent proxy-proxy coupling.

dari: Security + cross-region concern: if we allow proxy-proxy RPCs we must authenticate properly and respect tenant isolation (no tenant X leaking checkpoint to Y via misroute). How do we scope the lease?

maya: Good call — leases should include tenant-id and a MAC. Example token: `resume_token = HMAC(k_tenant, anchor|seq|expiry)` and we check tenant match on handoff RPC.

maya: For hybrid we also need atomicity: new edge must not claim resume and then fail to finish, leaving old proxy stopped. I sketched a tiny two-phase handshake:
1) new -> old: `handoff?anchor=abc123&claim=true` (old replies `ok` and keeps streaming until commit)
2) new rehydrates state and responds `commit=true` to control plane
3) control plane instructs old to gracefully drain that session after commit OR to continue proxying on failure.

alex: That control-plane step is important. We don't want dangling half-claimed sessions. Could we use existing runtime-leases service (eng-infra) to represent these anchors?

infra-bot: runtime-lease-service currently supports 30s leases with renewal APIs. Suggest bumping to 2m for handoff use-case.

sam: Tradeoffs:
- Complexity: hybrid adds proxy-proxy + control-plane + store path.
- Latency: stateless store path adds ~50-150ms depending on region.
- Reliability: stateful handoff reduces client retries but increases surface area for bugs during deployments.

dari: Also consider retries: if client library retries the same request on a new connection, resume token must be idempotent for truncated responses. We should define whether resume semantics are strong (exact token sequence) or weak (best-effort continue from nearest checkpoint). I vote for strong sequence numbers to keep evals deterministic.

maya: Implementation notes:
- Minimal token format: `v1|tenant:abc|anchor:abc123|seq:240|lease:inst-42|sig:...`
- Small checkpoint payload should include KV-cache digest + last-output-chunk checksum so we can verify continuity.
- Metrics: `edge.handoff.attempt`, `edge.handoff.success`, `edge.handoff.fallback_to_store`, `edge.resume.latency_ms`

alex: One more operational thing — how does this interact with early cancel through trailer metadata? If client cancels after resume but before commit we shouldn't leak resources. Need clear cleanup paths.

maya: Agree. Plan: old proxy keeps a short GC window (e.g., 60s) after session unclaimed. Control-plane can trigger fast GC if commit observed.

sam: I'd add a fallback policy: if resume fails and we can't proxy-through, we return `HTTP 409 Stream-Interrupted; Retry-After: 1` so clients can backoff-and-retry without double-processing.

dari: Tests: canary harness should include orchestrated rollouts with synthetic long-lived streams and region failover. Also add a fuzzer for malformed resume tokens.

maya: Next steps I propose: write a small RFC doc with sequence diagrams and opt for hybrid approach (lease + store) for now. I'll open a PR with diagrams and a minimal token spec.

alex: Sounds good. @eng-infra can you check runtime-lease bump and whether we can add a small fast checkpoint store?

infra-bot: @eng-infra requested: bump runtime-lease default to 120s for edge-handoff trials. Ticket RDW-ops#482 created.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment (edge-v2) finished at 2025-06-12T15:10:02Z :white_check_mark:

maya: Thanks all — will draft RFC and post here for review. :shipit:

title: eng-oncall
body:
eng-oncall

incident-bot: INCIDENT DETECTED: cont-batching p99 spike in us-west-2 (service: inference-api). p99 3.2s -> 9.8s, streaming stalls observed. auto-page oncall.

oncall-alex: ACK — I'm on it. paging SRE and runtime.

sre-maya: seeing big tail at cont-batch path. p95 ~ 1.1s, p99 ~ 9.8s, error rate ~0.4% (timeouts). Grafana: https://graf.internal/redwood/d/xyz/cont-batch?orgId=1

sre-maya: top signal: batch sizes jumped, mixed sequence-length queues starved short requests, packer waiting -> KV cache churn increases. KV eviction spikes in logs.

eng-ciro: oncall, can you grab `packer_queue_depth` and `avg_batch_size` from the affected hosts? I suspect scheduling fairness regression from last deploy.

oncall-alex: pulling metrics now, hitting node group "usw2-contbatch-01". avg_batch_size across pods: 48 -> spikes to 62 on 3 hosts. packer_queue_depth high: 1200 -> 3000.

sre-maya: that matches. Streaming calls are getting starved waiting for large packs to fill. tails amplify. We should do a live mitigation: reduce max_batch_size and enable shed for long-payload requests.

prod-jordan: how's customer impact? any customers hit timeouts?

support-liz: CS ticket stream shows a few customer errors for streaming timeouts (alpha-startup-prod). No broad outage yet. Escalating to CS on duty.

oncall-alex: immediate mitigations I'll do in this order: 1) reduce `max_batch_size` from 64 -> 32 on usw2-contbatch autoscaler group 2) flip `streaming_hedge_on_miss` to true 3) apply per-tenant soft-rate-limit to heavy clients.

eng-ciro: copy. I'll roll a quick config patch to the packer agent and greedy-scheduler. Patch snippet:
```yaml
# rollout: quick config
packer:
  max_batch_size: 32
  schedule_policy: fairness_v2
streaming:
  hedge_on_miss: true
  hedge_delay_ms: 60
```

eng-ciro: executing patch via `kubectl -n inference set env deploy/cont-packer --from-file=config.yaml` on group usw2-contbatch-01.

oncall-alex: running the patch now. Will post when applied to all pods.

sre-maya: also increase kv-cache capacity slightly to avoid eviction storms short-term: set `kv_cache_max_entries=2M` on those hosts. Might need restart of packer process if cache resize not hot.

eng-ciro: applied max_batch_size=32 to 5/7 pods, remaining 2 pulling image now (rolling).

oncall-alex: 7/7 pods updated. Observability: avg_batch_size moving down, packer_queue_depth dropping.

sre-maya: Metrics after change: p99 down from 9.8s -> 2.6s within 90s. p95 stable ~1.0s. streaming stall alerts silenced.

prod-jordan: good — any residual customer impact windows?

support-liz: ticket updates: customers seeing recovered streams, no new errors in past 10m. I will still send a proactive note to impacted tenants per playbook.

oncall-alex: followup mitigations we should consider: - enforce sequence-length-aware batching (split large seqs to own packs) - improve scheduler fairness weights - add packer preempt for long-waiting short requests - add canary throttles for heavy tenants

eng-ciro: I captured logs for the suspected regression: `deploy/cont-batcher v2026.04.12` included a scheduler heuristic change to favor throughput (greedy) which increased pack fill preference. Raising a bug: https://github.internal/redwood/issue/INC-7432

sre-maya: going to run a diagnostic across pods: `curl http://localhost:8080/metrics | grep packer_queue` and `journalctl -u cont-packer -n 200` to look for KV eviction traces.

oncall-alex: diagnostics collected and attached to the ticket. Noted a few `kv_evict` spikes correlated with tail windows.

prod-jordan: action for customer comms: support-liz to send templated note; alert sales for any high-commit customers.

support-liz: will send notice in 15m with status + mitigation + ETA for permanent fix.

eng-ciro: suggested long-term fixes: - revert greedy fill heuristic or implement max-wait fairness - sequence-length bucketing in packer - adaptive batching caps per tenant workload profile - applier: improve kv-cache autoscaling per instance

oncall-alex: handoff to next oncall (tomorrow): apply to runbook: 1) check `p99` on cont-batch dashboard, 2) if >3s follow live mitigation checklist (reduce max_batch_size, enable hedge, increase kv cache), 3) escalate to eng-runtime if packer queue depth >1500 for >10m. Runbook link: https://docs.internal/redwood/runbooks/cont-batch-tail

sre-maya: leaving detailed notes in the incident ticket. root cause suspected: scheduler heuristic change + mixed-seq workload amplifying tail latency via packer starvation.

ops-bot: live-mitigation: actions applied: max_batch_size:32, hedge_on_miss:true, kv_cache_max_entries:2M. Incident marked "mitigated" — monitoring for 1 hour.

oncall-alex: closing loop — still assigned to eng-runtime to triage code change. If p99 creeps up again, we'll roll the scheduler revert. Good job team :thumbsup:

support-liz: CS notify sent. will follow up if customers need credits per SLA.

eng-ciro: will open a PR for scheduler revert + tests that simulate mixed-seqlen workload. PR link in ticket.

sre-maya: I'll convert this into a postmortem template and link tests to nightly perf runs.

oncall-alex: handing off to next oncall now. Thanks all.

incident-bot: Incident HANDLED (mitigated). Duration: ~22m. Paging cleared.

title: incidents
body:
incidents

incident-bot: P1 alert — GPU quota errors detected in gcp-europe-west1. Autoscaler failing to create nodes (API errors: QUOTA_EXCEEDED). Backlog growing on dedicated pools. Paging oncall SRE.

pagerduty-bot: Paging sara (oncall-sre) — escalation level: pager.

sara (oncall-sre): on it. pulling up dashboard. queue length looks bad for `dedicated-pool-eu1` — 14k pending requests, 99th latency spiking to 9.2s.

raj (infra): confirming GCP responses show "insufficient quota for requested resource 'NVIDIA_TESLA_A100'" on region europe-west1. Attempts to create 8x GPU instances blocked.

maria (eng-runtime): autoscaler retries are hitting the same error: `QuotaExceeded: Quota 'GPUS_ALL_REGIONS' or region-level GPU quota`. Logs: ```2026-03-14T08:00:12Z autoscaler: createInstance(instanceConfig) -> 403 QuotaExceeded```

kevin (support): any customer-visible errors? Support pages show increased 429s and stream timeouts. I'm pulling a list of active customers with >1% error rate.

olivia (product): heads-up — two enterprise customers (AcmePlay, FinBatch) on dedicated contracts in EU are in the impacted pool. Need ETA for mitigation to craft comms.

raj (infra): checked quotas in console: project-level GPU quota for europe-west1 is zero for A100. We have capacity in europe-west4 and us-central. Autoscaler policy is region-bound; failover is disabled by default.

sara (oncall-sre): immediate mitigation options? ideas: 1) failover traffic to a different region 2) spin up CPU-only fallback nodes (lower perf) 3) reduce concurrency and route low-priority requests to cached/model-small variants 4) request urgent quota increase from GCP (slow).

maria (eng-runtime): we can flip routing policy to allow cross-region fallback to europe-west4 for affected customers. That requires a config change and deploy, but we can enable a per-tenant fallback quickly via admin API.

raj (infra): manual quota bump is fastest if we have support contact; otherwise create temporary capacity by moving some dedicated pools to other regions. But moving pools requires redeploy and model warmup.

kevin (support): AcmePlay is seeing ~40% request failures in the last 15m. FinBatch is seeing degraded throughput but not full failures yet. I'll open a private support thread and start customer outreach.

olivia (product): prioritize AcmePlay comms. We need a short message: acknowledge, say we're mitigating and offer explicit timeframe.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-03-14-1788888000. Priority: P1. Triage lead: sara (oncall-sre).

sara (oncall-sre): I'll take triage lead. Raj/maria — pairing on mitigation: raj please attempt to enable cross-region fallback; maria please prepare runtime configuration to route affected tenants to europe-west4 model endpoints with warm cache.

raj (infra): starting: `gcloud compute project-info describe` -> verifying quotas across regions. Also opening support case with GCP: `gcloud alpha services quota-allocations` (support ticket 123456789). ETA from GCP unknown.

maria (eng-runtime): admin API snippet to patch routing: ```POST /admin/v1/tenants/{tenant}/fallbacks {"primary_region":"europe-west1","fallback_regions":["europe-west4"]}``` I'll stage for AcmePlay first.

deploy-bot: Roll request queued: route-change for tenant AcmePlay. CI checks passed. Need explicit approval to apply to production.

raj (infra): quick check — europe-west4 has 120 A100 quota available in project. We can route some traffic there.

sara (oncall-sre): maria — go ahead with AcmePlay. raj — prepare routing and update DNS/edge rules if needed. I'll monitor queues and latency.

maria (eng-runtime): applying routing for AcmePlay now. ```PATCH /admin/v1/tenants/AcmePlay/fallbacks -> 202 Accepted```

kevin (support): AcmePlay reporting immediate drop in failures after ~90s. I'll update the customer.

olivia (product): Excellent. What's the plan for FinBatch?

raj (infra): FinBatch shares the same pool but lower traffic. We'll roll them over next; need to warm models. I'll schedule in 5m windows to avoid cache thundering.

maria (eng-runtime): rolling FinBatch now -> warm-up requests to europe-west4 to populate KV caches. Script: ```for i in {1..50}; do curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" https://eu4-runtime.redwood/api/v1/warm?model=gpt-small; done```

incident-bot: Note: autoscaler still failing to create new nodes in europe-west1 due to quota errors. No progress on quota increases from GCP support yet.

sara (oncall-sre): current delta: pending queue reduced from 14k to 3.1k after AcmePlay and partial FinBatch failover. 99th latency down to 2.1s for affected tenants. Good.

raj (infra): as a medium-term mitigation, we should enable region fallback in autoscaler policy and add an alert to warn if region quota is below threshold. I'll file infra ticket.

olivia (product): action items for comms: (1) notify AcmePlay & FinBatch of mitigation and follow-up (kevin) (2) public status update for EU customers if we see further impact (olivia) (3) timeline once GCP confirms quota request (sara/raj).

kevin (support): customer messages sent to AcmePlay (private), FinBatch updated. Both asked to accept cross-region routing; AcmePlay accepted, FinBatch opted for delayed failover — scheduling now.

maria (eng-runtime): FYI — fallback to europe-west4 increased cost for those tenants ~2.2x token cost due to egress and different instance pricing. We should flag billing/contract implications for finance/prod.

raj (infra): GCP support replied: case 123456789 in progress, but immediate quota increase not possible without sales support; they suggested filing a quota request which may take hours. I'll escalate through account manager.

sara (oncall-sre): handoff: my oncall window ends in 20m. I'll do a warm handoff to dan (next-sre). Dan, summary: P1 quota-exhaustion in europe-west1 caused autoscaler stall. Partial mitigation: per-tenant cross-region failover to europe-west4 applied for AcmePlay and in progress for FinBatch. Queues reduced from 14k -> 3.1k. GCP ticket open (123456789). Ongoing: monitor queue, complete FinBatch roll, and coordinate with raj on quota escalation.

sara (oncall-sre): tagging dan: @dan (oncall-sre) please acknowledge.

pagerduty-bot: Alert handoff — declaring new assignee: dan (oncall-sre).

dan (oncall-sre): acknowledged. Taking over. I'll stay on this until quotas resolved and backlog below 200.

kevin (support): customers acknowledged. AcmePlay says they're ok with cross-region but asked for a postmortem and SLA credit if prolonged. FinBatch wants confirmation when traffic moves fully.

maria (eng-runtime): long-term: propose setting autoscaler policy to allow regional fallback and add a 'soft-threshold' so we pre-warm other regions when queue > X. I'll open RFC.

raj (infra): quick follow-up actions I'm taking: 1) escalate quota with account manager 2) open infra ticket to add fallback to autoscaler 3) add monitoring for regional GPU quota percentage.

dan (oncall-sre): monitoring: dashboards pinned, alert routing adjusted to call infra on the next quota regression. I'll keep updates here.

incident-bot: Incident update logged (INC-2026-03-14-1788888000). Status: stabilizing.

olivia (product): thanks team. After this stabilizes we need a short internal postmortem and action list: autoscaler fallback, billing impact analysis, and improved customer comms playbook.

dan (oncall-sre): closing loop: pending queue now 420, 99th latency 1.2s for failover tenants. Leaving incident channel open until quota confirmed.

incident-bot: Incident marked as "mitigated" pending root-cause and quota confirmation.

sara (oncall-sre): adding notes for postmortem: root cause: region GPU quota exhausted and autoscaler lacked cross-region fallback; contributing factors: no low-priority routing, no quota pre-warn alerts, and automatic retries caused extra API calls.

raj (infra): created infra task INFRA-5372 for autoscaler-region-fallback and monitoring.

maria (eng-runtime): creating runtime follow-up: RUNTIME-2441 to add per-tenant failover toggle and warm-up orchestration.

olivia (product): I'll schedule the postmortem meeting tomorrow. Thanks all. :heart:

title: sales
body:
sales

jordan-sales: Heads up — prospect (FinSight) wants a Dedicated commit proposal. Asking for 6mo term, 32x A10G baseline with autoscale to 48x for bursts. They also want a 99.9% latency SLO and dedicated private network peering. Need deal desk guidance on burst pricing and SLA implications.

sam-se: Thanks. Quick POC note: they want to run a 3-week eval, ~100k tokens/day. We'll need a private VPC and KV cache enabled. No model fine-tuning initially.

leah-deals: Got it. Pricing questions: are we treating burst as "temporary capacity" billable at premium rate, or amortized into commit? Also need ARR/commit value to calculate discount band.

jordan-sales: They plan to commit $180k over 6 months (monthly invoice). Looking for ~15-25% discount range depending on autoscale terms.

sam-se: Technical constraints: autoscale adds pre-warm overhead. For A10G pools we need 15-45m warmup for additional nodes depending on model size. That affects effective SLA during large spikes.

rita-fin: Preliminary math: baseline unit price for A10G we normally quote $4.80 / GPU-hr. Burst rate historically 1.5x baseline for on-demand capacity. Rough calc: 32 baseline -> $4.80 * 32 * 24 * 30 ~= $110k/month baseline (this is raw example). With their $30k/month commit (that's the $180k/6mo), discounts need to preserve margin.

jordan-sales: Wait re numbers — they're expecting $30k/mo, not $110k. We need to map their usage pattern to capacity — they want reserved capacity but will only hit peak occasionally. So commit should be sized to baseline throughput (32) and burst charged above that.

leah-deals: Proposal option A: commit = 32x A10G baseline, fixed monthly price (after discount), burst up to 48 billed at 1.25x baseline instead of 1.5x if they sign 12-month term or accept a slightly higher commit. Option B: 6mo term with 18% discount, burst billed at 1.5x. Which does finance prefer?

rita-fin: For 6mo: 18% is doable but we need an explicit cap on burst hours per month or a soft threshold (e.g., first 120 burst hours/month at 1.25x, remainder at 1.75x). That protects margin and aligns incentives.

mike-legal: Also: no early termination credits in our standard addendum. They asked for a "single forgiveness" clause for one shortfall month — can add as an exception but needs exec sign-off.

jordan-sales: They've pushed back on strict burst caps — their workload is spiky unpredictably. They'd prefer steady invoice predictability. 

leah-deals: Tradeoff: we can offer a consumption smoothing add-on: fixed monthly buffer of 200 burst-hours included, additional at premium. Buffer cost can be folded into the commit pricing. That gives them predictability.

sam-se: From infra side, if we include a buffer we should explicitly note warmup windows and that SLO applies to baseline pool only. Bursts best-effort; we should avoid promising 99.9% latency during large concurrent bursts unless they accept higher baseline or specific pre-warm rules.

jordan-sales: Customer will accept best-effort for bursts if we commit to a documented escalation/runbook and transparent telemetry. They want a clause in the contract about failover to hosted API if private pool saturates.

rita-fin: Draft rate card snippet to include in proposal:
```
Unit: A10G GPU-hour
Baseline price: $4.80 / GPU-hr
Burst premium: 1.5x baseline (standard) => $7.20 / GPU-hr
Burst discounted band (first 120 hrs/mo): 1.25x baseline => $6.00 / GPU-hr
Buffer add-on: 200 burst-hrs/mo => $1,200/mo flat
Commit discount (6mo): 18% off baseline compute line-item
```

leah-deals: That looks reasonable. I'll submit to deal desk for provisional approval. Include the buffer option and early-termination exception as optional addenda.

approvals-bot: Deal Desk Ticket #DD-2397 created by @leah-deals — pending finance sign-off and legal review.

rita-fin: Marking provisional approval: 18% discount for 6mo with buffer add-on and burst cap tiering. Need explicit SLO language: baseline 99.9% latency, burst best-effort with documented warmup and failover to hosted.

mike-legal: I can draft the addendum language for the buffer and the single-month forgiveness clause. Will circulate for Leah's sign-off.

anya-csm: I'll own runbook + telemetry dashboard for their CSM during POC. Need to schedule a call with their infra team next Tues.

jordan-sales: Thanks all. Leah — please push DD ticket and tag me when it gets final. Sam/Anya — I'll coordinate POC kickoff after approvals.

leah-deals: Will do. Adding final ask: include a sentence in the proposal clarifying "burst capacity is subject to pre-warm times and may not meet baseline latency SLO during significant concurrent scale events." Need that before finance signs off.

sam-se: Agree. I'll add the pre-warm numbers and recommended autoscale policy in the POC runbook.

jordan-sales: Great — moving to action.

approvals-bot: DD-2397 status updated: Pending legal. Estimated SLA for review 48 hours.

leah-deals: Tagging @mike-legal for visibility.

mike-legal: Received. Will review and send redlines by EOD tomorrow.

jordan-sales: End of thread — will follow up with customer once contract language is in place.

all-hands

Maya (CEO): Thanks for a great all-hands. Opening this post-meeting thread for any clarifying questions about our mission, market positioning, and next steps. Short messages please.

Ethan (Sales): For enterprise decks: what's the tightest line contrasting us vs the 'model-first' vendors?

Maya (CEO): One-liner: 'We make models reliable in production — consistent SLOs, transparent cost controls, and deployment choices that meet compliance.' Keep it crisp.

Meera (PMM): For external comms, should we focus on 'predictable performance' or 'cost savings' as the lead benefit? Which converts better?

Priya (Head of Product): For PLG leads, lead with developer experience and predictable performance. For enterprise motion, lead with compliance and cost predictability. Two personas, two openers.

Jon (CTO): Technical nuance to add: call out routing, caching, and kernel selection as the ways we deliver predictability. Customers like concrete levers.

Harper (Support): Field ask: prospects worry about cost spikes during load spikes. Approved short answer?

Priya (Head of Product): Say: we limit surprises via adaptive batching, KV/prefix caching, and policy-driven fallbacks — plus routing that prioritizes SLOs over raw throughput.

Ethan (Sales): Need a clear rule to escalate trials to AE. Can we standardize?

Maya (CEO): Proposed thresholds: sustained usage > $7k/mo, explicit Private/KMS ask, or repeated p95 SLA misses (3+ in a week). Priya, please add to playbook.

Meera (PMM): Marketing needs two conservative, publishable performance lines. Can we get approved wording?

title: eng-ml
body:
eng-ml

anika_p: quick update — ran a focused KV-cache quant test comparing fp8 vs int8 on the 7B encoder-decoder we plan to onboard. goal: measure mem footprint, p50/p95 token latency, and small QA accuracy delta. sharing raw notes below.

ben_ml: awesome, ping me the harness config and dataset.

anika_p: harness: batch_size=8, seq_len=512, kv_cache_shard=per_gpu, sample_workload=prod-like (20% short chat, 80% long context), eval_set=TriviaQA+HellaSwag small slice.

chao_w: curious — did you test fused fp8 kernels or emulated fp8 via int8 paths?

anika_p: we used fused fp8 kernels on our runtime (same kernels we'll ship to dedicated). int8 used our current quant path (symmetric 8-bit with per-channel scales). note: both use cached kv in quant form with fast dequant on reuse.

anika_p: results summary (single-GPU numbers):
```
config           | kv_mem (GB) | p50_token_ms | p95_token_ms | tokens/s | QA acc delta
fp32 baseline     | 1.28        | 22.4         | 78.1         | 420      | 0.0
int8 kv          | 0.36        | 24.1         | 92.6         | 390      | -0.6%
fp8 kv (e4m3)    | 0.24        | 23.1         | 83.5         | 405      | -0.2%
```

anika_p: takeaways: fp8 saves ~81% vs fp32 on kv memory, int8 saves ~72%; fp8 gives slightly better tokens/s and lower p95 vs int8 because the fused kernel reduces dequant overhead on hot-paths. int8 shows a small p95 tail increase under spikes (seen in prod-like burst tests).

mike_r: did you run multi-GPU shard tests? how does network transfer affect p95 when kv is smaller?

anika_p: yes — on 4xA100 testbed we saw similar trends; smaller kv reduces PCIe/NVLink churn. int8 had a bit more jitter on p95 because our int8 path dequantizes per-request in a non-fused path when a cache miss occurs.

chao_w: what about quality on longer generative traces (story/assistant) — any sign of coherency drops?

anika_p: ran 500 long-form completions (avg 120 tokens). human-fluency score delta: int8 -0.9 pts (out of 100), fp8 -0.3 pts. automated perplexity-based shifts were consistent with the QA slice.

ben_ml: interesting. Are there specific tokens / attention heads where error concentrates? could be candidate for hybrid (fp8 for kv, int8 for weights) or selective higher-precision for certain layers.

anika_p: rough layerwise probing: errors are concentrated in late-layer attention K/V scales for int8; fp8 preserves dynamic range better there. Hybrid idea seems promising — also considering retaining fp32 for last 2 layers' kv.

deploy-bot: canary started: model=gpt-small-7b, kv_quant=fp8, rollout=5%, route=canary-us-west

mike_r: ops question — does fp8 kv require extra KMS/config on dedicated/private? we need to ensure runtime supports fallback to fp32 on OOM.

anika_p: no new secrets. runtime flag: --kv-quant=e4m3 or --kv-quant=int8. fallback: runtime will auto-fallback to fp32 for that request path if quantized decode OOMs (configurable: fail vs fallback).

chao_w: any perf regressions in batching? batch mixing short/long contexts can expose dequant locks.

anika_p: we pushed a small batching fix that makes dequant non-blocking — bucketed by seq_len. with that fix p95 improved ~8% for fp8, ~2% for int8.

ben_ml: next steps?

anika_p: propose: 1) ship fp8 kv as default for the 7B canary (already at 5%), 2) run 48h A/B to capture infrequent quality regressions with eval hooks, 3) pilot hybrid fp32-last-layers on a small split if we see >0.5% QA drop for int8 users.

mike_r: +1 on 48h. add observability: token-level mismatches, confidence deltas, and quick rollback if user-visible metrics cross threshold.

chao_w: also run GPTQ/AWQ artifacts on same model to compare weight-only quant vs kv quant — we should separate effects.

anika_p: noted — will enqueue GPTQ run. I'll drop the full logs in /mnt/ci/kv-quant/1768506789. short term: fp8 looks like best tradeoff for our runtime.

ben_ml: great thread — thanks anika. can you post the minimal reproduction script and perf harness in the thread when available?

anika_p: will do, uploading now. TL;DR: fp8 KV + fused kernels = best mem/latency/quality mix for 7B; int8 still useful for even tighter memory budgets but watch p95.

title: eng-platform
body:
eng-platform

Alex: Quick follow-up from the RFC: we need a short runbook for the admission splitter + handoff. Main question: how do we surface decisions at the edge when a request moves from token -> lease?

Pri: Proposal: admission-splitter attaches header X-Admit-Mode and X-Admit-Id. If splitter upgrades to a lease, it emits an event to central with provisional_id -> canonical_lease mapping.

Sam: Important: billing dedupe. Billing should ingest admit_id and prefer canonical_lease if present. If provisional never confirmed within ttl, mark as expired and emit provisional_expiry event.

Alex: Can we avoid extra round trips on common fastpath? Token path must remain one RPC. Only heavy-paths call confirm. So splitter returns provisional_id synchronously for token fastpath.

Pri: Agreed. Edge cache needs small LRU + background confirmer. Confirmer batches confirms to central to reduce write load. If central rejects, edge marks the session revoked and sets X-Admit-Fallback: true.

Sam: Failure modes: central timeout -> fallback to token but with multiplier penalty. Ops alert: confirm_batch_fail_rate > 1% for 5m -> pager. Also alert if provisional_expiry spikes.

Alex: API sketches (tiny): POST /admit {client_id,hints} -> {admit:true,mode:token|provisional,id:"p-...",ttl_ms:5000} PUT /confirm {provisional_id} -> {status:leased,lease_id:"L-..."}|{status:revoked}. Keep minimal.

Pri: Eviction plan: leases get soft_notice for grace_ms then hard_revoke. Emit events: lease_soft_notice, lease_revoked. Customers should see graceful 10s drain by default.

Sam: Telemetry to add: admit_mode, provisional_confirm_latency_ms, provisional_expiry_count, fallback_to_token_rate. Dashboards: split by tenant_tier + p95 latency per mode.

Alex: Migration plan: feature-flagged spike (1w) -> prototype (2w) -> staging canary -> 5% prod -> 25% -> 100%. Run chaos tests: central unavail, confirm reordering, clock skew.

Pri: Owners: eng-platform Pri+Alex, eng-sre Sam. I'll draft the follow-up RFC + runbook checklist (chaos tests, alerts, dashboard, billing dedupe).

ops-bot: Meeting created: Thu 10:30am PT "Admission splitter handoff playbook". Reminder 24h.

title: eng-security
body:
eng-security

morgan: Heads-up — new customer onboarding failing. SSO login returns 500 and SCIM provisioning calls return 400/invalid_payload. Started after the RBAC changes this morning. Anyone seen this pattern?

dev-bot: Deploy finished 2026-03-21T09:04:02Z for infra/rbac-service @morgan

sara: Can you paste the exact SCIM error payload and any SAML logs? 400 can be a schema mismatch or missing required attribute.

morgan: Pasting sanitized SCIM request + response:

```
POST /scim/v2/Users
{
  "userName": "jane.doe@example.com",
  "name": {"givenName":"Jane","familyName":"Doe"},
  "externalId": "acct-1234"
}
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
{
  "schemas": ["urn:ietf:params:scim:api:messages:2.0:Error"],
  "detail": "attribute 'roles' is required for provisioning to this tenant",
  "status": "400"
}
```

morgan: SAML error from auth-proxy: `failed to decrypt assertion: kms:Decrypt failed: access denied`

raj: KMS denial + missing roles in SCIM response. Sounds like two linked issues: RBAC change removed a role mapping that the SCIM logic expects, and the assertion decryption failing indicates the KMS key policy might not include the new service account.

elaine: Did we rotate KMS keys or change key policy this morning? ops-bot did a maintenance window around 08:50.

ops-bot: KMS key alias `alias/redwood-sso` rotated at 2026-03-21T08:47:31Z. Rotation triggered by scheduled rekey job. No failures reported at the time.

sara: Ok, two threads to check: 1) RBAC role mapping -> SCIM payload now expects `roles`. 2) KMS key policy -> auth-proxy can't decrypt assertions if it lost kms:Decrypt.

morgan: Quick check shows auth-proxy attempted decrypt with key-id `arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111111:key/abcd1234` but KMS returned `AccessDeniedException`. The key policy lists principals: `svc-auth-proxy@redwood` and `svc-kms-rotator@redwood`. The new RBAC service account is `svc-rbac@redwood` — not in the policy.

raj: That explains decrypt. Why would SCIM require `roles` now? We changed default role mapping so tenants with explicit role assignments fallback to `roles` field in SCIM payload. Looks like the onboarding flow expects that field for this customer (their tenant had role-sync enabled). The RBAC change accidentally made role-sync opt-in only.

elaine: Proposed immediate mitigation: 1) Add `svc-rbac@redwood` to KMS key policy (timeboxed), 2) Revert RBAC mapping change, 3) Re-run provisioning for affected tenant with `X-Replay: true` header to replay SCIM events.

morgan: I can push key policy change and restart auth-proxy. Who can revert the RBAC mapping?

raj: I'll revert the mapping commit and cut a canary patch to prod route. ETA ~20m.

sara: Morgan — after you update key policy, post the exact IAM statement you applied for audit. Also open a follow-up to validate KMS principal membership when rotating keys.

morgan: Applied temporary key policy — added `arn:aws:iam::111111:role/svc-rbac` with decrypt permission. Patch and restarting auth-proxy now.

dev-bot: auth-proxy restart triggered by morgan at 2026-03-21T09:18:01Z.

morgan: SAML log after restart: `assertion decrypted, validated audience 'https://redwood.example.com/sso/callback'` — login flow now progresses past SAML.

raj: RBAC mapping revert deployed to canary, monitoring for 5m.

elaine: Replayed SCIM provisioning for tenant `tenant-42` with `X-Replay: true`. First attempt: 200 OK, user created but missing role assignment in downstream app. Investigating mapping service.

sara: For audit, record: key rotation at 08:47, RBAC change deploy at 09:04, auth-proxy failures 09:06–09:18, mitigation timeline. We'll file a postmortem: impact = new-customer onboarding delayed ~35m.

morgan: Found edge-case in SCIM adapter — if `roles` is absent but `groups` present, we attempt an RBAC lookup and fail hard. Revert fixes it, but I'll add defensive fallback to accept empty `roles` and queue a retry if RBAC lookup errors. Filed PR #4123.

elaine: Also add a test simulating missing KMS principal during key rotation so CI catches it.

raj: I'll own the RBAC revert section of the postmortem. Morgan — paste the exact commands you ran for the key policy change so we can capture them in the incident timeline.

morgan: Commands added to incident doc:

```bash
aws kms get-key-policy --key-id abcd1234 --policy-name default > policy.json
# edit policy.json to include role ARN arn:aws:iam::111111:role/svc-rbac
aws kms put-key-policy --key-id abcd1234 --policy-name default --policy file://policy.json
kubectl rollout restart deploy/auth-proxy -n sso
```

morgan: Opening postmortem and follow-ups: CI test for KMS rotations, RBAC adapter defensive fallback, one-off audit for other KMS keys missing svc-rbac principal.

sara: Thanks team. Marking incident mitigated but keeping thread open for PM notes and review. :white_check_mark:

title: eng-infra
body:
eng-infra

alex: Hey team — putting together a proposal for mixed-capacity pools where we hold a min on-demand floor per region and keep small warm-standby spot lanes for burst. Goal: cut cost without jeopardizing p99 SLAs. Thoughts?

mira: Love the idea. Can you sketch the handoff flow when spot starts failing? biggest risk is sudden tail latency from draining + cache misses.

sam: Ran a quick sim with yesterday's traffic profile. If floor = 20% of nominal capacity, warm-standby = 5% spot, burst apron = 10% ephemeral, p99 stayed within 5% of baseline but cost dropped ~18%. Will paste numbers later.

omni-bot: [scheduled-run] capacity-sim v2 completed: 2026-03-17T11:03Z. artifacts -> /ci/sim/215001-sim-v2

jia: We should treat interruptions as a two-stage signal: 1) pre-drain preference (soft) to start refusing new long-lived work, 2) hard-evict after Xs. Add a debounce to avoid flapping during spot refurb windows.

omar: Regional note: ap-south has much fewer spare GPUs and network egress constraints. If we offload bursts cross-region we'll pay latency and egress cost. Prefer local warm-standby there even if it's slightly more expensive.

mira: agree. Also add a quick warm cache priming step: schedule tiny synthetic requests to populate KV caches in standby nodes before route-swaps. avoids first-token penalties.

alex: Good call on cache priming. For interruption handling I was thinking an "eviction budget" token-bucket per tenant/pool that controls how many tasks can be force-evicted per minute. If bucket empty, we throttle new spot allocations and escalate to on-demand.

sam: Token-bucket model sounds sane. I prototyped policy JSON for the bucket and burst window: ```{
  "eviction_budget_per_min": 30,
  "burst_window_secs": 300,
  "min_on_demand_floor_pct": 0.2,
  "warm_standby_pct": 0.05,
  "graceful_drain_secs": 45
}```

jia: When draining, send an application-level drain header so inference clients can finish short-lived calls. Also we should mark affected cached embeddings as stale and rewarm selectively.

omar: Ops question — how do we prioritize tenants for burst credit redemption? some customers need 99.9 vs others best-effort. We need per-tenant priority + emergency fallback queue that uses reserved on-demand only if high-priority.

mira: yes include tenant_priority in routing policy. And add a safety-leash: never allow floor to drop below absolute min GPUs (to prevent total regional starvation).

alex: Proposed rollout plan: 1) Canary in us-west with 1% traffic -> observe p50/p95/p99 + tail for 48h 2) Enable cache priming + graceful drain 3) Increase to 10% traffic, enable eviction_budget enforcement 4) Expand to AP with local floor tweak. Metrics: eviction_rate, rewarm_latency, p99 inference, egress cost delta.

sam: I'll attach the sim CSV and a simple headroom dashboard. If canary looks good we can automate floor tuning with a daily job.

alex: Awesome. @omni-bot can you schedule a short ops runbook writeup and attach to the canary ticket? Also flag jia/sam/mira for review. :thumbsup:

title: eng-oncall
body:
eng-oncall

incident-bot: PAGER: continuous-batching PERF CLIFF (kv-cache spike) for shard-prod-east-3. High tail latency and increased 5xxs. Alert: p50->p99 token latency jump, queue depth growing.

sara: Oncall here, looking now. Paging mike + raj. Any customer tickets?

mike: I'm on. I see request queues trending up on rn-serving nodes 12-16. KV cache memory going from ~30% -> 95% over 7m then OOM evictions.

raj: saw a burst of concurrent short chats from a single tenant causing extreme prefix cache churn. Continuous batching aggregation appears to be producing huge microbatch sizes under this traffic pattern.

anya: Confirmed — autoscaler didn't react because CPU fine; latency due to queueing inside runtime (waiting for batch). Traces pointing to batching component waiting to reach max_batch_size.

sara: TL;DR: continuous-batching is waiting to fill batches -> queue depth -> increased p99. KV cache thrash + memory pressure exacerbates because microbatches are reading many prefixes. Need a quick mitigation path.

mike: Mitigation options: 1) reduce `max_batch_tokens` and `max_batch_size` for the affected shard; 2) enable jitter (randomized microbatch cut) to avoid synchronized batching; 3) temporarily disable KV cache for shard-prod-east-3; 4) route risky tenant to dedicated pool.

raj: Routing takes longer. I can push batch config hotfix in <5m. Recommend reduce `max_batch_size` from 128 -> 16 and enable `per-request-jitter: true`, and `max_wait_ms` 25 -> 10. That should force smaller microbatches and cut queueing.

sara: Agreed. Anybody see downside? Might increase per-token CPU overhead but reduces p99. Customers affected: > 8 live prod tenants, small latency increase on single-token requests expected. Approve hotfix.

mike: Applying patch to runtime config (shard-prod-east-3). Command:

```
# apply batch overrides to shard
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/v1/shards/shard-prod-east-3/config \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_API_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"continuous_batching": {"max_batch_size": 16, "max_batch_tokens": 256, "per_request_jitter": true, "max_wait_ms": 10}}'
```

ops-bot: config-change: succeeded - rollout started to nodes [12,13,14,15,16] (change-id: cfg-20260315-983).

mike: Pushing to nodes. I'll monitor metrics.

(2m later)

mike: Initial metrics: queue depth halved, p99 tokens latency dropped ~63%. KV cache eviction rate still elevated but stable.

sara: Nice. Any remaining errors?

raj: 5xx rate down to baseline for most tenants, one tenant still showing bursts related to oversized prompt patterns. We should throttle or apply per-tenant concurrency caps next.

anya: Recommend follow-up: add per-tenant `max_inflight_requests` and add a circuit-breaker if cache thrash detected. Also add a synthetic test that simulates many short chats to catch this pattern.

sara: Agreed. For now we keep hotfix for 1h then gradually roll back to previous defaults after we validate. Documenting customer impact: Impact window 12:40–13:05 UTC, increased p99 and 5xx for ~25% of requests on prod-east-3. No data loss. Two customers filed support tickets; SEs notified.

mike: I also added a temporary alert rule to detect microbatch growth and kv-cache eviction spikes:

```
expr: increase(kv_cache_evictions_total[5m]) > 50 or avg_over_time(batch_size[2m]) > 32
for: 2m
```

ops-bot: alert-rule: created (id: ar-20260315-441).

raj: Handing off to next oncall (anya) in 20m. I'll leave runbook notes: how to revert config and how to route tenant to dedicated pool if needed.

anya: Taking handoff. I'll watch for regressions during the next 30m. If p99 rises again, we'll try disabling KV cache as last resort and open a jira for per-tenant rate limits.

sara: Thanks everyone. Post-incident tasks:
- create postmortem draft with timeline and config diffs (owner: sara)
- add synthetic test for short-chat burst (owner: raj)
- evaluate per-tenant inflight caps (owner: product/infra)

mike: One more note — the root cause appears to be an interaction: continuous batching heuristics + high conc/short sequences -> oversized microbatches. Runtime should prefer time-based flush vs size-based under low-token sequences. I'll put a patch in the queue.

sara: Okay. Handoff complete to anya. I'll mark incident as mitigated but not closed. If anyone sees anomalies ping in this thread. :thumbsup:

anya: Confirming stable at +25m. Closing paging loop. I'll include config diff and monitoring links in postmortem.

incident-bot: INCIDENT: mitigated (id: inc-20260315-77).

sara: Filing postmortem now, thanks team.

incidents

incident-bot: [PAGER] Spike in 5xx + gateway timeouts for customer 'NimbusClothing' on Dedicated cluster eu-central-1-dedicated-2. 5xx rate 22% (baseline 0.4%). Triggers: gateway 502, grpc DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, kube evictions. Paging oncall.
Tariq (oncall): ack — joining. Maya, can you grab cluster overview and recent evictions?
Maya (sre): on it. Prometheus shows node oom_kill and kubelet evictions starting 2026-04-02T01:05:xxZ. Two GPU nodes at 98% mem. pods restarting frequently.
Ethan (runtime): joining. Any request traces?
Tariq (oncall): pasting gateway excerpt:
```
2026-04-02T01:06:11Z gateway: upstream error 502 for /v1/chat from 10.20.30.5: connection reset by peer
2026-04-02T01:06:17Z gateway: grpc: deadline exceeded for backend=10.20.30.9
```
Asha (support): Nimbus reports many failures in checkout flows starting ~01:06 UTC. They are high-volume during promo.
Pablo (cs): i'm on call with Nimbus engineering — they confirm increased retries and some customer complaints. Prioritized for mitigation.
Maya (sre): checking top consumers: tenant=borealis-logistics (internal partner) has pods making repeated 8k-token batch requests; their worker instances spiked memory use. They share node group gtx-20-prod with Nimbus.
Ethan (runtime): that sounds like a noisy neighbor. On Dedicated we don't hard-enforce batch caps here yet. Options: 1) emergency route Nimbus to standby dedicated pool in eu-central-1b if available, 2) failover Nimbus to hosted fallback region (latency hit), 3) throttle/burst-limit borealis at proxy. Which is fastest?
Tariq (oncall): what's capacity in standby pool?
Maya (sre): standby shows 40% headroom in eu-central-1b dedicated-standby. We can shift Nimbus there quickly with a routing change.
Ethan (runtime): routing change preferred — preserves customer on Dedicated. Add temporary qps cap and increase tail timeout. Also tag requests for audit.
Tariq (oncall): do it. Maya, apply route change. Also start throttling borealis as a parallel mitigation.
Maya (sre): applying route: `rbctl route update --tenant nimbus-clothing --from eu-central-1-dedicated-2 --to eu-central-1b-dedicated-standby --max-qps 80 --header X-Incident-Fallback:yes`
DeployBot: route update job 9124 started by maya.
Maya (sre): (90s) DeployBot: route update 9124 completed successfully. Traffic shift beginning.
Tariq (oncall): starting proxy throttle for borealis: envoy rate limit rule to 12qps, concurrency cap 2.
Ethan (runtime): also lower priority class for their pods: `kubectl patch pod borealis-worker-*-* -p '{"metadata":{"annotations":{"redwood/priority":"best-effort"}}}'` and apply cgroup memory.limit for their containers.
Maya (sre): applied limit and envoy rule. I see borealis request rate drop and their pod memory usage falling.
Asha (support): Nimbus: "We see errors declining, checkout success returning. Latency increased ~200ms but acceptable."
Pablo (cs): Nimbus thanks the team; they want follow-up on root cause and long-term fixes.
Tariq (oncall): good. cluster-wide pod restarts decreasing; node memory dropping to 68% within 4 minutes. 5xx rate for Nimbus down to 3% now.
Ethan (runtime): next steps: block large-batch requests on this pool via admission controller, add per-tenant hard memory caps, and implement automatic tenant throttling when node pressure >85%. I'll open PRs.
Maya (sre): operational cleanup: cordon problematic nodes (node-gtx-23,node-gtx-24) to prevent new scheduling until stable. `kubectl cordon node-gtx-23` `kubectl cordon node-gtx-24`.
DeployBot: node cordon job 9130 succeeded.
Tariq (oncall): handoffs: Maya will own immediate remediation (cordon, scale down borealis), Ethan will own runtime limits PR, Pablo will coordinate customer comms and chase Borealis account. I'll put a summary in #oncall-handoffs and go offline in 30m.

title: eng-platform
body:
eng-platform

maya: Heads-up — planning a migration to per-tenant OTLP sharding + agent fallback for inference telemetry. Want to align on SDK init, batching/shutdown semantics, and sampling so we don't blow retention or CPU.

igor: 👍 high level? are we doing agent sidecars everywhere or per-cluster gateways?

maya: Proposal: sidecar-agent on Dedicated + Private nodes (to smooth bursts) and direct OTLP export from Hosted with per-tenant shard endpoints for scaling. Agent acts as buffering layer and handles async export/retries.

chen: Main SDK pain we see: Python's uvloop + async exporter behaves differently from go/rust when process shuts down — traces can be lost if not flushed. Need consistent init/shutdown patterns.

ryan: Also large volume of short-lived spans from token-level traces. We should avoid token-per-span by default. Suggest: one request span + child spans for major phases (prompt-build, kvcache-lookup, generation-blocks). Add attributes for token counts and sampling_keys.

igor: Agree. Token-level spans are too chatty. But for debugging perf regressions we sometimes want detailed subspans. Can we make detailed spans opt-in via route-level sampling? e.g., heavy_completions: sample 0.1, debug_routes: sample 1.0

maya: Exactly. Route-level sampling + tail-based sampling for error/high-latency traces. Also tag spans with route and model_name for downstream routing.

telemetry-bot: Reminder: retention tier changes will increase trace storage 10x for 7-day hot window. Check cost impact before enabling high-res sampling.

chen: For SDK specifics: Python (opentelemetry-python) has OTLP span exporter + batch span processor. We should recommend this pattern:
```py
from opentelemetry import trace
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace import TracerProvider
from opentelemetry.sdk.trace.export import BatchSpanProcessor, OTLPSpanExporter
provider = TracerProvider()
exporter = OTLPSpanExporter(endpoint=os.getenv('OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT'))
provider.add_span_processor(BatchSpanProcessor(exporter, max_queue_size=2048, schedule_delay_millis=200))
trace.set_tracer_provider(provider)
```
and enforce a flush on graceful shutdown: `provider.shutdown()` or `exporter.shutdown()`.

susan: For Go, the SDK's BatchSpanProcessor is reliable; the tricky part is how the runtime uses goroutines for exporter backpressure. We should standardize env vars: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, INFER_TELEMETRY_SHARD, INFER_TELEMETRY_MODE(agent|direct).

ryan: Rust runtime currently uses synchronous exporter in critical path for simplicity. We should move to an async export pipeline (tokio task + bounded channel) or do sidecar for now. Otherwise we risk blocking inference threads on network spikes.

igor: What about attribute limits and cardinality? We must cap dynamic attributes (tenant_id, session_id) and avoid putting prompt text into span attrs. Use a hash for prompt fingerprint if needed.

maya: Agreed — policy: no PII in attributes, prompt_text never in spans. Use `prompt_hash`,`model`, `route`, `kvcache.hit` (bool), `tokens.generated` (int). That keeps cardinality low.

chen: How do we route traces to shards? Suggest adding `resource` attr `tenant_id` and set exporter endpoint to include shard token e.g. `https://telemetry.internal/v1/traces?shard=${TENANT_SHARD}`. Sidecar can rewrite.

telemetry-bot: Note: OTLP gRPC vs HTTP/Protobuf matters for buffers. gRPC uses keepalive and multiplexing; HTTP can be simpler behind gateways. We'll need benchmarks.

maya: Rollout plan:
- Staging: enable agent-mode + route-level sampling 0.1 for 48 hours (staging traffic).
- Canary: 5% traffic on low-risk service (embedding) for 24h. Check CPU/latency and dropped spans.
- Gradual 25/50/100% with retention monitoring and quotas enforced.

ryan: Also need a small shim in all runtimes that provides a consistent init API: `InferTelemetry.init(config)` which sets tracer provider, processors, and exposes `flush()` for shutdown hooks. Can implement wrappers per language.

susan: Good. For go/python/rust we can publish a tiny repo with examples + k8s sidecar Helm changes. I'll own the Helm patch.

igor: Who owns benchmarking exporter backpressure? I can run load tests with gRPC vs HTTP and agent vs direct.

maya: Perfect. Action items:
- igor: perf bench exporter modes (gRPC/http) + memory patterns — due EOW.
- chen: produce language init snippets + recommended env vars for python/go/rust — due Wed.
- susan: Helm sidecar template + feature flag for agent-mode — due next Tue.
- ryan: implement `InferTelemetry` shim prototypes in rust & go — sync Fri.

devops-bot: New ticket created: INF-2153 "Telemetry: OTLP sharding + agent fallback plan" assigned to igor, chen, susan, ryan.

maya: Thanks all — let's avoid a repeat of last year's lost spans incident. Ping me if blockers appear. :thumbsup:

ajay (eng-runtime): Canary still getting ~2% of ACME traffic. We have prefix cache warming in progress — that might amplify failures. I see `RuntimeError: failed kernel launch` across 2/3 pods.

liz (dedicated-systems): On the Dedicated host side, I see OOM spikes then kernel failures on the same pods. Pod names: `acme-canary-0`, `acme-canary-1`. CPU fine, GPU memory pressure high.

marta (oncall): Marking P1 for ACME tenant impact. ACME CSM should be notified — @oliver can you ping them and let them know we're investigating and may rollback canary?

oliver (csm-acme): On it. Reached out to ACME support lead, they asked for ETA and whether their pinned artifact (v1-stable) will be restored. They said major workflows are failing for key customers.

kevin (platform): We should do a controlled rollback of canary to pinned artifact v1-stable and keep canary traffic paused. Plan: 1) scale down canary routing to 0% 2) deploy rollback (kubectl rollout undo / update image to v1-stable) 3) monitor for errors. Anyone object?

ajay (eng-runtime): +1 for rollback. But note: the canary was using a quantized runtime kernel that v1 doesn't use. Rolling back the model binary should be safe — ensure we don't mix KV caches across model versions. I'll add a cache-bust header in the router.

liz (dedicated-systems): Suggested commands:

```
# Pause canary traffic (platform router)
redwood-route update acme --pool acme-prod-01 --canary-percentage 0

# Force rollback on canary set
kubectl -n acme-prod set image deployment/acme-canary acme-inference=registry.redwood/v1-stable
kubectl -n acme-prod rollout status deployment/acme-canary --timeout=5m
```

marta (oncall): I'll perform the router change now and then hand to liz for the rollout. After rollback, we'll run smoke evals against customer prompt set `acme/core-smoke` and look at 5xx rate and latency.

sre-bot: ACTION — marta changed route: `acme` canary percentage 2% -> 0% by marta at 1718001302 :white_check_mark:

liz (dedicated-systems): Starting image update. Watching pods. If any pod eviction fails due to GPU allocation, fallback is to cordon node and schedule onto spare nodes.

marta (oncall): Handoff to ajay for deeper debug. I'll stay on until we confirm ACME is green and then flip incident to monitoring. @oliver please keep ACME updated that we rolled canary and are investigating root cause + mitigation path.

ajay (eng-runtime): I'll create a tracker ticket `INC-ACME-171800` with repro steps, kernel logs, and assign to eng-runtime + dedicated-systems. Will include suggested mitigations: revert quant kernel, limit sequence-length in routing, or bump GPU reservation for this pool.

sre-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigated at 1718001678 by marta :white_check_mark:

title: eng-platform
body:
eng-platform

maya: heads up — found a surprising interaction between project-key routing and quota inheritance when callers use cross-project service accounts. app hits the wrong quota and gets 429s even though the project has quota available. :thinking:
kevin: repro steps? can you paste minimal request / headers?
maya: sure — calling from project B but using a service account created in project A, routing currently attributes to the key's origin project. sample header:
```
Authorization: Bearer sk_projA_sa_abc123
X-Forwarded-Project: proj-B
```
Response shows quota-consumed-by proj-A.
samir: that matches the routing policy we implemented: keys are authoritative for attribution for billing/quotas. problem is UX; console shows usage under proj-B so users are confused.
elaine: yikes. users expect the call to count against the caller project (proj-B) not the key origin. do we have telemetry to see how common cross-project SA usage is?
maya: limited telemetry: about ~2% of token volume in last 30d, spikes from partner integrations. I can add an event to tag requests with routing_decision=key_origin vs caller_project.
kevin: two options I see: 1) change routing to prefer X-Forwarded-Project when present (simpler UX), 2) keep attribution to key origin but show a console mapping and explanatory tooltip. both have billing/abuse implications.
samir: also need to consider quota isolation and abuse surface — if we let caller project override, a malicious proj could drain another project's reserved quota if they control the header chain. but we do have service-token impersonation guards.
elaine: rollout UX: if we change routing semantics, we should canary to 5% of traffic and expose "attribution_preview" in the console so admins can see before commit.
maya: agree. plan: (a) add telemetry event 'authz.attribution.preview' with fields [request_id, key_origin, caller_project, decision_reason], (b) implement a runtime flag route.attribute_pref = 'caller_project_prefer' behind a feature flag, (c) console preview widget + admin opt-in.
kevin: API surface: we should add a short changelog entry and a compatible header that enforces policy: `X-Attribution-Override: allow|deny` so callers can opt-in if their infra vouches. default deny.
samir: implementation note: update routing code to evaluate in order: 1) explicit override header if signed by org admin, 2) caller_project (if present and verified), 3) key_origin. verification requires signed assertion from caller project.
elaine: for rollout metrics, capture 429_count_by_attribution and latency delta. alert if 429 increases by >5% in canary.

title: customer-success
body:
customer-success

emily: Customer reported 422 on /v1/rerank. They say same payload works locally against our dev container but fails in hosted. Error message: "Invalid input: duplicate field 'query'". Filing as CS-2345. Can someone take a look?

raj: Can you paste the exact payload (sanitized) and the curl call they used? Also which model and rerank version?

emily: Pasting minimal repro (customer removed ids):
```json
{
  "model": "rex-rerank-v1",
  "query": "what is the refund policy",
  "documents": [
    {"id": "d1", "query": "what is the refund policy", "text": "Refund policy is 30 days..."},
    {"id": "d2", "query": "return window", "text": "You can return within 30 days..."}
  ]
}
```
They call with: `curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank -d @payload.json`

logan: I tried a quick run in staging with that JSON and I get the same 422. Response body: `{"error":"Invalid input: duplicate field 'query' at /documents/0/query"}`. Strange because our validator should allow nested `query` inside documents.

jia: This looks like schema flattening in the input validation layer. We have a legacy validation path that flattens top-level field names and rejects duplicates if the nested object uses the same name. Repro steps I ran: (1) POST payload above to staging, (2) check logs on validation service, (3) see fastjson schema validator raise DuplicateFieldError.

jia: Quick workaround for the customer: rename the nested field to `query_text` OR move the per-document search phrase into `passages` objects like `{"passages": [{"text": "..."}]}`. We'll roll a hotfix but that might take a day due to compatibility checks.

emily: Customer is using a pipeline that auto-generates doc objects with `query` inside. They have ~150 candidates per request. Any impact on limits or scoring if they rename fields?

raj: Candidate/passage limits: currently the rerank endpoint allows up to 500 candidate objects, but each extra field increases payload size and may push the request past a size limit, causing a 413. Also noted edge-case where empty or duplicate query fields inside docs caused the model to return all-zero scores for some clients (we've seen this when tokenization fails).

jia: For immediate repro and debug you can run this curl that reproduces the 422 and show stack snippet: 
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer test' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rex-rerank-v1","query":"x","documents":[{"id":"1","query":"x","text":"a"}]}'
```
Observed: `HTTP/1.1 422 Unprocessable Entity`
Validation log excerpt: `ValidationError: DuplicateFieldError: field="query" path=/documents/0/query (validator=fastjson_flatten_v1) at input_validator.py:87`

jira: (internal note) tagging eng-runtime @jia for follow-up patch to input_validator to whitelist nested fields or use namespaced validation.

emily: Customer needs a short-term mitigation that doesn't involve changing their generator heavily. Any suggestions?

jia: If they can run a preprocessing step to rename keys on-the-fly (map `query` -> `q` or `query_text`) before sending, that's the fastest. If they can't, we can offer a temporary proxy we run in their VPC to rewrite payloads for them (requires ops ticket).

raj: I've sent the sanitized payload to eng-runtime, added CS-2345, and offered the simple key-rename script. Customer accepted the rename for now.

support-bot: Ticket CS-2345 updated: assigned to eng-runtime, priority P2, workaround provided. :thumbsup:

emily: Thanks all — logging this for the rerank schema cleanup epic. I'll follow up if the workaround fails.
