title: incidents
body:
incidents

incident-bot: :rotating_light: SEV-2 alert: spike in 5xx from public API in us-west-2 for the last 90s. Pager triggered: Eli (pager)

Eli (pager): paging oncall — seeing ~20% 5xx, errors mostly 504 from our front ELBs. Rolling 1m P50 latency is fine but tail is bad.

Alice (oncall): I'm on it. pulling dashboards. Which AZs impacted?

Ben SRE: looks concentrated in us-west-2b and 2c. us-west-2a healthy. ELB 5xx rates up, connection resets between ELB and targets.

Carol (net): I see a concurrent spike in EBS API detach/attach latency in the console for us-west-2b (AWS Console graph shows high detach latency). Could be stuck volume detach delaying instance replacement.

Dan (infra): AutoScaling recently ran a scale-in at 10:12 and a bunch of instances entered Terminating:Wait -> Terminating:Proceed hooks. Some targets remained registered with ELB longer than expected.

Alice (oncall): hypothesis: stuck scale-in + slow EBS detach => instances not fully drained => ELB connections stuck -> 504s. Any signs of ELB connection queueing?

Ben SRE: ELB backend connection counts show several targets with very high active conn. Health checks sometimes fail with 502. Sample logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T10:14:32Z] upstream read timeout from 10.0.45.23: read tcp 10.1.2.3:443->10.0.45.23:12345: i/o timeout
```

Carol (net): Also seeing some route flaps between AZb and AZc on the VPC overlay, transient path change metrics in our fabric. Might be amplifying client resends.

Maria (support): Customers are reporting timeouts on ingest endpoints. Ticket influx started ~10:13. No major data loss reported but retries are spiking.

Alice (oncall): Ok mitigations: 1) Redirect traffic away from us-west-2b/2c via Route53 weighted routing to us-west-2a (manual weight shift). 2) Increase ELB deregistration timeout to allow graceful drain. 3) Contact AWS support about EBS detach latencies and ENI state. Who can take which?

Eli (pager): I'll do the Route53 weight shift now. Will move 80% of traffic to us-west-2a for low-risk services, keep 20% to test rollback.

Dan (infra): I'll temporarily reduce ASG termination concurrency and pause scale-in to stop new terminations. Also increasing ELB deregistration timeout from 300s -> 600s for the affected target group.

Ben SRE: I'll open an AWS support case for EBS detach API rate limiting and request account-level throttle increase and investigate if detach failures are due to quota. aws-support-bot, can you create a ticket with logs?

aws-support-bot: Created support case 1234567890. Severity: elevated. Attached CloudWatch metrics and a capture of failed detaches. AWS advised to check for long-running I/O and in-use volumes preventing detach.

Carol (net): For the route flaps, I've flagged the VPC fabric team. For immediate relief, applying eBPF path pinning to reduce route churn for ELB subnets in 2b/2c. Rolling in 1 region at a time.

Alice (oncall): Maria, prepare a short customer-facing blurb: 'We are experiencing elevated timeouts for API ingest endpoints in us-west-2. We are shifting traffic and coordinating with AWS; we'll update in 15m.' Keep it factual.

Maria (support): Drafted and posted to status page and support queue. Customers with active incidents notified.

Ben SRE: Observability check: enabling target-level connection logging on ELB and adding short-lived guardrails to circuit-break repeated opens from the same target to avoid conn pile-up.

Eli (pager): Route53 shift applied at 10:20. Immediate drop in 5xx for services routed to us-west-2a. 5xx for remaining 20% still high.

Alice (oncall): Good. How are host replacement attempts going?

Dan (infra): We see several failed detach attempts; attaching a sample awscli trace: 
```
aws ec2 detach-volume --volume-id vol-0abcd --instance-id i-0fff --region us-west-2
An error occurred (InvalidVolume.NotDetached) when calling the DetachVolume operation: Volume vol-0abcd is in-use by instance i-0fff
```
Manual detach fails until we force stop instance -> not ideal. AWS case open.

Ben SRE: For immediate risk mitigation: mark problematic instances Unhealthy in ASG so they get removed from rotation, but because detach is slow we must be careful not to deadlock. I'm going to deregister targets manually from ELB and set connection-draining to true.

Carol (net): Applying temporary iscsi timeouts tweak on hosts in 2b/2c to reduce stall windows (will roll to a few hosts first).

Alice (oncall): Action checklist status: Route53 shift — done. ELB deregistration timeout increased — done. ASG scale-in paused — done. AWS case filed — done. Manual deregisters in progress — Ben. Customer comms posted — Maria. Net tweak rolling — Carol.

Maria (support): Support queue: ~12 tickets opened, top 3 customers on high-tier contacted via phone. No escalations yet.

Ben SRE: After manual deregisters, 5xx for the remaining 20% dropped from 18% -> 3% in ~3m. Looks like ELB->target stalls were primary.

Eli (pager): Still watching for edge cases; Lucy from Payments reported a spike at 10:31 but it's resolved after shift.

Alice (oncall): We'll keep the Route53 shift for now until AWS confirms EBS detach root cause and we can safely resume scale-in. Post-incident items: runbook update for ASG termination order when EBS detach latencies are high, add automated fallback to region-level weight shift, and add more robust force-detach SOP.

Dan (infra): I'll also add an alert for EBS detach latency threshold on ASG terminations to preempt this.

aws-support-bot: AWS support responded: "We see elevated detach latency due to control-plane throttling in us-west-2b/c correlated with high volume of detach/attach operations. We recommend staggering detach operations and reducing concurrent detach rate; provisioned throughput increase may be requested but not guaranteed."

Ben SRE: AWS recommends staggering ops — we'll implement a termination rate limiter in ASG lifecycle hook processor.

Alice (oncall): T-minus: moving to steady-state. Keep this thread active for another 30m. Next update at +15m. Great work all. :thumbsup:

Maria (support): Status page updated: "Degraded performance in us-west-2 - mitigations in place; partial traffic rerouted. Next update in 15 minutes."

Carol (net): Net tweak rollout to 25% of hosts done, metrics show fewer route churn events.

Ben SRE: Closing loop: 5xx back to baseline for >90% of traffic. Leaving fine-grained monitoring on.

Alice (oncall): Officially downgrading to monitoring-only in 20m unless new alerts. Postmortem owner: Ben. Timeline/event notes saved to incident doc.

Eli (pager): I'll handoff to oncall for the next shift at 11:00. Handoff notes posted.

incident-bot: Incident SEV downgraded to SEV-3 at 10:38.

Alice (oncall): Thanks team. We'll run the follow-up actions and schedule a blameless postmortem.

title: design
body:
design

Nora: Quick note from QA: in compact tables the kebab (⋯) is nearly un-tappable on desktop when checkboxes are shown. Folks missed actions in the last test.
Eli: Ack. Which page? rules or instances?
Nora: Instances table, compact, multi-select on. The kebab visually sits at the absolute edge.
Samir: Can we add a small hit token rather than increasing visual size? e.g. `--space-compact-action-hit: 6px` used as inner padding so icon stays 20px but target grows to 32px.
Nora: That would be ideal. Also toasts are appearing below the header and overlapping sticky filters. Copy is terse: just "Deleted". Suggest consistent pattern: `"<Action> <object> — Undo"` and anchor to bottom-right for dense pages.
Eli: Agreed on copy. For the toast anchoring maybe a per-page offset token like `--toast-anchor-bottom-offset` so pages with sticky footers or filters can tune it.
Samir: Implementation plan: CSS utility `.action-hit({size:32}) { min-width:32px; height:32px; padding:6px; }` and token `compact-action-hit` set to 6px. For toasts we'll render them in a `.page-toasts` container inside the page with `position:absolute; right:var(--spacer-3); bottom:var(--toast-anchor-bottom-offset,24px);`
ui-bot: Storybook story updated: https://storybook/s/compact-table--kebab-hitarea (branch: feat/compact-hit).
Nora: Accessibility: kebab must be a `<button>` with `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded`, and SR label: "Actions for <item>". Ensure focus ring meets contrast when compact.
Eli: Keyboard flow: Tab to row -> Tab to actions -> Enter opens menu -> Arrow keys navigate. If menu is portalled into body we need focus return. Add `role="menu"` / `role="menuitem"`.
Samir: PR incoming with token and small CSS util. I'll add a Storybook case for sticky-filter pages to test toast overlay.

title: eng-ml
body:
eng-ml

marta: quick update from this morning's shadow run — speculative decoder on llama2-70b (q4_0 build). summary: tokens/sec ~+60% vs baseline, p95 latency down ~40%, but p99 moved up ~8% on long tails. noticed a cluster of code-gen failures.

kevin: can you paste the exact runtime config you used? want to repro locally.

marta: gist of the command (sanitized):
```bash
./serve_infer --model llama2-70b-q4 --speculative_budget 0.4 \\\n  --max_lookahead 6 --early_accept_topk 3 --accept_thresh 0.08 \\\n  --confidence_smoothing ema:alpha=0.6 --fallback_kl 1.2 \
  --batch 16 --seq 2048 --shadow=true
```

kevin: interesting — max_lookahead=6 is fairly aggressive. where are the code failures appearing? truncated function bodies, or logic drift?

marta: mostly truncated helpers and missing closing brackets in generated code, plus a few multi-step reasoning math problems that diverged after an accepted speculative token. short completions and chat routes are fine.

ravi: do we have the top failure examples? can we see logits + accept flags?

marta: uploaded artifacts: s3://redwood-shadow/1945678901/failures_top20.jsonl (includes logits, accept_mask, baseline vs spec outputs).

eval-bot: auto-summary: 2k-prompt eval (mixed instructions):
- exact-match: baseline 44.1% -> spec 42.9% (-1.2)
- bleu: baseline 38.6 -> spec 38.2 (-0.4)
- ppl(1k): baseline 11.9 -> spec 12.2 (+0.3)
- latency p95: 420ms -> 250ms (-40%)
- latency p99: 1220ms -> 1317ms (+8%)
- tokens/sec: 680 -> 1088 (+60%)
(full report: s3://redwood-shadow/1945678901/report.json)

devops-bot: alert: observed memory pressure on A40-48G nodes when using quant kernel pack blocksize=16 + lookahead=6. swap-on-host triggered in one replica. recommendation: try blocksize=24 or reduce batch size.

kevin: lowering blocksize is a trade-off vs quant noise. did you try smaller speculative_budget? maybe 0.25 retains most perf and fixes some regression.

marta: not yet. plan: run a 10k-run sweep over speculative_budget in {0.2,0.25,0.35,0.4} and max_lookahead in {3,6} plus smoothing on/off. also test temps {0.0,0.7,1.0} since sampling interacts with early-accept.

ravi: add a targeted canary: n=500 on the code-synthesis holdout set (long functions + docstrings). if EM drop persists >0.5 pts we block rollout.

kevin: agree. also can we add a conservative accept rule: require accept confidence gap > 0.15 for lookahead>=4 (to avoid multi-step collapse)? simple rule in runtime but should reduce false accepts.

marta: I'll implement the gap threshold and run a 1k quick test after the sweep. creating PR: https://git.internal/rw/spec-decode/1945-conservative-gap.

eval-bot: note: when comparing per-route breakdown, chat/qa routes show negligible regressions while code and math routes concentrate >80% of EM delta.

devops-bot: scheduling note: the A40 cluster has a maintenance window tonight 02:00-03:00 UTC. any long runs should be queued before 01:30.

marta: thanks. will prioritize the budget sweep and the code canary, queue runs now. will also test blocksize=24 config to avoid OOM on 48G nodes.

kevin: if 0.25 + gap threshold + smoothing recovers >0.8 of EM while keeping ~1.4x tokens/sec, i'm OK with a canary in dedicated prod for non-long routes.

marta: plan posted. I'll drop final metrics here when done. ping me for artifact access if you need earlier visibility. :thumbsup:

title: product
body:
product

ellie: Quick thread to lock the DP pilot scorecard + exit criteria. Need something actionable for recruitment and handoff to sales. Thinking small cohorts (8-10), 4-week pilots, clear pass/fail and handover playbook.

marcus: Agreed. Suggest scorecard with three pillars: Reliability (latency / errors), Quality (eval prompts delta), and Adoption (active users + flows). Each pillar has pass/fail thresholds.

noor: Proposal: numeric thresholds + qualitative check. Example thresholds: latency p50 <250ms, error rate <1.5%, quality delta >= -3% from baseline, weekly active usage >=60% of agreed test users. If two pillars fail -> remediation or end pilot.

sara: Also include a "soft signals" bucket: partner engagement (meeting attendance), anecdotal investor-level quotes, support ticket volume. These inform go/no-go but don't alone fail a pilot.

ellie: Recruitment filters: prefer partners with real production traffic and a staffed contact who can run eval prompts. Prioritize one regulated partner for Private deployment validation. Keep intake low friction: 6 fields max.

marcus: Compensation tiers: Lead partners = $6k credits + co-marketing; Standard pilots = $3k credits; Observational = credits only. Offer a small success bonus for case studies. Legal = NDA + one-page pilot terms.

noor: Ops guardrails: add a "kill-switch" flag per partner to roll back model or route traffic away if quality drops >5% in a 24h window. Also require a weekly automated eval job and a per-partner scorecard page.

sara: Handoff checklist to sales: partner interest level, adoption metrics, open blockers, deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private), co-marketing permission, and follow-up ask (POC/contract).

ellie: Exit interviews: 20-min structured convo + 3-question survey (satisfaction, likelihood to buy, top blockers). Capture quotes for marketing only with opt-in.

marcus: Timeline: intake form + screening rubric by Thu; onboarding + runbook by next Tue; scorecard template + dashboard by next Wed; outreach copy + legal template by EOD Fri.

title: support
body:
support

Anika Rao: Hey team — customer (acct: acme-42) is hitting intermittent failures on our embeddings endpoint when they send batched requests. Started ~08:12 UTC, happening ~5-10% of requests, seems correlated with larger batches. Error: `ValueError: embedding dimension mismatch (expected 1536, got 768)`.
Jared M.: ugh. do we know which model they're hitting?
Anika Rao: They pinned `open-embed-1536-v1` in their route config but their route has dynamic routing enabled (fallbacks allowed). Their SDK call is a single POST with an array of 18 texts.
Priya S.: can you paste the request body + headers (no PII)? also route config?
Anika Rao: pasted snippet below — headers and route. request id examples: req-01F9Z8K8, req-01F9ZGL3 (from logs).
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Authorization: Bearer sk-***
Content-Type: application/json
X-Client-ID: acme-42
{
  "model": "open-embed-1536-v1",
  "input": ["short sentence 1","...", "item 18"],
  "batch_options": {"max_batch_size": 32, "dynamic_batching": true}
}
```
Anika Rao: route config (redacted): `allowed_models: [open-embed-1536-v1, open-embed-768-lite]`, fallback_policy: `['cost','latency']`
Tom H.: that jump to `open-embed-768-lite` would explain the 768 dim. But the client expects 1536. We should never return embeddings of different dims for same route unless we guarantee downstream compatibility.
ops-bot: deploy-log: batching-v3 rolled to prod on 2026-03-13T21:40Z (id: deploy-2026-03-13-batching-v3).
Jared M.: is the runtime choosing the lite variant because of capacity or latency thresholds? Any logs showing routing decision?
Priya S.: checked routing traces for req-01F9Z8K8: matched model `open-embed-768-lite` due to `fallback: cost` and availability zone had no 1536 capacity for that moment.
Anika Rao: customer says they get a dimension mismatch error client-side and their client library just throws rather than handling variable dims. They want a fix or workaround asap.
Tom H.: short-term workaround: instruct customer to set `strict_model: true` or remove cheaper fallback models from allowed_models. Also they can validate dims on client and retry with single-model pin.
Jared M.: medium-term we should prevent mixed-dimension responses for same route. Options: 1) enforce model families with consistent emb_dim (server-side validation) 2) when fallback selects model with different dim, do an automatic reshuffle/upgrade to compatible variant (pad/upsample?) — padding's sketchy for semantic integrity. 3) reject request with clear error if fallback would change dim.
Priya S.: logging note: need to emit `chosen_model` in the per-request trace so support+customers see it. currently console only shows final endpoint but not model variant.
Anika Rao: customer asked for repro steps we can give them to reproduce consistently. Below is a reproducible curl (we tested locally to trigger fallback) — toggle `allowed_models` to include smaller variant:
```
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/embeddings \ 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer SK' \ 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ 
  -d '{"model":"open-embed-1536-v1","input": ["a","b","c",...,"r"],"batch_options": {"max_batch_size":32, "dynamic_batching": true}}'
```
Anika Rao: expected -> embedding shape [18,1536]. actual (on failure) -> [18,768] leading to client ValueError.
Tom H.: adding a quick server-side guard: if route.allowed_models contains models with mismatched emb_dim, and dynamic routing is enabled, return 409 w/ body `{"error":"model_embedding_dimension_mismatch","details":"request would be served by a model with embedding_dim != configured primary model"}`. That avoids silent dim swaps.
Jared M.: agree. Also add a console warning when creating/updating a route that mixes embedding dims. GUI and API should validate.
Priya S.: filed ticket ENG-RT-8521 for runtime change + UI validation. assigning to eng-runtime. cc @eng-runtime.
eng-runtime: acknowledged. will triage priority-high. Proposed plan: (1) short-term: add request-time check and explicit 409 response + telemetry, (2) medium: block route updates that mix dims, (3) long-term: model family abstraction so all variants advertised for a route share emb_dim.
Anika Rao: Customer-approved workaround: set `allowed_models` to only `open-embed-1536-v1` and set `batch_options.dynamic_batching=false` temporarily. They asked for ETA on server fix.
eng-runtime: ETA for request-time guard: 48-72 hrs to roll canary plus docs. Blocking UI validation target: next sprint (2w).

title: architecture
body:
architecture

sara: quick Q — for rollout metadata do we store a freeform pin reason + schema version, or break it into explicit fields (compat_policy, pin_origin, scope)? thinking about cross-region fallbacks and migration complexity.

mike: leaning explicit. enums make router decisions faster than parsing text. we hit a perf wobble when we had to inspect freeform notes.

ajay: +1 on enums. also we need a pin_origin: {user, auto-eval, infra} for audit and automated rollbacks.

leila: what about layered pins? org-level vs project/route-level pins. schema should include scope so router and console can show precedence.

sara: proposed minimal schema example — would this be acceptable and backcompatible?
```json
{
  "model_id": "stable-7b",
  "pinned_version": "2026-03-01",
  "pin_origin": "deploy-tool",
  "compat_policy": "strict",
  "scope": "route",
  "ttl": "30d",
  "notes": "hotfix for decoding regressions"
}
```
would this break existing rollout store?

mike: migration path looks ok if we default missing compat_policy -> "best_effort". router can treat absent scope as "global" for older rows. recommend a lightweight DB migration that backfills defaults.

ajay: router perf note — avoid string compares in hot path. store compat_policy as small int/bitflag internally but keep enum string in API for readability.

leila: ops question — can we test this in staging as a canary? want to validate fallback behavior across regions. @ops-bot can you schedule a canary for /chat route pinned to that version in staging?

ops-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary for /chat with pinned_version=2026-03-01 in staging at 2026-03-18T12:30:00Z :white_check_mark:

sara: action items: I'll open a short migration RFC with samples, backfill script, and a validator in the model registry.

mike: +1. also add unit tests for router fast-path when scope is missing (old rows).

ajay: one more ask — include an optional "incompatible_versions" list for emergency blacklists so router can avoid known-bad versions quickly.

leila: :thumbsup: I'll draft DB index plan: queries we need are (route, pinned_version) and (scope, expiry). will post in RFC comment.

sara: thanks all — I'll post the RFC draft in #architecture later today and link the migration PR.

title: incidents
body:
incidents

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Hosted runtime KV cache OOM spike detected — cluster gpu-hosted-1 reporting repeated OOMs on inference pods (kvcache growth), autoscaler throttled. Related alerts: OOMCount>50m, AvgTokenLatency up 4x. Paging to #incidents and @carla_oncall.

carla_oncall: On it. I see a burst starting ~1849502000 from a handful of customers sending >200k token prompts (long-form context). Prefetch + continuous batching appears to have amplified stray long prompts into sustained kvcache growth.

ben_runtime: Confirmed. Reproduced locally with a 300k token synthetic prompt — kvcache never evicts due to our current windowing and the prefetch policy. Continuous batching merged prefixes and drove memory up.

carla_oncall: Impact? which customers are hitting errors?

frank_cs: Customer-reported: two hosted tenants saw 500s and timeouts starting ~10m ago. CS ticket IDs: #5432, #5433. They report partial responses then errors. No data leakage; just OOMs/timeouts.

dave_sre: Logs: `kubectl -n hosted logs inference-pod-7 --since=15m` shows repeated `gpu oom` and `kvcache alloc failed`. Stacktrace pointing at `kv_cache::insert_batch` and `continuous_batcher::flush_on_threshold`.

ben_runtime: Quick mitigation options: 1) Disable prefetch on hosted tier (config toggle) 2) Reduce batch_merge_window to 20ms 3) Force kvcache soft-eviction at 80% GPU mem for 30s 4) Roll back recent batching heuristics.

erin_prod: Recommend minimal user-visible impact: start with (1) + (2). Disabling prefetch should stop amplification quickly, reducing new growth. Then lower batch window to limit batch size. We'll only do (3) if OOMs persist.

carla_oncall: Agree. I'll patch platform config for hosted runtime: set `prefetch.enabled=false` for tier=hosted, and `batch_merge_window_ms=20`. Pushing via deploy-bot now.

deploy-bot: deploy started by carla_oncall: config-hosted-prefetch-off v2026.03.15-rc1 -> progressing.

carla_oncall: Patching finished, rolling restart inference pool. Monitoring metrics: kvcache_size, avg_batch_tokens, token_latency, OOMCount.

ben_runtime: Seeing kvcache allocation rate drop within 30s. avg_batch_tokens down from 18k -> ~4k. Token latency improved but still elevated for in-flight requests. No new OOMs in last 3m.

frank_cs: Customer updates: both tenants report degraded throughput but no errors now. They're okay with slower response for now. I'll keep them updated.

dave_sre: Need root cause write-up later: looks like a regression in the prefetch heuristic that incorrectly prefetches full context windows for sessions with large prompt spikes. Also continuous batching combined short-timer window with unlimited max_merge_tokens.

gina_devex: For post-incident: suggest adding a circuit-breaker that rejects single-request contexts >100k tokens with a clear 4xx and guidance. Also add a kvcache soft-evict metric alert earlier and a prefetch backoff when memory pressure >70%.

erin_prod: Agreed. Action items: (A) Hotfix landed (prefetch off + batch window lowered) — status: mitigated. (B) Postmortem owner: ben_runtime. (C) Customer comms: frank_cs to finalize. (D) Prod change: add token-length reject + prefetch backoff — proposal due EOD.

carla_oncall: Handoff to next on-call @ben_runtime in 1h. I'm staying for 15m verification. If any OOMs reappear, escalate to dave_sre and revert to emergency fallback model (smaller variant) for affected tenants.

ben_runtime: Taking handoff. I'll follow up with a short runbook: `1) check OOMCount, 2) if OOMs reappear -> enable kvcache_soft_evict, 3) if still failing -> failover tenants to cpu-hosted fallback-model`. I'll post runbook in #eng-runtime.

frank_cs: Thanks — I'll update both customers: we've applied a temporary change that reduces memory pressure and are monitoring; we'll provide ETA for permanent fix after postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident mitigated -> status: partial; severity lowered to P2. Created incident ticket INC-2026-481. Postmortem assigned to ben_runtime, initial timeline due within 48h.

carla_oncall: Closing active paging. Marking this thread resolved for now. Keep any follow-ups in INC-2026-481. :white_check_mark:

title: eng-runtime
body:
eng-runtime

marta: Heads-up — I landed an experiment for opportunistic buffer borrowing between in-flight batches to cut allocations for short requests. Quick profiling attached below.

li: curious numbers. what did you see?

marta: micro-bench on A10, model=gpt-small, seq=512, concurrency=8.
- baseline peak GPU: 1.04GB
- with borrowing: 0.92GB (≈12% drop)
- p50 latency: ~unchanged
- p99 latency: +2% on canary traffic
- observed: KV cache churn up ~8% for some prefix-heavy traces

jamal: +2% tail is annoying. any clue where the tail comes from?

marta: flamegraphs point to a few extra mutex+reclaim stalls in slab allocator when a borrowed buffer gets returned late and forces a compact path. Not huge but shows at high concurrency.

carmen: can you paste the runtime flag and repro commands?

marta: sure. config toggle we used:

```\n# runtime.conf\nallocator.enable_buffer_borrowing = true\nallocator.borrow_max_lifetime_ms = 50\nallocator.borrow_prefer_slab = true\n```

repro: `./bench --model gpt-small --seq 512 --concurrency 8 --iters 200 --enable-borrow`

li: borrow_max_lifetime looks suspicious. if a cached KV lookup or kernel swap stalls for >50ms you get pinned buffers. maybe make it adaptive based on observed kernel latency.

marta: agree. quick follow-ups I tried: reduce lifetime to 20ms -> tail goes back down but mem savings drop to ~6%. Also tried jittered return so not all buffers compact at once — helped tail by ~0.7%.

jamal: what about kernel selection fallout? borrowing may change allocation patterns that prefer different kernel shapes. any regression there?

marta: good point. on one canary we saw more fallback to the small-matmul kernel for very short sequences (due to tighter memory pressure on scratchpads). That increased cpu-gpu syncs in a few traces.

carmen: safety checklist before rolling:
- gate behind runtime flag (yes)
- add telemetry: borrowed_bytes, borrow_count, borrow_hit_ratio, borrow_spill_count
- add canary autopause if p99 latency > baseline * 1.05
- run dedicated KV-heavy trace set overnight

marta: added metrics in the patch (names above) and a quick alert rule. infra-bot created a canary: runtimes/r1 borrow-experiment (canary id 2024-03-borrow).

infra-bot: deploy started: runtimes/r1:canary/2024-03-borrow -> 3 hosts.

li: prefer adding an allocator fallback that forces eager free of borrowed scratchpads when a kernel selector downgrade happens. That should avoid the small-matmul thrash.

marta: prototype pushed. logic: on kernel downgrade event -> scan borrowed list and try to convert borrow->own (i.e., copy to new buffer) or free opportunistically. cheap scan with a cap of 16 entries.

jamal: sounds good. can we also record "kernel_downgrade_count" and correlate with borrow_spill_count in dashboards?

carmen: agreed. if correlation > 0.3 on canary we roll back.

marta: plan for next steps:
1) reduce default borrow_max_lifetime -> 20ms
2) enable jittered returns
3) add kernel-downgrade-triggered eager-free path
4) run KV-heavy overnight test and collect the new metrics
5) if stable, roll to 20% of fleet for a week

li: one more thing — add a tiny unit test that simulates borrow race where return arrives after kernel swap to ensure no double-free. saw one flaky in local.

marta: noted, added test and made return path idempotent.

carmen: thanks. please attach the overnight trace when done and post results here. :thumbsup:

marta: will do — starting the overnight run now.

infra-bot: canary finished initial pass: 3 hosts, 6h, no alerts. metrics uploaded to /canaries/2024-03-borrow/summary.json

marta: initial glance looks promising: borrow_hit_ratio ~0.28, borrowed_bytes steady, kernel_downgrade_count low. posting full graphs shortly.

li: great, keep us posted.

product

Asha Rivera: Pushed a first-pass PRD for the Optimize recommendations initiative (batching, prefix caching, quant hints). Need alignment on scope, acceptance criteria, and launch checklist by EOD Fri. Doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/prd-optimize

Mike Lee: Nice framing. Two asks up front: make perf targets numeric (p50/p95 tokens/sec, token-cost %), and add explicit rollback criteria for any quality regression detected in prod.

Leah Chen: +1. Also please enumerate edge cases: user switches model mid-session, wide variance in prompt lengths (1->10k tokens), tokenizer mismatches that cause KV cache misses.

Samir Patel: Telemetry requirement: per-route live shadow eval for 10 days + an offline sim pass. Proposed pass thresholds: BERTScore/semantic-sim change < 1% and embedding cosine delta < 0.5% on critical routes.

Eva Morales: Product POV: customers driving this are (A) scale-up SaaS with cost pressure, (B) enterprise customers with tight latency SLOs, (C) regulated customers needing deterministic outputs. Recommend v1 prioritize A+B; defer heavy compliance customization to v2.

Mike Lee: Draft launch gates (suggestion):
- cost: >= 25% token-cost reduction on batching-heavy workloads (median batch >= 10) measured on canonical benchmark
- latency: p95 generation latency <= baseline + 12% on interactive flows
- quality: automated eval drift <= 1% on golden prompt sets
- ops: staged rollout 5% -> 25% -> 100%, rollback within 60m if error rate spikes > 3x or quality alerts trigger

Leah Chen: Edge-case acceptance bullets to add to PRD:
- small prompts (<64 tokens): batching should not add >75ms median latency
- very long contexts (>20k tokens): runtime must fall back to chunked streaming to bound memory
- quant incompatibility: fallback to float variant and emit anomaly event for triage

Samir Patel: Infra checklist items:
- canary dashboards (per-model, per-route, per-tenant)
- drift alarms + sampling traces for manual review
- sampling hooks (0.05% qps) for spot checks

Eva Morales: Prioritization for v1: 1) batching autosuggest + autoscale configs (highest cost impact), 2) conservative prefix/KV caching with TTLs and tenant isolation, 3) quantization advisory as an experimental opt-in. Thoughts?

Mike Lee: Agree. Quant advisory should be opt-in, behind an SDK/runtime flag, and not default.

Asha Rivera: UX acceptance for SDK/Console: (1) one-line opt-in flag in SDK, (2) per-route toggle in Console, (3) visible cost delta + latency delta in Console metrics.

deploy-bot: PRD v0.4 published by asha at 2026-03-19T16:02Z: https://redwood.internal/docs/prd-optimize?v=0.4

Samir Patel: Sample eval command for infra testbed:
```
run_eval --suite optimize_v1 --model rdx-neo --variants float32,quant8 --samples 2000
```

Mike Lee: Need an acceptance test that simulates mixed-tenant traffic to validate isolation and fairness of batching/caching.

Asha Rivera: Next steps: I'll update the PRD with numeric targets, edge-case examples, owners, and a short launch checklist. Quick sign-off sync tomorrow 10:30am (30m). If no blockers we'll scope v1 as batching autoscaling + basic prefix caching + SDK toggles.

Eva Morales: I'll own release playbook and customer comms; will invite CS to the sign-off for messaging feedback.

Samir Patel: I'll own canary automation and dashboards; Eva pls pair on metrics.

title: eng-runtime
body:
eng-runtime

alice: FYI - noticed a ~6% drop in prefix cache hit rate after last night's runtime rollout (kernel v2.4 -> v2.5). Affected endpoints are high-QPS chat routes. Profile attached in the ticket but wanted the team to see here.

ben: Oof. Do we know if this is a kernel scheduling change or keying mismatch? Any diffs in tokenizer/version or sysprompt flow? :eyes:

carol: We did push tokenizer v3.1 for a few models yesterday (minor whitespace normalization). That can flip keys for any prompt-normalization scheme that preserves raw spacing. Also we changed the toolcall JSON serializer to use default json.dumps which doesn't sort keys.

alice: Confirmed two hits in the trace: 1) tokenization produced different token sequences for identical user strings w/ extra trailing spaces, 2) toolcall arg ordering changed so key string differs. Example keys from span: 
```
# old key (stable-sort + keep-trailing-space)
{"prompt":"Hello world ","toolcall":"search","args":"{\"q\":\"x\",\"lang\":\"en\"}"}
# new key (strip-trailing + unsorted args)
{"prompt":"Hello world","toolcall":"search","args":"{\"lang\":\"en\",\"q\":\"x\"}"}
```

dan: Also saw a tiny system-prompt formatting change in the canary config - we removed a trailing newline in the assistant system prompt. That would change any key if system prompt is included verbatim.

ben: Two quick levers: (a) normalize prompt/systemprompt by trimming trailing whitespace and collapsing multiple spaces, (b) canonicalize tool/function call args (json.dumps(args, sort_keys=True)). We should also bake tokenizer_version into the cache key so tokenizer upgrades are explicit.

carol: Agreed. Proposal: cache key components = [model_id, kernel_hash, tokenizer_version, normalized_system_prompt, normalized_user_prompt, tool_signature + sorted_args]. Put tokenizer_version as opt-in for canaries to avoid churn.

alice: For rollout plan: 1) patch keying logic to normalize whitespace + sort tool args (small PR), 2) add tokenizer_version to key but default to current version for stable cohorts, 3) run warmup/backfill for top-200 prefixes before flipping canary. Also implement a compatibility fallback: on miss try alternate keys (pre-normalized) for 100ms budget.

ben: Warmup command I used locally: `./tools/prefetch --cohort=top200 --parallel=8 --dry-run` . For backfill we can run with --commit and throttle to avoid load spikes.

carol: I'll open the PR for canonicalization + tokenizer pinning. Will include unit tests showing `json.dumps(..., sort_keys=True)` vs not.

dan: QA will run canary and verify hit-rate telemetry over 24h. If we still see >2% regression revert and roll forward incremental fixes.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: canary/runtime-key-normalize -> infra-canary-3 (ETA ~10m) :rocket:

all-hands

Anya: Thanks everyone for the great questions during the security segment — I'm starting a quick follow-up thread to capture clarifications and owners.

Kevin: Quick one — what's the current SOC2 scope? Is Hosted API covered or just Dedicated/Private?

Anya: Short answer: Hosted (prod in us-east-1/us-west-2) and Dedicated are in scope for the current SOC2 report. Private (VPC/on-prem) is not included yet; it’s planned for the next audit cycle.

Maria: Can you confirm whether 'Hosted' scope includes EU regions (eu-west-1)? Customers asked during the Q&A.

Samir: From compliance: EU regions are covered for networking and access controls, but we cannot claim full SOC2 coverage for eu-west-1 until the next audit. So please avoid saying EU-hosted is SOC2-covered in customer comms.

Kevin: Got it. Related — what log retention times are we committing to for SOC2 evidence? I need to tell a customer how long ALB / CloudTrail / app logs are kept.

Samir: Current evidence retention policy for SOC2: infrastructure audit logs (CloudTrail / GCP audit) = 365 days, application-level structured logs = 90 days by default, and we keep host/infra syslogs for 365 days. We can provide extended retention as an enterprise add-on.

Maria: Can we get a short checklist of what to provide for customer questions? e.g., "do we have immutable audit trail, who holds keys" etc.

Anya: Good ask. High-level checklist for customer-facing answers: 1) SOC2 coverage statement (regions + services), 2) Audit log retention windows, 3) KMS key ownership model (Redwood-managed vs customer BYOK), 4) Evidence access process (how to request), 5) Roadmap commitment for Private/ISO scope.

Kevin: About KMS — during the all-hands someone asked if customers can bring their own keys (BYOK) for Hosted. Is that available?

Samir: Not for Hosted today. Hosted uses Redwood-managed keys stored in our KMS with customer data encrypted at rest. BYOK is available for Private and will be in roadmap for Dedicated in H2. We are working on ORK (operational key rotation) docs.

InfraBot: deploy-bot: new doc published -> /internal/compliance/soc2/evidence-matrix (version 2026-03-10)

Maria: Samir, can you paste the short audit log query snippet we usually use for evidence requests? Saves me time.

Samir: Sure — here's the typical CloudTrail/GCP audit example we hand auditors (redacted):

```
# CloudTrail example: find IAM policy changes
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=PutRolePolicy --start-time 2025-03-01 --end-time 2026-03-09
\n# GCP example (BigQuery):

Samir: Ownership: Compliance (Samir) owns the final evidence pack. Engineering (Maria) will pull raw logs/artifacts, and Infra (Kevin) will produce infrastructure proofs (configs, network diagrams). I'll own sign-off and redaction for customer delivery.

Maria: Action item: I'll start a checklist doc and collect the dashboard screenshots + log extracts. @Samir — can you confirm redaction rules (PII removal) and a deadline?

Samir: Redaction rules: remove full customer data and IPs where required; we keep metadata context. Deadline: please share a draft pack by 2026-04-03, target final by 2026-04-10 for early customer asks.

Anya: Thanks — last bit: ISO roadmap question from the Q&A. We plan ISO27001 in next 12 months; will update the roadmap doc next week with milestones.

Rin: quick flag - ran Banyan customer LoRA (banyan-lora-v1) on int4 quick-eval, seeing numeric drift + one truncation in long-invoice prompt. summary: pass 45/60, numeric-integrity 0.82 (float16 baseline 0.98).

Devin: command + top failures?

Rin: cmd:
```
./bench/run_quick_eval --model banyan-lora-v1 --quant=int4 --prompts=customers/banyan/smoke_prompts.json --out=/tmp/banyan_int4.json --batch=6
```

failures (redacted): id7: "£3,210.00" -> "£3,210" (missing cents), id16: "0.75" -> "0 .75" (space), id41: long invoice table truncated mid-row at ~140 tokens.

Arjun: tokenizer mismatch or quantization head scaling. Did you lock tokenizer/merges?

Rin: yes same tokenizer. Tried bias-correct toggle, no change.

Rin: KV excerpt:
```
kv[136]=<$>
kv[137]=<3>
kv[138]=<,>
kv[139]=<210>
kv[140]=<.>
kv[141]=<00>
kv[142]=<\n>
kv[143]=<$>  # dp down ~0.13 vs float16
kv[144]=<4>

Arjun: two quick mitigations: enable per-channel rescale on quantization, or run a one-pass bias-alignment calibration. Can you try both?

Rin: ran per-channel rescale -> numeric_integrity 0.94, pass 55/60, truncation fixed on repro. Perf impact ~+5% at 1024 context on our perf harness.

oncall: Copy. What services/endpoints are affected? Any pattern by model or route?
support_lead: Chat completions/time-series streaming most impacted. Embeddings seem mostly OK. Gateway 502s with 'upstream connect error or disconnect'. Happens across AZs, but spikes higher when cross-AZ traffic flows.
eng_sre_maya: Pulling metrics now — CPU/GPU fine. Error rate on gateway in us-east2 rose from 0.1% -> 8% at 10:12. 95p latency for front-door proxies up ~2.1s -> 9.8s. Starting tcpdump on gw-edge1.
network_eng_raj: Seeing microbursts and packet loss on the edge-facing interfaces for that POP. Interface counters: ifInErrors increasing and retransmit rate ~3-5% for flows to provider ASN 64512. Provider shows short BGP withdraws ~10s around the same time window.
customer_success_sam: Customer provided curl repro: ```curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -d '{"model":"rwd-std-1","prompt":"test"}' --max-time 60``` returns 502 after ~18s. They say it breaks mid-stream often.
eng_sre_maya: Logs from gateway: ``[10:13:05] upstream connect error or disconnect while reading response header from upstream``. Tracing shows connection resets between proxy and backend hosts, SYN retransmits visible.
infra_bot: routecheck: us-east2 gw-edge1 -> next-hop 198.51.100.9 (providerA) path: [(gw-edge1),(providerA-pe1),(providerA-pe2),(transit)] — flaps recorded: 10:12:08,10:12:19,10:12:29.
network_eng_raj: Provider NOC alerted (ticket PN-9912). They report congestion on egress link and transient queueing causing packet drops for flows larger than MSS ~1400. Also an eBGP flap correlated to maintenance at their transit POP.
oncall: Temporary mitigation ideas?
eng_sre_maya: Short-term: shift control plane traffic to alternative provider for that POP, increase upstream connection retries, and enable more aggressive keepalive. Also enable small prefix-specific reroutes for heavy customers.
network_eng_raj: I can BGP-prepend to other peers for the affected edge to steer traffic to providerB. Will coordinate with infra to ensure no routing loops. Also recommend setting qdisc params to reduce burst queue depth: `tc qdisc change dev eth0 root fq_codel limit 1000` on gateway hosts.
support_lead: Customer asked about compensation and whether Dedicated would have prevented this. CS wants a succinct message to pass along.
customer_success_sam: Draft message for ACME: "We observed transient packet loss and BGP instability at our us-east2 edge provider causing gateway 502s. We've applied routing changes and will monitor; next steps include provider mitigation and a postmortem. We're issuing a goodwill credit while we investigate." Thoughts?
eng_sre_maya: Good. Add that embeddings unaffected and provide repro curl + diagnostics to help them validate fix.
oncall: Implementing routing shift now.
eng_sre_maya: Applied iptables conntrack timeout bump for established TCP to reduce premature state expiry: `sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established=86400` — monitoring for side effects.
network_eng_raj: BGP prepends pushed to router set-1 at 10:22 UTC. ProviderB started seeing increased inbound for the prefixes. Early telemetry: dropped packets on providerA decreased from 4.7% -> 0.3% over next 2m.
prov_noc_bot: ProviderA: Confirmed transient congestion due to maintenance on PE. Bulk queue flushed at 10:25 UTC; working on permanant fix. PN-9912 updated.
eng_sre_maya: Error rate back down to 0.4% at 10:28, latencies recovering. Still keeping rate limits and circuit protections in place for 20m.
support_lead: CS will send the message now and offer 24h credit. Also opening billing ticket to evaluate prorated credits under SLA.
customer_success_sam: Sent to ACME with repro + ask to confirm if they see improvements. They replied: "Initial tests look good, generating tokens normally again. We'll monitor for the rest of the day." :thumbsup:
oncall: Action items: 1) network_eng_raj follow up with provider for RCA (PN-9912) 2) eng_sre_maya run postmortem and include metrics + pcap extract 3) support_lead coordinate customer credit + comms 4) infra to add fallback routing playbook to runbook.

eng_sre_maya: Saving tcpdump snippet and logs to /var/log/incidents/3344556677/pcap-snippet.pcap and uploading to internal S3 (link redacted). Will include `tcptrace` analysis in postmortem.
support_lead: Closing customer escalation for now pending final RCA. Marking incident SEV-2 -> monitoring. :eyes:

customer_success_sam: Customer confirmed stability at 12:02 UTC and is satisfied with credit. Closing CS-4821.

title: eng-platform
body:
eng-platform

Ivy Park: Weird alert this morningp50/p95 steady but p99 in the global latency pane spiked at 07:14. Endpoint split shows no spike. Timeline buckets line up. Any quick hypotheses?

Derek Sun: Usually one of three: retries included in one view, a tiny % routed to a slower pool, or the global rollup is using a sketch that smoothed the shard tails oddly.

Olivia Grant: We had an incident last month where 0.8% of traffic hit a warm-up replica and the merged-sketch completely missed that tail until someone inspected raw shard p99s.

Ivy Park: Ok. The console query is the default aggregate. Endpoint pane explicitly filters retries. So retries could be the delta.

Derek Sun: UX idea that we haven't used: show a compact "lineage chip" next to each percentile that reads like: "lineage: ingress+backend (retries:included) | samples: 9.8k | shards: 12". Click opens a tiny panel with a one-click "run raw vs merged compare" action. That action runs an internal query and returns the two numbers and an estimated cost.

Olivia Grant: I like "lineage chip" wording. Feels different than "badge" or "provenance" and may reduce copy-duplication in docs.

Derek Sun: Technical note: merged t-digest approaches can underestimate extreme tails when sketch K is low and one shard has disproportionate tail mass. Two paths: (A) detect and auto-increase K when total_count < threshold OR (B) compute per-shard p99 and report the max-of-shards as a safety warning. Both have tradeoffs.

Ivy Park: We should start with detection+annotation not a compute-heavy change. If lineagediff > X% then flag and surface the raw numbers for the oncall.

ops-bot: telemetry-job scheduled "pctl_lineage_daily" at 03:30 UTC to inject 1.5% slow fanout and compare merged_vs_raw p99.

Derek Sun: Also suggest adding an internal-only API endpoint: /internal/metrics/pctl_lineage?svc=...&start=... that returns stringified bucket metadata: "bucket_ts,ingress_count,backend_count,retries_included,sketch_k". Keep payload intentionally small and internal-only.

Olivia Grant: UX: make the panel show three small tabs: summary, compare (runs the canned cost-estimate query), and RCA quick-links (routing weights, quota events, recent canary promotes). The RCA links should deep-link into rollout logs.

Ivy Park: Can we auto-annotate timeseries when quota-fallback events or routing weight changes occur? The annotation should include percent_affected and policy_id. That would help correlate p99 jumps to policy flips.

Derek Sun: Agree. Also standardize on UTC-aligned buckets across all console panes. We had subtle shifts around DST tests that made things confusing.

Olivia Grant: Implementation plan: 1) lineage chip UI (FF internal-only), 2) /internal/metrics/pctl_lineage API, 3) telemetry job + alert if merged_vs_raw > 12% for 3 runs, 4) annotate routing/quota events.

canary-bot: canary deploy "console/lineage-chip-v1" started at 6990012369 :rocket:

Ivy Park: Nice. If the canary looks good let's flip to internal-only and add a 1-paragraph runbook for oncall: "if p99 mismatch: open lineage -> run compare -> check routing/quota links -> jump to traces". Keep it short.

Derek Sun: I'll prototype the API and put a cheap cost-estimate in the UI before the compare action runs. Olivia, can you mock the chip copy?

Olivia Grant: On it. I'll post mocks in #design and tag you.

Ivy Park: Thanks team. This should reduce noisy p99 pages and speed root-cause identification. :pray:

title: eng-security
body:
eng-security

maria: Quick sync — we're proposing an audit event schema bump to v2. TL;DR: remove actor_ip (privacy), add session_id (opaque), add kms_key_id for KMS-related ops, and rename resource_owner -> owner_id. We need a versioning strategy, customer-facing validation approach, and a migration/rollback plan. Also: how do RBAC changes affect actor mapping in events?

kevin: +1 on doing a bump with an explicit schema_version field. Suggest envelope like:
```json
{
  "schema_version": "audit_event.v2",
  "event": { /* actual payload */ }
}
```
This lets us route validators. Keep v1 support for streaming customers for at least 180 days.

alex: We should not remove fields silently. Proposal:
1) Add new fields in v2 (session_id, kms_key_id, owner_id).
2) Mark actor_ip deprecated in v1 responses and add a deprecation notice in the schema docs and the /audit/validate API.
3) Emit both actor_email and actor_id for 90 days when available so customers can transition RBAC lookups.

jess: KMS integration notes: kms_key_id should be the key identifier only (no secrets). Only populate when the event involves key material or KMS ops. We must confirm with privacy/compliance that session_id format is OK (opaque UUID recommended). Also ensure we never log plaintext key names or KMS responses.

maria: For customer-facing validation: offer a versioned JSON Schema and a validation endpoint: `/audit/validate?version=v2`. Response should include `status: pass|fail`, `errors: []`, and `warnings: []` for deprecated fields. Example: `{"status":"warn","warnings":["actor_ip deprecated"]}`.

kevin: Example curl for validator (draft):
```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d @sample-event.json \
  'https://api.redwood.ai/audit/validate?version=v2'
```
Validator response body: `{"status":"pass","schema_version":"audit_event.v2"}` or `{"status":"fail","errors":["missing session_id"]}`.

alex: Migration coordination checklist (high level):
- Announce: 30 days pre-rollout + Slack thread to customers + docs (owner: maria)
- Opt-in: early adopter flag (owner: product-eng)
- Dual-write: runtime emits both v1 and v2 envelopes for 60 days (owner: eng-runtime)
- Validation: expose /audit/validate and publish JSON Schema (owner: eng-security)
- Telemetry: add rollout metrics and regression alerts if failed validations spike (owner: observability)
- Cutover: set official deprecation date, then remove v1 after 180 days unless escalated (owner: product)

jess: RBAC caveat — if we change actor mapping from email to service_principal_id, some customers may rely on actor_ip + email to map anomalous access. Recommend we keep actor_email (if present) in events and add actor_id. Also add `actor_role_snapshot` (list of role ids at event time) as optional to aid audits. This interacts with privacy policy so sync with legal.

maria: Good call. Also: vuln triage/incident response implications — if schema changes confuse our SIEM parsers, we could miss alerts. Actions: update parser configs in security tools, run a staging replay of 48hrs of events through new schema validator and SIEM ingest (owner: eng-sre).

kevin: Quick JSON example of old vs new (small):
Old v1:
```json
{
  "actor_email": "alice@example.com",
  "actor_ip": "1.2.3.4",
  "resource": "/models/foo",
  "action": "deploy"
}
```
New v2 envelope:
```json
{
  "schema_version": "audit_event.v2",
  "event": {
    "actor_id": "user_1234",
    "actor_email": "alice@example.com",
    "session_id": "uuid-opaque-...",
    "owner_id": "org_987",
    "resource": "/models/foo",
    "action": "deploy",
    "kms_key_id": "projects/.../keys/abc"
  }
}
```
Note: we keep actor_email for compatibility and to support customer mappings during transition.

deploy-bot: schema-validator service deployed to staging at `stg-audit-validate.redwood.ai` :white_check_mark:

maria: Action items and owners:
- Publish RFC + JSON Schema v2 (maria, 5 business days)
- Staging validator + SIEM replay (eng-sre, 7 days)
- Customer migration guide + sample parsers (docs + solutions eng, 10 days)
- Rollout calendar (product + eng, announce in 30 days)

alex: Also add a compatibility header for streaming clients: `X-Audit-Schema-Version: audit_event.v2` in streamed envelopes so clients can switch parsers quickly.

jess: I'll kick off the privacy/legal check about actor_ip removal and session_id format.

maria: OK, I'll draft the RFC and the customer announcement today. If no objections, we'll start the staging validator run tomorrow. :thumbsup:

kevin: :thumbsup:

alex: :+1:

(End of thread)

title: architecture
body:
architecture

noah: recap from today's incident: we had 30s of EU network tail that led to ~120 tenant migrations in 2m. main pain was cold-KV and a handful of hard-residency tenants bouncing unexpectedly. want to propose a probe-sample + voting model before promoting a region.

meera: sounds good. can you outline the voting model?

noah: idea: when local p95 crosses threshold, instead of immediate swap we 1) schedule lightweight workload-probes (kv lookup + small model inference) to candidate regions, 2) sample N proxies (not all) to avoid thundering, 3) compute a vote across probes + local metrics over window W, and 4) require majority+margin to promote. also honor residency stamp which can veto cross-border promotions.

ako: important: probes must be non-PII and mirror typical request shape. also sampling strategy should prioritize tenants with recent swaps. we should avoid probing every tenant to save cost.

meera: agree. propose probe_config:
```
probe_sample_pct: 5            # percent of proxies for tenant
probe_types: ["kv","model-lite"]
window_sec: 20
vote_margin_pts: 10
min_votes: 3
max_probes_per_minute: 1000
```

noah: residency veto: if x-residency is hard -> veto unless emergency_override. soft -> treat as vote penalty (e.g., -delta). veto must be surfaced in audit logs.

ops-bot: deployment note: probe-vote v0.1 -> staged canary: 2025-07-22T06:00Z.

ako: two more pieces: 1) rollback safety net: after promote, monitor for 30s; if post-promote tail increases beyond threshold, automatically roll back to previous region with a higher cooldown and mark tenant as "unstable" for longer. 2) prewarm ticketing: if promotion pending, enqueue prewarm and block promotion until a minimal prewarm success ratio achieved unless emergency_override.

meera: rollback auto is risky. needs operator config: auto_rollback_enabled=true|false and a clear window/threshold. also ensure rollback emits high-sev alert and creates a paged incident if instability persists.

noah: agreed. default disable auto-rollback for hard-residency tenants. config sketch:
```
promote_policy:
  use_probe_vote: true
  probe_window_sec: 20
  vote_margin_pts: 12
  min_votes: 3
  residency_veto: true
  auto_rollback_enabled: true
  rollback_window_sec: 30
  rollback_threshold_pct: 15  # post-promote p95 increase pct to trigger rollback
  post_rollback_cooldown_sec: 600
```

ako: where to keep per-tenant unstable state? control-plane DB with a short-lived cache in proxies. mark tenants as unstable with reason tags: PREWARM_FAIL, ROLLBACK_HIT, RESIDENCY_BLOCK, EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE. proxies consult cached unstable flag to avoid repeated immediate swaps.

meera: security: sec-bot, prewarm/probe traffic touches only anonymized keys and returns non-PII metrics. also probes must not cause cross-border model state writes.

sec-bot: noted. will require probe payload audit and whitelist for allowed endpoints. also mandate encryption of probe headers and hash-only consent-stamp in logs.

ops-bot: telemetry checklist: emit probe_event (tenant, probe_type, result), vote_snapshot (scores, votes_for, votes_against), promote_decision (from,to,reason), rollback_event (from,to,reason). add gauge: tenant_unstable{tenant}.

noah: tests: unit test voting math, integration: simulate 1k tenants with mixed residency, chaos: transient p95 blips vs real node loss, E2E: canary migrate 50 tenants with prewarm to measure SLO impact.

ako: runtime note: proxies should accept a shift_plan with epoch and sample_probes token. proxies perform probes asynchronously and report back. control-plane should timebox probe collection to avoid blocking decisions indefinitely. if probes time out, fall back to conservative behavior (no promotion unless emergency).

meera: operator tools: dry-run to show which tenants would move, manual promote/rollback endpoint, and a "stabilize" action that pins tenant to region for configurable TTL. everything should be auditable.

noah: next steps I'll author RFC section for probe-vote + rollback safety with config defaults and runbook for emergency override. please comment on the draft when I open it.

ako: I'll prototype probe harness and prewarm ticket queue; will add privacy gating.

meera: I'll wire telemetry and operator UI mocks.

ops-bot: reminder: RFC draft link will be posted in #architecture when available.

sec-bot: security review required before canary.

noah: thanks all. if no objections I'll open the RFC tomorrow. :thumbsup:

title: eng-runtime
body:
eng-runtime

mike: Heads up — saw a sharp drop in prefix-cache hit-rate after the attn kernel swap on canary (~1949990999). p50 workloads went from ~82% -> ~57%. Rolling up here to coordinate.

anna: ack. paste the numbers + canary id? :eyes: 

mike: Canary id: run/attn-kernel-v3b (deployed by ci-bot). Summary:
- baseline (before): pfx_hit=0.82, tok_cost=1.0x
- after canary: pfx_hit=0.57, tok_cost=1.3x, p95 latency +18%
- traffic: sample set = 50k requests from prod-sampled route

mike: quick perf dump from a sample worker:
```
2026-03-17 11:02:03 worker-7 perf: kv_prefix_hits=2850 kv_prefix_misses=2120
cpu_util=72% gpu_util=63%
kernel_variant=attn_v3b quant_profile=fp16_8bit_round
batching_mode=shared_batching_enabled
```

sam: we also rolled a quant-profile tweak in the same window (fp16->fp16_8bit_round) for kernel perf. could be interacting with keying? cc @lee

lee: possible vector: fused-attn kernels change intermediate KV layout + shared-batch routing enabled by default. Two suspects:
1) key normalization now picks up raw tensor shape metadata in a different ordering -> inconsistent keys
2) batching merge/padding makes prefix slices different, changing the canonical hash

anna: can you repro by toggling shared-batch off? if hit-rate recovers that's a big signal.

mike: repro steps I ran locally:
1) checkout runtime@attn-v3b
2) start a single worker with `BATCH_SHARED=0 KV_KEY_CANONICALIZE=1`
3) replay sample workload (script attached)
Result: pfx_hit=0.80 (almost back). With shared_batch=1 pfx_hit=0.56.

lee: suggests padding/merge ordering difference. Did you test canonicalize=0?

mike: with canonicalize=0 + shared_batch=1 => pfx_hit=0.58. canonicalize=1 + shared_batch=1 => 0.57. So canonicalize alone doesn't fix it; shared_batch seems biggest factor.

ops-bot: incident-alert: prefix-cache hit-rate anomaly detected on prod-sampled route — threshold breached at 2026-03-17T11:05:00Z :warning:

sam: could quant rounding subtly change float representation and affect hash if we include embeddings in key composition? @mike any embedding diffs?

mike: dumped first 10 prefixes for a reproducible request across variants. Diffs look like padding bytes and shape metadata — not embeddings themselves.
```
# canonicalized key before: keyhash=0x7a1b..., shape=(1,64,768)
# after: keyhash=0x3f2c..., serialized_meta=[pad_right=8, merged_batch_index=2]
```

lee: then make keying independent of transient batching metadata. I'll open a PR to strip batching fields and add a deterministic padding sentinel.

anna: short-term mitigations?

mike: suggestions:
- rollback canary to attn-v3a (recovers hit-rate)
- disable shared_batching on canary hosts
- add a hashing-salt that ignores batch routing fields

sam: are we scheduling a rollback? coordinate with releases.

lee: prototyping a lightweight key-normalizer. will run offline replay with shared_batch=1 to check hit-rate recovery.

mike: experiment matrix (ETA ~2h):
- baseline: v3a shared_batch=1
- v3b shared_batch=1 (current)
- v3b shared_batch=0
- v3b shared_batch=1 + key-normalizer
Collecting pfx_hit, tok_cost, p95 latency.

anna: post perf traces (nvprof / flamegraphs) if you see kernel or CPU regressions.

title: eng-infra
body:
eng-infra

alex: Heads-up: opened PR 1347 to add a new 'edge' subnet + PrivateLink endpoint in us-west-2 and update TGW attachments. plan looks OK but I want a quick sanity check before apply: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1347 :wave:

maya: thanks. please don't apply yet — last time we saw intermittent 502s when endpoint service and route propagation happened out of order. can you paste the tf snippets?

alex: sure — here's the relevant part from modules/network/main.tf:

```hcl
resource "aws_subnet" "edge" {
  vpc_id     = var.vpc_id
  cidr_block = var.edge_subnet_cidr
  availability_zone = var.az
  tags = merge(var.common_tags, { "k8s.io/role/elb" = "1" })
}

resource "aws_vpc_endpoint" "redwood_privatelink" {
  vpc_id            = var.vpc_id
  service_name      = var.endpoint_service_name
  vpc_endpoint_type = "Interface"
  subnet_ids        = [aws_subnet.edge.id]
  security_group_ids = [aws_security_group.pl_endpoint.id]
}

resource "aws_ec2_transit_gateway_vpc_attachment" "tgw_attach" {
  transit_gateway_id = var.tgw_id
  vpc_id             = var.vpc_id
  subnet_ids         = [aws_subnet.edge.id]
  tags = var.common_tags
}
```

sam: looks normal, but TF may create the endpoint before the TGW attachment or vice versa. the real failure we've hit is route table assoc happening before propogation, creating a temporary blackhole for services behind the endpoint.

ryan: exact problem: when the aws_route that points to the tgw attachment is created while the attachment is still 'pending', the route shows up but traffic is dropped. adding an explicit dependency or using `depends_on = [aws_ec2_transit_gateway_vpc_attachment.tgw_attach]` on the route resource fixes it. also `create_before_destroy` on subnets helped in a separate cutover.

alex: got it. the PR currently lets the module order handle it implicitly. i'll add `depends_on` to the aws_route resources that reference the tgw attachment and to the endpoint's subnet association.

maya: also FYI the plan shows the NAT GW getting replaced because of EIP rotation (we're rotating the eip pool). plan snippet:

```
  # aws_eip.edge_nat_eip must be replaced
-/+ resource "aws_eip" "edge_nat_eip" {
    ~ id = "eip-0123" -> (known after apply)
  }

  # aws_nat_gateway.edge_nat will be replaced because its eip changes
  ~ resource "aws_nat_gateway" "edge_nat" {
    ~ allocation_id = "eipalloc-abc" -> (known after apply)
  }
```

sam: replacing NAT GW in a busy AZ caused some ephemeral connectivity issues last rollout. recommend doing nat EIP rotation in a maintenance window or creating a new nat + switch routes gradually.

alex: plan: I'll split the PR into two smaller applies — 1) create subnet + privatelink + TGW attachment (with depends_on and a null_resource wait), 2) rotate EIPs and swap NAT routes in a follow-up. that should reduce blast radius.

maya: sounds good. i'll review the first PR today. can you add a null_resource with a local-exec that polls `aws ec2 describe-transit-gateway-attachments` until state=="available"? small example:

```hcl
resource "null_resource" "wait_for_tgw_attach" {
  depends_on = [aws_ec2_transit_gateway_vpc_attachment.tgw_attach]

  provisioner "local-exec" {
    command = <<EOT
for i in {1..30}; do
  state=$(aws ec2 describe-transit-gateway-attachments --filters Name=resource-id,Values=${aws_ec2_transit_gateway_vpc_attachment.tgw_attach.id} --query "Attachments[0].State" --output text)
  if [ "$state" = "available" ]; then exit 0; fi
  sleep 10
done
exit 1
EOT
  }
}
```

ryan: +1 on wait, and add a small delay (30s) after available before creating routes to let AWS propagate. also run the apply in one AZ first (canary) as maya suggested.

infra-bot: terraform-plan-bot: Plan for PR 1347 completed successfully (no errors). See checks -> infra/terraform.

alex: thanks all — i'll push the split PR and add the explicit depends_on/null_resource. pinging @maya for review when ready :pray: 

maya: will do. remind me to run the canary apply during low traffic window. :white_check_mark:

eng-runtime

sam: Heads up - saw a ~3x CPU increase on host-proxy after the 03:20 canary. p99 decode+serialize latency spiked, and syscall rate jumped way up.
perf-bot: alert: host-proxy cpu > 75% (2m) - group: eng-runtime - check 3250017876
maya: I saw that in the dashboard too. traces show a lot of tiny write syscalls from the streaming path.
sam: here's a short top-of-pprof (30s sample):
(pprof) top
Samples: 120 of 30 @ 0.25s
 38 31.7% sys_writev
 22 18.3% ingress::stream_frame_serialize
 14 11.7% grpc::net::write_small
 10 8.3% tokenizer::emit_token
 8 6.7% kv_cache::lookup_miss
jordan: interesting - kv_cache::lookup_miss is showing up. are we getting more cache misses for the micro requests?
eli: logs correlate: short requests (<200B) have ~3x more KV misses. Might be because we do per-chunk metadata lookups when emit_token fires.
maya: hypothesis: (1) tokenizer producing lots of tiny frames, (2) gRPC proxy sending many small writev syscalls (no coalescing), (3) per-chunk KV lookups causing blocking/fs/syscall churn. result = syscall storm + CPU in write path.
sam: repro I used:
# synthetic: many tiny streaming requests
for i in $(seq 1 2000); do
  grpcurl -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' -plaintext host-proxy:8080 inference.Service/StreamGen >/dev/null &
done
wait
jordan: did a wrk-style burst with 1k concurrent tiny POSTs, same p99 uplift. disabling tcp_nodelay on proxy reduced syscalls ~30% but added 4-5ms p50.
eli: kv hit-rate by req size (1h): "<200B: 65% , 200-1k: 87%, >1k: 94%" - tiny reqs hit more misses.
maya: short-term mitigations: (A) enable small-write coalescing in proxy (buffer up to ~4k or 1ms), (B) add tiny in-process per-connection KV cache to cut miss penalty for micro-requests. low-risk to try.
sam: long-term: improve batching heuristics so runtime avoids emitting per-token frames for single-token responses and offer a micro-batch mode for chat edges. also tune gRPC initial window/SETTINGS to reduce control frame noise.
jordan: will prototype proxy writev coalesce PR today - buffer until size>=4k or deadline 800us then flush. will run perf A/B.
eli: adding instrumentation: per-request KV hit/miss tag + trace samples linking to syscall counts to validate if misses cause sync I/O.
maya: I'll flip on local coalesce and run canary; also experiment with SO_SNDBUF + writev to see kernel coalescing.
sam: actions: jordan -> coalesce PR (ETA EOD), eli -> KV hit instrumentation (ETA 6h), maya -> canary + kernel tuning (ETA 3h). regroup in #eng-runtime 1PM PT.
jordan: noted. will run tcp_nodelay matrix and post results.
eli: for per-connection in-proc mini-cache, consider LRU 32-64 entries; micro-requests are transient but can be hot for certain customers.
maya: agreed, keep it simple first.
sam: thanks. pls paste traces/pprof in thread. :mag: :thumbsup:

marie (PM): Quick sync — we need to pick priorities for the cost/latency playbook work that feeds the inference advisor. Customer asks are stacking: batching recs, caching suggestions, quant profiles, and eval-triggered alerts. I sketched an MVP below — please react with :thumbsup: or call blockers

ajay (eng): SGTM. MVP proposal: 1) batching heuristics + route-level suggestions 2) prefix/KV cache detection + auto-suggest 3) per-model quant profiles + runtime fallback 4) eval hook -> alerting. Keep everything toggleable per-customer.

lina (ml): For quant, start with vetted 8-bit profiles and a conservative fallback. We need clear eval thresholds for acceptable quality delta — proposing 2% absolute metric drop as default, but adjustable.

anya (cs): Pilot candidates: AcmeSearch (very cost-sensitive) and NovaDocs (willing to experiment). Acme explicitly asked for conservative quant.

sam (sre): Note: batching helps throughput but increases tail latency variance. We must expose per-route SLOs and a low-batch fallback path. Also need circuit-breakers for cache issues.

ajay (eng): Telemetry requirements: per-route token cost delta, cache hit rate, 95/99 latencies, and counts of automatic fallbacks. Those should feed the console and alerts.

marie (PM): Proposed launch criteria: 1) Pilot w/ 2 customers for 4 weeks 2) Demonstrated >=10% cost improvement or <=10% latency regression in pilot 3) Eval alert precision > 95% (false positive tolerance) 4) SDK + Console toggles for pilot admins (console can be minimal). Thoughts?

kyle (data): Can we add an offline simulator that replays sampled traces to estimate econ impact per config? That would let product recommend settings before rollout.

lina (ml): We can extend the eval harness to compute quality delta per quant profile and run batching simulation for tail effects. Might need a small dataset from pilot customers.

anya (cs): I can surface sample traces and coordinate pilot onboarding. Acme will likely require white-glove config at first.

ajay (eng): Rough eng estimates: backend + routing changes 6 wks, console UX 2 wks, integration/pilot 2 wks -> ~10 wks. If we cut console to a CLI-only launch, we can shorten to ~7 wks.

marie (PM): Tradeoff is speed vs. onboarding friction. Faster pilot means quicker feedback but more manual ops. Which way do folks lean?

sam (sre): Safety requirements: automatic fallback to non-quant/model-variant if eval alerts spike or latency exceeds threshold. Cache poisoning protection is mandatory.

lina (ml): For eval-triggered alerts, propose triggers: quality drop > X over Y eval runs OR production feedback regression > Z over N samples. Standardize metrics (ROUGE, embedding-sim, LLR) by model type.

ajay (eng): Design sketch for policy config (JSON-driven):

Laura (PM): Quick sync — proposed sprint charter for Private Stack Connectivity. Goal: get a beta out for VPC/on-prem installer that reduces networking friction for customers. Concrete launch criteria below, please react with :thumbsup: if we can commit this sprint.
Shiv (Eng): high-level looks reasonable. We need to be explicit about what "minimal network surface" means — my ask: list the 3 supported egress patterns and declare which we treat as experimental.
Maria (Field SE): from field calls — most customers expect to keep their existing NAT/GW and only need outbound connectivity to Redwood control plane + optional metrics sink. If we advertise "zero-touch" it must work with behind-NAT setups.
Laura (PM): Good point. Draft support matrix I propose: 1) NATed egress (supported), 2) static egress IP (supported, docs + templates), 3) reverse-proxy/relay (experimental). We should call out the IP preservation caveat for migrations.
Anita (CS): Top customer (FinCorp) asked for an upgrade plan that preserves their egress IPs and avoids certificate churn. They'll pilot if we can guarantee <= 5m disruption for the operator upgrade and a rollback path.
Shiv (Eng): Implementation note — operator: add a `safe-mode` flag that keeps old dataplane running until new control handshake confirmed. That gives fast rollback. Cost: extra disk + migration logic.
Tom (Release): From release side, we need an automated canary: 10% installs use canary operator image, monitor health checks + tracer latency for 30m before rollout. If any tracer >200ms or >1% errors we abort. Can we wire that into the deploy-bot? @deploy-bot please confirm available gating hooks.
deploy-bot: Canary gating hooks available. Runbook: `./scripts/canary-checks --duration=30m --latency-threshold=200` will return non-zero exit on failure.
Maria (Field SE): Also add explicit troubleshooting checklist: how to confirm NAT egress, how to patch iptables on older kernels, and when to ask for customer netops help. Those are frequent support pages.
Laura (PM): Launch criteria (final proposal):
- Beta release to 3 pilot customers (including FinCorp)
- Installer presets: `default` (NAT-friendly), `static-egress`, `relay` (experimental)
- Upgrade path validated with <=5m mean disruption and documented rollback steps
- Network runbook + IP-preserve migration guide published
- Console flags for canary gating and `safe-mode` operator enabled
If we miss any of the above we ship as alpha not beta.
Shiv (Eng): Est effort: 3 sprints to get `safe-mode` + canary wiring + installer presets, plus 1 sprint for docs and field validation. We can compress if we drop `relay` from MVP.
Anita (CS): Field readiness: we can coordinate the pilots once we have the `static-egress` docs. I'll prep customer comms template and rollback SLA language.
Tom (Release): I'll add the gating job and ensure image tags follow `privdeploy-canary-<sha>` pattern. Also add a post-rollout quick-check list for oncall.

title: eng-runtime

eng-runtime

alexa: Heads-up — saw a +30% tail latency on FP8 on a small L40S rack after the last transformer-engine bump. repro in staging.

ravi: ugh, details? kernel selector change?

alexa: looks like a tiling/launch heuristic flip. TE now picks 128x32 tiles for matmul on seq_len=2048 which used to be 64x64. profiler shows increased L2 traffic.

maria: @alexa can you paste the perf top / nvprof snippet?

alexa: pasted below:
```
# perf summary (staged run)
GPU SM util: 92%
L2 read throughput: 1.8 GB/s (up 3x vs baseline)
DRAM throughput: 820 MB/s
warp_serialize stalls: +12%
kernel: te_fma_fp8_tile_128x32  48ms
kernel: te_fma_fp8_tile_64x64   34ms
```

jon: so selector picked 128x32 but 64x64 is faster for that shape. selector heuristic must have flipped due to occupancy calc change.

ravi: any correlation with thermal/clock changes? L40S clocks were pinned lower in that batch.

alexa: clocks were 1095MHz steady. baseline runs had 1200MHz. but even after normalizing, 128x32 is still slower by ~15%.

maria: hmm KV cache behavior? Did a cold cache cause longer kernels because of KV replays hitting slowpath?

alexa: traced a sample convo; KV hit ratio drops ~7% with the new burst batching shape, causing extra memops. snippet:
```
[trace] kv_cache_hits: 0.93 -> 0.86 during spike
[trace] microbatch shape: [1,4,8] -> [1,8,4] after batching heuristic change
```

jon: That microbatch reorder is suspicious. Our batching heuristics try to maximize batch dims but can change memory layout for KV.

ravi: action plan? rollback selector? add a safety check that compares tile latency estimate vs historical prior to switching?

maria: also surface a guard in TE config: TE_TILE_TOLERANCE=0.1 (if new tile is >10% slower than baseline, don't switch).

alexa: I can produce a small repro and telemetry patch to log selector candidate latencies for 24h. will also pin tile size for the failing workload.

jon: +1. add a perf-bot alert when L2 read throughput spikes >2x baseline for FP8 kernels. perf-bot can post flamegraphs.

perf-bot: noted. creating alert rule fp8_l2_spike_3654. will upload flamegraph to /artifacts/fw/3654321000.svg when triggered. :gear:

ravi: quick mitigation — roll back the selector heuristic CL in canary and re-run the 3 sample workloads. if stable, push rollback to prod.

alexa: starting a canary rollback patch now. will attach microbench numbers in this thread.

maria: thanks. also add a small eval to check generation quality; our FP8 calibration didn't change quant bias but tiling might slightly perturb math order and outputs. we should verify no regressions.

alexa: yes — will include 50 prompts regression check. expected QoQ delta <0.2%.

jon: appreciate it. keep this thread updated with numbers.
