title: support
body:
support

Maya S.: heads up — acme-prod reported a sudden drop in vectors/sec around 04:06 UTC, tokens/sec looks normal. customers getting slow responses and occasional 502/504. model: redwood-embed-large, region: us-east-1.

Tom R.: do we have GPU queue metrics for those hosts? queue depth or stalled kvcache ops?

Eli (infra): pulling metrics now. initial glance: GPU-util steady ~45%, but gpu-queue-length spiked to ~48 for a subset. interestingly kvcache-waits increased too. attaching a short snippet from the monitoring window.

Eli (infra): ``
2026-03-12T04:05:00Z host=gpu-14 queue_len=3 kvcache_wait_ms=2 gpu_util=44
2026-03-12T04:06:00Z host=gpu-14 queue_len=48 kvcache_wait_ms=120 gpu_util=46
2026-03-12T04:06:30Z host=gpu-14 queue_len=52 kvcache_wait_ms=180 gpu_util=47
2026-03-12T04:07:00Z host=gpu-14 queue_len=6 kvcache_wait_ms=3 gpu_util=43
``

Maya S.: that spike aligns with customer ticket timestamps. raquel from Acme posted curl and repro steps — raquel, can you paste the payload?

Raquel - AcmeProd: yup. I posted a minimal repro earlier but here it is again. we send batched vectors with varying inputs. payload used: ``curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer XXX' -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-large","input":["short","a bit longer sentence","another one"],"batch_size":64}'`` — response succeeds but vectors/sec drops and latency climbs. also noticed one return had dim=128 while expected 1536 (we validated client side).

Tom R.: dim mismatch is concerning. do we see any model fallback or quantized variant being routed? smart-routing logs?

Eli (infra): checking routing audit: around the window a few requests were routed to a fallback variant (redwood-embed-large-q8) due to a transient slot allocation failure in the primary pool. fallback should still return same dim but we saw an anomalous proto in the pipeline that zeroed the vector. logs: ``FALLBACK_ROUTE host=gpu-14 -> model=redwood-embed-large-q8 reason=slot_alloc_fail``

Maya S.: so two correlated problems: routing -> fallback -> some responses with wrong dim/empty vectors, and batching/queue spike that throttled throughput. can we repro in a sandbox? raquel, any hints about input size distribution?

Raquel - AcmeProd: 95% short (<32 tokens), a few 512-token docs. we use single HTTP request with batch_size=64 and rely on the API's batching. the strange dim=128 happened only once in ~10k requests.

Tom R.: plan: 1) capture a full trace (request id level) for affected window, 2) reproduce with same batch_size+token distribution against canary with instrumented runtime (kvcache + fallback verbose), 3) short-term mitigation: pin Acme to dedicated pool to avoid fallback until root cause fixed.

Eli (infra): I grabbed trace ids: trace=trc-20260312-04-06-9a7c. there are entries showing an early deserialize failure in the output serializer: "unexpected payload length" then we defaulted vector to zeros and returned HTTP 200. that's why dims were wrong. adding the exact log: ``[04:06:23] ERROR serializer: unexpected payload length (expected 1536, got 0) request=trc-20260312-04-06-9a7c``

Maya S.: ugh we return 200 with empty vector? that's a customer-facing bug. can we change to 5xx when serialization fails?

Tom R.: yes, we should not surface zeros silently. raising a quick PR to change the error path. will also flip a feature flag so fallbacks return 5xx if vector dim mismatch detected.

Eli (infra): repro checklist I ran:
1) run a loop to POST 1000 requests with batch_size=64 and token distribution matching Acme.
2) simulate a slot allocation failure by marking 1/12 slots as unhealthy to force some fallback routing.
3) watch for serializer errors and queue spikes.

Eli (infra): short repro script snippet: ``for i in $(seq 1 1000); do curl -s -X POST $URL -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d @payload.json >> /tmp/resp.log; sleep 0.02; done`` and payload.json contains a mix of short and ~512 token strings.

Raquel - AcmeProd: thanks — if you can repro I can validate on our side. pinning to dedicated pool would help immediately.

Maya S.: ops, can we pin Acme to their dedicated pool now? they have a contract.

deploy-bot: scheduled action: pin-customer-pool acme-prod -> dedicated-pool-7 (ETA 2m) :white_check_mark:

Tom R.: opened tickets: INF-1259 (fix serializer to return 5xx on dim mismatch), INF-1260 (fallback routing harden), and CS-5421 (customer follow-up + mitigation). I'll post PR links when ready.

Eli (infra): follow-up: after pinning, vectors/sec normalized and no further dim mismatches observed for Acme. still need to root cause why slot_alloc_fail happened (investigating autoscaler thrash).

Maya S.: thanks team. next steps: triage autoscaler events around 04:05–04:07, merge serializer fix ASAP, and communicate mitigation to Acme. I'll update the ticket and loop in support for the customer note. :thumbsup:

title: architecture
body:
architecture

Ravi: quick note from today's multi-region rehearsal: our fallback path allowed writes into a non-authoritative region for tenant R-19. residency enforcement gap.
Nora: short version: proxy fallback didn't validate current placement with control plane and accepted writes.
Igor: was it because of a stale cache?
Ravi: yes, proxy had a cached placement that said 'local-ok' and on failover it didn't re-check placement TTL.
Nora: proposal: two changes - (1) cheap placement stamp header from control plane on allocation (stamp + expiry) that proxy verifies on failover; (2) placement-cache must consult control plane on mismatch or expiry before accepting writes.
Igor: sounds fine. For (1) prefer HMACed stamp instead of full asymmetric sigs to keep CPU down. include region and expiry: e.g. X-Placement: region=ap-southeast;exp=1700001000;mac=...
Ravi: agreed, HMAC + short TTL (<=5m). If proxy sees a placement mismatch and no valid stamp, it should return 451 and create an incident draft.
Nora: operator override: allow a time-limited override token via Console that requires two approvers. token must be logged in audit trail.
Igor: add metrics: rejected_fallbacks_total, override_tokens_issued, stale_cache_hits. dashboard to SRE and legal.
Ravi: CI tests: a small harness that injects partitions and asserts no writes outside allocated region unless override consumed. add to chaos pipeline.
ci-bot: scheduled job created: residency-chaos-test -> nightly.
Nora: I'll draft a short RFC for the placement-stamp + cache-change and update runbook with override flow. target: canary by 2026-03-27.

Maya: Heads-up — I ran into a nasty onboarding gotcha in the embeddings quickstart. The README shows a JS snippet that hardcodes the API key directly into the client constructor (`new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: 'YOUR_KEY' })`). Folks are copy/pasting that into sample apps and accidentally committing keys.

Aj: Oof, saw one of those in last week's onboarding session. Users paste into examples then push to GH. We should never encourage that pattern — env vars only.

Olivia: I'll push a small fix. Plan: replace inline key with `process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY` in the JS sample and `os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY']` in the Python snippet. Also add a short warning box in the README about not checking in secrets.

Olivia: Yep — there are two divergent samples. I'll update the code blocks and add a short note that snippets are pinned to SDK version X.Y.Z and link to the SDK changelog.

Aj: Can we add a CI check that fails if `YOUR_KEY` or `API_KEY` appears in the repo (especially in `docs/` and `examples/`)? A simple grep in the doc-lint job would help catch future copy/paste footguns.

Olivia: On it. I'll add a doc-lint job entry and a one-line GH action that greps for common secret placeholders. Quick patch will be in PR #4587.

sasha_sales: FYI Prospect Orbitary asked us to validate perf for their conversational checkout flow. Requirements: sustain 250 qps, handle short spikes to 720 qps for 15-25s, and p95 < 200ms for interactive replies. They want a two-page runbook, quick cost delta hosted vs dedicated, and a short security appendix.
omar_se: Got it. Do we have their sample prompt set and average token counts? that'll affect batching and GPU memory.

body:
incidents

incident-bot: PAGING — Elevated 5xx + gateway timeouts observed for /v1/generate in us-west-2. error_rate=11.8% (3m), p95=3.6s, failures=503/504/timeouts. Paging SRE on-call: @anna :rotating_light:

anna: Ack, I'm on. Thanks for the page. Can someone pull top-traffic routes and model variants?

jess: Support seeing customer-reported timeouts from Acme Corp and NovaAnalytics, started ~17:24 UTC. They've hit repeated 500s.

mike: Looking at runtime dashboards — scheduler shard scheduler-7 has queue depth jump: +1200 pending, inflight batches stalled. Batcher backlog showing long-lived large-batch windows, appears head-of-line blocking smaller batches. KV cache growth for that shard is also high.

anna: Good data. Immediate mitigation plan (short list):
1) Throttle gateway traffic to /v1/generate from 100% -> 50% for us-west-2.
2) Disable large-batch-heuristic on scheduler-7 (force smaller batch size).
3) Reroute a percentage of traffic to fallback region (us-east-1) and compatible model variant.
4) Notify customers and set support banner.

omar: I can do the gateway throttle now. Running toggle: 

```bash
# throttle /v1/generate to 50% in us-west-2
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://gateway-api.internal/config/route/throttle \
  -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","region":"us-west-2","pct":50}'
```

omar: throttle applied, response: {"route":"/v1/generate","region":"us-west-2","pct":50} :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Route throttle change deployed to edge fleet (us-west-2) — rollout 10% -> 100% complete.

mike: On runtime side, I'm lowering scheduler-7 batch_size from 256 -> 128, and disabling the large-batch heuristic. Executing control-plane command: 

```text
CONTROL: set-scheduler-config --shard scheduler-7 --batch_size 128 --heuristics.large_batch false
ACK: config applied on 7 nodes
LOG: evicted 312 low-priority batches, queue_depth now 480 -> 180
```

mike: Seeing queue depth drop and mean latency for small requests improving. KV cache pressure reducing slowly.

anna: Nice. Reroute metrics?

omar: Reroute 30% traffic to us-east-1 variant (model-v1-compat). Command below and deployed: 

```bash
# soft-route 30% to us-east-1
curl -X POST https://gateway-api.internal/route/split -d '{"route":"/v1/generate","from":"us-west-2","to":"us-east-1","pct":30}'
```

deploy-bot: Traffic split enacted.

jess: Customer comms: sent holding message to Acme and NovaAnalytics, ETA update 30m. Support assigned: @jess to own customer loop.

anna: Quick customer impact snapshot: ~8% of requests globally experienced 5xx/timeouts during spike window. Major impact to two enterprise customers (Acme, Nova). Internal alerting shows increased retry loops causing some downstream latency.

mike: Initial root-cause hypothesis: A batch of long-token /streaming requests started hitting scheduler-7 that generated very large KV cache entries and kept big batches pinned for many seconds, preempting other smaller low-latency requests (head-of-line). That behavior produced batching scheduler starvation and eventual gateway timeouts.

carlos: Will open a follow-up ticket to add fairness preemption and eviction heuristics. Short-term we should also pump autoscale up for scheduler-7 to absorb burst while we implement fairness. I can request a temporary x2 capacity bump.

anna: Please do. @mike, can you validate if eviction prevented further timeouts?

mike: Yes — after reducing batch size and rerouting, error rate dropped from 11.8% -> 1.1% over 6 minutes. p95 latency fell from 3.6s -> 600ms for small requests.

pagerduty-bot: Incident annotated: batching-scheduler-hol-3188881234, severity=P1. Assigned to oncall anna.

anna: Handoff: I'm going to keep watching for 15 minutes. If stable, I'll hand to mike for postmortem and remediation work. Jess, please continue customer comms with ETA 1hr for full root cause and next steps.

jess: On it. Posting update to affected customers now.

mike: I'll collect logs + KV cache snapshots and open an RFC for fairness eviction. Will also add a regression test to the eval harness to catch HOL scenarios.

anna: TL;DR timeline for incident notes:
- 17:24 UTC: spike begins, initial 5xx/timeouts reported by customers
- 17:26 UTC: incident-bot page -> SRE oncall (anna)
- 17:27-17:30 UTC: throttle + disable large-batch heuristic + batch_size reduction executed (omar/mike)
- 17:33 UTC: traffic reroute to us-east-1 (30%) completed
- 17:36 UTC: error rate down to ~1.1%, p95 improved

anna: Next actions:
- Mike to lead RCA and remediation ticket (fairness + eviction + autoscale policy)
- Carlos to schedule capacity bump request and coordinate a canary for eviction policy
- Jess to maintain customer comms until resolved
- I'll keep monitoring for 30 more minutes, then close page if stable.

incident-bot: Note: runbook reference: /runbooks/batching-hol-eviction and postmortem template created under incidents/3188881234.

anna: final quick note — please add any timeline/nuggets into the postmortem doc. Closing message in 10m if no regress. :handshake:

anna: last update — 17:42 UTC, service stabilized, leaving follow-ups assigned.

devex

max: quick note — hit a surprising hang in the go sample when we rotate auth mid-stream and then cancel. posting a short repro and some proposed DX fixes.

max: repro (short): start stream, have a goroutine call iter.UpdateAuth(tok) on refresh, cancel ctx after first chunk. main returns but background goroutine sometimes stays around for tens of seconds.

max: tiny sketch:```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(parent)
iter := client.Generator.Stream(ctx, req)
go func(){
  for t := range authCh { iter.UpdateAuth(t) }
}()
_ = iter.Recv() // first chunk
cancel()
// sometimes goroutine stuck in UpdateAuth
```

anya: sounds like UpdateAuth is doing blocking IO or waiting on a handshake; since it doesn't accept ctx, cancel won't help.

drew: ergonomics thoughts: user expectation = cancel is a hard stop. options: 1) make UpdateAuth atomic/nonblocking (swap token + notify send loop), 2) accept a ctx in UpdateAuth so caller can abort, 3) expose an Abort/CloseNow that tears down transport immediately.

viv: +1 to nonblocking swap as default. Also surface a Done() channel on the stream handle so callers can select on resource cleanup: e.g., iter.Done() <-chan struct{}.

max: my plan: implement StreamV2 that returns a StreamHandle with these methods: Done(), CloseNow(), and UpdateAuthNonblocking(token). provide a compat Stream shim that maps old API to new behavior.

anya: test plan: add examples/stream-abort that rotates auth, cancels ctx, and asserts Done() closes within a short timeout. also include a server fixture that delays handshake to ensure CloseNow actually aborts blocked UpdateAuth.

pm-bot: note: prefix PR with devex/stream-abort to auto-request reviewers from devex + eng-runtime. include CHANGELOG + onboarding blurb.

drew: tiny naming nit: prefer UpdateAuthAtomic or SetAuthFast to make it obvious it won't block. and keep Reauth(ctx) for the blocking variant that surfaces errors.

viv: doc snippet suggestion for onboarding: "When interrupting a long-lived generator, cancel the ctx and wait for iter.Done() before exiting; if you need immediate teardown, call iter.CloseNow() (use sparingly)."

max: thanks — i'll open a draft PR with StreamV2, example, and tests. will ping runtime if CloseNow still leaves kernel-level race.

anya: this should also fix a handful of support tickets about the generator "hanging after ctrl-c".

title: devex
body:
devex

mira: hey, hitting a weird intermittent 401 when using AsyncClient inside an anyio TaskGroup. looks like token refresh races across tasks. repro below.

mira: minimal pattern:
```py
from anyio import create_task_group
from redwood import AsyncClient

client = AsyncClient()  # shared at module scope

async def work(i):
    await client.generate("hello")  # sometimes 401 here

async def handler():
    async with create_task_group() as tg:
        for i in range(8):
            tg.start_soon(work, i)

# run under uvicorn (anyio)
```

mira: logs show one task does the refresh and gets a new token, others keep using the old cached token and hit 401, then all retry and hammer refresh endpoint.

mira: noticed it only happens when running with anyio/trio backend; not reproducible with plain asyncio loop.

kyle: hmmm. are you using contextvars inside the SDK to store the token? sounds like contextvar propagation across task groups might be part of this. :thinking:

mira: yes the SDK stores a token in a contextvar per-client to avoid global state. i assumed anyio would preserve contextvars between parent and child tasks, but maybe task group does something odd with trio?

jess: anyio/trio have different semantics for contextvar copies, especially if a task is started from a different thread or an anyio worker. but usually contextvars should propagate to child tasks at start. do you have a tiny log of token ids?

mira: pasted snippet from logs:
```
[1723456792] task=3 token=tok_abc (valid)
[1723456792] task=5 token=tok_abc (401 -> refresh started)
[1723456793] task=3 token=tok_def (got refreshed by task 5)
[1723456793] task=5 token=tok_def (continuing request but still 401)
```

mira: looks like task 3 sees the new token nearly immediately, but its in-flight request still fails (maybe token changed mid-request on server?)

kyle: what does your retry logic look like? is the SDK doing an automatic refresh + retry inside the same request context? race there could cause double refreshes.

mira: SDK flow: on 401, attempt refresh (async, acquires a small in-process mutex per-client), update contextvar token, then retry original request. i thought mutex should prevent concurrent refreshes, but it seems multiple tasks enter refresh path.

jess: ah — contextvar + async mutex interplay can be surprising. if the mutex instance is stored in a contextvar, different tasks might have different copies, so the lock isn't shared. is the client storing the lock on the contextvar too?

mira: god no, the lock is an attribute on the AsyncClient instance (self._refresh_lock = anyio.Lock()). token is in contextvar.

jess: ok. then maybe what's happening is: both tasks detect 401 and both await the same lock, but the token used for the failing request was captured earlier (header already built). task 1 acquires lock, refreshes token, updates contextvar, releases lock. task 2 then refreshes too because it still thinks token is invalid (it re-runs its refresh logic since it still sees the prior 401). result: double refreshes and a brief window where some requests used old token.

kyle: that sounds plausible. two related mitigations: 1) ensure the check+refresh is done under the same lock (i.e., after acquiring the lock, re-check token value to see if someone else already refreshed), 2) avoid using contextvar for the token when you have a shared client object — store token on the client instance and make header-building read that attribute under a lock.

mira: i can try (1) quickly. currently code is:
```py
async def request(...):
    resp = await do_request()
    if resp.status == 401:
        async with self._refresh_lock:
            await self._refresh_token()
        return await do_request()
```

mira: so we refresh unconditionally once we win the lock. we don't re-check after getting the lock whether the token changed already.

jess: change to:
```py
if resp.status == 401:
    async with self._refresh_lock:
        if token_matches_header():
            await self._refresh_token()
    return await do_request()
```

jess: i.e., after acquiring the lock, check whether the header/token used by the original request still matches current token; if not, skip refresh because someone else already did it.

kyle: ^ that's the classic double-check. also consider making token storage consistent: either keep token on the client instance (self._token) and use contextvars only for per-request overrides, or keep everything in contextvars but ensure refresh lock is also in shared instance. mixing can bite.

mira: oh — side note: when i switched uvicorn to asyncio backend (--loop asyncio) the repro disappeared. that matches anyio/trio scheduling amplifying the race.

mira: quick patch test locally (re-check inside lock) seems to reduce frequency a lot. will open a PR with a test using anyio TaskGroup to catch regressions.

kyle: nice. can you add a small integration test that spawns N concurrent requests and asserts <=1 refresh call per failure window? helps prevent regression.

mira: yep will do.

auth-bot: thanks for the report! created issue RDW-DEVEX-4123 and assigned to mira.

mira: thx. filing PR in a bit. anyone think we should document "async backends and token refresh semantics" in devex docs? might save folks.

jess: yes please — a short note under "Async client gotchas" about contextvars vs. instance state and double-checking refresh under locks would be great.

kyle: also call out anyio/trio oddities and recommend the test pattern.

mira: will add a small snippet and link to the PR. :+1:

title: incidents
body:
incidents

incident-bot: P1 Alert — elevated 5xx rate detected on rtd-inference-prod (gateway errors + timeouts). Dashboard: https://redwood.ops/d/infra/rtd-inference?orgId=1 :rotating_light:
Priya Khatri: got paged. Seeing 5xx spike started ~10:04 UTC, error type: upstream kv/prefix cache failures + timeouts.
Jamal Ortiz: paging in — I'm on it. Can someone post which services show the errors?
Priya Khatri: gateway-service returning 502/504 to clients. Inference runtime logs show repeated errors like `kv_cache: checksum mismatch` and `prefix_cache miss_ratio=0.93` then `eviction: storm detected`.
Alan Wu: copying logs — here's the tail from runtime node-7: ```[10:05:12] ERROR kv_cache: corruption detected checksum=0x4f2a expected=0x4f2b key=prefix:abc123
[10:05:12] WARN prefix_cache: eviction_batch_size=1024; eviction_rate=0.87
[10:05:13] ERROR gateway: upstream timeout waiting for runtime (deadline exceeded)
```
Elena Park: I see spike in cache misses and then runtime saturates CPU waiting on cache rebuild. Metric: prefix_cache_evictions/sec jumped from 2 -> 900 in 3 mins.
Marta Chen: CS — we have 14 customers with active requests in last 5m. Top affected: acme-payments, travelmate, docsway. Potential SLA impacts.
Jamal Ortiz: immediate mitigation options: 1) disable prefix cache reads for susceptible routes 2) roll runtime nodes behind a canary with cache cleared 3) throttle client traffic / enable fallback model. Which do we want first?
Priya Khatri: disable prefix cache reads as hotfix — reduces correlation between malformed cache entries and downstream 5xx. How to toggle?
Alan Wu: ops-bot has admin API. Command to set runtime feature flag: ```curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://redwood.ops/api/admin/feature -d '{"name":"prefix_cache_reads","value":false}'```
ops-bot: runbook step executed by Priya Khatri at 10:07:40 UTC: feature toggle prefix_cache_reads=false. Response: 200 OK.
Priya Khatri: toggled. Confirming logs...
support-bot: Note: temporarily disabling cache reads will increase token compute cost. Notify billing? :information_source:
Elena Park: after toggle, 5xx rate dropped ~45% in 60s but timeouts still present for some requests. prefix_cache_miss_ratio down to 0.4.
Jamal Ortiz: good. Next, we should evict any corrupted cache shards and restart the smallest subset of runtime nodes to pick up clean state. Propose rolling restart of nodes node-5, node-7, node-8 (those with most corruption).
Alan Wu: can do rolling restart. Command: ```for n in node-5 node-7 node-8; do ssh $n 'sudo systemctl restart redwood-runtime'; sleep 30; done```
Priya Khatri: I'm starting the restarts now. Will monitor error rate and customer impact.
Marta Chen: contacting acme-payments + travelmate via CSMs to let them know we're mitigating. ETA to resolution?
Jamal Ortiz: estimate 20-35 mins for restarts + cache warmup. We'll also run integrity sweep on KV store to find corrupted entries.
Elena Park: found a likely root cause: a prior partial write to prefix_cache index when node OOMed — left inconsistent entries. Checksum mismatch triggered eviction storm because eviction policy attempts mass eviction which saturates IO.
Priya Khatri: running integrity sweep script: ```/opt/redwood/bin/kv-check --prefix-prefix --fix --dry-run``` then follow with --apply if results look sane.
ops-bot: integrity sweep dry-run completed on shard s3: 112 suspect keys out of 1.2M, top prefix=prefix:acme-* (67 keys).
Alan Wu: proceed with targeted invalidate for suspect prefixes instead of full sweep. Command: ```curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://redwood.ops/api/admin/cache/invalidate -d '{"prefix":"prefix:acme-"}'```
Priya Khatri: invalidated prefix:acme- and prefix:travelmate- entries. Monitoring.
Elena Park: after invalidation and restarts, recovered 5xx to near baseline for most routes. A small subset of long-running requests still hitting timeouts — looks like upstream queueing.
Jamal Ortiz: to reduce queueing, enable model-variant fallback for critical customers to a smaller context model to reduce runtime latency. Toggle: ```curl -X POST https://redwood.ops/api/admin/route-fallback -d '{"route":"/generate","fallback_model":"rw-micro-v1","customers":["acme-payments","travelmate"]}'```
ops-bot: fallback applied for routes /generate for acme-payments and travelmate at 10:20:03 UTC.
Marta Chen: keeping customers updated: acme-payments acknowledges mitigation, reporting improved success rate. Travelmate still seeing intermittent failures.
Priya Khatri: monitoring shows last_message_ts=10:24 UTC, 5xx is down to 2% (target <1%). Will continue stabilization.
Elena Park: follow-up actions for postmortem: - root cause: partial writes/OOM led to checksum-corrupted prefix cache entries - missing guardrail: write-atomicity check on cache writes - short term: add health check to detect eviction storms and auto-disable reads - medium: better backpressure from runtime when cache eviction rate > threshold - long term: migrate prefix cache to handle tombstones/atomic updates
Jamal Ortiz: creating incident doc and linking runbook: https://redwood.docs/incidents/1748001234-kv-eviction-postmortem. Assigning owners: Elena (root cause + fixes), Alan (ops automation), Priya (customer comms).
Priya Khatri: handing off to follow-up on-call: Alan Wu. I'll remain reachable if anything regresses. :white_check_mark:
Alan Wu: taking post-incident ownership. I'll run a full integrity apply and schedule a maintenance window to roll cache nodes with a patch.
support-bot: post-incident ticket SR-1458 opened for top affected customers for credits and details.
incident-bot: Incident closed to P2 at 10:32 UTC. Final note: total duration ~28 minutes, peak affected requests ~12k/min, impacted customers(>=error rate 5%): acme-payments, travelmate, docsway.

eng-runtime

maria: Heads up — noticed ~18% jump in cost-per-token on /chat-stream starting after yesterday's kernel routing tweak. Something changed in runtime selection.

maria: Quick aggregation I ran:
```
route    tokens_in    kernel_ms    kv_hits    kv_misses

title: eng-runtime
body:
eng-runtime

maya: Quick heads-up — FP8 enablement on a mixed H100/L40S farm is showing strange warmup jitter and an occasional decoder divergence for long-context prompts. Repro: 8 GPUs (4xH100, 4xL40S), batch sizes 1/4, seq=2048.

raj: ugh. seen any kernel fallbacks in the logs?

maya: yes, that's the weird part. transformer-engine picks fused kernels at runtime but for first few tokens it falls back to a more generic path. Profiling dump pasted below.

perf-bot: auto-profile summary:
```
Kernel    Calls  Total(ms)  Avg(ms)  %Runtime
fused_qk  240    1200.3     5.00     35.1
gemm_fp8  480     520.7     1.08     15.2
fallback_gemm  32  410.9     12.84    12.0
kv_writeback  64   210.4     3.29     6.1
other     100    680.2     6.80     31.6
```

maya: the fallback_gemm spikes align with first-token latency spikes. Also seeing KV cache miss penalty when mixing small batches with long prefixes — the runtime serializes writes to the host for some kernel combos.

olivia: can you paste the TE config you're using?

maya: sure — this is what the config looks like in the dev cluster:
```
transformer_engine:
  fp8_enabled: true
  fp8_recipe: e4m3
  kernel_selector: auto
  preferred_kernels:
    - fused_attention
    - fused_gemm
  fallback_policy: allow_fallback
  calibrate_on_start: true
  calibrate_min_batches: 8
  kv_cache_mode: async_writeback
  first_token_low_latency: true
```

raj: couple thoughts: (1) calibrate_min_batches=8 might be low for stable scaling across L40S vs H100 — calibration variance can change scaling factors and cause numeric instability during warmup. (2) kernel_selector:auto sometimes picks a slower but more numerically stable kernel for later tokens; but first-token path may prefer a universal kernel causing the observed fallback.

sasha: we've seen similar on other quant modes — calibration noise -> bad per-layer scaling -> non-deterministic GEMM choose. Could try increasing calibrate_min_batches to 64 and use per-device calibration seeds.

olivia: also the KV async_writeback is probably serializing small writes when the fused kernel can't handle the layout. Try switching to kv_cache_mode: batched_writeback or local_cache for L40S nodes.

maya: ran a quick experiment: calibrate_min_batches=64 + preferred_kernels pinned to fused_attention and fused_gemm removed the fallback spikes on H100, but L40S still had occasional fallback due to a missing fused kernel variant.

perf-bot: new profile after tweak:
```
Kernel    Calls  Total(ms)  Avg(ms)
fused_qk  240    820.1     3.42
gemm_fp8  480    420.5     0.88
fallback_gemm  4   28.8      7.20
kv_writeback  60  140.7     2.34
```

maya: latency p10 improved ~18% for long-context streams on H100, p50 ~20ms better. L40S p50 improved ~8% but p95 still has spikes.

raj: we need a durable routing policy: when kernel_selector:auto sees mixed hardware, prefer kernels that exist on all devices to avoid cross-device fallbacks. Also add a first-token path that prioritizes low-latency kernels irrespective of quantization throughput.

olivia: Agree. Proposed policy (pseudo):
```
if mixed_hardware:
  allowed_kernels = intersection(kernels_on_all_devices)
else:
  allowed_kernels = best_throughput_kernels
if token_index == 0:
  use_low_latency_kernel()
```

sasha: Another angle: calibration drift over time. We saw scale factors shifting after 1M tokens on L40S due to dynamic range changes in embedding updates. Need periodic re-calibration windowed by workload, not only startup.

maya: that's scary. We observed slight output quality degradation in a few eval prompts when calibrate_min_batches was too aggressive. Not catastrophic but noticeable in rouge/qa tests.

raj: add a quality guard: run a tiny eval set after calibration and if metrics drop, rollback to cached FP16 kernels for those layers. Could automate: if rouge_drop > 0.5 then disable FP8 for X layers.

olivia: here's a short checklist to try this week:
- pin preferred_kernels to fused variants where available
- increase calibrate_min_batches to 64 (per-device) and seed calibration RNG
- change kv_cache_mode to batched_writeback on mixed clusters
- implement intersection-based kernel routing for mixed hardware
- add post-calibration eval + automatic rollback threshold

maya: I'll run the checklist on a staging mix of 2 H100 + 2 L40S and report perf+quality.

deploy-bot: maya started a 4-node fp8-warmup experiment (<link>)

olivia: if staging is green, we should roll a canary with traffic split 1% for an hour, watch p95 first-token latency and rouge/qa diffs.

maya: noted. I'll also capture per-layer scale factors before/after to make drift diagnosable. Will post logs here.

raj: thanks — if you hit a hard divergence, dump memrefs for the failing layer and we can inspect quantized ranges.

maya: will do. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

perf-bot: reminder — add a perf regression ticket if p95 increases by > 10% post-rollout.

title: eng-ml
body:
eng-ml

anna: Quick report 90m canary of quark7b-int4 on dedicated pool. Noticed progressive mem fragmentation and a single OOM when we hit sustained batch=7 traffic.

liam: Can you share the runtime snapshot and the perf harness numbers? curious about avg seq length and kv-cache growth.

anna: Snapshot: sequences avg 220 tokens, peak long-tail 1200. Runtime output shows slot_map growth and many small free-slab entries. Perf harness numbers: p99 latency +12% at batch=7 vs batch=4, throughput nominally +18%.

rui: Sounds like slab fragmentation. Did you enable async_prefetch? That can increase temporary KV allocations. What were the exact flags?

anna: Config pasted:
```
model: quark7b-int4
batch_size: 7
max_new_tokens: 300
async_prefetch: true
kv_prefetch: true
soft_reserve: 0.08
slot_compaction: background
```

liam: Two quick experiments: 1) run with async_prefetch=false (serial prefetch) and batch=5; 2) reduce max_new_tokens to 128 to cap buffer growth. Both low-risk.

anna: Kicked off two smoke runs: run-A (batch=5, async_prefetch=false), run-B (batch=7, max_new_tokens=128).

ops-bot: deploy job #6124 started: canary-quark7b-int4 -> pool-dedicated-3.

anna: After 20m: run-A stable, fragmentation flatlined ~55%, no OOMs. Latency up slightly vs baseline but within SLO. run-B reduced fragmentation but still had micro-spikes when long-tail seqs arrived; one OOM correlate with concurrent long seqs and batch=7.

rui: Interpretation: async_prefetch likely exacerbates transient KV allocations causing freelist fragmentation. For int4 small-allocation churn is costlier. Suggest default per-model knob: disable async_prefetch for int4 7b family and set safe batch default = 5. Also add a soft cap on concurrent long-seq requests per GPU (queue them or route to large-memory hosts).

liam: Addendum: run quality A/B on evaluation harness (1000 prompts, mixture of short & long). If int4 with batch=5 shows >1.5% drop vs int8 baseline in Rouge or LM-likelihood, we should hold.

anna: I'll open PR with proposed defaults: {"batch_size":5, "max_new_tokens":128, "async_prefetch":false, "kv_eviction_threshold":0.65}. I'll also add a routing rule for long-seq requests.

ops-bot: deploy job #6124 success: canary stable at 30m.

anna: Thanks team. I'll post the PR link and eval artifacts here once the run completes.

title: support
body:
support

maria.su: @acme-oncall getting multiple p99 complaints, started ~03:20 UTC. p95 ~0.9s -> 1.2s, p99 spiking to ~2.8s. customer reports occasional 503s. Observed: gpu-node-17 showing OOMs and rising GPU memory pressure. Can SRE take a look?

devon_k: looking now. quick glance at traces — tails show long allocator stalls (~600ms) before token generation resumes. I see slab_compaction attempts failing and repeated 'OutOfMemory' warnings in runtime logs. grabbing logs for gpu-17.

maria.su: tenant: acme-42, model: gptq-blue-13b, avg seq ~1024 (spikes to 2k on some requests). bursty traffic—batcher saw batches up to 128 recently. sending sample request ids.

jake_r: pasted runtime log snippet:
```
[2026-03-17T03:22:01Z] worker=runtime-7 gpu=gpu-17 WARN MemoryAllocator: allocation failed: Needed=1.2GiB Available=0.9GiB
[2026-03-17T03:22:01Z] worker=runtime-7 ERROR KVCache: entries=2_340_123 growth_rate=+12%/5m
[2026-03-17T03:22:02Z] worker=runtime-7 INFO SlabAllocator: free_ratio=8% fragmented_segments=312
```
this looks like KV cache growth + fragmentation.

devon_k: confirmed. allocation pattern + long conversations = KV growth. fragmentation prevents large contiguous allocs -> OOM. immediate mitigations we can try:
1) enable tenant-level active eviction TTL (evict prefixes >10s) via admin API
2) reduce max_batch_size for acme-42 in routing policy to 32
3) temporarily route acme-42 to dedicated pool (if available) or fallback to smaller model variant (gptq-blue-7b)
4) schedule rolling restart for runtime workers on gpu-17 (drain then restart) to trigger compaction
5) apply per-tenant soft-rate-limit to smooth bursts

maria.su: customer prefers minimal downtime. Which of those are lowest risk and fastest to apply?

devon_k: order of low->higher risk: 1) enable eviction TTL (instant, no restart), 2) set route max_batch_size=32 (instant), 3) enable soft-rate-limit 100r/s for tenant (instant), 4) route to smaller model (warmup needed but lower risk), 5) rolling restart (30–60s request drain per worker). I'd do 1,2,3 now.

jake_r: small commands:
```
# enable eviction for tenant
POST /admin/tenants/acme-42/kv/eviction {"ttl_secs":10}
# set route batch size
POST /admin/routing/acme-42 {"max_batch_size":32}
# soft rate-limit
POST /admin/tenants/acme-42/rate_limit {"type":"soft","rps":100}
```
I also recommend adding a tmp flag to allocator: --allocator-compact-threshold=0.6 for more aggressive background compaction. That requires rolling restart.

maria.su: applied eviction TTL + batch_size + soft rate limit at 03:28. Observability: p95 dropped from 1.2s -> 0.45s within ~8 minutes. p99 improved but still at ~1.7s. no further OOMs so far. Customer asking for permanent fix.

devon_k: good short-term. For long-term: we should limit per-tenant KV growth (config kv_max_entries or bounded by token count), improve allocator so it can coalesce small free segments (patch to background compaction), and add eviction heuristics based on conversation activity. Also add alerting: slab_fragmentation_percent > 65% OR kv_entries increase > 500k in 10m triggers page.

jake_r: I'll draft a small runtime change: background compactor that triggers when fragmentation>70% OR free_ratio<10%. Also cap tenant KV at 1_000_000 entries with LRU eviction to avoid unbounded growth. Will open PR and can canary to a subset of nodes.

maria.su: customer is okay with rolling restarts during maintenance window, prefers we keep them updated. schedule?

devon_k: scheduling rolling restart for gpu-17 at 23:40 UTC (maintenance window). plan: drain requests on worker -> wait for active requests to finish (max 60s) -> restart -> verify metrics -> next worker. minimal impact expected. will also temporarily keep eviction TTL active until allocator patch lands.

sre-bot: Scheduled: Restart gpu-17 runtime workers at 2026-03-17T23:40:00Z. Maint window: 30m. Auto-notify customer. Rollback: revert eviction flag + routing if regressions observed.

maria.su: thanks, will inform acme. please add incident ticket and owners. :thumbsup:

devon_k: creating INC-2026 with action items: 1) telemetry dashboard for slab fragmentation + kv growth, 2) PR for background compactor, 3) runtime flag defaults change, 4) follow-up postmortem + customer notes. assigning to jake_r + devon_k.

sam: Quick share — ran a systematic head_dim x kv_dim sweep on llama-2-13b and qwen-14b across seq=[512,1024,2048]. Heatmap + csv uploaded. Short nits: qwen shows a sharp latency cliff at head_dim=64 with rope_scale>1.2 on A100 v4. Baseline Llama safe.

perf-bot: Uploaded artifacts: https://redwood.artifacts/1768012345/heatmap.png and /results/1768012345/sweep.csv :white_check_mark:

nina: Can you paste the exact run command and the profiler slice that shows the cliff?

sam: sure
```bash
run_perf --model qwen-14b --shard 1 --head-dim 64 --kv-dim 64 --rope-scale 1.5 --batch 8 --seq 2048 --kernel-selector auto --cache-prefill 0.8
```
Profiler snippet:
```text
[profile] attn_flash: 320ms
[profile] attn_gemm: 980ms
[profile] kv_load: 45ms
[profile] total_decode: 1.45s
```

ryan: Did kernel-selector pick flash or gemm? We've got a recent change that biases to gemm when head_dim <= 64 to avoid fragmentation on v4.

sam: It picked gemm for Qwen at that config. I can repro by forcing `--kernel-selector flash` and it goes down to ~1.05s total (so gemm path is the culprit).

maya: Interesting. Could be RoPE scale changing memory layout and causing more cache evictions; that might push attn_gemm into slower codepath. What's cache hit ratio?

sam: Measured KV cache hit ratio fell from 0.92 -> 0.67 when rope_scale increased from 1.0 -> 1.5 for seq=2048. Evictions spike visible in perf traces.

zoe: For a quick mitigation we could: 1) increase per-shard kv_capacity (config knob), 2) adjust kernel-selector to prefer flash for longseq, or 3) route these requests to dedicated gpus with higher memory. Option 2 seems lowest friction.

nina: Agree. Also need to update our model profile metadata so Optimize suggests head_dim=80 for qwen-14b to avoid the gemm cliff. Add to the model-catalog note.

- [ ] bump kv_capacity for canary pool + rerun sweep
- [ ] open perf-regression issue referencing commit fea2b3

title: support
body:
support

customer-jane: Hey team — starting ~2024-05-20T11:31Z some of our calls to /v1/generate returned 502s (~15% of requests). SDK retries didn't help. Sample X-Request-Id: 6f7c9b2a. Any quick checks we can run?

lydia: thanks — can you paste the exact curl you used and the failing response body (or a truncated header dump)?

customer-jane: minimal repro we used:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-xxx" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","prompt":"hi"}'
```
Failing snippet: `HTTP/2 502\ncontent-type: application/json\n{\"error\":\"upstream connect error or connection reset by peer\"}`
X-Request-Id: 6f7c9b2a

ben: oncall — I see a deploy completed at 2024-05-20T11:29:55Z (ingress-bot). Asking for traceroute + dig/nslookup from your egress so we can compare DNS/paths. Also roughly how many concurrent connections from your side and are you behind NAT/CGNAT?

customer-jane: we're behind CGNAT (carrier NAT) on mobile clients; ephemeral ports limited. Traceroute looks normal. dig +short api.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8 returned:
```
198.51.100.12
198.51.100.13
```
But we also saw a quick flip where the A record changed and our client stack retried immediately.

lydia: noted. eng-runtime — could be related to the recent cert rotation + edge resolver behavior. Past incidents show rapid A-record rotation + low resolver TTL -> clients hit nodes with different cert sets and see handshake timeouts. Can you pull edge logs for 6f7c9b2a?

ingress-bot: deploy job: ingress-edge/v2 finished, cert-rotation job kicked at 2024-05-20T11:30:05Z, certs pushed to subset of nodes 11:30:06-11:30:18Z

samir: grabbing logs now. From edge logs for 6f7c9b2a: several TLS handshake timeouts and early TCP resets. Relevant snippets:
```
[11:31:08] conn from 198.51.100.12:52344 -> accepted
[11:31:08] tls: ClientHello, SNI=api.redwood.ai
[11:31:09] tls: ServerHello -> error: tls: handshake timeout
[11:31:09] backend: upstream connect failed: dial tcp x.x.x.x:443: connection reset
```
Also seeing DNS resolver returning SERVFAIL sporadically for the same region around 11:30:50-11:31:10.

ben: two hypotheses: 1) cert rotation was phased and some nodes didn't get the full chain -> handshake fails; 2) client retries across very short DNS TTLs and CGNAT remaps source ports/ips so retry hits a different node without warmed cert/cached keys. The IPv6 path shows additional fallbacks.

lydia: customer can you run this focused repro?
```
curl -v --resolve api.redwood.ai:443:198.51.100.12 https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-live-xxx' -d '{"model":"redwood-1","prompt":"test"}'
openssl s_client -connect api.redwood.ai:443 -servername api.redwood.ai -tlsextdebug -brief
```
Send the s_client output if it hangs or shows an abrupt reset.

customer-jane: here's openssl output — it stalls after ClientHello, then socket closed:
```
CONNECTED(00000005)
write to 0x7f...: TLS 1.3, ClientHello
*** Received fatal alert: Internal Error
---
no peer certificate available
```
We also captured that our client saw the endpoint rotate IP during retries; TTL on some resolvers was 1s for a short window (looks like provider-side DNS low TTL).

samir: that matches. I pulled edge metrics: cert-rotation window overlapped with a resolver TTL shrink to 1s in one of our DNS caches. Result: some clients observed A-record flip while rotation in progress; because of sticky source NAT and ephemeral port exhaustion some flows landed on nodes that hadn't loaded the new cert chain yet, producing handshake timeouts and 502s. Also saw a handful of connections fallback to IPv6 which hit a different backend cluster with older certs.

ben: mitigation applied: 1) increased authoritative resolver TTL to 30s in the affected region, 2) paused immediate IP rotate during cert swap (forced atomic swap on LB), 3) enabled connection draining and prior cert chain fallback for 5 minutes post-rotation, 4) added a fast path in edge to accept both chains during handover.

lydia: customer — can you retest for a few minutes? We also reviewed your billing spikes and will credit failed token usage for the incident window.

customer-jane: retested — over 12 minutes failures dropped to ~0.5% (was ~15%). Looks much better. Thanks for the quick mitigation.

samir: root cause summary we will include in the postmortem: cert rotation happened concurrently with an anomalous low TTL on some caches; combined with CGNAT and client retry behavior this caused retries to land on nodes without the updated cert chain leading to TLS handshake timeouts surfaced as 502s.

action items (assigned):
- eng-runtime: implement atomic cert swap to avoid partial-serving window (samir)
- dns: enforce min TTL 30s for edge A records and add monitoring for drops (ben)
- sdk: add retry jitter/backoff guidance and SNI pinning example for customers (lydia)
- support: issue billing credit for 2024-05-20 11:30-11:40 UTC (lydia)

customer-jane: appreciated. Please link the postmortem and any SDK guidance. :thumbsup:

ben: will post a short incident note in #postmortems and link here when ready.

samir: will follow up with a short runbook entry for cert rotations and DNS TTL checks.

lydia: closing the thread when postmortem link posted. Thanks everyone.

title: eng-ml
body:
eng-ml

Maya Patel: Heads up — nightly eval failed on rwd-3b-int8-20260317, large spike in hallucination / incorrect completions for the 'codegen-safety' prompt set. Eval delta: +7.2% token-error vs baseline (rwd-3b-fp16).
Juan Soto: Oof. Any quick examples from the diff?
Maya Patel: Example 1 (input truncated):
```
# prompt: implement memoized fibonacci
def fib(n):
```
Output baseline: returns correct memoized impl.
Output rwd-3b-int8: returns weird recursive pseudocode with repeated filler comment lines and incorrect base case. Also extra unrelated text about caching strategy.
Maya Patel: eval-bot attached top 10 failing prompts and a small perplexity increase on instruction-following tests.
eval-bot: Automated summary: failures concentrated on prompts that hit long-context KV cache reuse patterns and code blocks > 512 tokens.
Liam Chen: Did quantization config change recently? Was this a model-only change or a serving runtime tweak?
Maya Patel: Model was re-quantized with updated per-channel scales (new GEMM packing). No runtime changes in canary cluster.
Alina Kaur: We also rolled in a micro-optimization to KV cache eviction last week in runtime (PR #487). Could be interacting.
Juan Soto: Can someone run a quick repro with kv-cache logging enabled? I want to see mismatched key lengths or early evictions.
Liam Chen: Running now on staging with rwd-3b-int8 and the failing prompt. Command: `rwdctl serve --model rwd-3b-int8-20260317 --kv-debug`
infra-bot: Deploy of rwd-3b-int8-20260317 to canary/staging succeeded (canary=0.5%).
Liam Chen: Repro confirmed. Logs show repeated `kv_eviction` events during generation and then model starts repeating previous tokens. Eviction window triggers at ~512 tokens.
Maya Patel: That matches eval-bot's clue (long-context prompts).
Juan Soto: Hypothesis: quantized attention kernel changes altered internal buffer sizes; eviction heuristic in runtime expects fp16-sized KV entries. With int8 packing the measured buffer fullness math undercounts memory leading to premature eviction. Evicted KV leads to missing context -> hallucination + repetition.
Alina Kaur: Nice catch. So root cause = mismatch between quantized packing math and KV eviction heuristics in runtime. Not a model semantics regression per se, but a serving/inference interaction.
Maya Patel: Immediate mitigation suggested: 1) rollback rwd-3b-int8-20260317 from hosted canaries, 2) pin runtime KV eviction to conservative path for all int8 models, 3) add CI gating tests that include long-context prompts for any quantized model builds.
Juan Soto: Agreed. I'll trigger rollback now. `rwdctl rollback --model rwd-3b-int8-20260317 --to rwd-3b-int8-20260301`
infra-bot: Rollback started. Canary traffic re-routed.
infra-bot: Rollback complete. Canary now at previous stable version.
Liam Chen: I'll push a temporary runtime patch that forces nv_kv_size_calc to use fp16-equivalent sizing for int8 until we properly fix packing math. Patch: `runtime/kv.cpp` diff (small):
```
- if (model.quantized) used_bytes = packed_size;
+ if (model.quantized) used_bytes = packed_size * packing_scale_factor; // conservative
```
Juan Soto: Good stopgap. Also add a unit test in inference-tests that runs failing long code prompts through quantized model + runtime in CI. If delta > 1% error => fail.
Maya Patel: Action items: 
- Juan: add CI gating rule + test harness (due EOD today)
- Liam: submit runtime patch to canary branch + perf regression check (due tomorrow)
- Alina: add an eval CI alert to block deploys if nightly eval codegen set error increases > 2% (due tomorrow)
- Maya: write up RCA and customer-facing blurb for workspace customers with dedicated capacity (due tomorrow morning)
Alina Kaur: Also recommend a longer-term fix: reconcile packing math in quantization pipeline and update eviction heuristics to compute based on actual byte footprint post-packing. We'll schedule a follow-up.
Maya Patel: For gating, proposed YAML snippet for deploy pipeline (example):
```
- name: quant-model-gate
  check: nightly_eval/codegen.delta_error <= 0.02
  action: block_deploy
```
Juan Soto: LGTM. Add threshold for hallucination-specific metrics too.
Maya Patel: I'll add failing prompt set as an explicit 'canary promptset' that runs in preflight.
Liam Chen: Note: short-term patch increases memory headroom; we should watch cost impact on Dedicated clusters. I'll add telemetry for memory headroom and token latency.
infra-bot: Canary metric alert: memory_headroom increased by +12% under temp patch (expected).
Maya Patel: Closing loop: rollback done, temporary runtime patch queued for canary, CI gating + tests to land today. We'll reconvene after runtime patch results. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Juan Soto: I'll update the incident tracker with RCA and link to this thread.
Maya Patel: Filed: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1292 (RCA + mitigation).
eval-bot: Nightly eval re-run scheduled after canary stabilizes.
Alina Kaur: Follow-up meeting scheduled 2026-03-25 10:00 PT to plan quantization packing fix.
Maya Patel: End of thread — leaving follow-ups in INF-1292 and PRs.

title: eng-platform

eng-platform

Alex M.: heads-up — seeing a spike in gpu pod evictions in us-west1 this morning. lots of Pending with \"Insufficient gpu\" even though aggregate GPU count looks fine. evictions ~120 in last hour. any quick ideas?

Sophia L.: ugh. is it fragmentation (many 1-gpu pods spread across nodes) or scheduler refusing to pack? can you paste output of `kubectl get nodes -o=custom-columns=NAME:.metadata.name,GPU:.status.allocatable.nvidia\.com/gpu`?

Alex M.: pasted metrics in ops dashboard — looks like many nodes with 0.5-0.8 GPU used (per pooled accounting), but pods request 1 gpu so they stay unsched while small leftovers exist across nodes.

Darren K.: sounds like classic binpack failure + small-request noise. quick mitigation: enable descheduler Balance or LowNodeUtilization to evict lower priority pods and let scheduler pack. we did similar in eu-prod before.

Infra Bot: alert: GPU fragmentation rate increased 3.8x in us-west1 between 08:00 and 09:00 UTC. Top namespaces: training, sandbox.

Eva R.: short term: reduce fragmentation by running a controlled drain/evict for non-prod low-priority pods. e.g.:
```
kubectl get pods -n sandbox -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}\n{end}' | xargs -n1 kubectl delete pod -n sandbox --grace-period=30
```
but prefer using descheduler so it respects priorities/taints.

Marco P.: another one-off: cordon a few low-util nodes and drain them to force consolidation, then scale down the empty nodes. saves cost vs adding new nodes.

Sophia L.: long-term: we should add a podAffinity/anti-affinity and a topology-aware binpacking policy. also consider marking some nodes with label `gpu.packable=true` and use nodeAffinity for batch workloads. patch example:
```
affinity:
  nodeAffinity:
    preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
    - weight: 100
      preference:
        matchExpressions:
        - key: gpu.packable
          operator: In
          values:
          - \"true\"
```

Darren K.: we could also tune kube-scheduler config to favor least-pods or launch the binpack plugin. If we do that we need to test on staging; risk is more evictions.

Alex M.: cost tradeoff question: running a defrag job (descheduler + drains) will cause transient extra pods and evictions — how much infra cost hit are we ok with vs leaving fragmentation (higher sustained GPU hourly cost)?

Marco P.: estimate: a 2-3 hour consolidation will spike ephemeral CPU for rescheduling but should reduce 10-15% GPU-hours ongoing. pretty positive ROI within a day for noisy namespaces.

Eva R.: operational checklist proposed:
- identify safe namespaces (sandbox, training)
- run descheduler policy: RemoveDuplicates + LowNodeUtilization for 30m window
- cordon/drain 3 lowest-util nodes in us-west1 during maintenance window
- monitor evictions and latency (<=2% increase threshold)
- rollback if >5% user-facing errors

Oncall Bot: scheduled maintenance: consolidation window proposed 2026-03-19T02:00-04:00 UTC. Owner: @Sophia L. Please ack or propose alternative.

Sophia L.: acked. I'll run a dry-run descheduler today and post results. tagging @Darren K. to prep staging config for scheduler plugin test.

Alex M.: thanks all. logging this as follow-up action in infra board. :thumbsup:

title: eng-oncall
body:
eng-oncall

incident-bot: P2 pager: elevated 429s and rising tail latency for /v1/generate (stream=true) in hosted-us-west. Observed 429 spike ~18% for top tenants; p95 stream latency -> 2.1s. Paging eng-oncall + eng-runtime + devex.

Anna: I'm taking primary. Dashboards show bursty concurrent streaming sessions from a handful of tenants. No cluster-wide 5xxs, looks capacity/ingress related. Impact: interactive apps degrade and background workers get slowed.

Miguel: I'm going to apply short-lived per-tenant ingress shaping at the edge: shrink burst window by ~45% and apply smoothing that converts big bursts into a queue with controlled dequeue rate. Will push a canary to 2 edges first.

Anna: Do that. Also consider a temporary toggled feature flag to disable server-side streaming multiplexing optimization that is increasing memory spikes. If we flip that we can favor p50 at cost of throughput.

Miguel: Good call. I'll revert multiplexing group allocation for 30m and push shaping. Rolling now.

Sasha: DevEx here. We need urgent client guidance and an SDK advisory. Two tracks: (1) short advisory for customers seeing 429s; (2) emergency SDK patch that implements adaptive client-side concurrency + backoff + idempotency.

Alex: I have a minimal JS/Python patch ready. Proposed changes: adaptive concurrency limiter (default 3 concurrent streaming requests per process), full-jitter exponential backoff on 429/503/network errors (max attempts 5), and recommend Idempotency-Key header for calls that modify state or are unsafe to replay. Also add honoring Retry-After header.

Anna: Approve those SDK changes. Also ask CS to notify top-10 tenants that they may see temporary stream rate limits.

CS Bot: Pinged Customer Success owners for top-10. They'll DM account owners and escalate any paying-realtime customers.

Miguel: Edge canary looks good on 2 nodes. 429 rate dropped to ~9% for canary tenants. Pushing to full fleet in 3 mins. Also toggled streaming-multiplex=false via feature-flag for 30m.

Anna: Nice. Once edge rollout completes, we'll monitor for 15m before relaxing shaping. Keep SDK advisory short and prescriptive; customers want copy-paste.

--- SDK advisory draft (share as single block in docs and in-app notice) ---

Sasha: Copy-paste guidance below. Keep it minimal and pragmatic.

Alex: Client/SDK emergency guidance for transient 429s and degraded streaming performance:

1) Backoff + jitter (apply immediately)
- Retry on 429, 503, and network errors with exponential backoff + full jitter. Cap to 5 attempts for interactive flows. Respect Retry-After when present and add jitter.

Python example:

```python
import time, random
from uuid import uuid4

def send_with_backoff(request_fn):
    max_attempts = 5
    base = 0.25
    for attempt in range(1, max_attempts+1):
        resp = request_fn()
        if getattr(resp, 'status_code', None) == 200:
            return resp
        if getattr(resp, 'status_code', None) in (429, 503) or getattr(resp, 'is_network_error', False):
            # respect Retry-After if provided
            retry_after = getattr(resp, 'headers', {}).get('Retry-After')
            if retry_after:
                wait = float(retry_after) + random.uniform(0, 0.5)
            else:
                wait = min(10, base * (2 ** (attempt - 1)))
                wait = random.uniform(0, wait)  # full jitter
            time.sleep(wait)
            continue
        return resp
    raise RuntimeError('retries exhausted')

# Usage: include an Idempotency-Key for unsafe calls
headers = {'Idempotency-Key': str(uuid4())}
```

2) Adaptive concurrency limiter (recommended defaults)
- Streaming endpoints: cap concurrent outbound streams per process to 3. For language model streaming heavy clients, reduce to 1-2 during incident.
- Batch/background: prefer single larger non-streaming requests where possible.

3) Idempotency for non-streaming stateful operations
- When retrying POST-like operations, include an Idempotency-Key (UUIDv4). The server will dedupe if the operation is replayed.

Curl example for idempotency:

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \\
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\
  -H "Idempotency-Key: $(uuidgen)" \\
  -d '{"prompt":"..."}'
```

4) Reduce request footprint where possible
- Lower max_tokens in high-concurrency interactive sessions.
- For bulk processing, switch to non-streaming endpoints which tolerate batching better server-side.

5) Client-side monitoring and heuristics
- If you observe >3 consecutive 429s for the same tenant, exponentially reduce concurrency and surface an alert.
- Log idempotency keys used so CS can correlate with server logs during postmortems.

--- end advisory ---

Sasha: I'm adding this to the SDK README, the status page advisory, and the in-app notification for tenants hitting 429s. Will include code snippets for JS and Go next.

Miguel: Edge rollout finished. Fleet 429 rate down to ~7%, p95 streaming latency back to 1.1s. We'll keep shaping and the feature-flag for 30m then reassess.

Anna: Great work. Keeping incident open until shaping and FF are reverted and metrics stable for 30m. Post-incident: we need a follow-up to discuss longer-term changes to streaming admission control and to measure SDK adoption of idempotency.

Infra Bot: Deploy logs: ingress-shape v2 -> success across 12 edges at 1764389435.

CS Bot: CS outreach in progress. Will report any escalations here.

Anna: Thanks all. I'll create an incident timeline and assign owners for postmortem actions once we close.

title: people-ops
body:
people-ops

luca r.: Quick question We had a group shuttle to/from the conference booked through ShuttleGo app. The booking confirmation is an e-ticket that lists only a total and a booking ref (no per-person line items or VAT). I paid with my personal card and need to split between 4 attendees. How should we submit this so Finance can reimburse each person?
zara t.: Do you have the passenger list on the confirmation? If yes, upload the e-ticket and a short note listing the 4 names and who paid which share. We typically accept a single claim with attachments and then split it internally.
luca r.: The e-ticket shows passenger names but it's not broken out by price. Total was $96.50. I split equally with Venmo after the trip but Venmo isn't on company policy for settlement. Can I still claim $24.12 each?
people-ops: Venmo is OK for informal repayment between employees, but Finance prefers a single reimbursement going to the person who paid the vendor (you). Best approach: submit an expense for the full $96.50 on your reimbursement tool, attach: 1) ShuttleGo e-ticket, 2) screenshot of rider list, 3) a one-paragraph attestation naming the 3 colleagues who reimbursed you and the amounts they sent, 4) proof of transfers (Venmo screenshots) if available. Then mark the reimbursement as "split - internal recoverable" and finance will create internal allocations to charge back each attendee's cost to their next expense run.
michael p.: If one of the attendees wants to claim separately (they paid you back in cash), is there a way to avoid duplicate reimbursements?
finance-bot: Automated rule: If an expense is marked "split-recoverable" and supporting attachments include payer receipts or internal payment proof, Finance will process one payment to the payee and generate internal ledger entries to allocate the cost. Do NOT submit separate identical vendor claims for the same shuttle. If someone paid you back in cash and they want reimbursement instead of allocation, attach a signed attestation from both parties and Finance will treat it as a reimbursement reversal.
zara t.: One more thing Some countries require VAT invoices for VAT reclaim. If ShuttleGo cannot provide itemized VAT, flag it in the expense and Finance will mark it as non-reclaimable VAT. That won't prevent reimbursement, but VAT won't be recovered.
luca r.: Got it. I'll upload the e-ticket, Venmo screenshots, and a short attestation naming everyone. I'll mark it split in Expensify and tag @finance. Thanks! :+1:
finance-bot: Received ticket #FIN-4853. Expect allocation confirmation in 2-4 business days. If any attendee needs direct cash reimbursement instead of ledger allocation, reply here with their name and proof of payment.
people-ops: We'll add a sample "group-shuttle attestation" template to the travel FAQ (two-line template: "I, [payer], confirm I paid [vendor] $[total] for [date]; [names] reimbursed me $[amount] each via [method].")

title: devex
body:
devex

maya: heads up — I just noticed the textgen sample README still shows the old auth + API usage, which is a pretty bad footgun for copy/paste.

maya: the README suggests `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-...` and then shows the python snippet `client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])` but our python SDK removed the `api_key` param and the env var we recommend is `REDWOOD_KEY` (and the example encourages pasting a long key into the README). :grimacing:

jon: ouch. do we have tests that catch snippet parity?

maya: not for that repo. it slipped in during the last example refactor — someone replaced the new quickstart with an older copy.

rachel: can you paste the exact snippet? want to file a small PR to fix wording + env var name.

maya: sure — here's the offending block from README.md:

```
# bad README snippet
export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-REDACTED
python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
resp = client.generate("Write a haiku about lakes")
print(resp.text)
```

elena: quick note from onboarding bench: MistralX-7B int4 shows intermittent token repetition and odd attention head phase jitter after ~800-1200 tokens

rob: hmm jitter how? entire head collapse or small amplitude noise?

elena: small amplitude but head-to-head inconsistent. head 2/7/11 show phase correlation dips vs fp16 baseline. with fallback (no fused int4 gemm) behavior matches fp16

chi: that points at fused packing math. our int4 kernel fuses rotary scaling into the q/k multiply and applies a per-block quant multiplier. might be rounding error across even/odd head groups

elena: logs: ```
[phase-check] model:mistralx-7b quant:int4 block=0 head=2 corr=0.74 baseline=0.99 delta=-0.25
[phase-check] model:mistralx-7b quant:int4 block=3 head=7 corr=0.71 baseline=0.98 delta=-0.27
[phase-check] model:mistralx-7b quant:int4 fallback-kernel corr=0.98 baseline=0.99 delta=-0.01
```

rob: ok so fallback kernel is fine. can we reproduce deterministically? any tokenizer funny business?

elena: yes repro prompt attached (short names, soft-hyphen and ZWJ included) -> https://rdrw/gists/mx-phase-repro-17688. runs deterministic on our bench harness; if tokenmap normalizes ZWJ to U+200D removal we see small token id collisions which change alignment

chi: token collisions + per-block quant drift = amplified phase mismatch. recommend two immediate mitigations: 1) add tokenmap audit that flags invisible char canonicalization collisions during conversion 2) add per-head scaling table in int4 profile applied post-packing (calibrated from fp16 reference)

title: devex
body:
devex

ana: quick note from pairing session: the Go generator sample app hangs after an auth rotation during streaming. repro attached.

ryan: can you summarize the symptom? hangs where exactly?

ana: sequence: start generator in stream mode, rotate token externally, SDK refreshes token and retries handshake. user-facing loop never returns and goroutine count stays high. logs: 
```
INFO generator: connected
INFO auth: refresh started
INFO runtime: handshake retry
ERROR generator: stream error: unauthenticated
<--- main goroutine still waiting on gen.Next() --->
```

bijoy: i've seen this. Next() is blocking on an internal recv channel. when handshake fails we do an internal state reset but we don't always close the recv channel in the failure path.

sam: that's a UX footgun for onboarding. sampleapp uses a naive `for { tok, err := gen.Next(); if err != nil { break } ... }` pattern. without a context-aware pull API it's hard to cancel cleanly from the app.

ana: exact snippet in examples/generator/main.go around line ~142.

ryan: options: 1) add `Next(ctx context.Context) (Token, error)` and keep `Next()` for compatibility; 2) keep API but document that caller must call `gen.Close()` on auth events; 3) SDK auto-closes iterator on handshake fatal. pros/cons?

bijoy: 3) is surprising: SDK auto-closing could race with consumer cleanup logic. 2) is low lift but brittle. 1) is nicer ergonomically and matches other libs (python/js have ctx-like cancel semantics).

ana: i prefer 1. add `Next(ctx)` and also a `Close()` that is safe to call multiple times. make Next(ctx) return ctx.Err() when cancelled.

sam: +1 for parity. also add an `--auth-debug` flag to sampleapp so onboarding shows token refresh lifecycle. right now refreshes are silent which confuses engineers running the example.

ryan: will prototype. small checklist: update generator interface, add tests for mid-stream refresh, update sampleapp with auth debug flag and docs update in README, add a perf microbench to ensure no regression for non-ctx Next().

bijoy: test suggestion: simulate token rotation by returning 401 on first handshake attempt and then OK after refresh. assert goroutine counts return to baseline and Next(ctx) unblocks.

build-bot: created issue #6291: "go sdk generator: blocking Next on auth refresh" and attached stack trace. CI label: needs-repro.

ana: i'll paste the minimal repro and a heap trace. also adding a tiny wrapper pattern we used as a temporary workaround:
```
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 20*time.Second)
resCh := make(chan error, 1)
go func() { _, err := gen.Next(); resCh <- err }()
select {
case <-ctx.Done(): gen.Close()
case err := <-resCh: _ = err
}
```

sam: ugly but good temporary mitigation. once PR lands let's run the sampleapp on a couple of machines to catch odd platform-specific channel semantics.

ryan: noted. i'll assign to self and @bijoy for a first-pass patch. will link PR here when opened.

ana: thanks everyone. adding reproduction steps and logs to the issue now. :wave:

title: eng-platform
body:
eng-platform

alex: Quick q on chat/completions streaming — when the model emits a func_call, should we send multiple delta events with the full "function_call" object each time, or only include `name` on the first delta and stream args separately? trying to avoid clients having to reassemble mixed shapes.

priya: We currently send a small shape in the first delta: `function_call: { name }`, then subsequent deltas contain partial arg text in `delta.content` only. That was to keep payloads tiny for high-qps, but several SDKs had to special-case reconstruction.

sam: Thinking about backcompat — what if we add an explicit `stream_event_type` enum: `func_start | func_chunk | func_end`? makes client parsing deterministic (no need to guess whether name repeats).

maria: I worry about adding enums that we then have to support forever. Alternative: keep one event type but *always* include `function_call.name` when present, and put partial args in `function_call.args_delta`. Shape stays stable: `function_call` is always an object or absent.

alex: That sounds reasonable. From a contract POV adding `function_call.name` to all deltas is additive and should be non-breaking, but we need to confirm SDKs won't assert exact keys.

priya: Agree. I'll prototype a shim in the JS SDK that tolerates both shapes. Plan: add compatibility lint that flags code assuming exact delta shapes, publish release notes.

sam: @priya can you open a small PR? I'll add parser tests in runtime to validate both old and new streams. Also can we add a short migration note in the API docs: code sample for streaming parsers.

deploy-bot: CI: schema-lint job #1234 failed on `js-sdk` — log snippet:
```
error: unexpected field `function_call.name` at streaming.delta.ts:45
```

priya: ok patch incoming. Action items: priya to submit PR by EOD, sam to add tests, alex to draft the API docs blurb. I'll also add an opt-in header `X-Stream-Compat: new-fc-shape` so we can rollout gradually for 2 weeks before flipping default.
