title: architecture
body:
architecture

leo.t: thinking about the ephemeral connector model: we mint per-tenant "leases" (connector sessions) that bind a tenant agent -> regional relay instance + nat-ip. need to nail lease protocol semantics and backpressure when the nat pool is near exhaustion. wanted quick takes before i draft an RFC.

nina_s: high level: what are the invariants we need from the lease? e.g., single-owner lease per tenant, predictable renewal timing, observable revocation, and graceful connection drainage on revoke.

leo.t: yes. invariants: (1) at most one active lease per tenant per region, (2) lease contains connector_id, nat_ip, cert_serial, expires_at, and a renew_nonce, (3) renew endpoint must be idempotent and cheap, (4) revoke should be immediate but allow short drain window for in-flight calls.

patrick: for backpressure, we should provide three signals to agents: ACCEPT (grant), QUEUE (soft backoff), and REJECT (hard). QUEUE returns retry-after and a queue-position token. that lets agents back off rather than hammering.

ops_cli: ops constraints: we can't let queue grow arbitrarily. need per-region queue depth, an overflow policy (spill to hosted or fail), and alerting for queue saturation. also audit trail for who got what nat_ip.

nina_s: renewal cadence: I'd prefer short-lived leases (5-15m) to limit exposure, but renew endpoint hit-rate will be high. we need efficient cache + db write pattern: renew should extend lease if caller proves possession (TLS + token). Use optimistic update + vector clock?

leo.t: sketch of API below. renew must be idempotent:

```
POST /v1/lease/renew
Authorization: Bearer <short_jwt>
{ "tenant_id": "t-42", "connector_id": "c-abc", "renew_nonce": "n-001" }

200 OK
{ "status": "ACCEPT", "expires_at": "2026-06-10T12:34:56Z", "nat_ip": "198.51.100.23", "cert": "..." }

202 QUEUE
{ "status": "QUEUE", "retry_after": 45, "queue_token": "q-zz" }

429 REJECT
{ "status": "REJECT", "reason": "nat_pool_exhausted" }
```

Renew must be cheap and avoid a distributed lock on nat allocation. we can pre-assign a small burst slot and use a local atomic counter in relay to serve transient spikes. longer allocations hit central allocator.

patrick: pre-assigned burst slots per relay is a good idea. also consider a grace window where an expired lease can be reactivated quickly if the same connector comes back within X seconds to avoid churn. maybe 60s hold.

ops_cli: draining semantics: on revoke we transition lease -> draining with a draining_until timestamp. relay stops issuing new sockets bound to that connector, but existing requests continue until draining_until. also expose a /v1/lease/force-revoke for emergency. must be audited.

nina_s: revocation propagation and consistency: relays should subscribe to a revocation stream (kafka) with sequence numbers. on partition we should fail-safe: either conservative fail-open (allow traffic) or fail-closed (deny). which one? security prefers fail-closed, but availability wants fail-open with telemetry. we need product input.

leo.t: product note: for private tenants allowlist use cases, failing open across revocation is risky. propose fail-closed for revocation critical paths (suspend/compromise) and fail-open for soft ops events (relay restart). define categories of events.

patrick: metrics to publish: leases_granted_total, leases_active, leases_expired, nat_pool_utilization, renew_queue_length, renew_latency_p50/p95, revoke_propagation_lag_seconds. add per-tenant last_seen_connector.

ops_cli: runbook: if nat_pool_utilization > 85% trigger autoscale and alert; if >95% start rejecting new leases and send admin page. routing fallback: when rejecting, we can optionally route to hosted control-plane if tenant opt-in. require explicit opt-in during onboarding.

nina_s: about queue tokens: they should be redeemable exactly once. queue token -> when granted we issue cert + nat_ip and invalidate token. also prevent token replay by binding token to connector's pubkey.

leo.t: security: lease issuance requires three proofs: short_jwt (time-limited, signed by control plane), client-sig over nonce (possession of private key), and optional mTLS during transport. cert TTL short (1h). maintain revocation list in central db and push deltas.

patrick: scale concerns: renews are N per minute per tenant. we should give clients a jittered renew schedule to avoid spikes. also support long-lived "stable" mode for whitelisted tenants (paid tier) with less churn and reserved nat ips.

ops_cli: compatibility: connectors should be able to present a header x-connector-lease to downstream logs for traceability. console should surface current lease map for tenant admins.

leo.t: open implementation questions i want feedback on: (1) default lease TTL (5m/10m/15m)? (2) hold window for recent-expired leases (30s/60s/120s)? (3) policy for queue overflow (spill to hosted vs immediate reject)? (4) fail-open vs fail-closed defaults for revocation stream partition?

nina_s: my picks: 10m TTL, 60s hold, overflow -> spill to hosted only if tenant opted in, default revocation partition -> fail-closed for security-critical ops else fail-open.

patrick: +1 for 10m and 60s. queue overflow -> reject by default; ops can enable hosted spill for select tenants.

ops_cli: agree but ops wants a configurable per-customer policy surface in console. we'll make defaults conservative. i'll start a runbook draft and sample dashboards.

infra-bot: brief created: https://redwood.internal/notes/2026/connector-lease-protocol (created by leo.t)

leo.t: thanks all. i'll turn this into an RFC sketch with APIs, sequence diagrams, and a canary plan (start with 5 tenants). ping if you want deeper dive on the renew allocator logic.

title: eng-runtime
body:
eng-runtime

maria: heads-up — seeing 15–25% tail latency spikes on the fp8 canary running on H100 when seq_len > 2k. Root traces point at a kernel handshake stall and a burst of KV cache evictions.

Tom: can you paste a trace snippet? short logs are fine.

maria: pasted sample from today (10:22 canary):
```
PROFILE_SNAPSHOT:
kernel_handshake_ms: [2.0, 8.9, 0.6, 18.7]
selected_kernel: [te_fp8_fast, nvfuser_fp8_slow, te_fp8_fast, nvfuser_fallback]
kv_cache_evictions_per_sec: 137
queue_fence_wait_ms: 12.9
microbatch_shapes: [(1,512),(4,256),(1,1024)]
```

ryan: hmm — that alternating selected_kernel vector is suspicious. sounds like our kernel selector is oscillating mid-request which causes TE to precompile/handshake then stall the queue.

sara: we saw something like this on L40S last week after the allocator patch. different root cause but similar symptom (kv churn + kernel flip).

maria: repro steps attached: small qps synthetic with mixed microbatch shapes, context=2500, enable_fp8=true, kernel_selector=auto. latency tail shows correlation with kernel switch events.

perf-bot: Canary deploy 2026-03-15T10:22 -> build/2849; observed 18% p95 increase at 10:30 for shard-7.

Tom: quick mitigation options:
- pin kernel selector to te_fp8_fast for long contexts (config flag).
- force synchronous precompile at warmstart so handshake isn't on hot path.
- add short backpressure window when queue_fence wait spikes.

ryan: agree. also add a kernel-selection cooldown window (e.g. don't switch kernel for same model+shape for 500ms). avoids oscillation in mixed microbatching.

maria: I ran a local experiment: pinning to te_fp8_fast removes the handshake spikes but throughput drops ~2% for short-context microbatches. tradeoff is expected.

Tom: can you paste the config snippet you used?

maria: config applied: `redwood.runtime.fp8_kernel_policy = "pin:te_fp8_fast;cooldown_ms=500;warmstart_precompile=true"`

sara: telemetry request: capture (1) kernel_switch_count per request, (2) kv_eviction_rate, (3) queue_fence_wait_ms percentiles. we need these to prove hypothesis across canaries.

Tom: I'll add a lightweight metric set to runtime-next (should be cheap).

ryan: I'll run a microbenchmark matrix: seq_len [512,1024,2048,4096] x microbatch_shapes [(4,256),(1,1024),(8,128)] on an isolated H100 to measure handshake probability and p95. Expect to repro quickly.

deploy-bot: Note: canary 2849 flagged for increased p95; automatic rollback is OFF for this channel.

maria: if this regresses customer traffic we should rollback. For now let's keep canary and gather metrics. If we confirm selector oscillation -> will push a hotfix: kernel cooldown and an explicit cost bias for te_fp8_fast for seq>1500.

Tom: action items:
- tom: add telemetry + dashboard by EOD (kernel_switch_count, kv_eviction_rate, fence_wait_ms).
- ryan: run microbench matrix and share perf table (~2h).
- maria: open runtime flag PR for cooldown+pin policy and a short changelog.

sara: ping me once metrics show stable — I'll schedule rollback if customer impact increases.

maria: also note: might be related to our microbatch shaping heuristics that try to fill occupancy; when shapes mix we end up juggling kernel footprints which reveals a handshake race. worth revisiting batching heuristic after we stabilize kernel selector.

ryan: +1 — I suspect a small change to the batching aggregator (prefer shape-homogeneous batches during high occupancy) will reduce kernel churn without hurting throughput.

Tom: ok. I'll post dashboard link here once ready. thanks all :thumbsup:

maria: thanks — keeping canary running and will report back with metrics + PR link. :mag:

title: eng-runtime
body:
eng-runtime

sam: quick heads-up — I ran the scrubbed-trace replay with the new sampling policy (strata-aware, 0.6 hot-cohort lift). results below, want eyes before we push to the nightly canary

anita: thanks! did you include KV warmup enabled? that was causing nondet last week

sam: yep — KV warmup ON, kernel hinting disabled (so we exercise kernel-selection path). also forced minibatch size 32 to match prod p50 load profile.

lee: can you paste the run summary from infra-bot?

infra-bot: replay-run 2412309876 by sam started
  config: {"sampling":"strata-0.6","kv_warmup":true,"minibatch":32,"kernel_hint":false}
  duration: 6m22s
  requests: 4,200
  deterministic_matches: 98.1%
  p50_latency_ms: 18.3
  p95_latency_ms: 74.6
  p99_latency_ms: 152.2
  token_throughput_tps: 1,200
  parity_failures: 32 (0.76%)

dinesh: 98.1% det is solid but parity_failures at 0.76% is higher than our target 0.1% — any pattern on failures?

sam: quick grep — failures cluster on long-prefix requests (seq_len > 1024) and where KV cache hits are > 80%. looks like reroute to fallback kernel sometimes picks a different attention kernel which emits slightly different logits (rounding diffs).

anita: that's the kernel-selection divergence we've seen. is it reproducible if you fix kernel to kernel-v3 for the whole run?

sam: good call — spawned a control run forcing kernel-v3. infra-bot posted diff:

infra-bot: replay-run 2412309889 (control) started
  config: {"sampling":"strata-0.6","kv_warmup":true,"minibatch":32,"kernel_hint":"force-v3"}
  deterministic_matches: 99.98%
  parity_failures: 1 (0.02%)
  p99_latency_ms: 160.1 (vs 152.2 baseline)

lee: so forcing v3 kills variability but costs ~5% on p99 for this slice. tradeoff.

dinesh: do we know why kernel-choice changes with KV hit ratio? sounds like warmup affecting allocator alignment or tile sizes -> kernel selector picks different GEMM.

sam: hypothesis: KV prefetch warms memory pages such that the kernel cost model favors kernel-v2 for long prefixes; v2 has a slightly different softmax impl that mismatches numerically at the 1e-6 level which cascades.

anita: can we produce a minimal repro? isolate a single trace with seq_len 1200 and high KV hit, replay deterministic seed, then toggles between v2/v3.

sam: on it — prepping a slice and will post logs. expected timeline ~30m.

lee: also thinking about batching heuristics — minibatch 32 matched prod p50 but maybe extremes (1, 64) show different selector paths. would be good to sweep minibatch sizes in the harness automatically.

dinesh: agreed. add param sweep to replay harness: minibatch in [1,8,32,64], kernel_hint in [auto,force-v2,force-v3], kv_warmup [true,false]. run combinatorial but sample traces to keep run time sane.

sam: noted — I'll update the harness config and add a new column to the infra report for "kernel_decision_reason" (what heuristic/score triggered kernel pick).

anita: last ask — can we augment anonymization so we preserve sequence-length and token-distribution buckets but scramble content? current scrub preserves length but some edge traces are filtered out because of PII heuristics; want a stable mapping so replay slices are identical across teams.

sam: will do. plan: deterministic token hashing with salt-per-org + preserve length & vocab-frequency buckets. should keep replay fidelity while anonymizing.

infra-bot: action items created: #A1 run-minibatch-sweep, #A2 isolate-long-prefix-repro, #A3 add-kernel-decision-logging, #A4 deterministic-anon-salt. tagging @eng-runtime.

lee: awesome. can we have a short post in #eng-runtime tomorrow with the key numbers and recommended default (force-v3 only for high-p99 sensitive tenants)? :thumbsup:

sam: yup — prepping TL;DR and a small notebook with comparisons. will ping when uploads complete.

anita: thanks everyone. feel free to DM if you want access to the raw scrubbed slices.

dinesh: great sync. if parity still >0.1% after kernel logging, we should consider uprevming softmax kernel to numerically match v3.

sam: noted — will include that in the next decision thread.

title: eng-ml
body:
eng-ml

Maria L.: Nightly eval alerted a regression on model:redwood-v2-3q for billing promptset. F1 down ~7.8% vs previous run. Examples show truncated XML invoice tags and wrong invoice dates (future dates).
Devon: Can you paste the eval deltas and 2 failing examples?
Maria L.: Diffs:
```
billing_promptset | F1               | 0.912 -> 0.841 (-0.071)
length_mean       | tokens          | 32.1  -> 20.4  (-11.7)
hallucination_rate| %               | 1.3   -> 6.9   (+5.6)
```
Failing snippets: one cuts off mid-"</Item>" tag, another replaces 2023-09-05 with "2029-01-01".
Ashish: Any recent quant/tok changes? I recall a new quant calibration run for v2-3q landed around 03:00 UTC.
Maria L.: Correct. calib run finished 02:10 UTC, profile applied in image rolled 03:05 UTC. No tokenizer changes.
Devon: Reproduced locally using the quantized image and the same prompts. Outputs are shorter and sometimes missing trailing tokens.
Olivia P.: Could be KV cache write/stride under the quant path — fused attention kernels + int8 path are sensitive to layout.
Ashish: Hypothesis: post-process of calibration metadata changed a kv_stride value (off-by-one) and runtime uses that to index flattened KV buffers. If stride is wrong, last writes can be dropped/overwritten.
Maria L.: I ran --dump-kv on a few failing traces. Quant runtime shows KV sequence length one less on the final step in ~40% of cases vs float32 image.
Devon: That matches truncated tails and higher hallucination: missing final tokens cause a different continuation and occasionally incorrect facts.
Ashish: I diffed calibration metadata: calib_v2-3q_20260418.json vs calib_v2-3q_20260419.json. Field "kv_stride" is 64 in the old file and 63 in the new one. Looks like a post-process typo.
Olivia P.: With kv_stride=63 the runtime flattens with the wrong stride, writes overlap and the final token write effectively drops.
CI-bot: Initiating canary rollback: reverting v2-3q to v2-3q@2026-04-18-0310 (previous quant profile). Canary evaluation traffic only.
Maria L.: Canary results: billing F1 back to baseline (0.913), length_mean 32.0, hallucination_rate 1.4. Confirms regression introduced by new profile.
Devon: Root cause (working): calibration post-process emitted incorrect kv_stride (63) -> runtime used it to index KV -> off-by-one writes -> truncated tails and downstream hallucinations.
Ashish: Mitigations applied: rollback done. Will patch calibration post-process, add metadata schema validation, and harden runtime to validate kv_stride upon load.
Devon: Added unit/integration tests. Example test snippet:
```
# test_kv_stride_validation
calib = load_calib('bad_kv_stride.json')
with raises(ValidationError):
  runtime.load_quant_profile(calib)
```
CI-bot: eng-ml/quant-validation #452 queued.
Olivia P.: Longer-term controls: 1) require automated nightly eval delta <0.5% F1 on critical promptsets before promoting quant profiles; 2) enable 48h 5% production canary for new profiles with auto-fallback to float32 on anomalies; 3) add dashboard card for length_mean and closing_tag_rate for promptsets that depend on trailing tokens.
Ashish: I will push the calibration script patch (guard: kv_stride must divide hidden_size/num_heads evenly) and bump metadata schema. Will regen calib and re-run full eval tomorrow.
Maria L.: Ops added PagerDuty trigger for billing nightly eval F1 drop >1% and support notified. Support-bot opened S-4421 for any customer impact tracking.
CI-bot: Test job eng-ml/quant-validation #452 passed.
Ashish: New calib merged with kv_stride corrected to 64. Starting canary at 14:10 UTC.
Maria L.: Canary eval at 15:00 UTC shows metrics within noise (F1 0.911 -> 0.914, length_mean 31.9, hallucination_rate 1.5).
Devon: Follow-ups: Ashish to file PR for calib script + schema, Maria to publish incident notes to #postmortems, Olivia to add dashboard card, Ops to add PD alert.
Maria L.: Closing thread, will move summary to postmortems after final verification. :thumbsup:

title: eng-runtime
body:
eng-runtime

maria: heads up — noticed persistent GPU memory growth on nightly serving runs after kernel-picker change (commit 3f8a9c). Repro below, looks like allocations never freed between batch windows. Can someone triage? :thinking:

ajay: can you paste the small repro you ran? sequence lengths, batch sizes, model variant? kernel-picker change could have switched to a streaming kernel that pins extra workspaces.

maria: sure — minimal repro (ran on a3-8):
```bash
# repro.sh
python - <<PY
import torch, time
from model_serving import load_model, infer
model = load_model('redwood/trim-7b')
for i in range(120):
    # simulate mix of short+long prefixes
    seq = 64 if i % 5 else 1024
    x = torch.randint(0,10000,(1,seq)).cuda()
    out = model.generate(x, max_new_tokens=64)
    time.sleep(0.8)
PY
```
maria: after ~30m resident GPU memory trending up ~200MB/hour until OOM on 40GB card. Attached perf snapshot from perf-bot.

perf-bot: uploaded profile: https://perf.internal/profiles/1798501123/snapshot.pb.gz (nvprof-like traces + heapinfo) :white_check_mark:

noah: I ran the same repro on a smaller repro run. Quick notes: kernel selection switched from fused-attn to attn-stream on long sequences (cost heuristic triggered). The stream kernel allocates a per-request workspace (kv+tmp) that isn't being freed fast enough because of continuous batching. nvprof excerpt: 
```
GPU Memory Allocations:
  active:  3.2GB
  reserved: 4.8GB
  pools: 
    pool0 (workspace): 1.6GB (3 blocks)
    pool1 (kv-cache): 2.4GB (many small blocks)
Free list fragmentation: several ~64MB holes
```

noah: doesn't look like a classic driver leak — counts of live allocations match expected live tensors, but reserved pool grows due to fragmentation + allocator failing to coalesce.

ajay: that points at allocator tunables (workspace sizing, merge thresholds). Did you run with our jemalloc-like GPU pool flags? (GPU_POOL_MAX_FRAG=0.2 etc)

maria: ran with defaults. I can re-run with GPU_POOL_MAX_FRAG=0.05 and DEFER_FREE=1.

sara: also check KV cache behavior — we recently added per-request prefix caching which pins kv slices across micro-batches for reuse; if batching heuristics now merges requests differently, lifetime of those slices extends and prevents coalescing. Try explicit kv eviction after inference call as quick check.

noah: I instrumented allocator and found many small 16KB frees that get held in per-stream caches — these prevent large contiguous free ranges from forming. Quick experiment: forced cudaFree on pooled buffers after every request reduces reserved size growth but increases latency by ~6ms.

maria: latency hit is okay for repro. Can we make a judgement call: is this fragmentation (allocator policy) or a leak (driver/ CUDA not returning pages)?

ajay: leaning fragmentation. Evidence: total allocated size (by application) stays bounded; reserved space by driver grows due to fragmentation and pool thresholds. If it were a leak, cudaMalloc counts would keep increasing without corresponding frees.

noah: attaching a tiny bisect script I used (paste below) — it toggles kernel-picker heuristics, workspace cap, and pool defers to find the trigger.
```bash
# bisect-kv-workspace.sh (very rough)
for flag in 
  "KERNEL_PICKER_MODE=cost" 
  "KERNEL_PICKER_MODE=latency" 
  "WORKSPACE_CAP_MB=256" 
  "WORKSPACE_CAP_MB=512" 
  "GPU_POOL_DEFER=1" 
  "GPU_POOL_DEFER=0"; do
  echo "RUNNING $flag"
  env $flag ./repro.sh > /tmp/out_$flag.log 2>&1 &
  sleep 1800
  pkill -f repro.sh || true
done
```

maria: thanks — I'll run the bisect overnight on a3-8. Any suggestions for instrumentation to capture coalesce failures?

noah: enable allocator debug logging: EXPORT ALLOC_DEBUG=1 and also set POOL_COALESCE_THRESHOLD_BYTES=65536. That will print coalesce attempts to stderr. Grep for "coalesce failed" in logs. Also run a short script to snapshot cudaMalloc/cudaFree counts from driver api (we have a helper: scripts/gpu_alloc_counters.py).

sara: if bisect points to kh-picker change, we should consider forcing the older fused kernel for sequences >512 until allocator improvements land. That avoids extra workspace allocations entirely. Can we add quick AB test via routing?

ajay: yes — routing policy can pin model variant or kernel-mode at request level. Put a canary on 10% traffic to older kernel for night windows. But first confirm with bisect.

maria: running now. Will dump logs and perf snapshots to perf internal and update thread tomorrow morning. Thanks all. :pray:

perf-bot: new snapshot uploaded: https://perf.internal/profiles/1798501423/snapshot-2.pb.gz

noah: quick follow-up — if we confirm fragmentation, propose short-term mitigations: 1) increase workspace cap to reduce frequent alloc/free churn 2) enable deferred frees so that small blocks accumulate and coalesce during idle 3) tune coalesce threshold to be more aggressive 4) revert kernel-picker change where feasible. Long term: implement a compaction pass in allocator to merge free segments during low load windows.

sara: noted. I'll draft a small ops runbook for emergency mitigation (how to set env flags, how to route to older kernel, and how to trigger a compaction job).

title: eng-runtime
body:
eng-runtime

Sam: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel selection change the eu-west-1 p99 jumped and we're seeing more cross-zone spillover. Quick capture: p50 48ms, p95 210ms, p99 498ms in eu-west-1. us-west-2 p99 stayed ~260ms.
Maya: Ugh. Do we know if it's batching or KV cache related?
Jordan: My initial trace shows increased cold-KV misses for spillover requests. When requests land in a different cluster they miss local prefix cache and end up doing longer KV loads + larger batches form.
Li: Also the new kernel picked a wider matmul path for long sequences which increases per-token cost/latency at tail. Could be multiplicative with cache misses.
Ellie: ops-bot reported cross-zone spillover rate +12% in the last 6h after rollout.
ops-bot: [alert] cluster-routing: cross_zone_spillover_rate: 12.4% (6h window)
Riz: TL;DR: two interacting effects — kernel selection increased per-token latency for long seqs; routing spilled more traffic across regions leading to cache churn and bigger effective batches.
Sam: Proposed short-term mitigation: tighten regional affinity and reduce spillover threshold to 0.55, plus reduce max_batch_wait_ms from 8 -> 4 for eu-west-1. That should cut tail by reducing KV churn and big batch formation.
Maya: Agree can try config tweak. We should measure token-budget targets too — some queues were allowed to accumulate large token budgets which encouraged big batches.
Jordan: I ran a quick sim locally. Patch config:```yaml
queue_policy:
  type: regional_affinity
  spillover_threshold: 0.55
  local_slot_reserve: 0.7
batching:
  max_batch_wait_ms: 4
  max_tokens_per_batch: 4096
  token_budget_target: 1200  # target tokens before forcing flush
```
Sim result (synthetic): p99 down ~28% for eu-west-1, throughput ~ -3% steady-state.
Li: Important: token_budget_target interacts with KV cache hit rate. Lower budget -> more frequent flushing -> more small batches but better locality. We'll need to watch cost.
Ellie: Can we run a short canary: 10% of traffic in eu-west-1 with these settings and collect: p50/p95/p99, kv_hit_rate, cross_zone_spillover, cost_per_token?
Riz: I'll schedule the canary. What about kernel rollback? Should we pin older kernel for eu-west-1 if canary not enough?
Sam: Keep kernel change active for now, but include kernel_version as a dimension in the canary metrics. If p99 improvement <20% or KV hit not improving we fallback kernel to previous.
Maya: Also add a debug trace flag for a cohort of requests to capture KV miss stack and batch composition. Something like: `x-debug-trace: regional-cache,kv,batch` and redact PII.
Jordan: I'll add trace flag + delta counters for "batch_size_at_flush" and "kv_hit_post_routing".
Ellie: Ops: run canary at 10% for 3 hours during low traffic window (0400-0700 UTC). If metrics look good, roll to 40% over 2h. If regressions, rollback to old queue_policy and/or kernel.
ops-bot: action_created: canary-job-1764003210. Owner: Riz. Window: 2026-03-18T04:00:00Z -> 07:00:00Z.
Riz: Started canary plan. Will post a short dashboard link when metrics stream in.
Sam: One more note — check that the KV cache's TTL/size isn't asymmetric between regions. We saw different eviction behavior in eu-west-1 last month. If cache size is smaller, affinity wins more.
Li: I'll pull KV cache memstats and eviction rates for last 7 days.
Maya: Good. After canary we should profile kernel hot paths with the profiler to see if matmul widening still hurts when locality improves.
Sam: Thanks all — timeline: canary this morning, small dashboard by +30m after start, decision at +3h. Keep messages short here and post findings in #eng-runtime once canary finishes.

title: support
body:
support

bob_acme: Hey team — during our nightly load test on Dedicated we saw a sudden burst of 401s and 429s around 02:12 UTC. Apps hit a hard stop, can someone take a look?
jen_support: Sorry about that — can you paste a request_id or example logs so we can trace?
bob_acme: request_id=rid_8a3f. Attaching a minimal repro curl below. This started after we started long-context sessions (~32k-64k tokens) concurrently.
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \\ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \\ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\ 
  -d '{"model":"rwd-large", "input":"<32k tokens repeated>", "stream":true}'
```
alex_sre: Looking at infra logs now. I can see a huge spike in KV eviction rate on the nodes that served tenant acme. Evict rate jumped then our write path started returning throttles (429). No GPU OOMs, CPU okay.
maria_runtime: Also seeing auth failures correlated with the same window: token validation returned 401s a lot of times during the eviction burst. Need to confirm if that's upstream auth or a side-effect.
devin_reliability: Hypothesis: long-context sessions fragment the KV slab/memory, causing aggressive eviction. That causes increased writes/repairs to KV which triages into throttle paths. Client retries + refresh flows produce auth churn (401s) we then surface. We should repro.
bob_acme: We can reproduce reliably. Steps: spawn 50 parallel sessions, each priming a 32k prompt, then send streaming continuations every 200ms. Errors appear ~3 minutes in.
jen_support: Can you enable debug headers for us? Header: `x-rwd-debug: kv` will surface KV stats per request, or set `x-rwd-tenant-test: acme` if you want a dedicated trace.
alex_sre: Repro command I'm using (k6):
```
import http from 'k6/http';
// simplified snippet: run 50 VUs, persistent long body, stream loop
```
Sample node logs during failure window:
[evict] tenant=acme evict_rate=285/s kv_write_errors=23 throttle=1
[auth] tenant=acme token_refresh_failed status=401 attempts=7
[api] request_id=rid_8a3f status=429 route=/v1/generate node=i-0abcd1234
maria_runtime: Immediate mitigations we can try: increase tenant kv_cache.max_entries to 2x, enable prefix_caching for long contexts, and reduce write amplification by batching small writes. I'll prep a tenant override.
devin_reliability: Longer-term: autoscaler tweak — when kv_evict_rate > 100/s for > 30s, scale Dedicated pool by +50% (capped) and temporarily relax eviction aggressiveness. Need to avoid runaway billing.
bob_acme: Please cap the autoscale so we don't get billed out of control. We can accept a manual approval on >2x billing.
jen_support: We'll add a billing guard. Also opened support ticket #18921 to track this.
ops-bot: Incident INC-18921 created and assigned to alex_sre (P2).
alex_sre: Action plan: (1) run controlled repro in staging with acme workload (2) apply tenant kv_max_entries=2x in prod for acme as a short-term fix (3) push autoscale policy PR to make kv pressure trigger faster scale but with billing cap. ETA 2h for mitigation, 24h for full fix.
bob_acme: We'll pause heavy load tests until you confirm.
alex_sre: Update: applied kv_max_entries override, enabled prefix_caching for tenant acme. Observed evict rate drop from ~280/s -> ~45/s and kv_write_errors reduced to 0; 401/429 counts returned to baseline within two minutes.
bob_acme: Confirmed on our side, errors stopped. Thanks everyone.
jen_support: Closing follow-up steps: (1) schedule a postmortem on Monday to discuss fragmentation mitigations (2) add dashboard panel for kv_fragmentation_ratio and per-tenant evict_rate alert (3) keep billing guard in place.

title: eng-ml
body:
eng-ml

sara_ml: bringing up orion-v1 (open checkpoint) on staging with int4 quant profile. baseline fp16 looks fine but int4 outputs have two weird regressions we didn't see before: Korean honorific suffixes are getting dropped in polite forms, and Arabic diacritics (harakat) are being reordered or duplicated, which changes pronunciation. unsure if tokenizer or quantization is the culprit. anyone seen this pattern?
kenji: can you paste minimal examples?
sara_ml: sure — examples below from the same prompt, fp16 vs int4.
```
# prompt: translate polite Korean
EN: "Please tell Mr. Kim the meeting starts at 3pm."
FP16: "김 선생님께 회의가 오후 3시에 시작된다고 전해주세요."
INT4: "김 선생님께 회의가 오후 3시 시작된다고 전해주세요."  # missing honorific connective '된다고' vs '시작된다고' -> sounds informal

# prompt: Arabic short vowels
AR: "كتبَ الطالبُ الرسالةَ"  (he wrote the letter, with harakat)
FP16: "كَتَبَ الطالبُ الرسالةَ"
INT4: "كتبَ الطالب الرسالةََ"  # diacritics merged/moved, duplicate fatha on last token
```
kenji: ugh, that Korean drop could be a token boundary/segment merge issue. The Arabic diacritics reordering smells like byte-level normalization or tokenizer treating combining marks differently after quantized embedding mismatch.
maria: i ran a quick tokenization diff between the FP16 tokenizer output and the orion int4 tokenizer table — there was a recent microchange in the merge table: commit 6b3f2a6 changed normalization for U+0652 (sukun) handling. tagging @ben_plat.
ben_plat: thanks — that commit was intended to collapse combining marks to reduce vocab size, but i thought we gated it behind a model-compat flag. maybe the quantized runtime is ignoring compatibility metadata. i'll bisect. can you attach a failing sample and the generated token ids?
sara_ml: attached token ids from staging (pasted below). note the Korean polite suffix tokens are split differently: 
```
FP16 token ids: [1023, 45012, 7831, 8902, 212]  # the polite suffix kept as single token
INT4 token ids: [1023, 45012, 7831, 89, 02, 212] # token split inserted extra boundary
```
kenji: split at the suffix -> combined with smoothing in int4 causes softmax to prefer shorter sequence. that could explain omission. for Arabic: are combining marks preserved in tokenization or dropped then reattached incorrectly?
ben_plat: infra-bot can you run a quick canary comparing orion fp16 vs orion-int4 with tokenization set to legacy-normalize?
infra-bot: canary job queued: canary-1717543210-01 started on staging (GPU pool: orion-staging).
ori-bot: quick eval results (summary): 250 samples bilingual set (Korean polite set + Modern Standard Arabic with harakat). BLEU: FP16=28.7, INT4=24.1 (drop 4.6). ChrF: FP16=0.532, INT4=0.488. Korean subset BLEU drop=6.2, Arabic subset BLEU drop=3.3. Noted tokenization divergence on 18% of samples.
maria: thanks. my local bisect shows the merge table change correlates with tokenization divergence. patch idea: restore combining-mark preservation for arabic and keep Korean suffix merges (don't split). but we need config gating at runtime so quantized models use compatible tokenizer metadata.
kenji: agree. short-term: pin tokenizer version for orion-int4 to legacy-normalize and re-run. long-term: we should add a tokenizer-compat-check at model load that fails fast if vocab/normalization differ from training config.
sara_ml: I'll prepare a regression PR with failing test cases (korean polite, arabic harakat). also adding evaluation hooks to flag >2 BLEU loss on locale-specific slices.
ben_plat: once PR's up, i'll schedule a canary rollback and retest. tagging @maria for review.
maria: ack, review incoming.
ben_plat: infra-bot, pause canary: canary-1717543210-01 paused to prevent more prod-like traffic.
infra-bot: canary-1717543210-01 paused.
kenji: thanks all. small ask: add one synthetic test that forces combining mark order permutations to ensure quantization doesn't re-order combining marks. that caught us later in prod last year. :eyes:
sara_ml: will do. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

title: eng-runtime
body:
eng-runtime

alex: Quick question for the group — I'm putting together a concise proposal for span naming + semantic attrs for LLM requests. Goal: low-cardinality span names, rich but scrubbed attributes, and clear guidance for exporters/retention. TL;DR idea below, please poke holes.

maria: +1 on doing this now. we're getting inconsistent keys across services.

jamie: can you post the concrete examples? hard to review abstractly.

alex: yep. draft proposal: 
```
span.name = llm.exec.{op}    # op in {generate, embed, rerank, score}
// examples: llm.exec.generate, llm.exec.embed

semantic attributes (low-cardinality preferred):
- llm.model.name = "gptx-3b"        # model family
- llm.model.variant = "q4_0"        # quantization/variant (optional)
- llm.model.version = "2026-03-12"  # pinned release tag
- llm.op.tokens.prompt = 42
- llm.op.tokens.generated = 128
- llm.op.tokens.total = 170
- llm.kv_cache.hit = true|false
- llm.kv_cache.entries = 7
- llm.routing.policy = "latency" | "cost" | "region"
- llm.routing.result = "primary" | "fallback:small-model"
- llm.fallback.reason = "quota" | "slow" | "hot"  # optional
- telemetry.sample_rate = "0.01"  # exporter hint
```
Notes in the doc: avoid adding tenant/customer IDs directly; instead provide `tenant.hash` (sha256 hex truncated) if needed, and never include raw prompt text in spans except in sampled debug traces.

ryan: This looks sensible. two questions: (1) why `llm.exec` instead of `llm.request`? (2) where do we put request-level latency vs model-internal latencies?

alex: Good q. `llm.exec` feels like an action (execution) vs a transport `request` — aim is to keep span.name focused on the operation semantics we care about for dashboards. For latencies: top-level span.duration is the full end-to-end time; we should also encourage sub-span naming like `llm.exec.kernel` or `llm.exec.kvcache` for internal breakdowns when services can instrument them.

maria: On cardinality: we need strict rules that `llm.model.name` values must be normalized to a predefined catalog (service should map aliases), otherwise dashboards explode. Ops: maintain a shared model registry.

jamie: Agree. Also propose we bucket token counts for high-cardinality prevention e.g. `llm.tokens.bucket = "0-32","33-128","129-512","512+"` for many dashboards and keep raw counts as numeric attrs only in sampled traces.

devex: +1 on buckets. UX note: console dashboard should show both buckets for distribution and median from metrics. We'll need a small ETL that rolls up token histograms from spans into metrics.

infra-bot: export: OTLP -> ingestion pipeline -> span-filter -> long-term store. recommended filters: drop `prompt`/`input_text` unless `telemetry.sample_rate >= 0.05`. retention policy: full spans with all attrs 30d, aggregated token metrics 365d.

ryan: About exporters: we need to keep an allowlist of attributes that go to external SaaS (Datadog/Lightstep). e.g., model family OK, tenant.hash OK, but not prompt. Also consider hashing model.version if it's high cardinality (commit SHAs).

alex: Another operational point: `llm.kv_cache.hit` should be boolean but we should also emit `llm.kv_cache.reason` only in sampled traces. `llm.kv_cache.entries` can be integer but again bucket it for dashboards.

maria: Edge case: embeddings route splits across specialized hardware. Add `llm.node.gpu_family = "a100"|"t4"|"cpu"`? is that too many dimensions?

jamie: We already expose region and instance-type in infra spans. For model-level metrics we can keep `llm.node.class = "gpu"|"cpu"` and `llm.node.region` to let us partition cost/latency. keep instance SKU as sampled attr.

devex: Small sample config proposal: default 1% full trace capture (includes prompt/content + all attrs), 5% debug for flagged customers, and 100% for errors above x% latency or model error codes. We can express this as `telemetry.sample_hint` attribute on spans to help exporters decide.

alex: Implementation plan: I'll open a tiny RFC with the name patterns and canonical keys + example code snippets for Go/Python OTEL instrumentation. Want to lock the attr names here first.

ryan: Please add a short migration guide for existing services that use old keys (we have ~12 services with slightly different names). also add unit tests for normalization mapping.

maria: Also add a compatibility guide for dashboards: mapping old fields -> new ones so Grafana/Looker queries don't break.

jamie: One more thought: span.name should include operation but not model to keep cardinality low. model belongs in attributes.

alex: Agreed. I'll iterate on the RFC and post a link. Thanks all — can people react with :thumbsup: if they approve the draft we put in RFC form?

maria: :thumbsup:

jamie: :thumbsup:

ryan: :thumbsup:

body:
eng-ml

nightly-eval-bot: nightly eval alert: long_context_instructions_v2 — model rwd/llama2-70b-q6 — overall QA score down 12% vs baseline, 2026-02-12 07:10 UTC. failing prompts clustered at >6k tokens. link: https://internal/evals/1769 (CI ticket created)

elaine-ml: saw this on my dashboard this morning. example generation drops instruction halfway through the long system prompt, instruction reappears in next token window as a stray token.

elaine-ml: snippet from failing run (trimmed):
```
[SYS] You are an assistant that ALWAYS follow instructions. Keep context and do not omit steps.
... (6500 tokens of context) ...
User: Do the following steps: 1) audit 2) summarize 3) give mitigation

=== model output ===
Step 1: audit...
Step 2: summarize...

[OUTPUT ENDS abruptly mid-sentence]

elia (note): instruction "Do the following steps" missing in mid-output, generation continues later with unrelated content.
```

arjun: which variant + quant config? any recent infra changes?

elaine-ml: rwd/llama2-70b-q6 (our 6-bit dynamic quant build), nightly commit 2026-02-11 that switched KV eviction heuristic from age-based -> prefix-fade heuristic (taylor pushed PR #412).

ben-ml: this smells like KV slot recycle / prefix pointer misalignment rather than pure truncation. if eviction marks oldest prefix incorrectly you can drop instruction references but still report full seq len.

taylor-research: yep that PR changed the eviction boundary math to prefer evicting large contiguous stale spans to help perf on streaming workloads. it passed unit tests but not long-context stress. rolling back now? or can we repro locally first?

vivian: I can repro on my dev rig with the nightly model build + the failing prompt set. running a repro now, will paste logs.

vivian: repro logs (KV debug enabled):
```
KVState[shard0]: seq_base=6120, kv_slots=8192, oldest_active_slot=6118, eviction_ptr=6118
KVState[shard1]: seq_base=6120, kv_slots=8192, oldest_active_slot=0, eviction_ptr=6118
WARN: prefix-fade found cross-shard gap, forcing slot wrap without migrating markers
```

ben-ml: there it is — cross-shard gap. looks like the heuristic didn't handle sparse marker distribution across shards when long prefix spans multiple shards. causes stale markers to be treated as free and reused mid-context -> instruction loss.

arjun: is this specific to quant builds? vivian, can you run same prompt against float32 (non-quant) nightly to rule out model-level KV encoding issues?

vivian: running float32 now, will compare.

elaine-ml: impact summary for product: failing prompts ~0.7% of long_context_instructions_v2 but they are high-severity (instructions missing). customers on Dedicated reported 1 similar support ticket overnight.

taylor-research: urgent plan: 1) roll back prefix-fade heuristic on nightly and dedicated canaries, 2) add cross-shard marker integrity check + unit test, 3) run full long-context stress harness across quant + float builds. agree?

ben-ml: +1. also add a short-term mitigation to detect odd slot reuse at generation time and trigger a fallback to a compatible model variant (e.g., fallback to float32 or smaller context config) with a warning in logs.

arjun: assign actions: taylor -> rollback PR and add unit test, vivian -> repro matrix (quant vs float) + attach KV debug traces to CI ticket 1769, ben -> implement runtime detection + fallback, elaine -> customer impact notes + support triage. target: hotfix and canary tomorrow morning (UTC).

vivian: repro matrix started: quant fails consistently, float32 run shows no instruction loss in initial 10 runs. attaching traces to CI ticket now.

nightly-eval-bot: CI ticket 1769 updated with vivian traces and regression diff (tagged @taylor-research @ben-ml).

elaine-ml: thanks team — please post rollback status here once done. :thumbsup:

kai: heads-up — around 03:12 UTC we saw a spike of tiny-pod evictions in sa-east1 after an AZ rebalancer moved several warm nodes. pending-tiny-pods 130 -> 610 in 25m, attach failures increasing.

leah: any logs? suspect attach/timeouts or attach-service websocket churn.

kai: snippet from sa-nv-11 at 03:14:

```
Mar 18 03:14:07 kubelet[3122]: attach: device attach error: rpc error: code = Unknown desc = websocket: close 1006
Mar 18 03:14:07 kernel: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
Mar 18 03:14:09 kubelet[3122]: kubelet: attach: context deadline exceeded while waiting for device
Mar 18 03:14:09 kubelet[3122]: evicting pod tiny-run-9b
```

omar: note the rebalancer did a backfill pattern: it cordoned a set of nodes in sa-east1-b then drained and reattached warm nodes across racks. That increased cross-rack attach ops and left many 0.5 GPU islands.

tess: infra-bot alert: sa-east1: tiny-evict-rate > 120/min for 10m (alert_id: infra:tiny-evict:3789).

ops-lead: immediate mitigations: 1) pause AZ rebalancer traffic for sa-east1 for 15m 2) reduce warm-node backfill concurrency (controller flag BACKFILL_CONCURRENCY=2) 3) push a scheduler "consolidate-tiny" soft preference to favor existing tiny-hosts to reduce attach churn 4) optional: canary bump nf_conntrack on 6 warm nodes if needed.

leah: prefer pausing rebalancer + controller throttle + scheduler hint. Rebalancer pause buys time and is reversible.

kai: i'll pause rebalancer now in sa-east1 and tag affected nodes with note=rebalance-paused.

omar: i'll prepare controller patch for backfill concurrency and jitter (backoff 100-400ms) and canary deploy to sa-east1-a. PR: https://github.com/redwood/warmpool/pull/4621 (wip).

leah: i'll open a small scheduler change: if pod.gpu <= 0.5 then add soft score +120 for node.tiny_count>0, but cap additional density to avoid noisy-neighbor (max_tiny_per_node=8). Will namespace-opt-in feature flag.

ops-lead: rollout plan: 1) pause rebalancer at 03:30 UTC 2) deploy controller throttle in sa-east1-a at 03:35 3) enable scheduler consolidate-tiny on 8 canary nodes (label canary=tinyconsol) 4) monitor 30m (attach-p95, evict-rate, pending-tiny-pods, nf_conntrack_count, node-cpu). rollback if evict-rate > 15/min or attach-p95 > 30s.

infra-bot: [update] rebalancer paused at 03:31 UTC.

kai: initial canary numbers at 03:42 after 7m: pending-tiny-pods down 38%, evict-rate down 45%, attach-p95 from 52s -> 21s.

omar: good. watch for CPU/GPU saturation on packed nodes; coalescing increases host CPU use. Also record metric attach_ops_saved and warm_backfill_blocked to evaluate if we need longer-term design changes.

leah: note tenant opt-in: some tenants rely on spread for hot-noisy workloads; we must not violate their anti-affinity. feature-flag by namespace only.

ops-lead: follow-ups: 1) add an attach-proxy experiment (reduce websocket churn) 2) review rebalancer heuristics to avoid simultaneous cross-rack backfills 3) quantify cost delta of packing vs extra warm hosts and include in postmortem.

infra-bot: [final] 30m canary snapshot at 04:05 UTC: evict-rate=7.1/min (target <10), attach-p95=19.8s (target <25s). recommending gradual rollout and re-enabling rebalancer with lower concurrency.

title: support
body:
support

Liam (CS): Heads up — customer 'stark-ind' opened a ticket: multiple backend services getting TLS errors to our Private endpoint in their VPC since rotation this morning.
Jess (Support): Can you paste the exact error they reported?
Liam (CS): They see java.security.cert.CertPathValidatorException: signature check failed and curl gives: "SSL: certificate subject name does not match" intermittently.
Maria (Eng): That combination could be chain ordering or missing intermediate, or possibly we uploaded a cert with wrong SAN during rotation. Which rotation job ran?
Alex (Infra): Rotation job ID rot-20240504-0623 ran at 06:23 UTC. Our upload logs show a 403 from customer-bucket on the first attempt. Retries succeeded later, but I'm seeing a partial artifact set on the instance.
Sam (Oncall): Do we have any TLS handshake logs from the private gateway?
Alex (Infra): Pasted from gateway logs:
```
2024-05-04T06:24:10Z tls: handshake error: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority
2024-05-04T06:24:11Z tls: client hello for host private.stark.example
2024-05-04T06:24:11Z tls: presented certificates: 1 cert(s)
```
Jess (Support): Customer says some of their services (go apps) work fine; their Java microservices fail. Typical AIA/OCSP/fetch behavior differences.
Liam (CS): I asked them to run these debug commands and send output:
```
openssl s_client -connect private.stark.example:443 -servername private.stark.example -showcerts
openssl x509 -in cert.pem -text -noout
```
Maria (Eng): They returned the s_client output showing only the leaf certificate and no intermediate(s). Chrome flagged NET::ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID. That explains the discrepancy.
Alex (Infra): Root cause likely: rotation uploaded only leaf.pem to the VM due to temporary permission failure on S3 PUT; later cleanup left leaf present but not the intermediate.
CertBot: cert-rotator: rot-20240504-0623 attempt 1 -> 403 Forbidden; attempt 2 -> success but missing post-upload verification (no fullchain check).
Maria (Eng): Action items: 1) Restore full chain on the customer's private gateway (fullchain = leaf + intermediate [+ root optional]) 2) Restart gateway process to pick up cert 3) Patch cert-rotator to validate fullchain after upload and fail/rollback on mismatch 4) Add IAM fix so upload won't 403 5) Add support playbook for manual combine + restart.
Jess (Support): Manual remediation snippet I sent to customer (and can run if they provide access):
```
# combine certs in order: leaf -> intermediate -> (root optional)
cat leaf.pem intermediate.pem > fullchain.pem
# place on gateway
sudo cp fullchain.pem /etc/redwood/ssl/private.stark.example.crt
sudo cp privkey.pem /etc/redwood/ssl/private.stark.example.key
sudo systemctl restart redwood-private-gateway
# verify
openssl s_client -connect private.stark.example:443 -servername private.stark.example -showcerts
```
Sam (Oncall): Also asked customer to temporarily open egress for OCSP/AIA endpoints if they can — helpful for clients that try AIA fetching; they said they have strict deny-by-default policies.
Alex (Infra): I've applied an IAM policy update to the rotator service role (s3:PutObject on customer bucket) — ticket INF-1241. Re-ran rotator with new validations.
CertBot: cert-rotator: re-run rot-20240504-0623 -> upload succeeded; post-upload s_client check now passes (full chain presented).
Maria (Eng): I'll push a small change to cert-rotator to require a two-step verification: (1) list objects and checksum, (2) s_client against the endpoint via our control plane to ensure chain length >=2. If verification fails, rollback and alert.
Liam (CS): Customer confirmed Java services recovered after we re-deployed fullchain and restarted gateway. They kept curl tests green as well.
Jess (Support): Documenting follow-up for customer: recommend allowing OCSP responses and AIA if possible for smoother rotations; offered to run rotations during maintenance windows.
Sam (Oncall): Follow-ups for internal teams:
- eng-runtime: add rotation incomplete alert to ops dashboards
- infra: ensure rotator has least-privilege but reliable bucket access; add retries/exponential backoff
- support: add short playbook entry for "missing intermediate" with commands above
Alex (Infra): Marking incident as resolved pending 48h stability check.
DeployBot: deploy: cert-rotator v1.3.5 -> prod (includes post-upload verification)
Maria (Eng): Root cause summary: cert-rotator experienced transient S3 403 during rotation which resulted in only leaf being deployed to private gateway. Clients without cached or fetched intermediates failed validation. Secondary contributor: customer's strict egress deny prevented OCSP/AIA recovery for some clients.
Liam (CS): Customer will confirm after 24h; closing ticket if stable. Thanks everyone.

title: eng-runtime
body:
eng-runtime

maria: Heads-up — repro'ing a KV cache reclaim latency spike on Dedicated when sessions go past ~18k tokens. Seen on on-prem racks and also in a handful of VPC Private installs.

josh: repro steps? tried hosted or just dedicated/private?

maria: Dedicated + Private (on-prem). Hosted seems less hit but still shows occasional p99 blips. Root cause feels like slow slab/page reclaim + GPU pinned frames not released fast enough.

chen: sharing profiling snapshot (short):
```
# perf top outline (aggregated stack)
40.3% runtime::kv::evict_loop
18.1% kernel:page_reclaim
12.7% runtime::gpu::pin_unlock
6.5% memcpy
4.2% other
```

chen: also saw high major_faults count when context length grows.

sean: interesting — hosted boxes use our tuned kernel (auto-tuned pagevec sizes + 2MB hugepages) while Dedicated VMs sometimes fall back to distro kernel. That could explain the severity delta.

aisha: are we sure it's not batching heuristics causing long-lived cold entries? maybe some workloads keep prefixes unique so cache reuse low -> more churn.

maria: yes we ruled out batching config: same request shape & batch size across envs. When we force reuse (same prompt prefixes) reclaim rate drops. So it's eviction pressure + allocator interaction.

josh: can you paste the vmstats during a spike? esp /proc/vmstat counters like numa_foreign_faults, pgpgin, pgpgout, nr_slab_objects.

maria: attaching a clipped sample:
```
pgpgin 45012
pgpgout 1208
nr_slab_objects 1.2e6
nr_page_table_pages 43000
major_fault 982
swapin 0
```

ryan: note Private on-prem uses older kernel (4.x) on several customer appliances. We had a known bug where pagevec batches are small and we hit page-turnover thrash under high KV insert/delete.

chen: another interesting bit — our GPU runtime keeps a small LRU of pinned host pages (for faster H2D), but the reclaim path tries to free them and ends up doing synchronous DMA unpin which blocks the cpu thread. On older kernels that path is less async-friendly.

sean: so two levers: 1) kernel/page reclaim improvements (hugepages+pagevec tuning) 2) runtime change to avoid sync unpin on critical path (deferred unpin, epoch-based reclamation).

aisha: deferred unpin would help latency but could increase peak memory. Private customers with limited GPUs might not accept that. Tradeoff.

maria: agreed. For Dedicated we have more headroom and could enable deferred unpin as an opt-in config flag. For Private/on-prem we may need a safer default.

josh: any evidence of fragmentation causing large contiguous allocation failures? e.g., failure to allocate big KV frames forcing many small allocations and extra bookkeeping?

maria: yes — fragmentation shows up in /proc/buddyinfo dumps. On affected hosts we see many order-0/1 free blocks and very few high-order. Runtime then falls back to multiple small frames which increases metadata and churn.

chen: short-term mitigation we tried: call madvise(DONTNEED) on stale pages to help kernel reclaim faster, and use MADV_FREE where available. That reduced p99 by ~30% in Dedicated.

ryan: for Private, customers with locked-down kernels can't accept madvise fiddling sometimes (policy). Also VPC appliances with custom NICs (SR-IOV) show higher page pin rates due to RDMA-zero-copy flows. That exacerbates pinned-frame reclaim cost.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: runtime/kv-evict-madvise-experiment -> canary on Dedicated tonight @ 02:00 UTC :rocket:

aisha: can we also try enabling 2MB hugepages in Dedicated and run the long-context replay suite? Hugepages reduced TLB pressure in earlier tests.

chen: will run replay with flags: --kv-evict-debug --deferred-unpin=off/on --use-hugepages=yes and compare.

josh: add a matrix for Private: (kernel 4.x vs 5.x), (hugepages on/off), (deferred-unpin on/off). Also include MIG vs non-MIG GPU shapes — MIG tends to pin more small buffers.

maria: Action items:
- chen -> run matrix across Dedicated config and post flamegraphs (by EOD PST)
- ryan -> list Private hosts still on 4.x kernel and check possibility of backporting pagevec patches
- aisha -> draft opt-in runtime flag for deferred unpin with config docs + memory budget guard
- josh -> create perf dashboard panel for kv-evict latency across envs (hosted/dedicated/private)

sean: also consider a graceful fallback: when reclaim path sees synchronous unpin > X ms, switch to a mode that reduces aggressive eviction (throttle background evict). Avoid cascading latency.

maria: good idea — that will reduce tail risk. Let's sync tomorrow in eng-runtime stand with short demo.

josh: noted. thanks all. :thumbsup:

maya: hey team — nightly eval CI failing intermittently since the quant-quantize merge, looks like shard workers are hitting queue backpressure and then we get duplicate counts in the metrics. job: https://ci.redwood.ai/teams/infra/runs/38291 :frowning:

akshay: can you paste the runner logs? is it OOM or 503s?

maya: paste below. mostly 503 / RPC errors, then the runner retries and we count the same sample twice.

maya: ```
2026-01-29T03:21:12Z runner[shard=21] ERROR: enqueue task failed: queue_full (capacity=4096)
2026-01-29T03:21:12Z runner[shard=21] WARN: rpc call to worker-17:503 ServiceUnavailable
2026-01-29T03:21:12Z runner[shard=21] INFO: retrying (attempt=1) id=sample-3f9a
2026-01-29T03:21:13Z eval-collector INFO: recorded sample id=sample-3f9a status=completed
2026-01-29T03:21:13Z eval-collector INFO: recorded sample id=sample-3f9a status=completed
```

tara: that double-recording is probably from the collector treating retries as new completions. We need idempotency keys on the collector side. Also I think the quantized model increased per-inference latency, so queues fill faster.

akshay: +1 on idempotency. Two parts: (1) dedupe at collector by sample_id, (2) make runner retries attach the same request_id or return a duplicate flag. Also reduce default shard count in CI so we don't oversubscribe the small runners.

julian: SRE alerted on CPU spikes for the eval-runners around the same window: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/ops/eval-runner?panel=3

runner:
  shards: 32
  max_workers_per_shard: 2
  queue_capacity: 4096

```

akshay: I'll open the dedupe PR for the collector. Plan: if collector sees sample_id already recorded, return HTTP 200 with body {"duplicate":true} and emit metric "eval.sample_duplicate" with tag model=<model>.

elaine_cs: 1) Try int8 quantization on the current 13B model for non-critical routes. 2) Route low-priority (batch) requests to the cheaper region pool. 3) Enable short batching window + prefix KV caching for the assistant prompts. 4) Run a small A/B canary of a 7B Mistral variant for latency/cost comparison.

jordan_ml: Short answer: negligible for QA on our eval set if we use dynamic quantization + recalibration on the prompt set. I ran a quick eval on 200 prompts from HelioForge's repro deck: Rouge/EM drops ~0.6-1.2% on average, but latency improved ~28% and token cost ~42%. I can share the eval table.

```bash
# quantize and run eval (demo):
python tools/quant_eval.py \\  --model checkpoints/13b/float32 \\  --quant int8 \\  --prompts data/helios_repro.json \\  --out results/helios_int8.csv
```

elaine_cs: Also propose routing policy change for non-SLA pool: send background embeddings + long-batch tasks to eu-west cheaper pool with throttled concurrency. That reduces pressure on the primary low-latency pool.

title: incidents
body:
incidents

incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: streaming p99 latency breach detected for service `generator-usw2` (rule: streaming_p99 > 1200ms) — current p99 2.1s, p95 420ms. Affected routes: /v1/stream, model=redwood-large. Incident id: INC-3587654321

maya: acked — I'm oncall. starting triage. pulling traces and logs now.

cheng: I can see a sudden cluster of stalled streams around 12:34 UTC, tail errors spike aligns with gpu-pool-3 node flaps. p95 jumped ~3x, p99 ~5x in last 6m. KV cache hit-rate dropped from 98% -> 72%.

raj: looking at infra side, node gpu-node-12 shows repeated correctable ECC events and several thermal-throttle logs: `nvml: Xid=79` and temp jumps to 95C before throttling. Also dmesg shows `GPU ECC corrected error`. Could be flaky accelerator.

oncall-sre: maya, can you confirm customer impact? which customers hitting p99? CS, please chime in.

customer-success: early look: 3 customers in us-west-2 reported degraded real-time ux (chat streaming stalls). Two are at PLG tier, one at enterprise (no SLA hit yet but close). We're drafting a short alert for them.

maya: ok mitigation plan: 1) quick traffic reroute away from gpu-pool-3, 2) cordon+drain gpu-node-12, 3) enable model fallback to cpu-variant for streaming for 5m window, 4) increase dedicated replicas for redwood-small to absorb load. Doing step 1 now.

dev-ops: routing update pushed: `routing-policy avoid-gpu-pool-3 set weight=0.0 for pool=gpu-pool-3` — effective in ~30s. Also added fallback rule: if model redwood-large p99 > 1s route 20% to redwood-small.

metrics-bot: grafana panels: https://grafana.company/d/streaming/streaming-latency?orgId=1&from=now-15m&to=now — p99 spike annotated.

cheng: graphs show initial improvement after reroute but we still see tail stalls for in-progress streams that were on the draining node. Those are the streaming stalls; likely KV cache warmup + in-flight sessions hitting the flakey GPU.

maya: starting drain: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-12 && kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60` — will allow in-flight pods 60s to finish.

raj: collecting GPU metrics: `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu,mem_used,mem_total --format=csv` output: `temp=95C, util=87%, mem=14GB/24GB`. Repeated ECC corrected count increments: +8 in last 10m.

infra-lead: please snapshot the kernel logs and NVML logs, then place node into quarantine for soak tests. Do not power-cycle yet; we need logs for vendor.

maya: done drain, pods evicted. node cordoned. Traffic for new sessions shifted. In-progress streams: we see many aborted frames -> we should surface to customers.

customer-success: sending initial customer note: "We're investigating elevated streaming latency & stalls in us-west-2. We're routing traffic away from affected hosts and will follow up with remediation steps." Will update customers at T+20.

dev-ops: proactive mitigation: increased redwood-small replicas by +3 in us-west-2 (deployment autoscale disabled temporarily). Verified new pods healthy.

cheng: tail traces: many stalls show stall point at KV cache miss followed by long backend retry (~1.5s) while waiting on node. Suggest enabling aggressive prefix caching TTL for 10m as short-term.

maya: toggled prefix cache -> TTL 10m for /v1/stream for redwood-large to reduce KV miss rate. Monitor impact.

metrics-bot: after reroute + drain + scale, p95 returned near baseline (~380ms) but p99 still at 980ms with a decreasing trend. Customer impact percent reduced from 1.2% -> 0.15%.

raj: we captured NVML logs and kernel oops snippets. ECC corrections correlate with thermal events. Hardware vendor ticket being opened. Posting logs to the incident channel: https://internal/attachments/INC-3587654321/nvml-log.txt

infra-lead: next steps: 1) quarantine node gpu-node-12 (marked unhealthy in provider), 2) kick off replacement workflow, 3) vendor RMA if ECC persists on replacement.

maya: scheduling handoff: I'm oncall for next 30m then dev-ops will continue mitigation and vendor coordination. @dev-ops please take primary after T+30.

dev-ops: taking over after T+30. I'll monitor until vendor confirms next steps. Also setting a temporary routing policy to avoid gpu-pool-3 for 24h.

cheng: note for postmortem — root causes to investigate: cache miss amplification due to node-level stalls, model KG memory pressure triggering ECC corrections, thresholding of routing not aggressive enough for tail events.

maya: adding action items to the incident doc: - escalate to vendor with NVML logs - add automated reroute at 95th percentile detection for streaming - refine draining grace for streaming sessions - notify impacted customers with timeline - run soak test on replacement node before returning to pool.

customer-success: will send update to impacted customers in 30m with current mitigation and ETA to resolution.

metrics-bot: final snapshot at T+25m: p95=390ms, p99=610ms, affected request rate 0.12%. Continuing to trend down.

maya: marking incident as 'mitigated' for oncall handoff conditions met — p99 under 1s and routing isolating faulty pool. Will keep channel open for follow-up.

dev-ops: noted. I'll continue vendor RMA and replacement plan. Please add any logs to the INC doc.

raj: attaching brief log excerpt for root cause timeline:
```
[12:33:48] nvml: ECC correctable error count increased by 3
[12:33:52] kernel: gpu thermal throttle engaged, temp=95C
[12:34:01] pod: stream-session-xyz stalled waiting on GPU op
[12:34:30] nvml: ECC correctable error count increased by 5
```

maya: thanks everyone — closing active paging. Will ping when vendor response or if p99 regresses. :thumbsup:

sam: Heads up — deploying payments-service Helm chart 2.4.0 to eu-west in ~15m. This includes a CRD schema bump and a data migration job (payment-migration). Deploy-bot preflight is flagging the migration job as missing. Thinking: manual gate + staged cutover. Opinions?

maya: Can we just pin to 2.3.9 for now and hotpatch the security fix?

lin: Pinning buys time but postpones the CRD migration forever. If the migration job is idempotent we should run it manually, then do a 10% canary on 2.4.0.

ops-paul: I prefer manual migration + small canary. Need a clear rollback playbook and release-notes entry that calls out the migration command and the DB snapshot plan.

To proceed run either: `kubectl apply -f migrations/payment-migration-v2.yaml` or enable via values: `--set migration.enabled=true`

sam: I can run the job in 5. Plan I suggest: 1) Run migration job manually (observe logs) 2) Trigger a 10% canary (helm values override to replicate low load) 3) If healthy after 30m promote; else rollback to chart 2.3.9 and revert any partial DB changes if needed.

maya: For the canary use an explicit values override: `replicaCount: 1`, `routing.canaryWeight: 10`, `global.maxRequests: 50` — keep image pinned to current digest during validation.

- Manual migration required: run `kubectl apply -f migrations/payment-migration-v2.yaml` before canary
- Canary: 10% traffic for 30m, smoke tests run by QA team

Will link migration manifest and the exact helm values used.

title: incidents
body:
incidents

support_erin: FYI customer Jordan from EduFlow reporting sudden 504s and p95 spikes on hosted API since ~09:12 UTC. They see a lot of "request timed out" errors and some 5xx  gateway logs.

sre_oncall: Copy. Any correlation with deploys or rate-limit spikes? Can you paste a sample error and the tenant id?

support_erin: Tenant: eduflow-prod. Sample error from their client: 
`HTTP/1.1 504 Gateway Timeout`
`{"error":"request queue timeout after 15s"}`
Also forwarded their curl repro loop. No deploys in the window per deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: No deploys recorded for eduflow-prod between 09:00-09:30 UTC. Autoscaler events: no scale-ups in that window.

alice_k: I'm attaching our edge/gateway excerpt — seeing a request-queue depth jump to ~12k concurrent queued requests on one gateway instance, queue_limit=8192, continued batching backlog. Logs: 
```
gateway queue_depth=12234 tenant=eduflow-prod action=enqueued
batcher backlog_ms=12430 continuous_batch_pending=214
request reject_reason=queue_limit_exceeded
```
Seems like continuous-batching accumulated longseq requests and kv-cache warmup stalled dequeue.

sre_oncall: Interesting — queue_depth > queue_limit triggers early-reject path, but here we have timeouts from tail latency not just rejects. Any sign of dequeue throughput drop (dequeue_rate/s) or GPU starvation?

alice_k: Dequeue rate fell from 850/s to ~120/s for the affected shard. CPU on the batcher worker is fine, but GPU utilization dropped because many longseq requests caused KV cache thrash and blocking dependency on cold KV loads. Also saw many `kvcache.miss` spikes.

mike_ops: Probable chain: tenant traffic microburst -> continuous-batcher groups longseq windows -> kvcache cold misses -> batcher stalls -> queue pileup -> tail timeouts. Short term: we can enable tenant-level fallback to smaller model and reduce continuous batching window to 50ms for this tenant. Also consider temporarily raising `queue_limit` to 16384 for eduflow-prod while we drain.

alice_k: Repro steps I used locally (shared to customer):
```
# simple repro loop hitting concat-longseq endpoint
for i in $(seq 1 5000); do
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-large-longseq","input":"'$(head -c 1000 /dev/urandom | base64)'"}' &
done
```
This produces the same backlog in our staging gateway after ~200s.

sre_oncall: Good repro. Runbook steps: 1) enable tenant fallback to redwood-medium for eduflow-prod 2) reduce continuous_batch_window_ms to 50 for their tenant 3) enable early-dequeue flush (admin toggle) 4) monitor queue_depth and dequeue_rate. Please run 1-2 and report metrics.

alice_k: Executed steps 1+2 at 09:26 UTC: fallback set, window changed, and issued an admin flush. Within ~45s we saw dequeue_rate jump to ~720/s and queue_depth fall from 12k -> 3k. Customer reports 504s dropping. Posting the metric samples: 
```
09:25 queue_depth=12234 dequeue_rate=118
09:26 set fallback->redwood-medium
09:26 set batch_window_ms=50
09:27 dequeue_rate=721 queue_depth=3021
09:28 queue_depth=820 dequeue_rate=760
```

mike_ops: Nice. Longer term: need KVCACHE async prefetch for longseqs + backpressure at ingress that prefers early-reject over piling up. Also consider per-tenant batching caps.

customer_jordan: Thanks team — reduction worked and traffic is mostly stable. We'll throttle a large client job on our side too. Appreciate the quick mitigation. :pray:

sre_oncall: Marking as mitigated. Follow-ups: (a) add automated detection for continuous-batching pileups (b) add kvcache cold-miss alert tied to dequeue_rate drop (c) create runbook section for tenant-level model fallback and queue_limit bump. Assigning follow-up tickets.

support_erin: I'll update the support ticket and include mitigation steps + repro script. Closing slack thread once follow-ups are created. :white_check_mark:

title: eng-platform
body:
eng-platform

Ivy W: Quick convo: we want to darklaunch v2 routing but keep billing/quota shown as v1 while we run reconciliation. Thoughts on minimal guarantees?
Luis G: Keep billing conservative: increment v1 quota per emitted token chunk (streaming) as soon as it's produced. That avoids big retroactive deltas.
Nora K: Agree. Need server-side dedupe for chunk resends (tenant+session+chunk-hash, 60s window) to avoid double billing for flaky connections.
Ivy W: Console UX: tiny badge on route "Darklaunch v2" + a "Reconcile" view that overlays billed (v1) vs observed (v2) tokens and shows anomalous sessions.
Luis G: Mapping table: model_v2 -> model_v1_id, plus token-normalization rules (strip telemetry/meta tokens for v1-equivalents). Make it runtime-config with audit logs.
Nora K: Telemetry signals: compat.dark_pct, compat.stream_token_delta, compat.dark_accept_rate, rollout.autoreduce.reason. Alert if stream_token_delta > 5% for 10m or dark_accept_rate < 90% for 5m.
Ivy W: Auto-reduce policy: if p95 latency for dark cohort > SLO*1.3 or error_ratio > 1.5 -> halve percent and post incident. Emit rollout.autoreduce.count for visibility.
flag-bot: FF guard applied: max step 20% per 5m for streaming routes.
Luis G: Implementation sketch: startBillingSession(tenant, v1_key); for each non-dup chunk: estimate tokens -> session.increment(tokens) -> routeTo(v2); emit compat metrics. Commit on stream end.
Nora K: Owners: Luis (billing mapping + dedupe), Nora (telemetry & alerts), Ivy (console copy + reconcile mock). I'll draft RFC and schedule 30m sync.
Ivy W: RFC: https://rfc.internal/redwood/darklaunch-stream-reconcile (internal). Sync tomorrow 10:30 UTC.
